- **#354 (8da70a9d).** "the staff side and the admin panel (phone)" logged in by clicking the login form's submit, then pressed Escape in the same tab. The CI log shows `cdp: the Escape key never reached the page` three times, with the page focused and visible. It now logs in with the form's own fields sent by `fetch`, through `logInWithFetch(…, { keepCookies: true })`. The new option keeps the session, so the Spanish chosen before logging in stays. author: sectr99
body:
Adds an opt-in macOS setting, **Match menu bar to theme**, which removes the pale strip behind the menu bar.

## Cause
macOS draws a frosted strip behind the menu bar wherever a window lies under it, and Glyphdrift's full-screen wallpaper windows count. Over the desktop picture the bar stays clear. With Glyphdrift stopped, the menu bar over a solid dark picture showed no tint.

## What the setting does
- **The wallpaper stops below the menu bar:** windows end at the top of `visibleFrame`. Nothing changes when the menu bar hides automatically.
- **Solid desktop picture:** each screen's picture becomes a solid PNG in the theme's background color, including the Icon readability veil, so the bar sits on the theme's color. It's re-checked once a second, which picks up theme changes, new screens and other Spaces.
- **The user's picture is preserved:** the picture and its scaling options are written to `desktop-pictures.txt` before anything changes. They're restored when the option is turned off, on quit, or on the next launch after a crash. If the user picks a new picture while the option is on, that becomes the one to restore.
- **Where to turn it on:** the Settings window checkbox, **Match Menu Bar to Theme** in the menu bar menu, or `match_menu_bar = true` in `[general]`. It's off by default because it changes the desktop picture. Windows ignores the key.

## Limitation
macOS keeps a picture per Space, and an app can only set the current one. Other Spaces switch within a second of being visited, but quitting only restores the Space you're on. This is documented in the README.

## Testing
On macOS 26, M1 Pro, one screen:
- [x] Turning it on: the menu bar is clear and on the theme color, and the contours start below it
- [x] Turning it off: the original picture (`DefaultDesktop.heic`) is restored and its files removed
- [x] Quitting the app bundle restores the picture
- [x] Killing the app keeps the original recorded, and the next launch handles it correctly
- [x] Settings checkbox and menu item reflect the setting
- [x] `cargo test`: 34 passed; clippy clean for macOS and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`
- [ ] Several Spaces, multiple monitors, auto-hiding menu bar

## 独立小切片：跨账号 UI_START 仍被旧运行清理间隙阻塞（Issue #121）

Baseline: exact accepted main `eaf10224e9aea411712b05eeea00180acb68ea29`。不混入 PR #120 的 AI 配置验证权威工作。

### Evidence from real failing CI (not guessed from screenshot)
- PR #120 exact HEAD `f5bb95b9fa70c2c5e6b7eaa430f337ac996e8b56` 的 [PR run #38117042133](https://github.com/ljjnb666-nb/AI-Question-Analysis-Assistant-Browser-Extension/actions/runs/38117042133) E2E **87/88**，`uiOwnerAuthFence.phase14bE3B2B1.spec.ts:167` fails; same-head Push passed 88/88. Historical failure retained.
- Downloaded actual Playwright error-context + trace from artifact **11694350984**. Trace timing: second real UI click at monotonic 100684ms; a new storage owner becomes visible ~100728ms; stale old STOP is correctly rejected ~100740ms; workspace's first snapshot at ~100743ms already returns `fullPage.running !== true` and stays false for 10s. Thus this is not simply late polling after a slow scan.
- `src/content/protectedWorkRunAuthority.ts` has `begin(): if (active.has(kind)) return null`, even when exact previous STOP has already **revoked** its execution lease. Its promise may not have reached `finally` when a different user STARTs a new generation. Sidepanel persists the new owner *before* sending START, so owner existence cannot prove that content accepted START. This is the suspected race; not yet declared fixed on real Edge.

### Bounded correction
- Exact tagged STOP still revokes old run; a **different tagged generation** may begin before the old async task's final cleanup, but only if old lease already `revoked=true`.
- Never replace a live nonrevoked run, never restart the same canceled generation, never use an untagged legacy START to bypass cleanup. Lease numbers monotonically increase; old `finish`, STOP, DONE and callback remain generation-fenced.
- Added deterministic tests I121-01 through I121-03, strengthened existing E1_01/E2_01 revocation and ownership assertions. No scan limit, auth owner, user submission or production UI changes.

### Gates
Exact HEAD Push + PR 9/9; 166+ unit files; 88 extension E2E; 20x50 Popup soak; RC manifest + restored image identity + SHA-bound artifacts; unresolved review check. Failure history preserved. Real user Edge acceptance still PENDING.

**DRAFT / OPEN / UNMERGED. Do not merge without a new explicit user authorization.**

author: ronaldtse
body:
Closes the ieee parseUrn parity gap - the flavor leaves the urn-parity KNOWN-DIVERGENT set at 9,502/9,502 rows.

The 26 misses were three grammar divergences from the artifact:

- **Adoption faces** (~19 rows, `urn:ieee:iso-iec-ieee:8802-1AB:2014`): the number rule carried a ts-only dash-digits group that swallowed `-1` and stranded letter parts; the artifact's number leaves dash continuations to the part rule, so `IEEE Std 8802-1AB-2014` now parses. The group's real job (dashed codes rendering dotted) moved to where it belongs: the part rule captures its separator (`part_sep`) beside the bare token, and the builder joins the code with the original separator - `62271-37-082` stays dashed, `802.3` stays dotted (both the flat and the corrigendum-base builder paths).
- **draft.D= tails** (6 rows, `urn:ieee:iec-ieee:P61850-9-3:draft.D=FDIS`): draft_version gains the artifact's dot-led alternative (`dot !(year) (alnum / dot)`), so the reconstruction `/Ddraft.D=FDIS` parses and round-trips the reference's own render byte-for-byte.
- **Glued `(E)`** (1 row): already handled by the year rule's silent `["(E)"]` consumption - it worked once the dashed part stopped breaking the route.

Also: 11 pends unmarked (the separator fix made them pass; 424 remain), and the urn-parity test asserts ieee strictly now (nist stays KNOWN-DIVERGENT on the reference's own render defect).

Full suite green locally: 188/188.

  - 確定離開後遊戲維持暫停直到換頁，存檔期間不會又打完一關。流程中途放棄時呼叫 `cancelLeave()`。

author: chiragjangiir
body:
## What this changes

A download that fails now names the yt-dlp that produced it, and adds that a
newer yt-dlp may already have the fix when the failure looks like the site
changing under the extractor.

Refs #39 — deliberately not `Fixes`, see below.

## Why

`yt-dlp` is collected into the installer at build time (`clips-studio.spec`),
while Twitch, Kick and YouTube change things regularly and yt-dlp fixes them
within days. So a site change breaks one platform for every installed copy
until the next release, and the failure itself says nothing about the version
that hit it. This is what a user gets today for an extractor break, captured
from `main`:

```
ERROR: [kick] 1a2b3c4d: Unable to extract video data; please report this issue
on https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q= . Confirm you are on the latest
version using  yt-dlp -U
```

Nothing there identifies the copy in use, so "Kick stopped working" cannot be
triaged without asking for a Feedback Hub report, and a user has no way to know
the fix already exists upstream. `KNOWN-ISSUES.md` explains the situation, but
only to someone who goes looking — the failure says nothing. #39 notes that
option 1 is worth doing regardless of the other two, and it is what this does.

Every platform's download already passes through one function
(`sources/dispatch.download`), so the version travels with the failure from one
place rather than three. The note reads from `yt_dlp.version.__version__` at
runtime — the same import `server/feedback.py` uses — so it reports the bundled
copy in an installed build, and nothing is hard-coded:

```
Clips Kitty's bundled yt-dlp is 2026.08.19. This reads like a change on the
site, which yt-dlp fixes within days — but the copy inside the app is fixed at
build time, so a newer yt-dlp may already have the fix:
https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases
```

Only evidence of an extractor change gets that suggestion: yt-dlp's own wording
(`unable to extract`, `no video formats found`, `unsupported url`,
`nsig extraction failed`) plus the `Confirm you are on the latest version` hint
it prints with those errors. A timeout or a sign-in wall gets the version as
context and no claim, because a newer yt-dlp would not have helped and pointing
someone at one moves them further from the answer.

## How you tested it

- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes (in `ui/`)
- [ ] Tried the affected flow in the running app
- [ ] Tested on a real video: platform and length:

None of the three apply: this touches no `ui/` file, and it changes no clipping,
tracking, caption or rendering behaviour. It was not run against a real video
because it does not need one — no download is made anywhere in the change or its
tests.

What was run, from the repository root:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest` — no yt-dlp (the CI `Python` job's environment) | 2345 passed, 482 skipped |
| `pytest` — with yt-dlp 2026.08.19 and defusedxml | 2416 passed, 473 skipped |
| `pytest tests/test_ytdlp_failure_diagnostics.py` — no yt-dlp | 12 passed, 4 skipped |
| `pytest tests/test_ytdlp_failure_diagnostics.py` — with yt-dlp | 16 passed |
| `ruff check .` | All checks passed |
| `python -m compileall -q analysis core creator llm longform multilingual plugins publish sdk server sources sports transcription video video_editor main.py` | exit 0 |

The two messages quoted above are real output, from the same probe run against
`main` and against this branch with the platform downloader replaced by the
failure. No network request is made and no download happens in any test.

The new file follows the split already used in `tests/test_input_safety.py`: the
version lookup and the wording live in `sources/ytdlp_common.py`, which imports
without yt-dlp, so those run in the `Python` job. The four tests that need the
source modules sit behind `pytest.importorskip("yt_dlp")`, so they skip there and
run wherever yt-dlp is installed.

## Anything reviewers should know

- **This is option 1 of the three in #39, not option 3.** It says which yt-dlp
  produced the failure; the app still downloads and installs nothing, adds no
  startup check, and makes no request for a version. That is why it is `Refs`,
  not `Fixes`.
- **The failure is preserved.** The exception is re-raised, not replaced, so
  `except DownloadError`, `except ValueError` and `except Exception` all still
  catch it and the traceback still points at the platform that failed.
- **Nothing is added where the app already explains itself.** Every failure the
  sources translate into plain English raises `ValueError` (`youtube._friendly_errors`,
  `kick._gone_or_raise`: age-gated, deleted Kick VOD, live stream, wrong-platform
  link), and cancellations are left alone. Appending a version to those reads as
  noise, and on the live-stream and wrong-link ones it is not even relevant.
  The trade-off: if a future source explained a failure with something other
  than `ValueError`, that failure would get a version line it does not need.
- **The signature lists are a heuristic, and they under-claim on purpose.** An
  extractor error worded differently falls through to the version-only note
  rather than being guessed at. A test asserts that a timeout and both kinds of
  sign-in wall are *not* told to update.
- **The note cannot leak anything.** It interpolates the version and no part of
  the failure text, so it cannot put a cookie, token or private URL back into a
  message the job layer scrubs. There is a test for that.
- **One limitation worth knowing:** `server/jobs.py` broadcasts the first 500
  characters of a failure (2000 are stored). The note is appended, so a very
  long upstream error could push it out of the live event. Prefixing instead
  would cut the original reason, which seemed the worse trade.
- **Not verified against a live site change.** No real upstream break was
  reproduced; the classification is asserted against the wording yt-dlp is known
  to use, which models the failure rather than being it. Worth keeping in mind if
  a signature list needs widening later.
- Only failures reaching `dispatch.download` are annotated. Channel listing
  (`sources/channel_feed.py`) and the split-setup probe
  (`sources/preview_frames.py`) keep their current wording, since #39 is about
  downloads — say the word if you want those covered too.

author: kkora
body:
## What this closes

`deploy-prod.yml` and `deploy-stg.yml` accept `workflow_dispatch`, which runs at whatever ref the dispatcher picks. As a result, `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml --ref develop` deployed develop to production with production's environment secrets.

The product's `promotion-gate.yml` had the same shape. A dispatch for `prod` from any branch received prod's `DOPPLER_TOKEN` and `FLY_API_TOKEN`, then ran that branch's own `tooling/`.

The GitHub environments stopped neither path:
- All four environments use "any protected branch". Since test, staging and main are all protected, `prod` admitted `staging` and `test`.
- `reviewer_team_ids` was never passed in, so stg and prod have no reviewer in any repository.

No stg or prod deployment has ever run in Docoris, Lexveria or the Control Plane. The gap was open but never used.

## Two layers, because each covers what the other cannot

**1. Ref guard, in the workflow files. It takes effect on merge.**
- `profiles/_shared/template/local/scripts/deploy-ref-guard.sh` is run by a `ref-guard` job. Every other job in `deploy.yml` and `promotion-gate.yml` waits for it.
- It allows `prod` only from `refs/heads/main` and `stg` only from `refs/heads/staging`.
- It allows only `push` and `workflow_dispatch` events.
- It allows only `deploy-<env>.yml` or `promotion-gate.yml` of this repository, at that branch, to start a run.
- An unknown environment, including `PROD` or `production`, fails closed.
- `dev` and `test` are not restricted.
- A wrong-ref run gets a concurrency group of its own. Otherwise a dispatch that the guard is about to refuse could still cancel a legitimate pending deployment.
- In `deploy.yml` the guard names the environment, as every job there must. The workflow's `required: true` secrets live on the environment, and a single job without one rejects the whole run. The existing generation test caught exactly that in the first version of this change. Naming the environment gives the guard nothing it does not reference.

The guard is read from the ref it guards, so a branch that edits it is not stopped by it. Layer 2 is what stops that branch.

**2. Environment branch policy, in Terraform. It takes effect only when applied, and this PR applies nothing.**
- `modules/github` binds `stg` to `staging` and `prod` to `main` with custom deployment-branch policies.
- It takes reviewer users as well as teams, plus `environment_prevent_self_review`, which defaults to false.
- It refuses a self-review rule that has no reviewer, because GitHub silently drops one.

**Required checks become a variable.** `required_status_checks` has `nullable = false`, and its default is the old literal list, so no product plans a branch-protection change. The root and `project-bootstrap` pass `null`, so the list is written once. A repository whose CI differs names its own list in `terraform.tfvars`. The Control Plane does, in its own PR.

## Files

**Workflows and script**
- `profiles/_shared/template/.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- `profiles/product/template/.github/workflows/promotion-gate.yml`
- `profiles/_shared/template/local/scripts/deploy-ref-guard.sh` (new)

**Terraform**
- `infrastructure/terraform/modules/github/{main.tf,variables.tf}`
- `tests/deployment_safety.tftest.hcl` (new)
- `modules/project-bootstrap/{main.tf,variables.tf}`
- `profiles/_shared/template/infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf`
- `profiles/{product,control-plane}/template/infrastructure/terraform/main.tf.hbs`

**Tests**
- `profiles/_shared/template/tests/security/test_deploy_ref_guard.py` (new)
- `profiles/_shared/template/tests/security/test_required_checks.py` (new)
- `generators/create-koras-app/tests/github-module-plan.test.ts` (new)
- `generators/create-koras-app/tests/fixtures/github-module.terraform.lock.hcl` (new): github 6.13.0, the estate's pin, with an `h1:` hash for linux, windows and darwin. It is a fixture rather than a module file because a module directory ships into every generated project and must carry no Terraform working files. CI found this on the first push.
- `branch-protection.test.ts` and `product-secure-files-promotion.test.ts` (updated)

**Docs**
- `docs/RISK_REGISTER.md` (R-053)
- `docs/ENVIRONMENT_STRATEGY.md`: it said stg and prod require one and two approvals, and no repository ever had either.
- `docs/PROVISIONING_RUNBOOK.md` (apply procedure)

## Evidence, local, on Windows

- **`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`:** pass.
- **`pnpm test`:** all `create-koras-app` suites pass, including `generation.test.ts`, `branch-protection`, `github-module-plan` and `product-secure-files-promotion`. `koras-docs-tests` passes 562/562, and its three R-042 findings on the first draft of R-053 were fixed.
- **`terraform test`:** 8/8 on Terraform 1.9.8 (CI's version) against a mock provider, with `init -lockfile=readonly`. `terraform validate` and `fmt -check` are clean.
- **Guard tests:** 23 refusal cases and 8 admission cases, plus the wiring: every job that names an environment waits for the guard; the guard has no `continue-on-error`, `if:` or `needs`; it names its environment exactly when the workflow requires secrets; it reads no secret; callers are named for their environment; the concurrency group is isolated.
- **Generated projects:**
  - product with `secure_files,clamd,worker`: 46 passed, including the promotion-gate wiring;
  - control-plane: 41 passed;
  - in both, `${{ github.workflow_ref }}` survives Handlebars.
- **Mutation checks.** Each of these mutations turned the suite red:
  - guard: admits everything, prefix match, `needs` dropped, `continue-on-error` added, environment dropped, old concurrency group, case-folding the workflow name;
  - module: prod back to protected branches, `nullable` removed, reviewer users dropped, stg unbound.

## Independent reviews (two, read-only, in parallel)

- **Security:** no Critical findings. It asked for:
  - the concurrency isolation;
  - forbidding `continue-on-error` on the guard;
  - case-insensitive owner/repo matching;
  - precise wording on what S0 does not cover.

  All were done.
- **Terraform:** no blockers.
  - All changes are in place, and no environment or secret is replaced.
  - It asked for the provider to be pinned by a lock file and for the self-review precondition. Both were done.

## Expected plan when a repository applies this

- **Product:** `github_repository_environment_deployment_policy.branch["stg"|"prod"]` are added, and `environments["stg"|"prod"]` change in place. Total: 2 to add, 2 to change, 0 to destroy, with no branch-protection change.
- **Control Plane:** the same, plus `protections["test"|"staging"|"main"]` in place. Total: 2 to add, 5 to change.

## Rollout and rollback

1. Merge this, then each repository's PR. The ref guard takes effect on merge.
2. In each repository, follow `docs/PROVISIONING_RUNBOOK.md` → *Binding stg and prod to their branch*: plan, read the plan, then apply outside a push to staging or main. Between an environment switching to custom policies and its policy being created, the environment admits no branch, so it fails closed. Afterwards, cancel any waiting stg or prod run.
3. **Rollback:** revert the PR and apply. The two policies are deleted, and the environments return to "any protected branch" in place. Neither direction touches an environment's secrets.

## Decisions needed (none taken here)

1. **Repository-level `FLY_API_TOKEN` / `VERCEL_TOKEN` (High, unchanged by S0).**
   - One token serves every environment, so each can deploy to production. Any branch can read them, with no environment involved.
   - S0 closes the routes that hand stg/prod *environment* secrets to an unauthorised ref. It does not stop deploying code to the prod runtime with these tokens.
   - The fix is per-environment credentials: a Fly deploy token per app, and for Vercel a separate team or deploy hooks. That is a credential chang

author: aburan28
body:
## Contribution

Store the indexed S3 roots' lifted y coordinates in polynomial form and apply inverse Frobenius to the public query point for each orientation. Batched point addition runs on the unrotated roots; rotating the two partner roots back preserves the exact canonical key and first-inserted witness lookup. This removes 4,000,000 target-time basis conversions relative to the prior point-partner implementation.

## Frozen N83 evidence

- Curve `EC1N83Ckb1h876c2921cb64`, workload `981ac530e67e`, one public target, 2,000,000 indexed pair states, 4,000,000 distinct root keys, 1,024 MiB RSS cap. Both arms recorded `state_cap_no_relation`.
- Full audit compared all 4,000,000 candidate partner pairs after Frobenius rotation with the original S3 evaluator; all 8,000,000 partner roots agreed. Seven Rust tests passed, including all GF(32) curve-point pairs and every Frobenius shift.
- Six counterbalanced same-point local runs had zero invariant mismatches. Median target process CPU was 2.470 s for S3 and 2.150 s for this candidate; the candidate was lower in all three adjacent pairs. Median target wall was 17.678 s and 16.921 s. These local timings are exploratory because host isolation was not established.
- Target field multiplication calls were 43,998,533 and 19,998,533. Candidate precomputation stored 64,000,000 additional bytes of lifted y coordinates; median index-build process CPU was 1.021 s and 1.718 s. The packed root table remained 83,922,944 bytes in both arms.
- Exact wrapper replay produced the same pair certificate for both arms: `01a3c02a7ca42fa75c6dfca9a0011ee2a83c66cca5487ff6a4446199223c0c16`. Phase sums, raw runs, memory, source/input hashes, full audit, and a six-repetition isolated-service manifest validator are retained in the experiment directory.

## Verification

- `cargo test --release --locked` with the frozen `NATIVE_S3_*` source/manifest hashes: 7 passed.
- Full native N83 `packed_sparse24_compact16_frobpointpartners_audit`: 4,000,000 matching pairs and 8,000,000 roots under the cap.
- `python3 run.py`: six raw same-point runs, `invariant_mismatches={}`.
- Both `benchmark_stage.py` wrapper arms verified their frozen raw output and shared pair certificate.
- `python3 make_manifest.py` validated the frozen inputs, source, audit, and paired replay, producing one six-repetition isolated-service case.

The next measurement is the prepared physical-host isolation replay, followed by full-pipeline one-target accounting under the repository contract.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Self-contained research experiment with audited equivalence to S3; no production service paths changed, though correctness of the new curve arithmetic affects benchmark validity only.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a frozen N83 E-1 experiment (`packed_index_e1_frobenius_pointpartners_cpu_20261011`) that extends the packed root-index native binary with **Frobenius-shifted batched point partners** versus the existing S3 reference arm (`packed_sparse24_compact16_unclocked_tag`).
> 
> The candidate **precomputes polynomial `y` lifts for indexed S3 roots** during index build (~64 MiB extra), then at query time applies **inverse Frobenius to the public target**, forms partners via **batched point addition** on unrotated roots, and **rotates partners back** before the same canonical lookup and first-inserted witness rules. Target-time **S3 partner calls drop to zero** (4M on reference) at the cost of index root-lift work and higher index-build CPU.
> 
> The PR bundles **`native_packed_index.rs`** (new modes + audit mode), **`run.py` / `benchmark_stage.py` / `make_manifest.py`**, protocol and **6-run counterbalanced** artifacts, a **4M-pair audit** matching S3, wrapper replay with a shared pair certificate, and an isolated-benchmark manifest validator—not changes to the main `crypto` crate (via symlinked snapshot).
>

author: tum17124
body:
## Summary
Rebuilds notes for the PDF/EPUB reader and the audio player: TipTap (MIT) rich-text editor with a compact, phone-friendly toolbar; highlights in four colours, each optionally with a note; page-position notes; audio notes at a timestamp ("Add note at 12:34", with a "pause while I write" choice); a notes panel (right side panel on desktop, bottom sheet on phones) grouped by page/chapter or by time, with search, type and colour filters, sort, in-place edit with autosave + "Saved" indicator, delete with Undo; a **My notes** page across all books; Markdown/PDF export; a local-first sync store (offline queue, idempotent retried saves, cross-tab).

## Root cause / gap
Notes were plain text only (280 chars), single colour, local-only offsets, no timestamps UI beyond a text field, no export/search/cross-book view, no offline.

## Files changed
`src/lib/notes/*` (types, doc helpers, API client, local-first store + registry + hook, view helpers, paint), `src/components/notes/*` (RichNoteEditor, NoteView, NotesPanel, SaveIndicator), `src/components/pdf-reader.tsx` (notes layer swapped: draft bar with colours/editor, coloured painting, page notes, panel; TTS/progress/zoom code untouched), `src/components/audio-player.tsx` (notes card + panel), `src/app/notes/*` (My notes), `src/components/ui/notch-navbar.tsx` (two "My notes" links — shared file, minimal), `src/lib/api.ts` (one type widened: `idempotencyKey` accepted by `contentFetch`), `src/lib/seo-rules.test.ts` (`notes` must be noindex), `package.json` (+@tiptap/*).
Not touched: books-showcase / 3D book, banners/ads/signals code.

## Security considerations
Notes are structured JSON, rendered only as React elements (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`); links are re-validated (http/https/mailto) and open with `noopener noreferrer nofollow`; the server independently rejects unsafe documents. Local copies are keyed per account (JWT user id) or guest, so two accounts on one browser never share cached notes. Nothing is logged to Activity signals.

## Tests
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; vitest 269 passed (new: store offline/queue/backoff/in-flight edits/two-device LWW/tombstones/undo/cross-tab/refused-note/account isolation; paint colours; filters/sort/grouping; editor toolbar a11y + formatting round-trip (every mark/list/task/heading survives an edit); NoteView XSS; panel search/filter/jump/audio grouping/delete+undo/Escape/read-only/export). ESLint: no new problems (existing errors in `pdf-reader.tsx`, `audio-player.tsx`, `notch-navbar.tsx` are unchanged, pre-existing).
Real Chromium against the local backend (desktop, phone 390x844, dark): migrated legacy notes appear; highlight → green with a rich note (bold + bullet list) saved to the server as structured JSON and painted green; page note + 📝 page marker; panel is a 400px right drawer on desktop and a bottom sheet on the phone; search/edit/autosave ("Saved ✓")/delete→Undo; jump scrolls to the highlight; Markdown and PDF exports download; offline: note shows "Offline · will sync", is not on the server, then syncs after reconnect; persists across reload; audio: note at 0:12 pauses playback while writing and resumes after saving (toggle off keeps playing), bookmark in one tap, panel groups by time, jumping seeks to 0:30; My notes page lists everything and exports; no console/page errors.

## Decisions made
- Highlights keep the reader's existing offset/quote anchoring (so jump-to and painting behave as before); colours are per note, overlapping highlights are clipped (earlier wins).
- Pages with a page-position note get a small 📝 marker; tapping a painted highlight opens the panel.
- Editing happens in the panel (autosave, 600 ms debounce); the draft bar is only for creating. My notes is read-only (edit in the book where the context is) with per-book export.
- Notes need a login or a guest link; logged-out readers see a "log in to keep notes" hint.
- The editor autofocuses when opened (found in the browser that omitting autofocus left the editor unmounted in the phone layout; the editor now only passes the option when true).
- Old local-only highlights (never synced) are imported once into the new store on first open, then the old local key is cleared.

## Not done
Edit-in-place from My notes; tapping a painted highlight does not scroll its note into view in the panel; the pop-out/PiP reader pane shows highlights but not the editor; the audio chapter is not recorded (the player has no chapter data) so audio is grouped by 10-minute blocks.

## Deployment notes
New dependencies: `@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/pm`, `@tiptap/starter-kit`, `@tiptap/extension-{highlight,task-list,task-item,placeholder}` (MIT). `npm ci`, `rm -rf out && npx next build`. Requires the backend PR deployed first (migrations 0091/0092). May conflict textually with the open EPUB reader PR in `pdf-reader.tsx` (different regions; merge by hand if needed).

Regression tests added; GitHub CI pending.

The index editor's field list (字段列表) rendered columns in table ordinal order, so picking a column from a wide table meant scanning the whole list to find one (Closes #11747).

body:

body:
## Purpose

Turn the #238 open-abort flaky-test post-mortem into a **small, reusable concurrency test-authoring method** without turning tests into product authority.

Refs #238; related #195 and PR #220. **Do not auto-close #238:** its historical incident and later follow-ups remain discoverable.

## Scope (docs only)

- `docs/development/concurrency-test-design.md`: the five-question authoring contract (**property, precondition, legal outcomes, observation boundary, falsifier**); minimum wait-for/producer→consumer DAG; three test shapes (deterministically pinned premise, contract-legal multi-outcome invariant, bounded Loom exploration); safety vs liveness; timeout/sleep restrictions, non-vacuity, negative control and cleanup.
- `docs/README.md`: one routing entry for timing/concurrency test writing and review.
- `AGENTS.md`: compact requirement that **new or materially modified** timing-sensitive tests apply this method, without inventing authority or imposing a retroactive audit.

Four evidence-backed worked examples pinned to the exact merged #237 baseline (`39f53d4`):
1. #238 pre-routed pause before spawn: avoid an unsatisfiable wait.
2. #238 pause arriving mid-read: establish entry with a latch, then verify the next loop-top.
3. #195 pended seek × live update: accept legitimate competing schedules **with per-outcome assertions**; leave seek park/actionability authority OPEN.
4. PR #220 `Failed` Fact vs data-plane terminal: take the correct post-`dispose()` witness, including the producer-side negative control.

Existing PcmEdge Loom (`loom_edge_tests.rs`) is **reused**, not rediscovered or installed as a new dependency.

## Authority and non-goals

`ADR-PBK-001/002/003`, K0 authorities and the relevant protocol contracts retain all product semantics. This is a **NON-NORMATIVE developer guide** about how to establish and falsify test claims.

No production code changes, no changes to existing tests, no new scheduler/test framework, no test registry, no global timeout increase, no bulk inventory/audit and no implied closure of #195.

## Review checkpoints

- [x] Five questions, three test modes, safety/liveness boundary and explicit non-vacuity.
- [x] Two deterministic real-code examples and multi-outcome / Fact-vs-edge examples.
- [x] Navigation via docs router and short AGENTS cross-reference.
- [x] Exact main base SHA and docs-only three-file diff checked via GitHub compare.
- [ ] Required local `lefthook run pre-push --all-files` — **NOT_RUN** in this connector-only authoring session; run on checkout before merge.
- [ ] GitHub CI results — pending / verify from actual checks; do not infer PASS.
- [ ] Owner review and merge.

**Diff base:** `39f53d4ce7319c2958efb140220b187b9a5d8741`
**Branch:** `docs/concurrency-test-design-238`

Please review the protocol as a *test-writing obligation*, not a new semantics/architecture authority.

author: naplesexperiences-netizen
body:
I quattro punti ad alta priorità emersi dalla revisione del sito live.

## Claim incoerenti

Il case study dell'agenzia tour in home diceva **"da 5 a 20 prenotazioni in 90 giorni"** e **"+€20k revenue/anno"**. L'articolo che si apre cliccando documenta tutt'altro: la crescita è su **dodici mesi** e il fatturato passa da **€21K a €92K**. Un numero che il lettore può verificare con un clic non può contraddire la pagina che apre.

La scheda riporta ora le cifre dell'articolo: 12 mesi, 4× prenotazioni, 38% vendite dirette, +14% ticket medio, €21K→€92K.

**"Zero overbooking garantito"** è una promessa contrattuale: se succede lo stesso, è contestabile. Diventa la descrizione del meccanismo reale — *disponibilità allineata su ogni canale, niente doppie prenotazioni*.

**"100% soddisfazione"** non poggia su niente di misurabile e nessuno se lo beve. Sostituito con **<24h tempo di risposta**, che è verificabile e al cliente interessa di più.

Il portfolio dichiarava che tutti i siti *"generano prenotazioni reali"*, ma contiene un centro medico, un museo e un ente di formazione: basta un clic per accorgersene. Ora dice cosa sono davvero.

## Dati societari nel footer

Ragione sociale, sede, P.IVA e REA mancavano dal piede di pagina, dove l'art. 2250 c.c. li vuole. Si compilano dal Personalizzatore → **Dati legali**, insieme ai campi già presenti dalla v2.6.0, con due campi nuovi (REA e capitale sociale).

La riga compare **solo quando c'è più della sola ragione sociale**: una riga con dei buchi sarebbe peggio di nessuna riga. Anche il copyright prende il nome dal campo invece di averlo scritto dentro.

## Meta mancanti

`/configuratore/` era indicizzabile con **description vuota**, perché la pagina è costruita dal template e non ha contenuto da cui ricavarla. `/blog/` non aveva description affatto: `is_singular()` è falso su un archivio e nessuna delle funzioni esistenti lo copriva.

I due testi sono ora scritti a mano, con il titolo che li accompagna, tutti sotto le soglie di taglio di Google:

```
configuratore   title  49 char · desc 150 char
blog            title  51 char · desc 149 char
home            title  51 char
```

Il `<title>` della home era quello grezzo di WordPress — *nome del sito – motto* — generico e diverso dall'`og:title`, che dice cosa facciamo. Ora coincidono. Dove la description resta vuota il tag non viene più stampato: un tag vuoto dice a Google che la pagina non ha niente da raccontare.

## Sitemap

`wp-sitemap-users-1.xml` pubblicava i nomi utente di chi scrive, che sono metà del lavoro per chi prova a entrare in bacheca. Disattivata.

**Una cosa che ho corretto in corsa:** avevo tolto anche la sitemap dei tag dando per scontato che fossero inutilizzati. Controllando sono popolati e pertinenti (`channel-manager`, `seo-locale`, `napoli`…), quindi toglierli sarebbe stata una perdita di SEO non richiesta. Rimessi com'erano.

## Verifiche

Banco di prova su titoli e description per home, elenco articoli, configuratore e pagina generica; riga societaria con nessun campo, un campo solo e tutti compilati; footer a 390 px senza overflow. `php -l` su tutti i 16 file.

### Stato del sito prima di queste modifiche

Verificato che la v2.11.0 online funziona su tutto il resto:

```
nav            Servizi · Lavori · Anteprima · AI · Prezzi · Blog · Contatti
consenso       analytics e ads "denied" di default
tabulazione    0 stop nel menu nascosto
footer         3 colonne desktop, 2 mobile
mobile 390     banner 390px, bottone 44×44, nessun overflow
avatar         358×636 verticale, facciata attiva, nessun iframe prima del clic
configuratore  attivo, CSS applicato, nessun errore
```

## 改了什么

把界面里两类不自然的文案改掉了。

**口号腔**：登录页的“想法不必完整，先留下一句。”，加上“写下 / 继续 / 带走”三段卖点；首页的“写下你正在想的。先留下一句，以后可以接着写。”；回看页的“把分散的念头放在一起，找到值得继续想的地方。”。这些要么删掉，要么改成一句说清楚这是什么的话。

几个例子：

| 原来 | 现在 |
|---|---|
| 想法不必完整，先留下一句。 | 记想法的地方 |
| 留一个自己的空间 / 欢迎回来 | 创建账号 / 登录 |
| 开启并开始串联 | 开启并开始找 |
| 等你判断 | 待处理 |
| 联系说明 · AI提出 | AI 的理由 |
| 导出云端全部想法 | 导出全部想法（JSON） |
| 下载本机内容 | 导出还没同步的内容 |

回看的隐私说明（发给 DeepSeek 的范围：最近 20 条想法的开头和最新一段、最多 3 组）保留了，只是换成了直白的说法。

The fixture and tests use an in-memory store and an email sink, so they do not write live Firestore or send SMTP. It does not import #132 or #134. ## Square webhook `POST /api/payments/square-webhook` reads the raw body. `express.raw` is mounted on that path in `server/index.ts` before `express.json()`. Signature is HMAC-SHA256 of `SQUARE_WEBHOOK_NOTIFICATION_URL` + those exact bytes, keyed with `SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY`, compared timing-safe to `x-square-hmacsha256-signature`. There is no `APP_URL` or `FRONTEND_URL` fallback. A missing key or notification URL returns 401, logs `webhook not configured`, and writes nothing. A bad signature or a parsed (non-raw) body returns 403 and writes nothing. `payment.created` and `payment.updated` with status `COMPLETED`, and `invoice.payment_made`, resolve the invoice with the existing matcher (invoice id note, `reference_id`, Square order id, payment link id) and follow `redirectInvoiceId`. The paid write and the unlock write run in one Firestore transaction. Idempotency is `squareWebhookEvents/{event_id}` plus `appliedSquarePaymentIds` / `squarePaymentId`. A replay, or a later `payment.updated` for a payment already counted by `invoice.payment_made`, does not add to `amountPaid`, write another history line, or send another receipt. A full payment sets `clientGalleryDownloadsUnlocked`, turns `lockDownloads` off, sets `downloadsReleased` and `downloadEnabled`, and sets `paymentStatus` / `invoiceStatus` to `paid` on the linked listing and gallery. History on `orders.history` and the listing audit log is `Payment received $X via Square; downloads unlocked`. A partial payment updates the balance and logs history, and does not unlock. An unknown invoice returns 200 and is logged, so Square does not retry it, and no invoice is written. Playtest invoices take the same path. ## Receipt `payment_receipt` is table-based, inline-styled HTML (Arial/Helvetica) plus a plain-text part. Processing is charged on top. The local `processingFee` matches #132: half-up cents of `baseCents * 0.028`, where base = subtotal − promotions + fees. TODO: import #132's shared helper after that PR merges and pass that same base. The receipt shows the stored `processing` field when the invoice has one, otherwise 2.8% of the base. It shows that amount only when the dollars paid include it. A fully paid Showcase is subtotal $549, processing $15.37, total paid $564.37. A legacy invoice charged without the fee, and a comped invoice, show PROCESSING $0.00. `server/services/clientLinks.ts` exports `presentationLinkForReceipt(listing)`, which returns null until #134. The swap after that merge is one line: `return clientPresentationLinkFor(listing);`. While it is null, the receipt omits "View your listing presentation" and makes `/gallery/:id` the primary button. Every absolute link uses `publicSiteUrl()`. The send goes through `sendEmail`. With `CLIENT_NOTIFY_LIVE` unset, only an exact `NOTIFY_TEST_ALLOWLIST` address is delivered. Everyone else is suppressed and the history line says so. The graffiti PNG is at `public/media/logos/iconic-graffiti-logo.png` (the same asset #132 adds). The email `src` is `publicSiteUrl() + /media/logos/iconic-graffiti-logo.png`. `api/index.mjs` was regenerated with `vite build --config vite.config.vercel.ts`. ## Office and marketing links `office_new_order` and the `booking_received` `dashboardUrl` variable use `publicSiteUrl()/admin/order-request/:id`. GMass `marketingPublicUrl` uses `MARKETING_PUBLIC_URL`, then `publicSiteUrl()`. It does not read `APP_URL`. `booking_received` and the booking-confirmation SMS stay ungated on purpose. The go-live doc marks them **intentional, keep live**. Still built from `APP_URL`, and left alone because they are not a link in an email or SMS body: - `server/routes/sms.ts` Twilio webhook URL (`/api/sms/webhook`). Twilio signs that callback. It is not message text. - `server/routes/presentations.ts` `originOf` for the presentation page and the URL returned when a token is created. Creating a token does not email or text. #134 owns the client presentation link. - `server/services/studioQueueKick.ts` cron tick, `server/services/playtestBootstrap.ts` seed origin, and `server/node-build.ts` request origin. ## Go-live checklist `docs/client-notify-go-live.md`

body:
TermiX cloud hosting explains the service but does not execute the research engine. This adds a local report builder, read-only provider order queue, and exact-content human review/delivery handoff for fual-treasury.agent's BSC research listing.

Reports cover one to five explicit Spot USDT pairs and optional portfolio weights using 120 aligned closed UTC daily candles from a fresh host-injected Binance MCP snapshot. Malformed/gapped/stale data blocks generation. The existing BNB/BTC regime, relationship, shock and risk checks remain research only; historical live-readiness gates remain failed.

The queue paginates authenticated provider orders scoped to this agent/listing. Drafts require indexed on-chain identity, FUNDED/IN_PROGRESS, unexpired delivery deadline, canSubmitDelivery and operator-reviewed structured intake. It rechecks live state after calculation, locks per order, publishes drafts atomically and verifies artifact hashes on retries.

Review creates a separate editable client-facing Markdown copy without overwriting source evidence. An explicit approval command binds the human's instruction to the exact report bytes, source manifest, job and live order. Changed content, source evidence or order terms invalidates handoff. Preparation emits a local delivery recipe with upload/register/submit request shapes and an indexed DELIVERED verification step. It clears old plans before fresh checks. The transaction-envelope guard requires the expected BSC chain, escrow contract, submitDelivery action, calldata format and zero native value, while explicitly requiring actual wallet simulation/call review.

Validation: all 46 unittest cases pass; git diff --check passes. Live authenticated BSC inspection succeeded and returned zero orders for this listing. Funded-order review/handoff behavior is tested with fixtures; no real customer approval or delivery is claimed. Earlier read-only live Binance data produced a research draft for CAKE/XVS/THE.

No A2A inbox polling, messages, automatic quotes, artifact uploads, real transaction preparation, wallet signatures, submission or trades are performed by these commands. This is not a continuous deployed worker or proof of Set & Earn qualification. Next deployment needs durable storage and runtime data access; actual delivery uses the official skill after human review and live rechecks. Client input, snapshots, reviews and plans remain ignored by git.

author: rbuergi
body:
## What & why

Maintainer decision (rbuergi, 2026-10-11, repeated): **"again, we want to roll platform independently of packages"**. It is registered as policy `platform-rolls-independently-of-packages` in `Doc/Architecture/PolicyNotProse`; source, tests and docs cite the id and carry no date or name.

Measured on partnerre.meshweaver.cloud the same day: `Admin/UpdatePolicy` read `HOLDING 3.1.10502 — the framework identity of release 3.1.10502 is not resolvable — no content bake has been published for it …` (`heldIndeterminate=true`). At the same time, every package update on that instance was held because it needed platform `>= 3.1.10493`. The platform waited for the packages and the packages waited for the platform. memex.systemorph.com runs 3.1.10502 without problems.

**New rule:** a package-availability verdict is never a hold on the platform roll. It is an advisory: it is logged, recorded on `Admin/UpdatePolicy` (`Advisories`/`AdvisoriesTag`, no `HeldTag`), carried on the check verdict (`PACKAGE ADVISORY …`), and shown on the Updates and About tabs. The roll proceeds to the newest admitted tag. Packages catch up through their own update policy or the held-update lane. This covers a missing bake (including under `Modules:RequirePrebuilt`), an unresolvable framework identity, a package without an artifact, an indeterminate or unreadable catalogue, an unloadable module, a declared break, and an unwired gate.

### Changes
- **`UpdatabilityVerdict.ForPlatformRoll()`** (+ `WaivedHold`, `Lagging`). One waiver, applied at every decision point for a platform roll. The pure predicate `ReleaseAvailability.IsUpdatable` is **unchanged** and still answers the package question truthfully, so the CI build gate (#1755) and the package surfaces are unaffected. `Blockers` is now empty on an updatable verdict.
- **Poller** (`GateThenApply`, `GateNotWired`): it no longer calls `RecordHold` with a refusal. It logs a Warning, records the advisories, clears any stale hold and applies the roll. `FirstRollable` takes the newest admitted candidate. A hold an older build recorded is also cleared when nothing is newer (`ClearLegacyHold`), which is the path a recovered instance takes after its external roll.
- **RollSelection / `SelectRollTarget`**: the walk accepts the newest admitted candidate after exactly one verdict. An unread or empty plugin list, or an unreadable published root when candidates are supplied, selects the head with an advisory (`RollSelection.Unjudged`). CD (`/api/plugins/roll-target`), manual rolls, the reboot image step and the poller now agree.
- **`/api/plugins/is-updatable`** answers the roll question and exposes the waived reason as `waivedHold`. Package statuses are still listed.
- **Manual "Apply update now"** and the **reboot image step** apply the same rule and show every advisory the verdict carries (the waived hold, and the boot-compile, link and declared-floor advisories of an already-updatable verdict), plus the combo one.
- **About tab**: `PlatformUpdateStatus.HasAdvisories` (a boolean: the status is projected to every user, so the package names and reasons do not leave the admin scope). The About line says, in one translated sentence, that the platform rolls (or rolled) with package advisories and points to the Updates tab. The advisories themselves are untranslated server diagnostics and stay on the admin-scoped Updates tab. It no longer says "Update held — a package … is not available" (`about.updateHeld` is reworded; the new key is `about.platformRolls`, en and de).

### Combo gate: made advisory too
This was a small, consistent change, so I did it rather than leaving the recorded RED as a hold. A recorded Red names modules this instance has landed that do not survive the candidate, which is a statement about packages. The poller now records the failing modules as advisories and rolls. The candidate walk no longer skips a Red, and neither the manual button nor the reboot refuses on it. The About status no longer renders a Red as "held", and the Updates tab shows the release line with the failing modules underneath (`ui.updateBlocked` is reworded as an advisory). `SelfUpdateVerdict.ComboBlocked` is kept as a type but is no longer produced.

### Docs
- `Doc/Architecture/ReleaseStrategy`: the section "The availability gate — newer is not sufficient" is replaced by "The platform rolls independently of its packages", with the maintainer quote and the measured deadlock.
- `RollSelection`, `ReleaseGates` and `ComboGateWiring` are rewritten to the new behaviour: the package verdict (unchanged, still what the build gate reads) and the platform-roll decision (advisory only) are stated separately, and retired behaviour is marked as history.
- Operational pages that told operators `isUpdatable: false` means "do not roll" now describe the roll decision and where the package answer is: `DeploymentAKS` ("Self-update ops"), `SelfUpdateSchemaWall`, `ModuleAdoptionPolicy` ("What the platform roll gates on") and `ModulePlatformLinkGate`.
- The XML documentation of `RollSelection`, `ReleaseAvailability`, `ReleaseAvailabilityService` and the poller states the same contract.
- New register row `platform-rolls-independently-of-packages` in `Doc/Architecture/PolicyNotProse`.
- No dated What's New file (policy `whatsnew-cadence`). The 2026-09-01 entry "An instance will not roll into an image that cannot serve its modules" is marked as superseded and links to the policy and to Release Strategy.

### Tests
- New: `PlatformRollsIndependentlyOfPackagesTest`. It drives the real poller on a monolith mesh with partnerre's exact verdict (unresolvable framework identity / indeterminate) and with a missing bake under RequirePrebuilt. It asserts that the roll lands, that the stale hold is cleared, that the advisory is recorded and stated on the check verdict, and that the About status is not "held". It also covers the pure `ForPlatformRoll` rule.
- The manual "Apply update now" decision is a pure function (`UpdatePolicySettingsTab.ManualRollDecision`), pinned behaviourally (a refusal and a combo Red become advisories on the result line; nothing refuses), and its wiring is pinned by source order (the decision, then the hand-over and the patch, with no early return between them).
- Also in `PlatformRollsIndependentlyOfPackagesTest`: the reboot image step names every advisory (with and without an availability gate, and not when wedged), a legacy hold is cleared when nothing is newer, and the JSON contract of `/api/plugins/is-updatable` (`isUpdatable`, `waivedHold`, `indeterminate`, `advisories`, package statuses).
- New in `PlatformUpdateStatusTest`: the About line announces the advisories before and after the roll, and does not carry the diagnostics.
- Tests that asserted the old hold behaviour were updated: `RollSelectionTest`, `RollSelectionInventoryTest`, `ReleaseLinkGateTest`, `DeclaredBreakRollHoldTest`, `ComboGateRollTest`, `ComboVerdictRecordingTest`, `FrozenHoldIsHistoryTest`, `PlatformUpdateStatusTest`.
- Local results:
  - `Memex.Portal.Shared.Test`: full suite, 2598 tests, 0 failed, 1 skipped.
  - `MeshWeaver.Documentation.Test`: 824, 0 failed.
  - Localization tests: 66, 0 failed.
  - `dotnet build -warnaserror`: 0 warnings.

## MeshWeaver.Plugins

`Dependent suites (MeshWeaver.Plugins)` measured four cases in Plugins' `SelfUpdateAvailabilityGateTest` (realm `hosts`) that asserted the old hold. The expand step, [Systemorph/MeshWeaver.Plugins#3406](https://github.com/Systemorph/MeshWeaver.Plugins/pull/3406), is merged: those cases now hold under both poller behaviours (7/7 against core main and against this branch). No break is declared, and no semver bump is needed.

## Localization

Mirror-sync: MeshWeaver.Plugins runs `npm run sync:i18n -- --ref <merge sha>` after this lands — two keys added (`about.platformRolls`, `ui.updatePackageAdvisoriesManual`) and three re-worded (`about.updateHeld`, `ui.updateBlocked`, `ui.updateAdvisories`), en and de.

author: hexafield
body:
> **Stacked on [#1390](https://github.com/coasys/ad4m/pull/1390)** (`Session` and `Principal`). Review that PR first. When it merges, this PR's diff shrinks to its own changes.

### What

This PR makes `/api/v1/ws` open a `Session` for each connection. The connection's context (capabilities, operator flag, user email, DID) now comes from the session. The check that each request and event runs goes through `Session::check`. Behaviour does not change.

### Why

#1390 added `Session`, unused. This PR gives it its first caller: the WebSocket connection, which carries almost all client traffic. Later PRs move the handlers and the other transports onto the session, and then delete the old identity helpers. Each of these steps has to keep behaviour the same, so this PR adds a test that compares the old and new context for every kind of token.

### How

```
ws_rpc(token)
  └─ connection_context(token, admin_credential, auto_permit, reach)
       ├─ Session::open ─ Ok ──► context from the session
       │                         TokenCheck::for_session(session)    // check() = session.check()
       └─ Session::open ─ Err ─► the old derivation, unchanged:
                                 resolve_user_session(capabilities_on(..)) → Err capabilities
                                 TokenCheck::new(token, false)
```

A token that opens no session (invalid, expired, revoked, or a user whose DID does not load) keeps today's connection with `Err` capabilities. A later PR replaces that branch with a close at connect, after the SDK learns to treat such a close as "log in again".

| Change | Where |
|---|---|
| `connection_context`: builds the connection's `RequestContext` and `TokenCheck` | `api/ws_rpc.rs` |
| `TokenCheck::for_session`: `check()` delegates to `Session::check` (same revocation and expiry rules, same error strings) | `agent/capabilities/mod.rs` |
| `Session::capabilities()` (the operator holds every capability) and `Session::user()` (email, DID) | `agent/session.rs` |

`RequestContext` keeps its fields in this PR. The handlers start to read the session in the next PR.

### Tests

| Test | Covers |
|---|---|
| `connection_context_tests::every_kind_of_token_gets_the_same_context_as_before` | 9 tokens (admin credential, empty, app, app without capabilities, user, user without a DID, expired, revoked, garbage) × admin credential set or not × loopback or network × multi-user on or off: the new context equals the old one |
| `connection_context_tests::a_session_connection_stops_working_once_its_token_is_revoked` | a revoke reaches a connection that opened a session |
| existing `ws_rpc::socket_tests`, `connection_tests`, `events_ws` tests | real sockets through the new path: revoke mid-connection, expiry, event gate |

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --lib ws_rpc:: session:: capabilities:: auth:: connection_tests events_ws` | 110 passed |
| executor lib tests, core `tsc` + jest | pass |
| `cargo fmt --check` | clean |

### Changelog

author: tanish2k09
body:
Part of #1343 (cursor lag), done jointly with @jerrykimo's #968.

## What
The brush outline and the crosshairs (Precise, crosshair-while-painting, the big-tip hotspot) were OS cursor bitmaps only on Windows (#1160). On macOS, X11 and Wayland the app painted them into the canvas, so they trailed the hardware pointer by render + present + compositor latency and "jumped to catch up" on slow frames, which is what the #1343 reports describe. The latency-surface experiments didn't perceptibly help, which fits: the outline was the lagging thing, not the strokes.

`tool_cursor` now uploads the bitmap on every desktop root viewport (eframe/egui-winit 0.36 upload `cursor_image` through winit `CustomCursor` on all of them). The web build and immediate viewports keep the painted path.

- **macOS sizing (from #968):** winit takes an `NSCursor` image's size in logical points, so on macOS the bitmap scales only with the UI zoom (`native_scale`); Windows, X11 and Wayland take physical pixels.
- **Size cap off Windows:** 255 px, because X servers and hardware cursor planes commonly cap at 256 and fall back to software cursors (or reject the image) past that. #968 used 128. A larger tip keeps today's fallback: the painted full-size outline plus a small OS crosshair at the hotspot. Windows keeps 2048.
- **Out of scope:** the Pencil's square stays painted (it snaps to the pixel grid, and a cursor hotspot can't follow that). The pipette stays painted too (an SVG icon; it's a follow-up and could come from #968's pipette bitmap). The Hand bitmap stays Windows-only, because the other platforms draw their own hands.

Credit: @jerrykimo is co-author (the cross-platform approach and the macOS point sizing in #968).

## Tests
- The native-cursor tests (bitmap survives motion and changes with the tool, the painting preference and zoom; no outline in the canvas draw list) now run on every desktop OS, not just Windows. The Precise crosshair test expects a bitmap on every desktop OS.
- New: `cursor_bitmaps_stay_within_the_platform_limit`.
- Local (Windows): `cargo test -p photocraft-ui-egui --lib` gives 1827 passed. Clippy `-D warnings` is clean, the wasm check is clean, and fmt is clean. CI covers Linux and macOS.

## Needs a hardware check
I can't try X11/Wayland/macOS here. #1343 testers (X11 + NVIDIA, Wayland, Iris Xe, macOS Retina): does the outline now stick to the pointer? Is it the right size at 100 % / 200 % scaling?

body:
[HA-379](https://hatch.yeetsoft.net/apps/hatch/issues/HA-379)

WorkDto now carries the board's statuses alongside each child's bare StatusId, so Prompt.Compose's "Its children" section can print each child's column name after its title (e.g. `- AER-13  [task]  A child  (To Do)`), resolved from the board's own columns rather than a bare id. A child whose status the dispatch did not carry falls back to the numeric id, the same way `hatch show` already falls back for the ticket's own status.

## Summary
- `WorkDto` gains a trailing `Statuses` field (nullable, defaulting to null for clients too old to read it - a bare `= []` collection-expression default is not a compile-time constant in C#, so this follows the same nullable pattern `Messages` already uses)
- `WorkController.ResolveAsync`'s one production call site passes the already-loaded `statuses` list through `ToStatusDto`, at no extra query cost
- `Prompt.cs`'s "Its children" block resolves each child's column name from `work.Statuses`, falling back to the bare id
- Test fixtures and new tests in `Hatch.Cli.Tests` and `Hatch.Api.Tests` cover the happy path and the fallback

- [x] `make build` and `make build-hatch`
- [x] `make test-api` (2377 passed, 114 skipped - pre-existing DB-only skips)

author: jfubrio
body:
## Resumen

Proyecto **TikTok Shop México mediante creadores afiliados, sin inventario**. Incluye la documentación de investigación (T00–T02, preliminar), la estrategia de audiencia que pidió el propietario antes de invertir, ocho skills de proyecto y el **MVP interno T04–T08** en `tsmx/`, construido sin conexiones externas por decisión del propietario (D-11). Los archivos de LABSIA no se modifican.

## MVP interno (`tsmx/`)

Python estándar y SQLite, sin dependencias ni costo. Línea de comandos más reporte HTML.

| Ticket | Qué hace cumplir el código |
|---|---|
| T04 | Esquema con NULL como "no disponible" y auditoría de solo inserción. Arquitectura en `docs/tiktok-shop-mx/15_ARQUITECTURA_MVP.md`. |
| T05 | Importadores de plan, videos, comisiones, costos y productos. Validación por fila, archivo idempotente, conflictos sin sobrescribir. Una fila inválida se rechaza sola, sin tumbar la importación. |
| T06 | Editar invalida aprobaciones. Solo se publica la versión aprobada, comparando versión y hash. Un revisor no aprueba lo propio. Divulgación comercial obligatoria con producto. |
| T07 | Comisiones estimadas, aprobadas y liquidadas con retenciones de `09_...` [S-8]. El resultado solo cuenta liquidadas netas menos costos. Indicadores ordenados por intención de compra, no por vistas. |
| T08 | Roles propietario, editor, revisor y lector. Respaldo con manifiesto SHA-256 y restauración comprobada, también sobre la base activa. |

El adaptador de TikTok Shop implementa la firma oficial de "Sign your API request" pero no inventa rutas de endpoints. La conexión queda para el final (§7 del documento de arquitectura).

## Calidad

- **77 pruebas** con `unittest`; cobertura de ramas del paquete del 96 %. Incluyen la línea de comandos completa, ocho regresiones de una revisión de código, la petición firmada a TikTok verificada sin red y los cuatro scripts de las skills sobre copias de los documentos.
- Cuatro mutaciones deliberadas de reglas críticas fueron detectadas por la suite.
- `ruff.toml` con linter y formato para `tsmx/` y los scripts de las skills.
- `.github/workflows/tsmx.yml` corre linter, formato y pruebas en Python 3.11 y 3.13, y falla si quedan recursos sin cerrar.

```bash
cd tsmx && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
```

## Documentación (`docs/tiktok-shop-mx/`)

- `00`, `03`, `07`, `08`: guía, protocolo, backlog con registro de cambios y decisiones D-01 a D-11, pendientes P-01 a P-13.
- `09` (T01), `10` e `investigacion/` (T02): requisitos con fuentes oficiales fechadas y seis fichas; preliminares.
- `11` a `15`: herramientas existentes, guía de ronda 2, estrategia de audiencia con guiones de las semanas 1 y 2, alta de cuenta y arquitectura del MVP.

## Skills (`.claude/skills/`)

`tiktok-shop-mx`, `tsmx-ficha-nicho`, `tsmx-matriz`, `tsmx-backlog`, `tsmx-decision`, `tsmx-requisitos`, `tsmx-validar-producto`, `tsmx-audiencia`.

## Limitaciones

- La red del entorno bloquea `*.tiktok.com`, Mercado Libre y Amazon México; T01 y T02 se basan en fragmentos del buscador.
- El MVP se construyó antes de validar productos y economía (T03), por decisión del propietario. El modelo admite los datos de T03 por CSV sin rediseño.
- Ningún candidato se declara validado ni de baja competencia.

## Restricciones respetadas

Sin cuentas abiertas por el agente, sin publicaciones, sin gasto, sin credenciales en el repositorio. La base y los respaldos están fuera de git.

body:
## What this changes

Roadmap M3, criterion 5 (API snapshot, ADR 0015) and criterion 4 (the verified viewer, decision A4).

### API snapshot 1
- `raw/core/api_snapshot.hpp` declares `kApiSnapshot = 1`. `api/snapshot-1/` holds the manifest and a declaration dump: 552 declarations from 25 headers (the scene description and the renderer layer, without the GPU check fixtures).
- `scripts/api_dump.py --check` runs in CI. Additions pass. A removed or changed declaration fails and names the line; that break moves the engine to snapshot 2 with a migration note. The dump is textual: comments, bodies and private members are removed and multi-declarator members are split. It is not a compiler's ABI view, and `api/README.md` says so.
- `--selftest` checks the parser with three controls: a changed parameter type and a removed member must break the snapshot; an edited function body must not.
- `tests/test_api_snapshot.cpp` is the compatibility suite: 18 contracts the headers document, written the way a user writes code. It checks behaviour, not the renderer's numbers.
- **Open:** the plugin C ABI part. The C ABI is not built, because ADR 0007 is still proposed.

### Verified viewer
- `web/viewer/` opens a glTF or GLB file (or the owned assets, exported in the page) and renders it through WebGPU and on the CPU reference. It shows the GPU frame, the CPU reference, the per-pixel error map, an AO error map when the ray-traced reference is on, and the GPU certificate with its verdict.
- `tests/web/viewer.py` runs in CI on SwiftShader. raw-hero and raw-hall both render `verified` at 128 px. The control, a broken GLB, must render nothing.
- **Bug found by that control:** a model that failed to load on the `--gpu` and `--bench` paths left `main` as an uncaught exception, and the native CLI crashed. It now exits 2 with `cannot load --model`, as the CPU path did.
- Light and dark screenshots were checked by eye before commit.
- **Open:** hosting the viewer inside the site's Studio page. That belongs to the site's lane.

### Also
- media-smoke reached 42m55s of its 45 minutes on #98. ctest now checks a quarter of the clearcoat grid; `--json` and `--strict` keep the full grid.
- SSR exploration on raw-hall is recorded as negative results and error categories in `evidence/m3-post-runs.json`.

author: kumhou
body:
## What

Final form of the test-isolation work for issues #234 and #226, per the frozen PRD `docs/zh/prd/PRD-234-test-port-isolation.md` and the independent design review on #234.

- **S1** — exact site table: network-touching sites in `tests/` = 0 on the base (78 x 7788 / 18 x 4096 occurrences, all string assertions, hermetic fakes, pure data, or counting-only sockets). Delivered in this PR body's first comment.
- **S2** — `tests/_ports.py`: `unused_loopback_port()` and `listening_loopback_socket()`; the two real-socket watchdog tests migrated to it with assertions unchanged.
- **S3** — the runtime guard stack is deleted (`tests/port_guard.py`, the guard parts of `tests/conftest.py`, the child-process sitecustomize injection regressions, the fresh-interpreter `RESERVED_PORTS` and install/uninstall pins, `tests/test_run_isolation.py:115-120`); the Node/PowerShell child-process scanners are **promoted (moved byte-identically, not rewritten)** into the new static check `tests/test_port_isolation.py`; the session precondition now **REPORTs** occupancy (bind probe without `SO_REUSEADDR`, never classifies the occupant, never asks `/healthz`). S3 net line change **-643** (338 added, 981 removed, 85 promoted lines cancel on both sides) — a deletion, so the stop rule did not fire.
- **S4** — two full-suite runs, verbatim: 7788 free → `3237 passed, 5 skipped`; 7788 occupied by a trivial listener → `3237 passed, 5 skipped`; the only difference is the precondition report line.
- **S5** — `tests/_test_daemon.py`: real test daemon on an ephemeral port through the product up path, `DaemonClient` readiness + `POST /daemon/shutdown` teardown, `proc.wait` + `returncode == 0` exit assertion; refusal registers the PID with the logged `tests/session_sweeper.py` and **never kills inline**; honest documentation that the in-daemon watchdog is inert on intentional teardown.
- `.gitignore` gains `.mnemoseeding/` (#240).

## In-batch incident (found and fixed by the author before handoff)

`subprocess.Popen` under a uv venv spawns a trampoline parent, so `proc.pid` aimed at the launcher and the exit assertion plus the sweeper were aimed at the wrong process. Fixed with `sys._base_executable` plus `PYTHONPATH`, pinned by a regression test; six orphaned daemons cleaned through the authorized sweeper only. QA reproduced the fix and verified zero leftovers.

## Accepted scope deviation (owner decision 2026-10-11)

The frozen contract pinned `tests/test_reserved_port_static_check.py` and `tests/test_test_daemon_self_teardown.py`; the shipped batch instead creates `tests/test_port_isolation.py` (the static check, which also carries the promoted child-process scanners), `tests/test_ports.py` (helper tests), `tests/_test_daemon.py` (private daemon harness, kept out of `conftest.py` import weight) and `tests/test_daemon_self_teardown.py`. The deviation, its reasons, and the contract-to-artifact mapping are disclosed in the ledger execution fact; the owner accepted it with this disclosure. The frozen PRD pins the `tests/**` surface, not these file names.

## Verification

- Independent adversarial QA (senior-qa-reviewer, independent author): **CLOSABLE-WITH-CONDITIONS**, no BLOCKER. All four gates reproduced green in the QA seat's own runs; the S4 occupied-port variant reproduced independently (identical results, only the precondition line differs); promoted scanners verified byte-identical; net deletion recomputed; mutation probes (a/c/e) red, the allow-list teeth proven.
- QA environment note: QA measured `3235 passed / 7 skipped` vs the author's `3237 / 5`; the two-test delta is environment-gated skips outside this batch's file surface (junit itemized: bge-m3 model missing x2, POSIX permission skips x2, `*_PERF` gates, module-level skip).
- QA conditions and their disposition:
  - **IMP-1** (the precondition REPORT has no unit oracle — killing the report leaves the suite green): satisfied for this batch by the archived S4 double-run evidence in this PR and its QA reproduction; a unit oracle is filed as a follow-up issue rather than blocking this merge.
  - **IMP-2** (AC3's "no `socket.socket` monkeypatch" is literally false against a pre-existing, unrelated atlas no-I/O assertion): the wording is narrowed in the closeout record; no test is touched.
  - **IMP-3** (exit-code strictness never perturbed): optional hardening, filed as the same follow-up.

Closes #234. Refs #226 (side-effect closure) and #240.

body:
Allow single-homed VLAN-aware bundle members to bind an IP-VRF in `interface_less` mode. Type 2/3 routes keep their member Ethernet Tags; routed Type 5 prefixes use Ethernet Tag 0 and the IP-VRF L3VNI, RD, route targets and Router MAC. Gateway-IP and ESI origination modes remain rejected, and bundle members stay outside receive-side gateway recursion.

Real-converger regressions cover member unlink, relink, movement, sibling preservation and failed publication. A kernel actor regression protects local connected routes through remote import, withdrawal, restoration and shutdown. Linux SVI/VRF attachments remain operator-provisioned.

The M120 SR Linux leg checks two bundle members, resolved routed next hops, complete managed FDB state, exact RIB/FIB inventories, generation ordering and packet delivery. Its traffic probe selects a Type 5 host route; withdrawal removes that /24 and exact /32 while preserving the destination and the other prefix pair. Warmup requires exact learned host IPs. Before stopping packet capture, a bounded handshake requires all three scored requests; final assertions still inspect the original PCAP.

Validation:

- All 17 focused bundle tests passed at `1d3d6b56c`. Removing the gateway-recursion guard failed the intended regression; restoration passed. Both kernel L3 regressions passed before integration; removing the ownership guard reproduced connected-route takeover and restoration passed.
- M119 oracle checks pass 14 methods/105 scenarios; M120 passes 52 methods with negative inventory and packet-witness controls. Bash syntax, ShellCheck, pinned Ruff 0.16.0 and diff checks pass. Normal Rust commit hooks passed formatting and strict workspace/all-target Clippy.
- The full local SR Linux 25.10.1 native leg passed 37 checks with native exit 0, including all eight fresh-ARP warmups, routed probes, the original three-request PCAP assertion, strict Type 5 transitions 10→8→10, installed-route transitions 4→2→4, rejected reload, member unlink/relink and complete route/FDB restoration without a session flap. Lab corrections require learned host IPs after warmup, drain capture before shutdown and retain the tenant route target while rejecting unadvertised local gateway host routes. Failed preceding attempts remain retained; the strict inventories were preserved.
- The final native execution at `9af0ad2e0e91f143bc5c4953d237987732ccbd51` passed all 37 checks again. It reused the immutable daemon image built at `8d455523d`; the four review corrections change only CI and documentation, and exact runtime inputs/source ID are unchanged. All 39 provenance, native and cleanup exits are 0; every observed process lifetime, owned container and exact lab network is reaped. The earlier public receipt remains immutable historical evidence with its original provenance.
- On `8d455523d`, with the same runtime inputs, `just gate` and `just gate-rib` passed. Both real Linux L3 regressions passed in the pinned netns image; all owned gate processes and containers are reaped. On `9af0ad2e0`, the new CI archive step passed both inventory replay and original packet-witness checks; all 52 M120 checker tests, syntax, ShellCheck and relevant links also pass. Dated ADR history is preserved with a qualification addendum, and maintained support claims now describe the shipped scope.
- The final review-correction push succeeded and the remote head matches `9af0ad2e0`. Normal Rust push hooks naturally skipped for the CI/documentation-only followup; this adds no new Rust-gate claim. Push processes are fully reaped. Final-head hosted checks and another advisory review are pending.

This remains an alpha slice. It adds no bundle multi-homing, locally assigned VNIs, non-zero-tag Type 5, GW-IP/ESI resolution or Type 2 symmetric host routing, and does not broaden the unicast v1 contract.

body:
## 摘要

瓢蟲追擊令（DAT）單人與雙人的修正。依賴「前端共用」PR；`submissionId` 去重需要「後端」PR。

## 修正

- **平均反應時間**：只算實際按鍵，不再把「不要按」題的 10 秒等待算進去。
- **第 3 關檢查點**：第 4、5 關中途離開時，統計只算到第 3 關結束。
- **雙人存檔重試後無法離開**：離開時依目前存檔狀態判斷。
- **存檔結果未確認時卡住**：每筆成績帶 `submissionId`，重送同一筆是安全的；按重試或離開會重送，不會重複寫入，也不會卡住。
- **不再在較高關卡之後送較低的檢查點**。
- **單人**：升級圖載入失敗保留目前的動物；練習固定顏色、數學各一題。
- **命中判定**：依目前顯示的圖片建立遮罩；素材平台的圖片以 CORS 載入（平台有回 `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`）。
- **離開**：先確認再存檔；存檔期間遊戲暫停並忽略作答與瞄準。
- **本機 SQLite 測試伺服器**：接受 levelAccuracy 字串、只提供前端檔案、`/health` 回 JSON、重送去重。
- **E2E 登入 mock**：到期時間改為一小時後（原本 2099 年會讓計時器溢位）。
- **單人存檔沒帶 `endTime` 時送出 null**：改成用現在的時間（真實後端會對 null 回 422）。

## 測試

- 在這個分支單獨執行：
  - `cd tests && npm test`：101 passed
  - 本機 SQLite 伺服器：22 passed
  - `tests/frontend` 的 DAT 相關 spec：45 passed、3 failed（`save.spec` DAT_single ×2、`double-save.spec` DAT 雙人），三個都在 main 上就已失敗。

## 這組 PR 的背景

對整個專案做了一次對抗式審查，找出 42 個問題，逐一由使用者確認後修正。每個修正都先寫出會失敗的測試，修正後再確認通過。依區域拆成 8 個 PR：

| PR | 分支 | 依賴 |
|---|---|---|
| 後端 | #43 `mdtsai456/fix-backend` | 無 |
| 前端共用 | #44 `mdtsai456/fix-shared-frontend` | 無 |
| DAT | #46 `mdtsai456/fix-dat` | #44 前端共用；建議先合併 #43 後端（`submissionId` 去重） |
| DCCS | #47 `mdtsai456/fix-dccs` | #44 前端共用 |
| EFT | #48 `mdtsai456/fix-eft` | #44 前端共用 |
| IM | #49 `mdtsai456/fix-im` | #44 前端共用 |
| TGame | #50 `mdtsai456/fix-tgame` | #44 前端共用 |

body:
## T-40: one interaction seam across every mode, and the extension UI surface

**The seam.** Ambient user interaction now flows through one internal `IUserInteraction` (`Notify` / `UpdateStatus` / `RenderExtension`) with a per-mode implementation: the interactive mode shows notices in the live area, status in the footer and extension blocks as styled output; print and JSON write `lunate:` notices to stderr with stdout byte-pure (the answer, or the event stream); ACP logs — the protocol has no notice frame. Print mode now also surfaces retry/compaction/step-limit notices it previously dropped. Approvals keep their existing per-mode chain (considered and rejected: folding them in — churn on three reviewed surfaces, no gain).

**The extension UI surface** (contract, API 1.3.0 → 1.4.0): a JSON-safe `TextSegment` model, `IToolResultRenderer` (renders a named tool's result) and `IStatusWidget` (extra footer segments), registered through `IExtensionContext` — registration only, duplicate renderers resolve last-wins with the conflict logged, a throwing contribution is omitted for that update, logged and retried on the next (the hook failure policy, applied to UI). Footer widgets append after the core fields and drop before the branch at narrow widths.

**The matrix is the contract** — every degradation cell has a test, one file per mode, plus contract round-trips and failure degradation. Gate: 1843 tests · 0 failed · both passes · startup 46 ms · `verify: OK`; archived 16/16 strict.

**Review:** APPROVE. The reviewer confirmed approvals untouched, machine-mode stdout purity asserted (not just non-empty), markup escaping safe, no rules violations. Three non-blocking gaps recorded as follow-ups: the extension host is not yet composed into the CLI (pre-existing — registrations and hooks have no production effect until it is; card filed), the styled-block NO_COLOR/ASCII path is claimed but untested, and ACP's "logged" extension-UI cell is not reachable end-to-end (card filed).

author: regenscheid
body:
## Summary

The trusted worker now creates, revises and deletes the OpenShell sandboxes behind logical environments (D73, proposed). The orchestrator is semi-trusted and holds no gateway credentials (threat model, Z2). It names an environment, a project, a base profile (D46) and a policy revision, and supplies no policy itself.

**Creating an environment:**
1. Load the revision from the pool's policy store, the middleware's state directory. Only an operator adds revisions there, with `sandbox-science-worker policy add`, which compiles each one and prints its findings.
2. Compile it under the pool ceiling with the deployment's targets.
3. Check that every provider the policy lists is registered with a profile that names no endpoints (D57).
4. Create the sandbox (`ss-<environment>-<hash>`) from the profile's image, with exactly those providers, and bind it to the revision.
   - A failed creation leaves no sandbox and no binding.
   - A sandbox left by a crash is replaced on the next request.

**Revising:**
- A revision whose providers differ is refused, since OpenShell attaches providers only at creation.
- Otherwise `openshell policy set --wait` applies the new document, carrying the sandbox's live filesystem section, and the sandbox is rebound.
- Between the two steps the middleware denies requests as `policy_stale`, so a revision fails closed.

**Deleting:** stop the executor, delete the sandbox and unbind it.

**New routes:**
- `POST /v1/environments`
- `GET /v1/environments/{id}`
- `POST /v1/environments/{id}/policy`
- `DELETE /v1/environments/{id}`

The harness's `WorkerClient` has matching methods. Static `sandboxes` mappings keep working.

## Correction to #21

OpenShell refuses a revision without the filesystem section ("filesystem policy cannot be removed on a live sandbox"), as seen on babbage the same day. `OpenShellPolicy.network_only()` therefore becomes `with_filesystem(live)`, and `docs/POLICY.md` and the lab 5 record now say so.

## Verification

- **Tests.** 17 environment tests use a fake `openshell` that follows the behavior and error shapes captured on babbage. They cover idempotence, conflicts, provider checks, revisions, deletion, crash recovery, a failed creation, the API, the client and `policy add`.
- **Lab 6** ([report](.agents/docs/agent-reports/babbage-openshell-lab-6-2026-10-11.md)), against a real gateway:
  - a sandbox was ready in 11.3 s, with the provider's placeholder visible inside;
  - the executor ran in it at tier 3, with `/dev/shm` writable, the cache reachable and `pypi.org` refused;
  - a revision took 9.2 s and the sandbox was rebound;
  - an unregistered provider was refused;
  - delete removed the sandbox and its binding.

  Torn down afterwards.
- **Other changes:** `policy-middleware` is now marked typed (`py.typed`); one of its tests patched `zlib` through `gitproto` and now patches the module directly.

## Checks

ruff, pyright, pytest (6173 passed, 30 skipped), license check: all pass locally.
