author: gaborbernat
t1nkieplayz
body:
## Problem

The loopback HTTP embed page addresses YouTube's Error 153 / missing-Referer requirement, but the player now reaches a separate failure: **“Your browser can't play this video.”** Disabling AV1 did not help, so this PR no longer disables AV1 or changes decoder rankings.

## Fix

- Configure GStreamer plugin discovery before WebKitGTK starts.
- In AppImages, prefer the bundled plugin directories and matching bundled `gst-plugin-scanner`, avoiding incompatible host plugins being mixed with the bundled GStreamer ABI.
- If the AppImage's plugin directories are missing, clear the empty `GST_PLUGIN_SYSTEM_PATH_1_0` override so GStreamer can fall back to its normal system discovery instead of seeing zero plugins.
- Leave AV1 and other decoder choices enabled; let the installed codec stack negotiate supported streams.
- Add a focused unit test for identifying GStreamer plugin directories.

## Research

- [Tauri AppImage documentation](https://v2.tauri.app/distribute/appimage/) says multimedia support depends on bundling GStreamer and ensuring the build system has the needed plugins.
- [Tauri issue #15665](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/15665) documents AppRun's `GST_PLUGIN_SYSTEM_PATH_1_0` override suppressing default plugin discovery when the bundled directory is absent, and warns about bundled/host GStreamer mismatches.
- [A Linux AppImage implementation discussion](https://git.woodsee.com/woodsee/worldmonitor2/commits/commit/79c087c2a90def70a65fb2043aad9cdb63a80964/src-tauri/src) likewise identifies plugin-path and ABI mismatches as causes of unavailable WebKitGTK video codecs.

## Validation

CI and Rust unit tests should be checked for this commit. A real YouTube playback test still requires running the packaged app on Linux; this PR remains open and unmerged for your pull-and-test step.

author: dxhize
body:
## The symptom

A run reported `PARTIAL`, then failed to build a PDF three times:

```
WARNING backend.main: PDF build failed for 'How can topological qubits be
stabilized against environmental decoherence witho': Flowable
<Table@0x7F25485CACF0 1 rows x 1 cols(tallest row 718.0)> ... too large on
page 34 in frame 'main'(475.27559055118115 x 703.8897637795277*) of template 'all'
```

## Root cause

`report.py:793` deliberately hides non-critical pipeline advisories in an HTML comment. That is correct for the `.md` export, where a renderer ignores it.

`parse_references()` has no comment guard. When a comment landed inside the References section it fell through to the catch-all branch:

```python
else:
    current["meta"] += " " + s     # unbounded accumulator
```

Reference `[15]` (the QuEra qLDPC glossary page) reached **4,292 characters**. That becomes a single-cell `Table`, and ReportLab cannot place a row taller than the page frame — so one oversized card destroyed the entire 31-page document.

Reproduced and measured **718.0pt** against a **703.89pt** frame before making any change.

## Fixed at three layers

1. **`strip_html_comments()`** — removes comments once in `build_pdf()`, so the body renderer, reference parser, note builder and word/citation counters all see the same text. Reference 15's `meta` drops **4,292 chars → 43**.
2. **`_cap()`** — bounds `meta` and `note` on a word boundary, so no single field can produce an over-height card regardless of upstream format.
3. **`splitInRow=1`** — lets an over-long card break across pages rather than raise. Same rule the rest of the pipeline follows: one bad element degrades, it does not take the run down.

## A second bug, found while verifying

`report.py` writes the evidence-integrity disclosure **after** References. But `build_pdf` cuts the report body at `## Evidence by Source`, which sits *before* References, and `render_refs` only draws cards.

```
208: ## Conclusion
220: ## Evidence by Source      <- body_md cut here
245: ## References
307: ### How this run went      <- rendered nowhere
```

So the disclosure was rendered by neither path. On a `PARTIAL` run the evidence-integrity warning was present in the `.md` and **completely absent from the PDF a reader actually receives** — precisely the failure the disclosure exists to prevent:

> *"a pipeline problem hidden in markup is a pipeline problem nobody reads"*

`trailing_disclosures()` / `render_disclosures()` now extract and draw it. Rendered from the markdown rather than the bundle, because `report.py` has already filtered to integrity-grade notes; reconstructing from `analysis.notes` would surface the per-batch detail the design deliberately hides.

## Also fixed

`build_ref_notes()` already prefixes `"Cited from:"` for the citation list, and the caller appended the same prefixed list again — printing it twice on every card that had any locations.

```
'Cited from: p.12, p.19, p.24; p.40, p.41; p.55 Cited from: p.12, p.19, p.24; p.40, p.41; p.55'
```

## Verification

- The failing report rebuilds: **31 pages, valid `%PDF-1.4`**
- Worst card now **97pt** against a 703.9pt frame (was 718pt)
- Comment text no longer leaks into the PDF; disclosure text now present
- **22/22** exports carrying References build clean
- **542 passing** (513 → 542, +29 regression tests)

## Not addressed here

`Evidence integrity: in round 1, evidence extraction returned nothing usable for 30 of 40 passage batches` — a separate, real quality issue. This PR only makes the PDF *display* that warning correctly; the underlying extraction failure is untouched.

author: 12ashish1234
body:
## Problem
When muxing external subtitles into a video file that already contains bitmap subtitle tracks (such as Blu-ray PGS `hdmv_pgs_subtitle` or DVD `vobsub` streams), FFmpeg failed with exit code 234:
```text
[sost#0:2 @ 0x7be8e2c600] Multiple -codec/-c/-acodec/-vcodec/-scodec/-dcodec options specified for stream 2, only the last option '-codec:s srt' will be used.
[sost#0:2/srt @ 0x7be8e2c600] Subtitle encoding currently only possible from text to text or bitmap to bitmap
Error opening output files: Invalid argument
```

## Root Cause
SubMux applied a global `-c:s srt` (or `-c:s mov_text`) flag. In FFmpeg, a global stream codec specifier overrides the default stream copying (`-c copy`) for **all** subtitle streams in the output container. Because bitmap subtitles cannot be transcoded to text subtitles without optical character recognition (OCR), FFmpeg aborted.

## Solution
1. Replaced the global `-c:s srt` and `-c:s mov_text` flags with stream-indexed flags (`-c:s:<stream_index> srt` / `-c:s:<stream_index> mov_text`) strictly targeting newly appended subtitle tracks.
2. Preserved existing subtitle streams untouched under `-c copy`.
3. Added automated unit tests to verify that videos with existing subtitle tracks do not emit global `-c:s` flags and properly target only new stream indices.

Closes the darwin gate red found while re-measuring 1276-mugq (row 1586-gway).

**Defect.** Arm 4 of `scripts/test-hook-phase-instrumentation.sh` gave its injected `sleep 0.05` phase a fixed 30ms budget. It assumed the phase lands at 1x–4x (30–120ms). Under `taskpolicy -b`, which is how every macOS gate runs, background-QoS timer coalescing stretched the sleep to about 140–260ms (`sleep 0.05` itself measured 243ms versus 64ms). The phase landed past 4x and warned, so two consecutive darwin gates were red on this arm alone. It is not load: 5/5 runs passed beside a CPU hog (20× `yes` on 10 cores).

**Fix.** The budget is now half the phase's *measured* elapsed time, read from arm 3's warning, which puts the phase near 2x. The assertion only counts a run that the hook's own timing table places in the band. A run that drifted out recalibrates from itself, up to 3 tries, and if it never gets in-band the arm fails rather than passing.

**Measured on darwin, in one script run** (taskpolicy -b unless noted; elapsed/budget ms):
| | result |
|---|---|
| pre-fix | 3 of 5 FAIL ("a phase between 1x and 4x now warns") |
| post-fix | 5 of 5 pass: 262/121, 237/89, 199/54, 216/73, 142/60 |
| post-fix, plain | 3 of 3 pass: 64/32, 55/32, 64/32 |
| band-closed mutation (hook warns at 1x) | 3 of 3 FAIL, under -b and plain |

**Severity table. Approved by Scott on 2026-10-10.** The "fires at merge?" column comes from the pre-merge dry run on `civo-sandbox-use1-serving`, 22:30–22:38Z.

| Alert | Severity | Fires at merge? |
|---|---|---|
| `WitselfPostgreSQLOOMKilled` (OOM reason and a restart within 30m) | critical | no (restarts in the last 30m: 0) |
| `WitselfPostgreSQLRestarted` (non-OOM restart within 30m) | critical | no |
| `WitselfPostgreSQLMemoryNearLimit` (>90% of limit, for 10m, keep_firing_for 5m) | warning | not now. Ratio 0.82; 24h above 0.9 is 6.25%, with 16 crossings, so expect a few low-urgency incidents a day. Accepted. |
| `WitselfNodeMemoryWorkingSetHigh` (>90% of allocatable, for 15m) | warning | no (ratios 0.826 and 0.831) |
| `WitselfPostgreSQLVolumeFillingUp` (7-day forecast below 0, for 1h) | warning | no (forecast +4.92 GB) |

Declined options, recorded as follow-ups: `keep_firing_for: 15m` on the memory alert, a silence, and a fill-level guard on the forecast.

**Dry-run checks.**
- The PostgreSQL working set (330.4 MB) equals `kubectl top` (315Mi).

- The node working set is `MemTotal - MemFree - Buffers - (Cached - Shmem) - SReclaimable`. Across three samples it is within 1.6% of the kubelet's own `node_memory_working_set_bytes` on both nodes.
  - The first formula, `MemTotal - MemFree - Inactive_file`, read about 31% high (ratios 1.07 and 1.03) and would have fired permanently.

**Review.**
- Three lenses, with every finding independently verified.
- Fix pass 1: the 5m hold is restored on the memory alert. The restart rule no longer pages a false non-OOM restart after an OOM followed by a pod replacement or an exporter gap. Promtool cases R1–R3 cover this.
- Fix pass 2: the node formula above.

author: toddgbenson
body:
# feat(ci): upload ShellCheck results to MyKronos as sast from lint

Closes #105

## What and why

CodeQL implements no shell, and shell is most of keel, so MyKronos reads about 70% of the repo as read by no analyser (MyKronos B-051, TheHub #60577). The `lint` job already ran ShellCheck on every push and uploaded nothing.

- `ci/scripts/shellcheck.sh` writes a `json1` report at `-S style` to a new `mykronos-results` output. That is the format MyKronos's `sast_shellcheck` adapter parses. The report is written **before** the gate, so a gate failure still has results to upload.
- `ci/pipeline.yml` `lint`: the `shellcheck` task gets an `ensure:` upload through the shared `mykronos-upload.yml`, with `CAPABILITY: sast` and `TOOL: shellcheck` and the same anchor and pin as every other lane.
- **A defect found along the way and fixed, because the upload depended on it.** Running the script in its own image showed the existing gate had never checked a file. It read `$OUT/files.txt` by a relative path after `cd "$WORK"`, so shellcheck got no arguments, printed its usage and exited 3. `| tee` then returned tee's 0. The task printed `clean (30 files)` with none read. The list path is now absolute, and the gate uses shellcheck's own exit code.

AC from #105:
- AC-1 sast/shellcheck upload from `lint`: done.
- AC-2 `ensure:`: done.
- AC-3 a broken scan is not uploaded as clean: done. On exit >1 or empty output the report is deleted, so the uploader sees an empty results dir and records a run that broke.
- AC-4 gate unchanged at `-S warning`: the threshold is unchanged. The gate now actually runs. It is clean today, so lint stays green.
- AC-5 validation passes: done.

## What I made worse

- `lint` now depends on MyKronos being reachable. An ingestion outage turns lint red at the upload step. There is deliberately no preflight first, so an outage cannot stop the lint gate itself from running (reasoning is in the pipeline comment).
- ShellCheck runs twice per build (json1 + gcc). It takes seconds.
- The ShellCheck version is now written in two places (`ci/tasks/shellcheck.yml` tag and `TOOL_VERSION: "0.10.0"`).
- One new `shellcheck disable=SC2046` (refs #105, expires 2026-11-11), the same deliberate word-splitting as the existing one.

## AI authorship — required (AIC-6)

- [x] **Parts AI-authored:** all of it: `ci/scripts/shellcheck.sh`, `ci/tasks/shellcheck.yml`, the `lint` hunk of `ci/pipeline.yml`, and this PR text.
- [x] **Agent / model:** Claude Code, claude-opus-5.5 (1M context)
- [x] **What I verified personally, not just read:** I ran `ci/scripts/shellcheck.sh` in `koalaman/shellcheck-alpine:v0.10.0`. On `main` it prints `clean (30 files)` after `cat: can't open 'shellcheck-report/files.txt'` and `No files specified`. On this branch it reports 27 comments (all info) and a clean gate. With a seeded `ci/scripts/zz-seed.sh` (SC2115, SC2164, SC2086) the gate exits 1 and the report carries all three. MyKronos's adapter at the pinned `mykronos_ref` f8d8cfd parsed that report: 30 findings, 0 skipped, status success, seeded rows at the right file and line. **Not verified:** a live Concourse run or a live upload. Nothing was set or triggered.

## Acceptance criteria → tests

| AC | Test | Fails without this change? |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1/AC-3 | seeded-script run of `ci/scripts/shellcheck.sh` in its image + pinned adapter parse (manual, described above) | ✅ (`main` writes no report) |
| AC-4 | same run: gate exits 1 on the seed | ✅ (`main` exits 0 on the seed) |
| AC-5 | `python scripts/validate-pipeline.py` (rc 0, 26 jobs, 20 accepted tag-pin warnings, unchanged); YAML parse (37 files); `bash -n ci/scripts/*.sh`; `test/checkov-gate.test.py`, `test/dashboard.test.py` all passed | n/a |

There is no automated test for the script itself. keel has no shell-test harness, which is a gap.

## Definition of Done

**Code**
- [ ] Every AC implemented, each with a test that **fails without the change**. Implemented and demonstrated by manual runs; there is no committed test.
- [x] Error paths and boundaries tested, not just the happy path (seeded findings; the scanner-failure branch reviewed but not exercised)
- [ ] **Negative-case test for every control the threat model allocated**: no threat model for this change
- [ ] Coverage threshold met, no drop vs. `main`: n/a, no application code
- [x] Lint, format, static typing clean (the changed script passes its own ShellCheck gate)
- [x] No new High/Critical SAST, SCA, IaC, or container findings
- [x] No secrets in source or history
- [x] No suppressions without a written rationale **and an expiry date**
- [x] New dependencies: none

**Verification**
- [x] Required logs / metrics / traces emitted (the report count is printed in the build log)
- [ ] Accessibility verified: n/a
- [ ] Threat model updated if the design changed during build: none exists for this lane

**Governance**
- [x] Issue linked; commits conventionally formatted. [ ] Commits are **not signed**.
- [x] Docs / runbook updated if behavior changed (in-file comments; `ci/README.md` not changed)
- [ ] Control evidence written to `evidence/105/`: not written
- [x] ADR explicitly not needed (same uploader and pattern as the existing lanes)

## Security

- **Security-relevant?** yes, it is a detection control. No G2 approval was sought.
- **Controls implemented:** SI-2/RA-5 shell SAST reporting → `ci/pipeline.yml` `lint` ensure → verified by the manual seeded run.
- **New attack surface:** the `lint` job now receives `((mykronos_ingestion_token))`, the same token the existing `mykronos-*` lanes already use.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. No data migration. Findings already in MyKronos stay there, and they close by ShellCheck's own absence, not CodeQL's.

## Reviewer notes

- After merge, MyKronos still treats keel's `lint` as a stub: `KEEL_STUBS_THAT_LOOK_MAPPED` in `backend/mykronos/ci.py`. `(keel, lint) -> sast` should be declared there **after** this merges, so the coverage cross-check can see it. That is a follow-up in mykronos, deliberately not done first: mapping it before this lands would credit the stub again.
- What I'm least sure about: whether a gate that has now actually turned on could redden `lint` on a script added later. That is the intended behaviour.

## Self-review — required if nobody else approves (solo mode, POAM-008)

- **Record:** not written (`evidence/105/g3/self-review.md` absent)
- **Opened / reviewed:** not done. This PR was opened by an agent session; the operator reviews it.
- **Verified independently:** listed under AI authorship above
- **Agent findings:** none run
- **Not verified:** a live Concourse build; a live upload reaching MyKronos; the scanner-failure branch (exit >1)
- **Cold-read notes:** none yet

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Approval transitions and placement moves read rows again after their owner already has the authoritative state. Placement move lookups also retain a synchronous Gateway path despite an existing worker operation. Group-catalog snapshots issue separate queries for order and defaults.

## User Impact and Design

Use INSERT/UPDATE RETURNING for approval insert, resolution, denial, consumption, and expiry, and for placement completion/draining. Keep the approval decision and mutation in the same transaction, with the security check intact. Route placement move reads through the existing worker, delete the superseded synchronous readers, and remove redundant internal source/move and membership rereads. Load group order and defaults together. No schema, stored-format, permission, public SDK, update, or lifecycle change.

The lane's source inventory is **43 → 40 T1 expressions** on the paired base, and **44 → 41** against the final integrated main parent (which reclassified one retained restart-clear compatibility primitive as T1), excluding the separately owned GitHub publication family. The original 92-call assignment included that family. This is a bounded cutover, not a claim that Gateway T1 has reached zero. Remaining calls need an owner or compatibility redesign: released synchronous placement/standing-grant SDK methods, native approval commit callbacks that must remain atomic, workspace-reservation authority at an external effect, process-held incognito databases, and deprecated synchronous Mention Inbox operations. Their contracts and retirement paths are recorded in `worker-access.md`; no new compatibility path is added.

## SQL Measurement

Three alternating pairs, M/C/M/C/M/C, on one otherwise idle AWS c7a.8xlarge using the shared workload unchanged. Base `18941faa9629ce0a9fa318f979351fd385878850`; candidate `b60c2bb48c6ba4cafab351b662571bd6d2c7c626`. Final head `b6df4ae33403643a5e1cddd0658d29493e827bf3` includes two main integrations. Only the generated inventory conflicted; it was regenerated. Upstream placement recovery and SDK deprecation-warning changes merged cleanly. The PR-owned SQL edits remain unchanged, so the paired proof is reused under the campaign integration rule.

| Metric per warmed turn | Base median [min–max] | Candidate median [min–max] |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| All-thread statements | 456.0 [455.2–456.5] | 451.0 [450.8–456.5] |
| Worker requests | 90.8 [90.4–91.0] | 90.4 [90.4–90.9] |
| Main-thread statements | 4.1 [4.1–4.1] | 4.1 [4.1–4.1] |

| Phase | Base statements median | Candidate statements median | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 01.boot | 2079 | 2078 | -1 |
| 01.connect | 944 | 948 | +4 |
| 02.first-turn | 1315 | 1307 | -8 |
| 04.second-session | 1808 | 1808 | +0 |
| 05.control-plane | 104 | 104 | +0 |
| 06.cron | 674 | 673 | -1 |
| 07.compaction | 201 | 201 | +0 |
| 08.shutdown | 100 | 106 | +6 |

The measured base is already below the 500 warmed-statement aim. The raw warmed median falls by 5.0 statements and 0.4 requests, but that difference comes from unchanged session-owner work (`database.prepareWrite`, `session.turn.commit`, exact-entry/row-fact reads). It is **not attributed to this PR**. The repeatable shared-harness saving is `sessionGroups.snapshot`: **5 → 4 statements**, one request in both versions, during boot. Warmed paths touched by this PR do not add work.

The largest candidate/base phase-duration median ratio is 1.057; warmed duration is 15.780 → 15.796 seconds. First-turn and warmed medians do not rise. Connect +4 and shutdown +6 are within the campaign's absolute non-turn tolerance: unchanged session prewarm/registry timing, audit-prune busy-timeout statements, and agent clean-close bookkeeping account for those deltas. No extra pair was needed.

A separate synthetic probe invokes the public asynchronous approval owner after warming the database, using the same all-thread statement observer. Both revisions produce the expected outcomes:

| Operation | Base statements | Candidate statements | Worker requests, both | Main-thread statements, both |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Insert approval | 8 | 7 | 1 | 0 |
| Resolve approval | 7 | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| Consume allow-once | 7 | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| Force denial | 7 | 6 | 1 | 0 |
| Expire one approval | 6 | 5 | 1 | 0 |

## Removed Checks and Accepted Edges

- Approval post-write rereads and duplicate mutation predicates: the initial decision and mutation share one synchronous write transaction, so another writer cannot intervene there.
- Group membership rereads around admission/commit: the owner serializes membership and mutation; no supported outside writer participates.
- Placement preparation/recovery source and move rereads: unexpected out-of-band same-session cancellation can allow recoverable preparation before exact worker completion rejects it. Normal moves remain coordinator-serialized. Actual environment/session/policy authority checks at external effects and exact completion predicates remain.

## Evidence

- 329 focused tests across 21 files passed, including placement recovery, current environment authority, approval first-answer/allow-once behavior, write-receipt visibility, group mutation, and destination-authority E2E. The remote `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <21 files> --maxWorkers=1` wall time was 1034.23s, including cold worker compilation/cleanup; Vitest reported 690.58s for the 20-file shard and 77.07s for the E2E shard. No new CI test job was added.
- SDK compatibility and approval settlement/web-push suites passed; the additional fixture-lifecycle mock test passed on the merged head (4.76s wall time).
- `check:changed` passed on the measured candidate, including types, Knip, type-aware lint, source contracts, T1 and dialect ratchets. Madge and export collisions passed. On the merged head, type-aware lint, export collisions, the generated inventory check, Madge, and T1/dialect ratchets passed.
- Final-head Knip reports only the inherited production unused export `src/infra/agent-run-terminal-writes.ts: captureAgentRunTerminalWriteContext`; the full-tree and scripts scans pass. The merged-head `check:changed` stops at the inherited max-lines suppression in `src/web-search/runtime.test.ts`. Both exact findings were reproduced on main `e7e3b949ae134060cc8c2a7cd8d224ad27edcd91` with its frozen dependencies installed; neither affected file nor the relevant baselines/configs are changed by this PR. These are the only static exceptions. Required changed-file static checks were run separately after that stop; no PR-caused static finding remains.
- Two Codex autoreview rounds completed with no remaining P0/P1 findings. The subsequent correction preserves the existing in-process environment authority check before opening a tunnel and removes no security check.
- Required CI and security gates passed on the final integrated head `b6df4ae33403643a5e1cddd0658d29493e827bf3`: [CI run 38129718475](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38129718475). Earlier CI failures in the changed code were fixed; the earlier session-files failure also failed in scheduled main run 38122045725 and disappeared after integrating main.
- Published-driver × candidate update cell is not applicable: no update, Doctor, schema/migration, plugin loading, or service lifecycle changes. No SDK API surface change.

LOC against the integrated main parent: production **+137 / −277**, tests **+128 / −174**, docs/tooling **+11 / −34**, generated inventory **+12 / −15**; 32 files total.

author: ak125
body:
## Ce que fait cette PR

Le Safety Auto-Gate (familles sécurité-critiques, `quality-gates.md` §7) n'était qu'à moitié câblé : `gap1_auto_review.py` calculait ses propres conditions, certaines marquées `NOT_YET_WIRED`, et avait une option `--adr091-amended` pour lever le blocage tout seul. Il est maintenant décidé **dans le décideur canonique** `promotion_decision.py`, et gap1 se contente de rapporter cette décision.

### Conditions (toutes doivent être prouvées ; si une manque ou ne peut pas être évaluée, la fiche est bloquée)

| Condition | Calculée dans | Preuve exigée |
|---|---|---|
| `dim_A_floor` | `evaluate_tier` | score A ≥ 22 (un score impossible à calculer échoue) |
| `dim_C_floor` | `evaluate_tier` | score C ≥ 15 (un score impossible à calculer échoue) |
| `no_quality_gate_fail` | `evaluate_tier` | gates exécutés = `CANONICAL_GATE_NAMES`, et tous passent |
| `numeric_exactitude_verified` | `evaluate_tier` | toute valeur chiffrée avec unité affichée est ancrée sur une source capturée **et** couverte par une plage `validated` corroborée par ≥ 2 sources |
| `no_disputed_claims` | `evaluate_tier` | frontmatter `no_disputed_claims: true` explicite (booléen) |
| `diagnostic_live_authority_not_claimed` | `evaluate_tier` | aucune revendication d'autorité sur le moteur diagnostic LIVE |
| `no_manual_review_policy` | `evaluate_tier` | ni `safety_rules` ni une entrée de couverture n'impose de revue manuelle |
| `coverage_strict_pass` | `decide_promotion` | couverture stricte PASS |
| `regression_gate_pass` | `decide_promotion` | NEW / NEUTRAL / IMPROVED |
| `provenance_pass` | `decide_promotion` | provenance PASS |

Le résultat est une seule raison `SAFETY_HUMAN_REVIEW` qui porte `conditions`, `blocking_conditions`, `details` et `policy`.

### La politique reste coupée

`SAFETY_AUTO_APPROVAL_ADR = None` : c'est une **constante de politique dans le code**. Ce n'est ni une variable d'environnement ni une option CLI, et elle fait partie de l'empreinte du moteur (`_EVALUATION_ENGINE_FILES`). Tant qu'elle vaut `None`, une fiche safety dont toutes les conditions sont prouvées reste bloquée avec `policy.status = not_ratified`. Pour la lever, il faut une PR WIKI qui cite l'ADR vault acceptée amendant ADR-091 §4 / ADR-093.

Comme **aucune plage n'est `validated` aujourd'hui**, toute valeur chiffrée avec unité dans une fiche safety la bloque déjà.

### gap1

- `_safety_auto_gate` reprend la décision canonique et y ajoute ses conditions sur les claims bruts (page entièrement capturée, aucune source `pending_source_validation`, et quand ils sont fournis : exactitude numérique et `raw_ref` du source-catalog).
- Verdicts : `safety_auto_blocked` / `blocked_by_current_safety_policy` / `safety_auto_approved`. Aucun verdict « humain ».
- `--adr091-amended`, `NOT_YET_WIRED`, `DIM_A_FLOOR` et `DIM_C_FLOOR` sont retirés. Le rapport expose `safety_auto_approval_adr`.

### Supports

- `contradiction_gate.py` : texte visible uniquement.
- `check-coverage-map.py` : `visible_text_blocks`, qui couvre aussi titres, blocs de code et texte alternatif d'image.
- `numeric_exactitude.py`.
- `NUMERIC_RANGES` devient une entrée du manifeste (rôle `numeric_ranges`, anti-TOCTOU).

### Reste pour une V2 (écrit dans §7)

Détection des contradictions dans la prose, valeurs chiffrées du frontmatter, workflow de validation des plages.

## Tests (locaux)

- `pytest _scripts` : **751 passés, 13 en échec**, tous dans `_scripts/test_build_exports_seo.py`. Les **13 mêmes échecs** apparaissent sur la base `cc04f08` (copie `git archive`), donc ce n'est pas une régression. Cause : Click 8.1.6 en local, dont le `CliRunner` mélange stderr dans `result.stdout` (une ligne `SKIP …` précède le JSON). La CI exécute ce fichier et est verte sur `main`.
- `_scripts/gates` : 21 passés. Suites promotion : 228 passés. gap1 : 43 passés.
- `quality-gates --all-local` : 24/24 PASS (3 WARN, déjà présents avant).

## Effet runtime

Aucun. Aucune fiche n'est promue ni modifiée, aucun export ne change. La politique coupée ne fait que **rendre explicite** le blocage qui existait déjà.

Verdict : REVIEW_REQUIRED.

author: skalaliya
body:
PR B of the wiki plan (the plan's PR 4). **Builds on #254: merge that first.** Until then this diff also shows #254's commits; its own commit is the last one.

## Download PDF
- Every exported page has a pre-built PDF at `/pdf/<id>.pdf`. The page menu gains **Download PDF**, a plain link with a file name like `sggs-kb_api-quickstart_2026-09-27.pdf`.
- **Built inside the site build** by an Astro `astro:build:done` hook, when `DOCS_PDF=1`. Both deploy jobs run their own `vercel build` and deploy only what it writes, so a step after the build would never ship.
- **Rendered at the published address.** Each page is opened as `https://docs.gurbanisoul.com/…` with every request answered from `dist/` on disk. Links inside a PDF are real, nothing is fetched from the network, and the build cannot call production.
- Requests are refused **by file, not by path**: wiki pages live under `/api/` too, so "block `/api/`" would have blocked those pages.
- **Fail closed:** a page that cannot be rendered fails the build.
- **137 PDFs, 43 MB, 16 seconds.** The plan estimated minutes and a cache; neither is needed.
- Tagged for assistive technology, with a bookmark outline. Made from the same `print.css` and `print.ts` as the browser's Print.

## The gate: `check-pdf` (in `check:all`, and run again by each deploy job on its own build)
- One PDF per exported page, no strays; titled, tagged, bookmarked.
- **Every run of Gurmukhi that contains a letter is set in Sant Lipi.**
- An Ang citation is on the same sheet as its quotation.
- No link to the machine that built it.
- Each file ≤ 3 MB; all ≤ 75 MB.

A PDF cannot be proven byte-exact for Gurmukhi, because shaping reorders glyphs inside the file. The verbatim export remains the Markdown; this gate proves font, presence and place.

## Fixed: Gurmukhi on the wiki was not drawn in Sant Lipi
The gate's first run found Gurmukhi set in a **system font**. The cause is older than this work: page text is never marked `lang="pa"`, so the style rule that gives Gurmukhi its font never applied to it. In prose, tables, headings, code and diagrams it took whatever font the reader's device had. On a Linux build server with none, the PDFs would have shown empty boxes.

- **Fix:** Sant Lipi now leads every font stack (`--sl-font`, the mono stack, the serif stack, and Mermaid's). Its `unicode-range` covers Gurmukhi and the dandas only, so nothing else changes. This is how the main site does it.
- **Result:** all 755 runs with a letter are Sant Lipi, on screen and in the PDFs.
- **The one exception:** 20 isolated vowel signs (a sign shown alone on a dotted circle, on three pages that explain the script). A browser cannot use a range-limited web font for a sign with no letter under it. The gate counts and allows them.
- **Not done here:** marking Gurmukhi as Punjabi for screen readers (WCAG 3.1.2). That needs a markup change across pages and is worth its own PR.

## Workflow
`deploy-docs.yml`: `DOCS_PDF: "1"` on the three builds; `check-pdf` on `.vercel/output/static` in both deploy jobs; timeouts +5 to +10 minutes. `actionlint` clean. `docs_smoke.py` fetches `/pdf/index.pdf` on builds that announce `pdf1`.

## Checks
- Unit: 130 pass (4 new: each promise of the gate, broken, is reported).
- `build` with `DOCS_PDF=1` + `check:all`, including `check-pdf`: green.
- e2e: 441 pass. The 2 new PDF tests skip in a build made without PDFs.
- Typecheck clean; `docs_check` 0 errors; `tools/tests` 63 pass.
- I read real output PDFs: a setup page, a Scripture 101 page, a poster page, the data dictionary.

## What only CI and staging can show
1. The fonts on the Linux runner. `check-pdf` prints the list of embedded fonts; the Gurmukhi rule is enforced there.
2. `vercel build` picking up `DOCS_PDF` and shipping `/pdf/`. The deploy job now checks its own output, and the smoke check fetches a PDF.

**Merge with `--merge`, after #254.**

author: sebgod
body:
This adopts three of zig's own loop rules. Each one retires special cases rather than adding new ones.

- **`LoopStatement <- inline? (For / While)`.** `inline` is now part of LoopStmt, so `outer: inline for` and any position that takes a loop accept it.
- **`ForExpr <- ForPrefix Expr (else Expr)?`.** A value loop's `else` is an optional `LoopElse`: `whileValue`, `forValue` and `inlineForValue` each take one or not.
  - The loops sit in the last groups and `LoopElse` sits earlier, so an `else` after the body still shifts.
  - An else-less loop in a statement position is lowered as the statement loop. That retires `ProngBody -> LoopStmt` and `whileNoElseExpr`.
  - Std shapes this covers: `=> for (l.items) |e| h.update(e),` (Build.zig), `=> |s| inline for (…) { … },` (zon/parse.zig), and a value switch prong `=> for (…) { … } else .tuple,` (zig/Ast/Render.zig).
- **`ForPrefix AssignExpr (; / else Statement)`.** New `forStmtThen` and `whileStmtThen` cover a body with no `;` that is ended by `else` (zig/WindowsSdk.zig). This is the statement loops' version of `stmtIfThen`.

**Correctness.** zig reads `=> for (xs) |x| sum += x` as an assignment to the loop and rejects it with "invalid left-hand side to assignment". dotcc's grammar reads it the same way, and it is now rejected with the same message.

**Verification**
- Probe: 525 to 528 (Build.zig, zig/Ast/Render.zig, zig/WindowsSdk.zig), with no file breaking. zon/parse.zig now gets past its prong and stops at a `comptime` field.
- New precedence decisions:
  - At statement start the statement loop wins on `;`, an assignment operator, or `else` into ThenExpr.
  - An `else` after a value loop's body shifts into LoopElse.
  - The plain `for` still beats `inline for` in a prong.
- Unit suite: 2704 passed. New pins `A_value_loop_has_an_optional_else_and_inline_is_a_loop_statement` and `Rejects_an_assignment_to_a_loop_in_a_prong`.
- Oracle row `loop_expressions` matches `zig run`.
- Sharded functional suite with the zig oracle (4 shards): 1709 tests, 922 passed, 0 failed.

author: objectstack-fleet[bot]
body:
Fixes #22769

Clause-②: yes

The inbound flow hook (`POST /api/v1/automation/hooks/:flowName/:hookId`) now accepts a second, versioned form of `x-objectstack-signature`. Its timestamp is inside the signed material and is checked against a fixed five-minute tolerance window. The body-only form is still accepted and now logs a deprecation signal. Our senders are unchanged. This is the additive scheme from triage's answer (`6105617130`). Refusing body-only signatures (the cutover) is the maintainer's decision and is not in this PR.

## What changes

- **One definition, in core.** `packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts` gains three things beside `signHttpBody`:
  - `signHttpBodyAt(body, secret, timestampSeconds)` returns `t=SECONDS,v1=HEX`. HEX is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, under the secret, of the string `SECONDS`, a full stop, and then the raw body bytes (the Stripe shape).
  - `HTTP_SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300`. It is a named constant, ⛔ not a configuration key.
  - `verifyHttpSignature(body, secret, header)` returns `HttpSignatureVerdict`: `{ valid: true, scheme: 'v1' | 'body-only' }`, or `{ valid: false, reason: 'absent' | 'malformed' | 'mismatch' | 'outside-window' }`. It is the receiver's half of both forms. It re-signs through `signHttpBody` / `signHttpBodyAt` and compares with `timingSafeEqual`, so no receiver holds a second copy of the HMAC input. The window is symmetric: a `t` more than 300 s ahead of the clock is refused too.
  - All three, and the type, are exported from `@objectstack/core` (`src/security/index.ts`). This is an additive public surface.
- **trigger-api verifies through it.** `ApiTrigger.handleRequest` and the exported `verifySignature` (same signature, still returns `boolean`) call `verifyHttpSignature`. The local `createHmac` copy of the signed material is gone. Every refusal is the existing `401` envelope `{ success: false, error: { code: 'INVALID_SIGNATURE', message: 'Signature verification failed.' } }`, the status PR #22779 declares for the inbound-hook member, and nothing is enqueued.
- **Deprecation signal on the body-only form:** one `warn` line per armed hook (`ArmedHook.bodyOnlyDeprecationLogged`). It names the flow and the hook, spells out the timestamped form, and states the window. Re-arming the hook (stop/start, which the engine does on a flow update) logs it once more. A sender that keeps posting cannot flood the log.
- `packages/triggers/trigger-api/vitest.config.ts` aliases bare `@objectstack/core` to source, with an anchored `find`, the same way `service-queue` does. Without the alias, the new value import would make these pins judge core's `dist/`, and `check:test-source-alias` would refuse the unregistered import.
- The route-ledger note (`trigger-api-route-ledger.ts`) names both forms.
- ⛔ Not touched: `service-messaging`'s outbox, `service-automation`'s `http` node, `packages/spec`, `packages/lint`, docs, and `trigger-api/src/plugin.ts`.

## Why this shape

- **One header, with the form told apart by its prefix** (`sha256=` against `t=`). The self-hosted mount already passes the one header through unchanged, so `plugin.ts` needs no change. PR #22779's transport-neutral member says "Anything a later signing scheme adds (a timestamp, for one) arrives in the same forwarded request, so this signature gains no field for it", and this shape keeps that true. A separate timestamp header would need a mount change and a new `handleRequest` input, and this card's scope excludes both. ADR-0041 names "GitHub/Stripe style", and this is the Stripe grammar.
- **A strict grammar, with no fallback.** A value that starts with `t=` is judged by the timestamped form alone. If it is malformed, carries the wrong HMAC, carries the body-only HMAC, or has a stale `t`, it is refused. It never drops back to the body-only check. The grammar is: a canonical decimal `t` of at most 15 digits, one 64-digit lowercase hex `v1`, and exactly those two elements in that order. Verification re-signs the value and compares the whole thing, so any other spelling is refused.
- **Nothing speculative:** no multiple `v1` entries for key rotation, no `v0`, no configuration key, no new header.

## Tests

On HEAD `ffb30285d`, after merging `origin/main` `c74d84399` and rebuilding (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/trigger-api...' --filter '@objectstack/objectql...' build`):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 93 passed, Tests 2362 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/trigger-api test`: Test Files 2 passed, Tests 38 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core --filter @objectstack/trigger-api typecheck`: both `Done`. Core's `check:test-typecheck` held its ledger: 4 files, 4 errors, 4 pinned signatures, no growth. trigger-api compiles against core's rebuilt `.d.ts`, and `verifyHttpSignature` exists only in the new build.

The pins (every refusal asserts the whole `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` envelope and that nothing was enqueued):

- `api-trigger.test.ts`, "the timestamped signature form": the sender's value is computed with `createHmac` straight from the recipe, not through core.
  - A fresh timestamped post is accepted (`202`, enqueued, the flow runs, no deprecation line).
  - A replay outside the window is refused: the exact post that was accepted is sent again once the clock is 301 s later.
  - A stale timestamp that the HMAC genuinely covers is refused, and so is a future one past the window. The two edges are accepted.
  - A stale timestamp carried with a valid body-only signature is refused, in both the `v1=` and the `sha256=` spelling.
  - Malformed values are refused with the same envelope a bad signature gets.
  - A wrong secret and a different body are refused.
  - CONTROL: a body-only post is still accepted, and the deprecation line is logged once per armed hook.
- `http-signature.test.ts`: literal-value pins of the wire form, the window edges, the replay, no fallback, the malformed set, and trimming. A constant-time pin wraps `node:crypto`'s `timingSafeEqual` and asserts that it makes the one decision for every well-formed value of either form.

**Ablations.** Each mutation went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode. Every one landed (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed) and was restored: the blob equals the HEAD blob and `git diff HEAD` is empty. A script `trap` restored on EXIT, INT and TERM. Both suites resolve the subject from source: core's test imports it relatively, and trigger-api through the alias. So no `dist/` leg applies, and the trigger-api reds below show the alias reaching source. Runs on `115cd41f4`, except A3b on `9cb44814e`. Neither source file has changed since.

| # | Mutation | Red |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | window check disabled | core: edges, replay · trigger-api: replay, stale/future, `verifySignature` stale |
| A2 | `v1` signs the body alone, not `t.body` | core: literal pins, "signs the timestamp", no-fallback · trigger-api: fresh, replay, stale, no-fallback, CONTROL, `verifySignature` |
| A3b | a `t=` value falls back to a `sha256` element | core: no-fallback · trigger-api: "stale timestamp with a valid body-only signature" |
| A4 | `timingSafeEqual` replaced by `===` | core: constant-time pin |
| A5 | the once-per-hook flag never set | trigger-api: CONTROL (two lines, not one) |
| A7 | header lower-cased before parsing | core: malformed set · trigger-api: malformed envelope |

The first A3 run left core green, which showed that core's suite did not cover the `sha256`-spelled downgrade. `9cb44814e` added that case, and A3b turned core red as well.

**Gates.** The list was derived on this branch at `ffb30285d` with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, which gave 65 commands. Each command's exit code was recorded to disk before any pipe. `--ran` reconciled them: "Run reconciliation — 65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN." All 65 exited 0 on `ffb30285d`, including `check:test-source-alias`

author: mamz93us
body:
## What

Four things HR asked for.

- **Non-Saudis column** on Saudization: professional groups (with a totals row), By department, and each profession inside a department. The assistant gets the same figure.
- **Saudization by manager**, a third tab. Oracle's manager, not its supervisor. One level only, so the rows add up to the company.
- **Nationality from Oracle's API.** `/employees` now sends it; the sync writes it for everyone holding their Oracle number. Oracle's wins where it sends one, and a blank erases nothing.
- **The Oracle HR import remembers decisions.** A row linked, created or skipped by hand is matched or skipped the same way on the next import.

## Why the import asked again

A decision lived on the staged row and died with its batch. Two people linked on batch #39 share only their Oracle number with their record, the matcher wants two signals, and they came back unmatched every morning for three weeks.

`HrImportDecision` keeps the decision. It is recognised by Oracle number and person id, or number and name where a sheet gave no id, because the SSS Egypt series shares numbers. A remembered link gives way, back to the review list with the reason shown, when:

- the matcher is now sure of somebody else, or
- another row of the same import is the same record.

`resolveUnmatched()` also refuses a link onto a record another row already is. One record holds one Oracle number: on 2026-10-11 somebody new in Oracle was linked onto a namesake matched by their own row, and Apply wrote the namesake's facts back five minutes later.

## Also

- The review page shows why an unmatched row is waiting. The note was only shown for error rows.
- The note is cut to its 255-character column.
- The department target sum moved to `Saudization::standing()`, shared by the department and manager pages.
- Gender arrived in the API with nationality and is left to the review page: it drives the gender Azure groups and the signature template.
- By manager is not offered to the assistant: a manager with one or two people would hand it an individual's nationality.

## Deploy

Two migrations, both additive: `hr_import_rows.nationality`, and `hr_import_decisions`, which carries over the links already made (9 on NOC2).

## Tests

- New: `SaudizationByManagerTest` (13), 17 cases in `EmployeeSyncTest` for nationality and decisions, plus cases in `EmployeeFactsTest`, `MigrationsTest` and `SaudizationTest`.
- Unit suite: 1547 pass, 17 fail, which is the documented baseline (TunnelWatchdog 15, AccessApp 2).
- Dry-run on production in temporary tables and a rolled-back transaction: the next import matches 615 of 616, three by a remembered link, and leaves the namesake to be decided. Nothing was written.

author: poyrazk
body:
## Milestone

M9 recovery hardening: managed PostgreSQL preview acceptance.

## What

Real Neon testing found that its legitimate migration owner was rejected by SQL verification: the adapter grants database CREATE for custom schemas, while the shared verifier treated that grant as runtime privilege drift. Accept database CREATE only for migration access. Runtime CREATE, temporary-object privileges, administrative CREATEDB, unsafe memberships and role flags remain denied.

The deployed SQL probe retains separate writer and reader pools and declares the existing after_restore hook. Its callback resets captured sockets and verifies existing data before readiness. A real delayed-TLS regression reproduced the shared-deadline gap in serial reconnects; independent writer/reader readiness reads now run in parallel within the unchanged 1.5-second budget. Native acceptance adds a required disconnect-and-restore phase; six-phase evidence is rejected.

Local tests also reproduced the SQL fixture's healthy-session expiry at 30 seconds and the new probe's autocommit write completing after pre-commit cancellation. Explicit disconnect/outage controls replace fixture deadlines; the probe uses an explicit transaction and never automatically replays writes. Failed COMMIT outcomes can still be uncertain.

Full CI exposed a single-shot fake-vsock listener that stranded a reconnect after a dropped handshake. A deterministic regression reproduced the same timeout. The fixture now accepts replacement connections and joins its goroutine during cleanup; production hook deadlines are unchanged.

The routing architecture test also required classification for the SQL probe file: its Acquire calls borrow semaphore permits, and its private customer pools use pooler-safe reads and explicit transactions. Add the documented registry entry while preserving the global routing gate. The same race-enabled gate failed before and passes after the entry.

Main integration exposed test-fixture and generated-source drift. Explicitly configure the worker test's per-app instance cap, exercise historical alert rollback at its own migration boundary, assign the new queue-push metal test to its native phase, and regenerate Python SDK output and the capability matrix with the canonical generators. Production worker limits and deployed migration SQL are unchanged.

## Spec / ADR impact

- Existing contracts: [ADR-155](docs/adr/155-provider-neutral-managed-postgres.md), [ADR-348](docs/adr/348-customer-after-restore-hook.md).
- No new architecture, quota, API, or CLI contract. TLS pool configuration reuses the existing credential verifier validation.
- Repair inherited ADR collisions: scenario TCP fault injection is ADR-981, and the internal apid package decomposition is ADR-982. Both numbers were checked against current remote main and all 137 open PR titles. Scope renames to those documents, index entries and matching comments; decisions and runtime behavior are unchanged.

## Verification

- Local PostgreSQL 16.15 with TLS/SCRAM: three race/shuffled runs each of the SQL verifier (24 named passes), Neon SQL role tests (72), and full SQL pool suite, including delayed concurrent reconnects (27). No skips or race failures. Real custom-schema DDL succeeds and runtime CREATE/TEMP/unsafe-role drift remains rejected.
- Before/after regressions independently reproduce and fix migration verification, idle-session expiry, pre-commit cancellation and fake-vsock reconnect failures.
- Resume-hook and reconnect contracts: 20 race/shuffled repetitions, 120 named passes.
- Linux/amd64 static guest-binary contract and native suite cross-compilation passed on commit f0810c4dfb; the final commit changes only one generated documentation row. Six verdict-parser tests, phase partition, sqlc drift, gofmt and diff checks passed. Compilation does not establish native execution.
- [x] Live Neon direct/pooled pool acceptance on runtime commit 87553f83a2 (provider/pool source and the complete credential-probe SQL implementation remain unchanged after integrating main): two complete runs, 22 actual phase passes. Both retained four writer/reader connections over 31 seconds, preserved all writes, rejected pre-commit cancellation, recovered terminated sessions, and retired both held/fresh old writer credentials. Hook readiness took 562–958 ms. Each run independently verified project deletion.
- [x] All six workflows succeeded on commit 51bb1aff22, including the [full workflow](https://github.com/poyrazK/faas/actions/runs/38153563262) with 36 successful jobs. The selected Linux worker-scaling and historical migration shards passed; the migration also has an explicit named local PostgreSQL race pass. Nonverbose CI does not provide individual pass/skip counts. Canonical SDK regeneration is stable across two further runs; capability matrix, phase partition, SQL and ADR checks passed. Original failure and cleanup evidence remains retained.
- [ ] Native test-managed-postgres-native, test-metal and host leak checks on a supported x86_64 Linux KVM acceptance host.

Local rotation supplies an explicit scheduler retirement receipt because it has no guests; deployed acceptance requires the real scheduler receipt. Live testing uses disposable projects only. Production provisioning stays disabled and Neon Launch/billing are unchanged. The temporary organization API key is revoked (DELETE 200, subsequent authentication 401). All seven disposable projects were independently confirmed absent; all three local test clusters, their private credentials, and private Neon credential/AX files were removed.

One earlier final-commit live attempt failed during idle retention and its first cleanup request did not verify deletion. The explicit cleanup retry and independent GET returned 404; that failure and cleanup proof remain retained. The two subsequent instrumented runs passed all checks. The cause of that earlier idle failure remains unclassified; the original failure evidence is preserved alongside the two complete passes.

On the GPU target the StableHLO emitter now interpolates the histosys rows of all channels in one lane tensor. The FlatPPL is unchanged and the CPU target is byte-identical to main.

## Commit

**Interpolate histosys rows of all channels in one lane tensor on the GPU target** (`crates/stablehlo/src/pyhf.rs`).

- When the GPU target reaches a `pyhf_helpers.histosys_shift.(lo, nominal, hi, alpha)` call, the emitter collects every such call reachable from the module's bindings, bound or inlined. A call qualifies with `[rows, bins]` anchors and `alpha = addaxes([a1, …], …)` of shape `[rows, 1]`, or with bin-vector anchors and a scalar alpha.
- The anchors of all calls are flattened into one lane vector, one lane per row and bin. Alpha is one gather of each row's parameter per lane. `histosys_shift` runs once over the lanes, with its arithmetic unchanged.
- Each call reads its block of lanes back as its own `rows × bins` view (a slice and a reshape). The per-sample row selections and their segment sums downstream are unchanged.
- The reverse pass sums each parameter's lanes in one scatter. On main, each channel reduces its alpha column over bins inside the gradient assembly.
- The lanes are built only in module scope, and calls inside callable bodies keep the per-channel lowering.

This is the layout of the earlier converter-side lane tensor, moved into the emitter so that only the GPU target takes it. That converter form was a GPU win and an XLA:CPU loss whatever the reduction shape.

Sizes: production +179, tests +38 / -10.

New test `gpu_target_interpolates_every_histosys_call_in_one_lane_tensor` (`crates/stablehlo/tests/pyhf_yields.rs`). It checks the determinized module first: `wide` stays bound because it has two uses, and a second call is inlined into `outputs`. On the GPU target both calls share one alpha clamp and one 8-lane alpha gather. That is 2 x 3 lanes for `wide`, counted once although two paths reach it, plus 2 inlined lanes. The CPU target keeps two clamps. The test fails without the change.

## Census (forward StableHLO, unbatched, 177 pyhf workspaces)

All 177 conversions are byte-identical FlatPPL. `parameter_names` emits on neither side, a pre-existing limitation of the census query.

| cpu f64 | main | 32 | 1293 | 1228 | 3874 | 4888 | 321 | 3608 | 32332 |

On the gpu target, 71 models change. 66 small one-call models grow by 1 to 11 view ops (the full-width slice and reshapes of a single call's lanes). The timing models shrink:

author: terryncew
body:
# GATEWAY-SUBSCRIPTION-001: subscription-cancellation demo

**Do not merge. For owner review only.**

## What this is

The enterprise gateway (`experiment/openline-gateway-001`, frozen at
38e33ce) stays the product. This branch adds its first understandable
consumer-facing use case: subscription cancellation through OpenLine
Wallet (mandates), Receipt Gate (Envoy + ext_authz + signed decision
tokens), and verifiable receipts. Not a separate product.

Base: 38e33ce (frozen baseline, history preserved untouched).

## The demo

```bash
cd gateway
./subscription001/run_demo.sh
```

One command. Fictional customer, fictional merchant (`merchant-acme`),
fictional funds. 25/25 checks passed on 2026-10-11:

- Owner authorizes the merchant to charge up to $20 (mandate).
- One $20 charge succeeds; the simulated ledger moves exactly $20.
- Duplicate billing (replayed charge, replayed token) is refused.
- A $200 increase is refused (`payment_limit_exceeded`).
- Forged tokens, unsigned API calls, and tampered request bodies fail.
- Owner revokes; the next charge is refused (`agent_revoked`), $0 moves.
- A signed refusal receipt is verified with the receiver public key
  alone (standalone verifier, no gateway code).
- The hard case, shown honestly: a token minted *before* revocation,
  presented *after* it, is refused by the execution-time standing check
  ($0 moved). Without the check it executes — the 60s TTL window,
  disclosed on a contrast instance, not hidden.

Evidence: `gateway/subscription001/EVIDENCE-demo.md` + `evidence/`
(transcript, refusal receipt, receiver pubkey, final balances).
Independent verification: `gateway/subscription001/VERIFY.md`.

## The 60-second window

Not closed to zero — narrowed. With the standing check (the demo's
configuration), the residual window is the check-to-commit interval
(p50 ~1.4 ms, max 35.6 ms measured, n=30). Without it, pre-revocation
tokens execute to their 60s TTL. Race tests: 10/10 pass
(`gateway/tests/test_standing_races.py`); results in
`gateway/docs/STANDING-CHECK.md` and
`gateway/subscription001/EVIDENCE-races.md`. No instant-revocation
claim is made anywhere.

## Docker verification — NOT fully verified (20/22)

6 CI runs on GitHub Actions (`ubuntu-latest`, real Docker). The
compose path had never been executed before; this mission found and
fixed 7 real blockers (empty config volume, in-container 127.0.0.1,
STATIC-vs-STRICT_DNS, build context, `internal:true` killing port
publish, authz silent exit, `--max-cents` space form, mockapi bind).

20/22 checks pass: full HTTP path, exact ledger deltas,
tamper/replay/revoke denials, `verify-receipts` clean, persistence
across service restart, receipt survival across full-stack restart.
The gap: balance reads via Envoy after a FULL-stack restart timed out
(90 s); the mockapi container logged nothing post-restart. Balance
persistence itself is proven (service-restart + DB-volume checks), so
this is not data loss — but the root cause (Envoy upstream recovery
vs compose restart ordering) is unisolated. Full attempt record:
`gateway/subscription001/EVIDENCE-docker.md`.

## Public materials (docs only, no claims beyond evidence)

- `gateway/subscription001/docs/ADOPTION-GUIDE.md` — for infra engineers
- `gateway/subscription001/docs/VIDEO-STORYBOARD.md` — 20–30s X video
- `gateway/subscription001/docs/PRESENTATION.md` — visual presentation frames
- `gateway/subscription001/docs/GUARANTEES.md` — established vs limitations

## Standing limitations (also in the docs)

- No per-period billing caps in the mandate model (per-charge caps +
  revocation only).
- Simulated payment API; no real money, merchants, or banks.
- Nothing here makes a real bank or merchant honor an OpenLine mandate —
  the receiver must integrate the check.
- Proof of a right is not the power to exercise it.
- Production non-bypassability depends on network isolation.

## Checklist for the owner

- [ ] Demo runs clean on your machine (`run_demo.sh`)
- [ ] Evidence reads honestly (EVIDENCE-demo.md)
- [ ] Decide: keep the standing check opt-in or default-on for the gateway
- [ ] Decide: authorize isolating the post-full-restart upstream stall

## For Humans

### Why

Windows support is paused: getting Mission Control on Windows to an acceptable performance standard would take too much work. `release/windows` stays frozen at `597cc4f6`. This PR is unit W of the [pause plan](docs/plans/pause-windows-support/plan.md). It removes from `main` everything that existed only to serve that branch, and records the pause in the fork tracking.

### What changed

- **Sync runbook deleted.** `docs/windows-branch-sync.md` is gone, along with its links in `docs/README.md`, `docs/upstream-sync.md` and `docs/fork/README.md`. The fork-tracking plan's two links (md and html) now point at the [`d44bda68` permalink](https://github.com/ramiro314/mission-control/blob/d44bda68/docs/windows-branch-sync.md), and their text is unchanged.
- **Windows plan marked Paused.** A note under the title of `docs/plans/windows-support/plan.md` and its `plan.html` gives the date, the reason, the frozen SHA, where the runbook went, and a link to the pause plan.
- **Fork report.** `scripts/fork-report.mjs` no longer queries `release/windows` PRs or annotates merges with "includes N release/windows PRs".
- **Seam comments.** The three platform-seam comments no longer name `release/windows`. The empty per-platform maps are unchanged.
- **Example branch is now `release/2.0`.** This covers the Dispatch "Base branch" placeholder, both MCP tool descriptions, `BaseBranchSchema`'s doc comment, `docs/dispatch-and-backlog.md` and every test fixture. `git grep release/windows` outside `docs/plans/` and `CHANGELOG.md` prints nothing.

**External steps, already done (2026-10-11):**
- Closed as *not planned* with the plan's closing comment: #342 to #362 and #372 (22 issues). #369 and #319 are still open.
- Deleted two remote branches. GitHub keeps the objects for a while, so they can be recovered by SHA:
  - `fix/win32-e2e-fast-assertions` at `87e78b6e77f9556a751fb5f02c05f62daca2e292`

This is a human step.** Following plan R1, I listed live missions once on the operator daemon this task reached, `GET http://127.0.0.1:7317/api/schedules`, and it answered `HTTP 200` with body `[]`. No "Sync main into release/windows" mission is listed there, so nothing was archived and no other route was tried. **Human step:** check Missions on every machine that runs a Mission Control daemon, and archive "Sync main into release/windows" wherever it is listed.

### Evidence

- Local runs on Linux (Node 24):
  - `npm run docs:links`: "Verified 685 Markdown files", exit 0.
  - Touched unit tests plus every docs-reading test (`grep -l '\.\./docs/' test/*.test.ts`), one `node --test` run: 279 tests, 279 pass, 0 fail.
  - `test/startup-handover.test.ts`: on this host, the unchanged test failed with `spawnSync /usr/bin/open ENOENT`; with the macOS guard, 11 pass and 1 is skipped.
  - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` and `npm run smoke`: all exit 0. Lint reports only warnings that were already there.
  - `npm run test:e2e -- e2e/specs/diff-task-base-branch.spec.ts`: passes after a fresh build. It asserts the placeholder `e.g. release/2.0` and captured the screenshot below.

- Issue and branch state after the external steps: all 22 issues show `CLOSED NOT_PLANNED` with the comment, and `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/fix/win32-*'` is empty.
- **Screenshot.** Captured by the e2e spec from the built dashboard: the Dispatch dialog with Backlog details open and the empty Base branch field reading "e.g. release/2.0".

  ![Dispatch dialog, Backlog details expanded, empty Base branch field showing the placeholder e.g. release/2.0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbddc32d-93fc-444f-835c-d98ee6baa8b0)

author: abenezer1244
body:
## Summary

Release A (#496, live and verified) taught the Celery delivery tasks to open a sealed envelope. **This PR switches every producer**, so PII and bearer links stop sitting in the Redis broker, its retries, task events, and a worker's `Received task` line. Every worker already runs release A, so it can open these messages.

| Producer | Now enqueues |
|---|---|
| Job delivery email (`tasks.py`) | `job_id` plus sealed `{scraper_name, record_count, download_url, recipient_emails, fmt}` |
| Batch delivery email (`batch_export.py`) | run id plus sealed `{..., summary_message, link_expires}` |
| Duplicate-signup email (`registration.py`) | sealed `{email}` only |
| Job webhook (`tasks.py`) | `job_id` plus sealed `{url, payload}` (URL can carry a secret; payload has the signed download link) |
| Generic dialer webhook (`dialer.py`) | `job_id` plus sealed `{url, payload}` (payload = leads with names, phones, emails, addresses) |
| Tracerfy ingest (webhook route, dispatcher redrive, self-recheck) | `queue_id` only. The task already reads the link and counts from Tracerfy's own record (audit #5 S3-15) |

If sealing fails, each site takes its existing enqueue-failure path: an ops alert, the dialer claim release, or the duplicate-signup gate release.

## Deploy notes

author: abdallahelficky-wq
body:
## Summary
Fixes the ZATCA chain race found while building #150. **Two postings in the same company at the same moment could get consecutive ICVs with the same PIH**, which breaks the hash chain. Sec 4.3 of the guideline requires PIH = the hash of the last generated document.

### The defect
`reserveZatcaChain` did two things that could disagree under concurrency:
- It reserved the ICV with `UPDATE companies SET "zatcaNextIcv" = "zatcaNextIcv" + 1 … RETURNING`. That is atomic.
- It took the PIH from `params.company.zatcaLastInvoiceHash`, a company row each caller read **before** its transaction started.

When two postings overlap, the second waits on the row lock. When the first commits, the second gets the next ICV but still holds its stale PIH, which is the **first** document's PIH. The new test reproduces this on `production` every time (3 of 3 runs): "ICV 5 PIH: expected … to be …".

### The fix (one function, every path)
Inside the caller's transaction, `reserveZatcaChain` now:
1. runs `SELECT "zatcaNextIcv", "zatcaLastInvoiceHash" FROM companies WHERE id = … FOR UPDATE`;
2. uses that row's counter as the ICV and that row's hash as the PIH;
3. builds and hashes the document;
4. writes **both** `zatcaNextIcv = icv + 1` and `zatcaLastInvoiceHash` in one `UPDATE`.

The lock is held until the caller commits, exactly as long as the old `UPDATE`'s lock was, so lock exposure does not grow.

**Paths covered:** every reservation goes through this one function.
- **Sales invoices:** create-and-post and draft post. **POS** goes through `createSalesInvoice`.
- **Credit notes and debit notes:** create and post.
- **Compliance-test documents:** via `evaluateZatcaPostingGate`.
- **Station sales:** they create no ZATCA documents (journal entries only), so nothing to cover.
- **Re-issue (#150, not merged):** already re-reads the company under the lock and calls this function, so it inherits the fix. The two PRs merge without conflicts (checked with `git merge-tree`).

## Mirror / reversal statement (CLAUDE.md rule 1)
Not a new control; this is the correctness of the ZATCA counter and hash.
- **Mirror:** a journal entry mirrored to another company never reserves a ZATCA chain. Only the issuing company's sales documents do, and the lock is per company row, so one company's postings never wait on another's.
- **Reversal:** documents in the chain cannot be un-posted (existing rule, unchanged), so nothing ever rewinds the counter or the hash.
- **Reversal of a mirror:** not affected.
- **Tenant isolation (rule 4):** unchanged. The lock and the read are keyed by the company `id` the caller already resolved within its tenant.

## Found during testing, not changed here
`reserveDocumentNumber` (`src/lib/docNumbering.ts`) uses a Prisma `upsert` to create a company's numbering-settings row the first time a document type is used. Prisma's `upsert` is not atomic. If the **first-ever** credit note (or debit note, or invoice) of a company is posted twice at the same moment, one request fails with a unique-constraint 500. The whole transaction rolls back, so there is no gap and no chain damage; a retry succeeds. The test creates the first credit note and first debit note before the burst so it measures only the chain. The fix is an `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; I left it out to keep this PR to the chain race and can do it separately.

## Test plan
- [x] `src/lib/zatca/chainConcurrency.integration.test.ts`: Postgres via HTTP, real builder, **real ECDSA signing**. Only ZATCA's acceptance is mocked (an outside response, CLAUDE.md rule 2).
  - **Mixed burst:** 18 parallel postings in one company: 6 create-and-post invoices (standard and simplified), 4 draft posts, 3 credit notes and 3 debit notes.
    - ICVs are gapless and unique.
    - Every PIH equals the previous document's hash, across the three tables.
    - The company's counter and last hash match the end of the chain.
  - **Repeated bursts:** 3 bursts of 8 invoices; the whole chain from ICV 1 is unbroken.
  - **Fails on `production`** (3 of 3 runs) and **passes with the fix** (6 of 6 runs).
- [x] Full suite on a freshly created local Postgres (`prisma migrate deploy`, lint, build, `npm test`): **1031 passed, 0 failed**, 1 skipped (the existing Python-dependent ZIP check). `tsc`: 0 errors.
- [x] No ZATCA calls, no production database, no environment-file reading.

author: abstractversion
body:
## Why
On every KubePool, the small CI tooling steps spent 9–18 minutes installing kubectl before about 5 seconds of real work. These steps are `check-drift` in `ci-reconcile` and `ml-ci-reconcile`, plus `ml-autoscaler-healer`, `ml-nodepool-janitor` and `ml-compute-catalog-probe`. Each ran `google/cloud-sdk:alpine` (a floating tag) and did `gcloud components install kubectl`, and also `apk add jq`, because that image has no jq either. They set no resource requests, so their pods were BestEffort. All of them are pinned to the pool's 2-node e2-standard-2 system pool, and they piled onto one CPU-saturated node.

Effect on the dev hub e2e (2026-10-11): a fresh ML KubeApp's designed first-build trigger runs `<app>-ci-sync` → `ml-ci-reconcile` (force) → `ml-ci-build`. It started 17.5 minutes late, which broke the golden-path check that the first CI build starts within 900s of app creation.

## Change
- **check-drift** (both reconcilers) now uses `alpine/k8s:1.36.4`, which ships kubectl 1.36.4, jq 1.8.2 and curl with busybox `sh`. The platform already uses this image family for the projectmlstack composition's kubectl/jq steps. The install lines are gone. A fail-fast `command -v kubectl` check keeps the old "could not install" exit. The rest of the script is unchanged.
- **healer / janitor / compute-probe** now use `google/cloud-sdk:585.0.0-alpine`, pinned (gcloud and python3). No single small image ships gcloud, python3 and kubectl together; the full Debian cloud-sdk image does, but it is over 1 GB. Instead, a `kubectl-bin` init container copies the static kubectl from `alpine/kubectl:1.36.4` into an emptyDir. The step mounts it read-only at `/opt/kubectl-bin` and puts that directory on `PATH` where the install block used to be. The rest of each script is unchanged.
- **Requests**: cpu 50m and memory 64Mi, or 128Mi for the gcloud steps since gcloud is Python. The init container requests 50m/64Mi. There are no limits: the janitor's `kubectl get workflows -A -o json` grows with the cluster, and an OOMKill would only hide the result. The pods become Burstable.
- The images and requests are set in values under `tooling.*`, with the same defaults in the templates.
- kubectl 1.36 is within one minor version of the hubs (GKE 1.35.6) and the pools (GKE 1.36.4 on the current e2e pool).
- Added `tests/tooling-images`, wired into `validate-charts`. For each of the 5 CWTs it checks: the image tag is an exact version, the script installs nothing (`components install` / `apk add` / `apt-get` / `pip install`), and cpu and memory requests are set. For the gcloud steps it also checks the init container, the emptyDir and the PATH.
- Chart `0.12.109` → `0.12.110`.

Out of scope, and unchanged: other runtime installs in steps that are not on this path. These are the pending-reaper's `apk add jq coreutils`, ml-ci-build's report/pr-render `apk add` / `pip install`, and the Hera nodegroup steps' floating `google/cloud-sdk:alpine`.

## Tests
- `helm lint`: passes. `helm template`: renders. `argo cluster-template lint` on the 6 rendered tooling CWTs: no errors. `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` on the dev hub, which runs Argo v4.0.5 CRDs with full schemas: all accepted, and `initContainers`, `volumes` and `resources` survive the round trip.
- New `tooling-images` suite: 26/26 pass on this chart, and 26/26 fail on 0.12.109.
- All existing suites pass, with the same counts as on `main`: ci-secrets-prep 19, reconcile-trigger 18, untrusted-workspace 30, retry-safety 29, git-token 44, render 24, stale-deploy 52, render-order 2, retry-window 4, report-observable 3, clone-token-scope 14, enhancer-drift 30.
- **In the production images** (linux/amd64):
  - `enhancer-drift` (30) and `reconcile-trigger` (18) run inside `alpine/k8s:1.36.4` with `DRIFT_SHELL=sh`. That means the rendered check-drift runs under that image's busybox sh and jq 1.8.2, against the suites' stub kubectl and curl. All pass. `${x:0:12}` works in that shell.
  - `sh -n` passes for all 5 rendered scripts under their own image's shell.
- **Live on the dev hub**, in a throwaway namespace that has since been deleted: one Argo workflow ran the rendered janitor step's exact init container, volume, mount and requests with a probe script, alongside an `alpine/k8s:1.36.4` step with 50m/64Mi.
  - Both succeeded with QoS `Burstable`, each on a system node.
  - gcloud step: `kubectl` resolved from `/opt/kubectl-bin` (v1.36.4), an in-cluster `kubectl get workflows` worked, and gcloud 585.0.0 and Python 3.14.6 were present.
  - kubectl step: `kubectl get workflows | jq` worked, and curl to api.github.com returned 200.
  - Pod start to finish took about 25–30s, including cold pulls of all three images. Before, the kubectl install alone took 9–18 min.

## Rollout
Pools take the chart version from the operator (`buildDefaultSystemToolsConfig` in kubecore-operator, `ciWorkflows.version`). After this merges and the release workflow publishes 0.12.110 to `https://novelcore.github.io/charts/`, a kubecore-operator PR bumps that pin to `0.12.110`.

author: cterence
body:
## Summary
- Fix `Update flake` workflow failing with `HTTP error 403` from `gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/es-de/emulationstation-de/...`
- Root cause: the `emulationstation-de` flake input (`gitlab:es-de/emulationstation-de/v3.4.1`) makes Nix call the GitLab API **unauthenticated**. GitHub-hosted runners share IP ranges and gitlab.com now rate-limits unauthenticated API traffic (60 req/h/IP; brownout windows Oct 7 & Oct 14, full enforcement Oct 19, 2026).
- Add `--access-tokens gitlab.com=PAT:${{ secrets.GITLAB_TOKEN }}` to all 4 nix invocations that touch flakes:
  - `update-flake.yml` (the failing scheduled job)
  - `build.yml`: `flake check`, `nix build`, `nix store diff-closures`

## Why the `PAT:` prefix
Nix's gitlab fetcher expects the token value as `TYPE:token` (`PAT:` or `OAuth2:`) — see `GitLabInputScheme::accessHeaderFromToken` in `src/libfetchers/github.cc`. Without the prefix, Nix warns `Unrecognized GitLab token type` and sends the request without a valid auth header, so gitlab.com answers 403.

## Setup required
Add a repository secret **`GITLAB_TOKEN`**: a GitLab PAT with `read_api` scope (repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions). Keep the raw token value (starts with `glpat-`); the `PAT:` prefix is added in the workflow.

## Verification
- YAML validated locally for both workflow files
- Will be confirmed by the next scheduled `Update flake` run (daily at 00:00 UTC) and the PR `Build` workflow once the secret is set

body:
Closes #652.

## What
- Release: `release.yml` now tags `v<version>` on a commit that sets both plugin manifests to the version, on top of the CI-tested commit and off main's history. It still sets the plugin version on main afterwards, as before. Until now the tag was the released commit itself, whose manifests said the version before (`v0.22.0` says 0.21.0). Both harnesses cache the plugin by its manifest's version. Decision 0011 and its index line say the current rule.
- `aeolus-trierarch upgrade [version]` installs the plugin of the version it upgrades to, for each harness on offer. That holds also when the trierarch is on that version already, and when no version is given (the latest on npm). It points the aeolus-fleet marketplace at `v<version>` first:
  - Codex: `codex plugin marketplace remove aeolus-fleet` (it keeps the plugin and its cache; there may be none to remove), then `add ThomasHendrickx/aeolus-fleet --ref v<version>`, then `upgrade aeolus-fleet`. All of this runs inside the step that keeps and puts back version folders (#581, #653).
  - Claude Code: its marketplace is never removed, since `claude plugin marketplace remove` uninstalls the plugin and deletes its data (the crew identities). Instead, the aeolus-fleet entry in `extraKnownMarketplaces` of its user settings (in `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude`) is dropped, and the rest is kept. Then `claude plugin marketplace add ThomasHendrickx/aeolus-fleet#v<version>` declares the new source, followed by `marketplace update` and `plugin update`.
- Releases up to 0.22.0 have no tag that holds their plugin. For those, upgrade points the marketplaces at main and says so.
- Codex downgrade: Codex starts new sessions on its newest version folder, and upgrade keeps the newer folder for the sessions running on it. So new Codex sessions keep starting on the newer plugin, and upgrade says so plainly. orchestrator-1 files the downgrade itself as its own issue.
- "The aeolus plugin for X is on Y, the latest, already" now reads "... is on Y already": with a pinned version it is not always the latest.
- Docs: docs/trierarch.md, docs/architecture.md, the trierarch README and the plugin README.

## Checked on real Codex 0.160.1 and Claude Code 2.1.296 (throwaway CODEX_HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR only)
- Codex: `marketplace add` with another ref is refused while the marketplace exists. `remove` keeps the plugin, its config entry and its cache. After `add --ref <tag>`, `upgrade` installs the plugin from the tag. With a newer folder beside it, `codex plugin list` reports the newer one.
- Claude Code: `add owner/repo#<tag>` is refused while settings declare another source. With the settings entry dropped, `add` declares the new source, and `plugin update` moves to the tag's plugin, downgrades included. `marketplace remove` uninstalls the plugin and deletes its data.
- Ran the built adapter against both real CLIs in those throwaway homes, with a tag and with main. Both ended with the marketplace pinned to the tag in their own config (Codex `config.toml`; Claude Code `settings.json` and `known_marketplaces.json`) and the tag's plugin installed.

## Tests
- `adapters/plugin-update.test.ts`: Codex remove, add with `--ref`, then upgrade; add without a ref for main; goes on when there is nothing to remove; says what Codex said when add fails, and upgrades nothing. Claude Code add with `#<tag>`, then marketplace and plugin update; main without a ref; drops only the aeolus-fleet entry from the settings, follows CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and leaves other settings untouched (and writes none where there are none).
- `cli/upgrade.test.ts`: the tag of the given version for each harness; the tag of the latest on npm; the tag when the trierarch is current; main for 0.22.0, said; nothing said of main from a tag on; the Codex downgrade said, not when Codex has the version, not for Claude Code.
- Full `npm test` locally, integration included: 6115 passed, 8 skipped.

## Noticed, not done
- The release change is first exercised by the next release (0.23.0). Until then no tag holds its plugin, so every upgrade still installs from main.
- The repository `ThomasHendrickx/aeolus-fleet` is fixed in upgrade: a marketplace added from a fork or a local path is pointed back at it.
