author: sisshiki1969
body:
Before: an Array carried nothing about the types of its elements, so the JIT had to guard every `a[i]` result before Fixnum arithmetic.

After: every Array carries `ARRAY_ELEMS_FIXNUM` (header flag bit 5), which, when set, guarantees that every element is a Fixnum. Nothing reads it yet; this is stage A of E1 (maintaining the bit). Stage B (the JIT typing `a[i]` from it, with a loop-entry check) follows as a separate PR.

## How

- **Conservative by default.** `Value::as_array_inner_mut`, which the `Array` wrapper's `DerefMut` and all of its inherent mutators go through, clears the bit. A mutation path that knows nothing about the bit loses precision, never soundness.
- **Kept where it is cheap.** `push`, `insert`, `set_index`, `set_index2`, `resize` and `fill` keep or set the bit when the stored values are Fixnums and no nil padding appears. `rotate!` and `reverse!` keep it, and they no longer take a bulk write barrier, since a permutation adds no new references.
- **Set at creation.** The bit is set on:
  - `[]`;
  - `Array.new(n, fixnum)`;
  - constant literals and VM-built literals that are all Fixnum.

  It is part of `NEWBORN_FLAG_MASK`, so `dup`, `clone` and literal copies inherit it. `swap_kind` (`map!`) carries it along with the payload.
- **JIT stores (x86-64 and aarch64).**
  - The inline `a[i] = v` gets the store's static kind (`StoredKind::{Fixnum, NonFixnum, Unknown}`).
  - Because FROZEN and the bit share a byte, one `testb` covers both checks. The clear sits on a cold path, and for `Unknown` a Fixnum value jumps straight back.
  - `<<` and `a[s, len] = other` clear the bit too.
- **Epoch.** Clearing a set bit moves a process-wide epoch (`elems_kind_epoch`). Stage B's safepoint poll will compare it, the same way `ivar_ty::poison_epoch` works.
- **Debug check.** Debug builds assert, at every GC mark, that any array carrying the bit really is all Fixnum, so a forgotten clear fails the test suite. I checked this by disabling each x86 clear in turn: the new tests in `tests/array_elems_kind.rs` catch every one.

## Cost (cachegrind Ir vs master with #1728)

| bench | Ir |
|---|---|
| optcarrot | +0.21% |
| fannkuchredux | +1.1% (a flag check on every mutable access; `q[0..-1] = p` runs ~3M times) |
| binarytrees | +0.9% (all in `execute_gc`, whose logic is unchanged in release, so most likely code layout) |
| sudoku, nqueens, matmul, chunky-png | within ±0.1% |

Wall-clock times for fannkuch and binarytrees are within run-to-run noise.

## Testing

- The full integration suite and the lib tests pass locally. The one exception is `fork_block_child_runs_the_exit_sequence`, which also fails on master in this environment.
- The aarch64 backend is not built locally (no cross toolchain), so the macOS CI is its check.

author: copilot
body:
The payment-bypass promo code `TOUT2026` shipped in the frontend bundle, and SEC-004 limited bypass to `is_admin` accounts only. This PR removes the code from `frontend/` and lets the owner authorize specific accounts, not just admins.

- **Authorization (`services/promo_bypass.py`)**
  - An authenticated user may bypass if `is_admin=true` **or** their email (case-insensitive) is in `PROMO_BYPASS_ALLOWED_EMAILS` (comma-separated).
  - Guests are always rejected, since a guest can type any email.
  - Sentinel `__ADMIN_BYPASS__` is resolved server-side to `PROMO_BYPASS_CODE` (default `TOUT2026`). The existing active/quota/CAS/redemption-log logic then applies. The real code is never returned to the client.
  - `promo_bootstrap.py` now seeds the DB row from `PROMO_BYPASS_CODE`.
  - `backend/.env.example` documents both variables.

- **Composer (`routes/composer.py`)**
  - Removes the `_PROMO_CODES` dict, which gave 100% off to anyone.
  - `/checkout` now goes through `try_consume_promo` (authorization, quota, redemption log). `/apply-promo` rejects unauthorized users.
  - The code no longer appears in the fake session id or in transaction metadata.
  - Both endpoints now read the optional user via `get_optional_user`.

- **Frontend**
  - `AdminGenerateReadings.js` sends `promo_code: '__ADMIN_BYPASS__'` and no longer displays the code.
  - Placeholders and comments mentioning `TOUT2026` are neutralized (`PromoCodeField`, `ThemeNatalOneshot`, `ComposerPage`, `SalesPageV3`, and a stray copy under `public/branding/pr139/`). `grep TOUT2026 frontend/` now returns nothing.
  - `ComposerPage` now sends `Authorization: ****** to `/apply-promo` and `/checkout`. Without it, authorized users would be treated as guests on this page.

- **Tests**
  - New `backend/tests/test_promo_bypass_unit.py` covers admin, allowed email (case-insensitive), unauthorized user, guest, and sentinel resolution (env override and default).

```python
# frontend sends the sentinel; backend resolves it
try_consume_promo('__ADMIN_BYPASS__', {'id': uid, 'email': email})
# → looks up os.environ['PROMO_BYPASS_CODE'] (default 'TOUT2026')
```

**Review notes**
- `TOUT2026` remains in git history, older tests and docs. If the repo or site is public, set a new `PROMO_BYPASS_CODE`.
- Set `PROMO_BYPASS_ALLOWED_EMAILS` in production to grant accounts access.
- A user typing the real code manually still works through `/api/promo/validate` and `PromoCodeField`, which is unchanged. Bypass is enforced at checkout.

body:
# Pull Request

## What this changes

The 0.3.0 redesign: Prompt Maker Studio becomes a home for prompts people keep retyping into chat assistants. One sections editor replaces the two old editors, the library becomes the home page with a sidebar of folders, the app gets a coral-and-plum visual system, and features that were shallow or misleading for that job are removed. Refinement and evaluation are deferred (backend kept, no UI). Rationale is recorded in `product/DECISIONS.md`.

- **Sections are the only thing clients write.** The server renders the prompt text from its sections on every write (create, PATCH, restore, MCP). New `POST /api/prompts`; PATCH rejects `generated_prompt`.
- **Data recovery, run once at startup.** Migration 023 rebuilds the sections of hand-edited prompts, keeping the originals as a version. Migration 024 names old History entries and files them under "Recovered history".
- **Editor.** Live preview with Template/Filled modes and copy, variable hints, inline checks, starter templates, Import text, Ctrl/⌘+S with version notes, draft recovery, conflict handling, and a History panel with diff and restore.
- **Library and shell.** Sidebar folders with counts, bulk folder rename/remove endpoints, list/grid, delete with undo, a phone drawer, and a simplified Settings page.
- **Removed.** Generate/History, dashboard and analytics, the standalone Playground, tags, code snippets, notification emails and the weekly job, density, the metrics bar, and the related metrics and Grafana panels.

The commits are grouped by step (data recovery → API and editor → shell → removals → seed, screenshots and docs) and can be reviewed in order.

## Type of change

Feature · Breaking change · Refactor · Docs

## Related issue

None — the plan was settled in a design interview and a clickable prototype review.

## How you tested it

- `make ci-local` passes: 693 backend tests (96.1% coverage), 176 frontend tests, 13 Playwright tests including axe audits of every redesigned screen in both themes, the Docker smoke test, and the security and image scans.
- Migrations: unit tests cover exact splits, the cases where splitting must not be trusted, consistent prompts left alone, and recovered-history naming.
- Manual: drove the real app in the isolated e2e stack and reviewed screenshots on desktop (light and dark) and phone. README screenshots were regenerated with `make screenshots` from the new demo seed.
- **Not yet done:** running the migrations against a copy of production data.

## Checklist

- [x] `make ci-local` passes
- [x] New backend code has tests — CI enforces 90% coverage
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or real `.env` values in the diff
- [x] Docs updated if behavior, endpoints, or configuration changed

## Deployment and migration notes

Full steps are in `docs/deployment.md` under "Upgrading to 0.3.0".

1. Back up with `make backup-db` and rehearse on a copy first: migrations 023 and 024 rewrite prompt sections and names once.
2. Remove any `make send-weekly-summary` cron entry; the target is gone.
3. Breaking API changes:
   - removed: `/api/prompts/generate`, `/api/prompts/history`, `/api/prompts/tags`, the Playground endpoints, and `/api/analytics/dashboard`
   - PATCH rejects `generated_prompt` and `tags`
   - responses no longer include `tags`, `run_count` or the `notify_*` preferences
4. MCP clients should refresh their tool schemas: `list_saved_prompts` lost `tag`. See `docs/mcp.md`.
5. The changelog entry is under `[Unreleased]`, to be moved to `[0.3.0]` when tagging.

author: jongtae
body:
## User outcome

An API connection required by an existing request can now be proposed in conversation, confirmed by the owner, and completed on the existing one-time secret-input page. After a required read and requested account check succeed, the same Work resumes and returns its substantive result without a second request. Static keys and the supported RFC 6749 client-credentials shape share this path.

## Runtime impact / what changed

- Add `api_connections/connect` to existing Settings and phone/local input; public metadata and exact confirmation stay separate from HTTP-only secrets.
- Adapt Fernet/Keychain/QuickStore to immutable encrypted credential references, staged readiness and atomic slot/publication receipts. Failed input preserves the previous connection.
- Use installed oauthlib for Basic/body client credentials and token parsing. Encrypted Bearer caches bind credential revision, metadata and expiry; renewal uses the existing transport and current-authority checks.
- Reuse the existing continuation queue. Corrections, expired pages and restart preserve the original Work; temporary key/cleanup failures do not consume its wait. Duplicate/late/cancelled input cannot revive it.
- Money-capable slots floor every non-read method to payment and retain exact one-use approval before token renewal or execution.

The chosen AI supplies public metadata, chooses tools and performs the original task. Core code generalizes connection/secret/authority/recovery boundaries; it contains no provider, site or task-specific workflow.

## Goal / authority

CONNECT-01 #1295, ordered child #1300 after merged #1299/#1353; implementation plan: https://github.com/Jongtae/agentos/issues/1300#issuecomment-6106453318. Owner authorization covers this PR and ordinary squash merge after required checks and risk review. No deployment, real accounts, live model checks or scheduler activation. #1307's merged work is reused. Whole-program CC1–CC8 and cumulative/scheduled execution audit remain #1301.

## Constitution / specification alignment

C15 Adopt/Adapt and C16 AI execution; Connection and Delegation §§3/12, Presence's necessary-input-page rule, #1300's original-request completion clarification, and existing #1298 exact-effect semantics. No new grants, Memory ownership, scheduler or protocol framework.

## Existing solutions review (Adopt / Adapt / Build)

- problem/boundary: owner-mediated generic API credential input, usable-read verification and same-request recovery, including RFC6749 token renewal.
- internal repository candidates: `ApiRequests`, `save_slot`, `http_request`, token/finish callback; `SettingsOrchestrator`, common continuation; `PhoneInput`; `KeychainKey`, `QuickStore.secret` and SQLite publication.
- search evidence (paths/symbols/docs checked): `api_requests.py`, `connection_slots._oauth_token`, `phone_input.py`, `quickstart_service.resume_settings_work`, `browser_jar.py`, encrypted Google adapters, `current_context.redact_known_secrets`; #1300 compatibility comments and implementation plan.
- standard-library/platform candidates: Python urllib/base64/SQLite/thread/file locking; existing macOS Keychain key provider. Existing locks and transactions retained.
- official SDK/reference/standard candidates: RFC6749 client credentials, existing oauthlib 3.3.1 `BackendApplicationClient.prepare_token_request/parse_request_body_response`; MCP URL elicitation remains negotiated-only.
- mature open-source/framework candidates: installed oauthlib (OAuth serialization/parsing) and cryptography Fernet (encryption), both existing dependencies; existing namespace-specific encrypted adapters considered for storage reuse.
- maintenance/security/supply-chain fit: no dependency/version/download change; installed oauthlib 3.3.1 compatibility tested with actual SDK and local HTTP transport. Prepared headers copied to avoid shared SDK map mutation. Exact existing lockfile applies; this is not a new advisory or universal protocol audit.
- licence fit: oauthlib BSD-3-Clause and cryptography Apache-2.0/BSD-compatible existing dependencies; compatible with repository AGPL-3.0-only. No vendored code.
- runtime/deployment/compatibility fit: current Python runtime, QuickStore and supported macOS Keychain; MemoryKey/fake clocks/transports for deterministic tests. Static encrypted references remain readable; encrypted slots cannot be downgraded through legacy registration.
- decision: Adapt
- why rejected candidates are insufficient: Google-specific stores deliberately constrain their namespaces and cannot directly own generic API slots; widening them would alter their contract. A separate OAuth/workflow/secret framework adds no missing protocol capability to the existing SDK and host primitives. Nonstandard issuer protocols require an observed mismatch/fallback rather than provider branches.
- AgentOS-owned policy/authority boundary kept outside the dependency: owner/Work/request binding, approved destination/scope, exact credential revision, money/effect floor, current authority, no replay, publication and continuation receipts.

## Authority / threat model

Owner-confirmed public metadata names allowed API hosts and optional HTTPS token endpoint/scope. Only the contextual HTTP input receives static keys or key pairs. Fernet ciphertext is stored in the existing owner-local secret file; its key remains in the existing Keychain primitive. Model context, Settings drafts, tool results and Evidence contain references/public metadata, not credentials. Staged/active/retired encrypted values participate in redaction; unreadable keys fail closed.

Readiness is read-only, bound to required fields and optional subject, with current Work/input checks before and after transport. Failed publication cannot replace another revision. Cleanup is revision-guarded. Token requests have no redirects or automatic retries; a 401 invalidates the cache without replaying the API action. Money marking cannot be lowered by registration; no standing payment delegation is introduced.

## AgentPackage / runtime delta

No package/runtime identity, install lifecycle, filesystem grant, Memory candidate, background subscription, sandbox or dependency delta. Connector delta: owner-confirmed static/RFC6749 API input and renewal. Three input checks and three page starts per Work, bounded transport sizes/timeouts, existing common continuation cap; program-wide budget continuity remains #1301.

## Lifecycle / recovery impact

Credential staging grants no authority. Verified slot metadata and its Settings receipt commit together; failure preserves the previous slot. Successful migration removes the previous plaintext key. Interrupted cleanup or temporary key loss remains waiting until recovery, without repeating the readiness call. Restart expires an uncommitted page and permits bounded renewal on the same request. Changed owner/request/account/credential and cancellation invalidate the continuation. Removing a slot removes its current encrypted references; retired ciphertext retained for redaction grants no authority. Rollback must preserve owner secret files/Keychain; old binaries do not understand new encrypted/OAuth slot metadata.

## Validation

Focused model-free checks on this branch:

```
PYTHONPATH=src:tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_connect_api_oauth.py tests/test_connect_api_input.py tests/test_connect_slot.py tests/test_connect_mcp_continuation.py tests/test_connect_skill_continuation.py
```

129 passed, 114 subtests passed.

```
PYTHONPATH=src:tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_api_requests.py tests/test_connection_slots.py tests/test_owner_profile.py tests/test_phone_input.py tests/test_owner_settings_conversation.py tests/test_no_scenario_code.py tests/test_connect_effects.py
```

227 passed, 74 subtests passed. Total: 356 tests and 188 subtests across these two focused runs. `verify_master_plan_docs.py`, `verify_assistant_execution.py --check-spec` and `git diff --check`

author: erikbeauvalot-sg
body:
Tout ce qui règle l'agent se modifie depuis l'écran **Administration**, sans accès au serveur. Le document d'architecture décrit la fonction (section « Configuration depuis l'interface »).

**Qui modifie quoi** (matrice des rôles mise à jour)
- Administrateur : `catalog/sources/*.yaml`, glossaire, relations, `config/models.yaml`, `config/poc.yaml`, `agents/*.yaml`
- Superviseur : `playbooks/*.yaml`, `prompts/*.md`, `eval/cases*.yaml`
- Superviseur, Administrateur, Auditeur : lecture de tout et de l'historique
- Comptes : formulaire (création, rôles, désactivation, nouveau mot de passe), jamais `auth/users.yaml` en texte ; les empreintes ne sortent pas de la passerelle ; le dernier administrateur actif est protégé

**Garanties à l'enregistrement** (`src/diagagent/config_files.py`)
- validation par les règles de l'orchestrateur (playbooks, rôles, fournisseurs, budgets, variables des prompts, ids égaux aux noms de fichier) : un fichier invalide est refusé, rien n'est écrit ;
- refus d'une version périmée (409) si quelqu'un a modifié le fichier entre-temps ;
- écriture atomique, commentaire obligatoire, historique dans `config-history/` (auteur, commentaire, empreintes ; version d'origine gardée au premier enregistrement), écart avec l'actuel et reprise d'une version ;
- journal d'accès : `config_changed`, `user_created`, `user_updated` (sans mot de passe) ;
- hors interface : code, secrets, `runs/`, `audit/`, `knowledge/`.

**Vérifié**
- 153 tests passent, dont 16 nouveaux (chemins refusés, dix contenus invalides, conflit, historique et retour arrière, création de fichiers, droits par rôle, comptes).
- Parcours réel dans Vivaldi headless, sur une copie de la configuration : liste, éditeur, erreur de validation, enregistrement, historique et écart, comptes ; affichage sur téléphone (390 px).

Point ouvert ajouté au document : relecture par un second Superviseur, ou rejeu obligatoire du jeu d'évaluation, avant qu'une modification de playbook ou de prompt prenne effet.

body:
## P1-A — 현장 CSV 등록 전 점검 및 복구
이 PR은 이미 병합된 P0 CSV→DuckLake→분석→검토 흐름의 앞단에 **정확한 CSV 파서 기반 사전 점검**을 추가합니다. 제품이 저장할 수 없는 CSV를 단순 문자열 추정으로 "가능" 처리하지 않습니다.

### 사용자 경로
- 감독형 Web의 "CSV 분석 전 점검": PC UTF-8 CSV 업로드(1MiB 이하) 또는 작업공간 상대경로를 현재 선택한 신호·시간·상 역할에 맞춰 실제 `validate_csv_sensor_source`로 검증
- 결과: 표본 행 수·시작/종료 시각·실제 원본 SHA-256, 이력 적재 시간대 조건, 3상 매핑 제출 여부, parser 품질 경고
- blocked 시 원본 파서의 행 번호·컬럼과 간단한 한국어 조치 안내. 이력 시간대 미설정은 "추가 확인 필요"로 구별
- 파일/설정 변경 시 옛 사전 점검 결과 무효화. Web의 시간 컬럼은 실제 요구조건에 맞게 필수 표시

### 구현 원칙
- 이미 사용 중인 `FileSourceConfig`, `_file_phase_bindings`, CSV 어댑터를 재사용. 분석기 신규 제작 없음
- same-origin + CSRF + supervisor 브로커, 임시 staging 및 즉시 삭제. preview에서는 사전 점검 불가
- **사전 점검은 저장된 소스·수신·이력·Run/Evidence를 만들지 않음**. 기존 실제 등록 경로도 독립적으로 다시 검증
- 조건 만족은 데이터 구조·등록한 역할이 분석 입력 형태에 적합하다는 뜻으로, 실제 물리적 단위·배선의 진위 또는 고장 진단은 아님

### 검증
- [ ] 실제 CSV 유효 / 비숫자 행·열 / naive timestamp / 불완전 R/S/T 매핑
- [ ] Supervisor HTTP 임시 업로드 preview: CSRF 거부, 원본 읽기 후 무영속·stage 삭제
- [ ] 실제 Chromium: preflight→원본 등록→수신→이력→분석→검토/재시작
- [ ] Ruff/mypy/Core, Runtime, Operations, Package, systemd, Interactive Analysis 및 main 병합 후 검증

현장 사용자·실물 OPC UA 환경 검증(P1-B/C)은 별도 실제 데이터가 필요하므로 아직 완료됐다고 주장하지 않습니다.

author: dawsontoth
body:
## ⊙ Problem

Studio has no view of Harper's jobs — the background runs behind CSV/S3 loads, exports, bulk deletes and backups — so there is no way to see what ran, what failed, or why. A CSV import also blocks behind an "Importing…" spinner that shows neither whether Harper has started the job nor how long it has been running (#1266).

> ❓ **Your call:** #1266 lists Jobs, a table view, refresh, "live" event binding, and an import toast. This PR does the first three and the toast. Live binding is left out because it needs the WebSocket precedent in #1261 (`human required`), and the issue's "or invoking a job as a result of another operation?" is an open question, so only CSV imports get the toast. Hence `Refs`, not `Closes`. Reversible: either can follow as its own PR.

## 💡 Solution

**A Jobs tab on the instance Status page.** It lists jobs started in the selected window, newest first, via `search_jobs_by_start_date`, with status, type, start time, duration, user and message. Each row expands to show the full record. Harper sometimes records a job's message as an object (a refused bulk load's permission report), so the [expanded row](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-bee36c2513390346b9d6e936ad4a24d03f64ade868fd58ed01f204ca1c2fc927R203) renders it as JSON text, never `[object Object]`. The tab:

- **Has its own poll.** It [keys on the window *width*](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-3cb185084f83ffe2fa88c73bd954d1f124eb5299e7eaf46f105d4f5c8e42714fR64) and computes the bounds when it fetches, so each poll slides the same query forward. It polls on the page's existing `refresh` interval [through `pollUnlessForbidden`](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-3cb185084f83ffe2fa88c73bd954d1f124eb5299e7eaf46f105d4f5c8e42714fR66), so a 403 stops the timer, and shares the existing `range` parameter.
- **Sits outside the analytics gate.** It reads no `get_analytics`, so it joins Overview in [`ANALYTICS_FREE_TABS`](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-326c18f5ba8c0f12968351140b2c3fa0d1cd2ef63a6dac99b93a82959ca367dfR45): a failed analytics probe [no longer redirects](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-326c18f5ba8c0f12968351140b2c3fa0d1cd2ef63a6dac99b93a82959ca367dfR187) `?tab=jobs` to Overview or swaps in the "analytics unavailable" notice.
- **Runs only for roles that can list jobs.** `search_jobs_by_start_date` is super_user-only in Harper on every version (harper `utility/operation_authorization.ts`; `release_4.7.0` `:217`). [`canListJobs`](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-05beb14af6746361e7f796b97a7e9e93c125c03c41a9b179652abd8b31994710R18) lets any other role see an explanation, and the query [stays disabled](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-bee36c2513390346b9d6e936ad4a24d03f64ade868fd58ed01f204ca1c2fc927R51), so no request is sent.
- **Bounds what it fetches and renders.** The operation takes no limit or cursor, so every poll re-fetches the whole window. Jobs therefore [offers windows up to 7 days](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-bee36c2513390346b9d6e936ad4a24d03f64ade868fd58ed01f204ca1c2fc927R32) (a `range=30d` link reads as 7 days there), [renders at most the 200 newest rows](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-bee36c2513390346b9d6e936ad4a24d03f64ade868fd58ed01f204ca1c2fc927R113), and says how many it held back.
- **Says it is per-node on a cluster.** `hdb_job` is in harper's `NON_REPLICATING_SYSTEM_TABLES`, so a cluster route shows the jobs of whichever node its request reached, and [the copy says so](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-bee36c2513390346b9d6e936ad4a24d03f64ade868fd58ed01f204ca1c2fc927R65).

**CSV imports show their job in a toast.** `waitForJob` reports every polled job through a [new `onUpdate`](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-12bde07e0211231edd2715c8cc4cc48cf42adfeaa36d8274a611748ad70bf36dR44), and the import shows a [loading toast](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-11d142ccce3ef88a1d3104a42b2ec9b6f81068dae73df8604de2faab65658f9fR12) — `Queued · 2s · job <id>`, then `Running · 14s · job <id>` — that turns into the result when the load finishes. Harper writes nothing to a job between starting it and finishing it, so the toast shows state and elapsed time, not a percentage. The toast is settled from [`useImportDataMutation`'s own `onSuccess`/`onError`](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-3065d40433a02990e9e202237a023bd6676b4eae8c81a2bb346667f7fdc54f88R128), so it still settles if the modal unmounts mid-import, which the old `mutate(…, { onSuccess })` toast did not. A throw from any listener callback — [per poll](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-12bde07e0211231edd2715c8cc4cc48cf42adfeaa36d8274a611748ad70bf36dR66), [success or error](https://github.com/HarperFast/studio/pull/1880/changes?w=1#diff-3065d40433a02990e9e202237a023bd6676b4eae8c81a2bb346667f7fdc54f88R117) — is caught and logged, so it cannot turn a load Harper finished into a reported failure.

The change stays self-contained to avoid kylebernhardy's open Status work (#1456, #1458, #1459, #1460, #1485, #1486, #1516, #1517): new files under `status/jobs/`, plus one tab registration and a shared tab predicate in `StatusTabs.tsx` and `statusSearch.ts`.

## ⚖️ Alternatives

The planning review returned `better-alternative-exists`, and the graded leg kept three of its points as majors through round 2. Gemini ruled all three of those overrulings factually right. Here is how each point was resolved:

- **Adopted:** cap the window at 7 days and the rendered rows at 200, keep the tab outside the analytics gate with one predicate used for the redirect, picker, hint and body, settle the toast from mutation-level callbacks, isolate every listener callback, and gate on super_user rather than trusting an allowlist grant.
- **Overruled — a server-side bound before shipping.** Harper creates an `hdb_job` row only in `executeJob` (harper `server/serverHelpers/serverUtilities.ts`), once per job-type operations call, and each job starts its own worker thread (`jobRunner.ts` `launchJobThread`). So the graded leg's "100 jobs a minute" history is not a workload Harper sustains. The 7-day cap and the 200-row render cap bound the rest.
- **Overruled — fan out per cluster member.** Studio has no per-member client on a cluster route. The Fabric Connect proxy also routes cluster operations to the first `RUNNING` instance (central-manager `src/resources/cluster/Cluster.js` `handleProxiedOperation`), so the answering node is stable there. The node-scope copy covers the rest.
- **Overruled — extract a generic `StatusTimeControls` from `TimeRangePicker`.** #1456 (custom time range and brush/zoom) is about to reshape that component. Jobs uses the same `TIME_PRESETS`/`REFRESH_OPTIONS` and URL params in its own small toolbar instead.
- **Overruled — widen `HarperJob.message` and normalize it in `waitForJob`/`importData` here.** #1868 (open) makes exactly that change in exactly those lines. A COMPLETE job's message is always a string (harper `jobProcess.ts`), so the success toast never receives an object; only the ERROR path's `[object Object]` remains, and #1868 fixes it.
- **Overruled — stop the StatusTabs refresh tick while Jobs is open.** Overview relies on the tick to clear a failed panel, and stopping it on Jobs would leave the charts on a stale window when the user switches back. It also touches refresh logic owned by #1516/#1517. The cost is one re-render per refresh interval (at least 30s).

> ❓ **Your call:** Who can list jobs? Chosen: super_user, plus any allowlist grant the role editor's catalog does not call inert (`isGrantGateInert`), so the tab and the role editor always agree. Today the catalo

author: dawnop
body:
An erased Int or Bool in the native backend (a type variable, a closure capture, argument or result, a cell, an effect operation) used to be a 16-byte heap box. This series makes the word itself carry the value: bit 0 set, value above it. Ints outside 63 bits (31 on wasm32) still fall back to the heap box, so Int stays 64-bit wrapping. Bool is always an immediate. Float, Unit and references are unchanged.

Commits:
- Design doc for tagged immediates, with the tag-check matrix.
- GPU launch reads its Array[Int] arguments through `dawn_peek_int` (the only GPU-section line touched; moves the tile inputs digest).
- Runtime and emitter: every point that reads a header or a box checks the tag first (dup/drop plain and inline, work list push, is_unique, two kind checks, Int reads, bulk readers); `unbox_expr` emits `dawn_peek_int`/`dawn_peek_bool`.
- `scripts/imm-contract`: 16 mutants, one per tag-check point, each red in plain, inline-RC, ASan and inline+ASan builds; a 31-bit narrowed run; JVM vs native transcript equality on `imm.dawn`; an emitter mutant.
- wasm32 run of `imm.dawn` with rc-balance 0, plus a ledger mutant.
- The tag check is spelled `(p == NULL) | dawn_is_imm(p)` (one branch); the two-branch form cost 4 percent on rbtree/binarytrees.
- Measurements and the three tile ledgers (sm_86, sm_90, sm_100) at inputs 5fa7e4f98aff.

Measurements (same emitted C, base runtime/emitter vs new, best of 5 to 11 interleaved):
- counter 3.240 s -> 1.643 s
- nqueens-cons 0.866 -> 0.763, nqueens-pvec 3.546 -> 3.378
- native compiler emitting itself 9.301 -> 8.822 s
- rbtree, binarytrees, cfold, gen-sum, rbtree-ck-pvec within 1.5 percent
- deriv 1.04 to 1.05 slower on two of three runs (a third read 1.007)

CI: the immediates contract adds about 70 s to contracts-2.

Gate-Budget(push-total): 19693s -> 19763s is declared in the runtime commit.

selfhost-prev-diff agrees with v0.86.0 on every emit label; no label covers native C.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Full audit of the public site, admin panel, and API. These fixes are already live on bainslamusic.com; a backup was taken before deploying.

**Security**
- Removed `api/deploy-helper.php` and `api/fix-permissions.php`. Any request to deploy-helper (even a HEAD) rewrote `api/config.php` with the public `admin / Bainsla@2024` login. On the server, these two files and a publicly downloadable `config.php.bak.*` were moved to `/root/bainsla-quarantine-20261011/`, not deleted.
- Admin credentials are no longer in git. `config.php` now exposes `adminCredentialsValid($user, $pass)`, which reads server-only `data/admin.json` = `{"user": ..., "pass_hash": password_hash(...)}`. Nginx already denies `/data/`, and `data/admin.json` is in `.gitignore`. `login.php` is now POST-only and calls `session_regenerate_id(true)`. A failed login waits about 0.8 s.
- The 401 response no longer includes `session_id`.
- Nginx (server only, not in this repo) now returns 404 for `*.bak`, `*.oldsrv`, `*.orig`, `*.tmpN` and dotfiles.
- Old passwords removed from README.md and HANDOFF.md.

**Data safety**
- `readData()` used to return `[]` when it couldn't parse `content.json`. If it read a half-written file, the next save would wipe all site content. It now returns a 503 instead.
- `writeData()` and the three cron workers (`atomicWriteJson`) now write to a temp file and then `rename()` it into place, so a reader never sees a half-written file.

**Bugs**
- Home page scrolled sideways (the page was about 2.9k px wide) because `.swiper{overflow:visible}` let the label/artist/album sliders spill past the screen edge. Fixed by clipping those sections horizontally.
- Footer social icons with no URL set pointed to `#`; they are now hidden.
- Contact form: fields are trimmed and length-capped, and an invalid email returns a 400 with a message that the form shows to the user.

Verified locally and on live:
- Every admin section renders and its Add modal opens with no JS errors.
- Add, edit and delete work.
- Chunked 20 MB upload works.
- SVG files containing script are rejected.
- Public routes, sitemap and 404 pages work.
- The old helper login is rejected and the real login works.
- Cron workers write valid JSON and the file stays owned by www-data.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ab8218cb3f00450889f5c6b69aed9f89
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/ab8218cb3f00450889f5c6b69aed9f89?variant=devin

author: andygout
body:
This PR accommodates `Time` instances having `fromDate` and `toDate` values that are BCE (Before the Common Era). E.g. Julius Caesar was assassinated on 15 Mar 44 BCE. JavaScript represents BCE dates as historical dates whereas Neo4j represents them as astronomical dates, e.g. | Historical | Astronomical | | ---------- | ------------ | | 3 BCE | -2 | | 2 BCE | -1 | | 1 BCE | 0 | | 1 CE | 1 | | 2 CE | 2 | | 3 CE | 3 | Therefore when inserting BCE dates values into the database they must be converted from historical to astronomical. And when retrieving them from the database they must be converted back from astronomical to historical. See architectural diagrams below that describe which conversions take place and where. --- The checks for ensuring a date is valid have also changed to allow BCE dates for `Time` instance `fromDate` and `toDate` values but not for `Production` or `Review` instance dates as it is unlikely there will be any recorded BCE dates for those (or at least is something that doesn't need to be worried about for some time). --- The checks for ensuring corresponding start and end dates are in chronological order must now also consider whether a date is BCE, e.g. (unlikely but used for the purposes of demonstration) - 1st January 1950 CE and 31st January 1949 CE is not chronological - 1st January 1950 BCE and 31st January 1949 CE is chronological --- Some other interesting JavaScript behaviour demonstrates why construction of earlier dates (not quite BCE but still closer to that time) must be handled very specifically (e.g. see `src/lib/is-chronological.js`), as using the most obvious aproach doesn't always return the expected value: ```js new Date("44-03-14"); // -> “Mon Mar 14 2044” ❌ new Date(44, 2, 14); // -> Tue Mar 14 1944 ❌ new Date("0044-03-14"); // -> “Sun Mar 13 0044” ✅ new Date("79-03-14"); // -> Wed Mar 14 1979 ❌ new Date(79, 2, 14); // -> Wed Mar 14 1979 ❌ new Date("0079-03-14"); // -> Mon Mar 13 0079 ✅ ``` The leading zeroes are necessary to prevent JavaScript from inferring a different century closer to the current one (I'm not sure why sometimes it opts for the 20th century and in other cases the 21st century). --- ### Assassination of Julius Caesar (15th March 44 BCE) Here is an example of how the transmission and retrieval of a BCE date value would be handled from the client-side of the CMS to the Neo4j database persistence layer. ```mermaid --- config: theme: base themeVariables: actorBkg: "#E6E6E6" actorBorder: "#808080" actorTextColor: "#000000" --- sequenceDiagram %% Components and grouping boxes actor CLIENT as Client box rgb(245, 223, 238) CMS participant DRAMATIS_CMS as dramatis-cms end box rgb(218, 231, 242) API participant DRAMATIS_API as dramatis-api end box rgb(223, 240, 216) Database participant NEO4J_DATABASE as Neo4j database end %% Relationships Note over CLIENT: dramatis-cms
client-side code
converts
"0044-03-15"
isBce: true
to:
"-0044-03-15" CLIENT ->> DRAMATIS_CMS: "-0044-03-15" DRAMATIS_CMS ->> DRAMATIS_API: "-0044-03-15" Note over DRAMATIS_API: Converts
"-0044-03-15" (historical date)
to
"-0043-03-15" (astronomical date) DRAMATIS_API ->> NEO4J_DATABASE: "-0043-03-15" NEO4J_DATABASE -->> DRAMATIS_API: Date {
year: Integer: { low: -43, high: -1 }
month: Integer: { low: 3, high: 0 }
day: Integer: { low: 15, high: 0 }
} Note over DRAMATIS_API: Converts
"-0043-03-15" (astronomical date)
to
"-0044-03-15" (historical date) DRAMATIS_API -->> DRAMATIS_CMS: "-0044-03-15" DRAMATIS_CMS -->> CLIENT: "-0044-03-15" Note over CLIENT: dramatis-cms
client-side code
converts
"-0044-03-15"
to:
"0044-03-15"
isBce: true ``` --- ### Crucifixion of Jesus Christ (3rd April 33 CE) Here is an equivalent diagram for a CE date. ```mermaid --- config: theme: base themeVariables: actorBkg: "#E6E6E6" actorBorder: "#808080" actorTextColor: "#000000" --- sequenceDiagram %% Components and grouping boxes actor CLIENT as Client box rgb(245, 223, 238) CMS participant DRAMATIS_CMS as dramatis-cms end box rgb(218, 231, 242) API participant DRAMATIS_API as dramatis-api end box rgb(223, 240, 216) Database participant NEO4J_DATABASE as Neo4j database end %% Relationships Note over CLIENT: dramatis-cms
client-side code
converts
"0033-04-03"
isBce: false
to:
"0033-04-03" CLIENT ->> DRAMATIS_CMS: "0033-04-03" DRAMATIS_CMS ->> DRAMATIS_API: "0033-04-03" DRAMATIS_API ->> NEO4J_DATABASE: "0033-04-03" NEO4J_DATABASE -->> DRAMATIS_API: Date {
year: Integer: { low: 33, high: 0 }
month: Integer: { low: 4, high: 0 }
day: Integer: { low: 3, high: 0 }
} DRAMATIS_API -->> DRAMATIS_CMS: "0033-04-03" DRAMATIS_CMS -->> CLIENT: "0033-04-03" Note over CLIENT: dramatis-cms
client-side code
converts
"0033-04-03"
to:
"0033-04-03"
isBce: false ``` --- This is how respective BCE and CE dates will appear in the CMS (changes applied in this PR: https://github.com/andygout/dramatis-cms/pull/316): ### 44 BCE (time) ### 1960s (CE) (time) --- There are no changes required for the presentation of BCE dates in the user-facing apps ([dramatis-spa](https://github.com/andygout/dramatis-spa) and [dramatis-ssr](https://github.com/andygout/dramatis-ssr)) because currently the only dates that have the potential to be BCE dates are `Time` instance `fromDate` and `toDate` values and these are not surfaced in the UI — they are values used exclusively for the purposes of ordering results (in the `/times` list and also for a `/times/{timeUuid}` instance show page for its sur-times and sub-times).

## Summary

1. **Fixed Modal Input Focus Bug (`components/ui/Modal.tsx`)**
   - Stabilized `onClose` and `dismissOnEscape` via refs in `Modal.tsx` so parent state updates while typing in inputs never re-run the initial focus effect or steal focus away from active inputs.

2. **Remove manual CSV ledger export from Settings and delete `/api/export`**
   - Keeps backup (`pg_dump` via `.github/workflows/backup.yml`) distinct from ad-hoc Supabase Dashboard exports (`Table Editor → Export to CSV`).
   - Prevents RA 10173 unencrypted local-file exposure (`workers`, `clients`, `attendance`, `payroll`, `advances`).
   - Deletes `app/api/export/route.ts` and `lib/export/csv.ts` and removes `ledgerExport` from `lib/rateLimit.ts`.
   - Updates `tests/audit-log.test.ts` and `docs/SECURITY.md` (§1, §7, §10).

3. **Founder Account Management, First-Sign-In Password Setup & Supervisor Payroll Link (`/users`, `/api/users`, `/api/auth/setup-password`)**
   - Founders can provision new `founder` or `supervisor` accounts with a real email address, assign Supervisor project sites at creation time, and generate a strong temporary password (`lib/users/admin.ts`, `app/api/users/route.ts`).
   - **Supervisor Attendance & Salary Inclusion:** When provisioning or managing a Site Supervisor, Founders can check **"Include Supervisor in Daily Attendance & Payroll Engine"** with their daily rate (`₱/day`) and contact number, automatically maintaining a 1:1 linked `public.workers` row (`id = user.id`).
   - **Zero Button Clutter:** Each account card on `/users` has a single **`Manage`** button that opens one unified modal for role, project sites, payroll inclusion, temporary password reset, and safe account removal.

4. **Single Canonical Workforce Directory Tab (`/attendance`, `/api/workers`)**
   - Added a 3rd tab (`Workforce`) inside the existing `/attendance` segmented tab bar (`Daily Roster` · `Logs & History` · `Workforce`) so both Founders and Supervisors can register newly arrived site workers (`POST /api/workers`) and Founders can edit craft/pay rates or toggle active status in one clean place without extra buttons on Payroll or Advances.
   - Supervisors appear at the top of the Daily Roster badged as `Supervisor`, and self-logged supervisor attendance is badged as `Supervisor Self-Attendance` in `Logs & History`.

5. **Project Site Filters across Attendance, Bale/Advances, and Payroll Engine**
   - `app/advances/page.tsx`: Added Project Site filter dropdown and scoped summary cards to the active project filter.
   - `app/attendance/page.tsx`: Added Project Site, Status, Date, and Search filters to the **Logs & History** tab.
   - `app/payroll/page.tsx` & `lib/data/store.tsx`: Added Project Site filter dropdown, project site badges on payroll rows and printable payslips, and a Project Site Scope selector in the **Compute Weekly / Bi-Monthly Payroll** modal.

body:
## Summary

First, backend safety slice of #147 — **does not close the issue**.

- Accept native location only after root/session/turn validation; rejected/retired-turn deliveries cannot move it. Verified session replacement/continuation publishes the new location atomically with lifecycle and signal health.
- Keep main-only report provenance/time and explicit current-session versus last-reported evidence. Completed/idle turns, native session boundaries, lifecycle loss and elapsed time do not prove vacancy; agent retirement/exit or removal from the live terminal table ends observed occupancy.
- Add authenticated observed containment to main-owned terminal usage without changing cwd, checkout launch binding, filesystem/Git authorization or MCP grants. Wire direct release IPC, reconciliation/release, prune, local Git inspection/removal, equivalent-host SSH activity and isolated-checkout transaction counts (including services).
- Recheck local occupancy after asynchronous Git preflight immediately before move dispatch; unknown local directories fail closed. SSH desktop cwd is excluded from local Git activity.
- Document the contract and verification limits. Isolate unrelated OpenCode CLI discovery in the Claude/Pi real-history fixture: its timeouts also reproduced on unchanged `e64083c` with the locally installed CLI.

## Tests

`npm run validate` passed: branding → lint → typecheck → Fallow → security-check → build → **385 files / 7,851 tests**.

Focused regressions cover accepted/rejected location provenance, atomic session transitions, repeat-report freshness, launch-versus-observed disagreement, idle/boundary/lifecycle-loss/exit behavior, unregistered and missing paths, local symlinks, SSH host isolation/equivalent targets, direct release IPC, service/agent lifecycle occupancy, and real-Git inspection/removal including a location report arriving during preflight.

## Boundaries / follow-up

- No new renderer selection behavior, Explorer decorations/poller, MCP fields or relocation grants. #147 B/C and remaining provider/UI regression work stay open.
- Tests prove common-layer contracts, real local Git behavior and mocked SSH coordinator behavior, **not live native multi-harness/SSH smoke**.
- Reports arriving after destructive host dispatch, unreported shell/tool directory changes and remote symlink spellings not canonicalized by the provider remain observational limitations. Existing reservations, dirty-file/branch checks and remote recovery journals are retained.

## Confirmed production failure
DEX v16 r4 smoke run #38118224710 deployed 32 contracts, reached Stage 1 value-pool discovery and actor funding at 06:35 UTC, then hung until its 90-minute deadline at 07:59 UTC. No Stage 5 telemetry ever ran. Stage 1 was scheduling all token×holder×spender ERC20 and Permit2 approvals as individually mined fork transactions.

## Repair
- After proving each ERC20 or Permit2 allowance mapping's exact storage slot against the contract's live read method, use Anvil's temporary fork-state `anvil_setStorageAt` to set the intended allowance; verify each getter after writing. Always restore test probes and use the original transaction approval path for unsupported/failed verification. Keep evidence of every mutation and fallback transaction.
- Preserve actor funding, approved spender set, Permit2 allowance amounts/expirations and the 300-call smoke acceptance threshold. Add Solidity and Vyper-layout tests for actual allowance getter values and accelerated approval counts.
- Restrict smoke simulation process to 15 minutes within a 20-minute job, capture stdout/stderr, retain partial deployment/fixture/raw telemetry artifacts on failure, fix the fixture evidence path, and enforce Stage 5 observation-count reconciliation.
- Incorporate the newly merged Stage 1 discovery/RPC/Medusa repair from PR #597, preserving its parallel discovery and deadlines.

Validation: [V7 qualification #38123805458](https://github.com/CurveYield2/Contract-Automation/actions/runs/38123805458) **PASS**, including all Node tests and repository static checks. author: knightniwrem
body: Refs #161. **Stage (d)**: the shared-behavior matrix, as a table-driven test that runs per chat type over #169's shared services. Only test code changes. ## Summary - **New: `tests/shared_chat_behavior_test.ts`.** Each row of `SHARED_BEHAVIORS` is one behavior that private chats and supergroups share, with the chat types it applies to. Every row runs once for each of those chat types, through a session built by `buildSessionServices()` on the production root. - **The subject.** `createSharedChatSubject(chatType)` puts Ada and a bot in one chat of the given type: - a private chat that Ada started; - or a supergroup that Ada owns and the bot is a member of. It gives each row the same entry points of the shared `MessageSendingService` and `MessageEditingService` for either chat type. It also gives the ID the chat's members address a message by, and Ada's view of the chat's history. The clock is test-controlled. - **20 new tests**: 10 behaviors × 2 chat types. ## The matrix "Before" is where each behavior was tested before this PR. | Shared behavior | Before | Now | | --- | --- | --- | | A bot's text is trimmed, has its commands marked, and is dated by the session | private (service test) | both, here | | A bot's text is limited by characters, and a refused text is not stored | private | both, here | | An account's text is trimmed and has its command marked; blank text is refused | private; supergroup trimming only | both, here | | A bot's inline keyboard holds callback data of up to 64 bytes | private | both, here | | A bot's text edit is dated, recomputes entities and drops the keyboard | private | both, here | | Changed formatting alone is an edit; formatting that normalizes the same is not | private | both, here | | A keyboard edit keeps the text and its last content edit date | private | both, here | | A reply within the chat; a reply to a missing message is refused or sent without it | private; supergroup only the "without it" case | both, here | | An album is numbered in order and shares one album, or is refused whole | private; supergroup numbering only | both, here | | An account edits its own text, normalized again, but not the bot's message | private; supergroup only "own message" | both, here | | Failure order of sending, editing, deletion, pinning and pressing | both (`tests/http/message_*_test.ts`, `reply_interfaces_test.ts`) | unchanged | | Each observer's numbering of interleaved chats; a deleted message's ID is not reused | both (HTTP) | unchanged | | An edit reaches the bot only for an account's message; inline messages are edited by their inline bot | both (HTTP) | unchanged | | Pins and unpins reach the bot; a removed keyboard stops showing | both (HTTP) | unchanged | | A former participant is turned away before its message is looked up | both (HTTP) | unchanged | The HTTP scenarios in the last five rows already run per chat type through `tests/support/chat_type_scenarios.ts`, so they stay where they are. ## Design decisions - **Service level, on the root.** These are behaviors of the shared services. A root-backed session reaches them without HTTP, and its time sources are the test's, so a row can advance the clock to date an edit. - **One subject, two wirings.** The subject maps each entry point to that chat type's service methods. A row reads only what both chat types expose: results, the domain message, the chat's IDs and Ada's history. - **Chat-specific tests kept.** The private and supergroup service tests keep their cases. They also check things that differ between the chat types: message boxes, published events, permissions, and which messages a bot sees. Removing their overlapping assertions was out of scope. ## Tests and checks 1455 tests pass, 20 of them new. On `96ec0a7`, based on `1c0a810`, each of these passed with exit status 0: - `deno task fmt:check` - `deno task lint` - `deno task check` - `deno task test` - `deno task openapi:lint` - `deno task openapi:coverage` - `deno task architecture:check` ## What remains for #161 - Measuring the suite's runtime against the baseline under the same Deno and cache conditions. That is an acceptance criterion I haven't measured. - Whether the acceptance criteria are all met, which is the owner's call. This PR is `Refs`, not `Closes`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Implements stage (d) of #161: the shared-behavior matrix, a table-driven test that runs each behavior private chats and supergroups share once per chat type, through one root-backed session. Only test code changes. **The matrix** - Adds 20 tests in `tests/shared_chat_behavior_test.ts`: 10 behaviors × 2 chat types. - Covers behaviors previously checked in only one chat type's service test: text normalization, character and callback-data limits, bot text, formatting and keyboard edits, replies, albums, and an account's own edits. - The keyboard-edit row edits the text first, then checks that a later keyboard-only edit keeps that text edit's date, per the status quo pending #241. - HTTP scenarios already run the shared failure order, numbering and reply interfaces per chat type, so they stay in `tests/http/` and `reply_interfaces_test.ts`. **Design decisions** - `createSharedChatSubject(chatType)` places Ada and a bot in either a private chat or a supergroup Ada owns and maps the shared services' entry points to that chat type. - Rows run on the production root with a test-controlled clock, so an edit can be dated without HTTP. - Permissions, message numbering and which messages a bot sees remain in each chat type's own tests. Written for commit c0acd86afa8eacff0d2b1b6f25bb419d0ab3197f. Summary will update on new commits.

author: dominicboettger
body:
Refs #18 · standalone, off main.

## Why
Orbot alternates between a universal APK and per-ABI builds (17.9.7-BETA-1: universal only; 17.9.7-RC-1, 2026-10-09: arm64 only). The lock's universal entry disappears, an arm64 entry appears, and the rule "same packages and ABIs" made every such release a `review` issue - for a change phones never notice. Dob decided (2026-10-11) to let a *clean* change through.

## What
`apks/refresh-lock.sh`: `safe` also covers an app whose set of ABIs changed when
- it was in the lock before,
- an **arm64-v8a** build (the phones' ABI) is among the new entries,
- **every new versionCode is above every old one**,
- the **signer is the same**.

Removed entries are allowed only as part of such a change. Still `review`: an app that leaves the lock or loses its phone build, a version that goes back, a different signer. The emulator may lose a build this way, phones never do. The summary gets a "Builds per ABI changed" table saying for each app whether the change was clean. AGENTS.md (the one-exception section) and the workflow header say the same.

## Tests
`tests/refresh-lock.test.sh` (33 cases, 6 new):
- universal → newer arm64, same signer: **safe**, and listed in the summary;
- universal → x86_64 only: review;
- to an older arm64 build: review;
- under another signer: review;
- next to an app leaving the lock: review.

`make check` and `tests/lint.sh` green.

Note: today's scheduled refresh (05:17 UTC) still runs the old rule and will open a `lock-refresh` issue for Orbot; once this is merged, the next run takes the change itself and that issue can be closed.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Lock refreshes can now be committed automatically when an app switches between universal and per-ABI builds, provided the new builds include arm64 support, have higher version codes, and retain the same signer.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * ABI changes that involve older builds, a different signer, loss of arm64 support, or app removals are flagged for review rather than treated as safe.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified which lock refresh changes are eligible for automatic commits and which require review.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: c8m6
body:
## Summary

Puppet catalogs can lock root with a shadow value of `!` and disable the system SSH daemon, leaving the serial login unusable for administration. This branch adds numeric-root `node exec` and a real interactive VM `node shell` through the existing private VirtIO management service, and exposes the existing serial socket separately as `node console`.

Exec preserves literal argument vectors, streams stdout/stderr separately, forwards confirmed guest exits (including 255), and supports unlimited-by-default execution, explicit timeouts and confirmed process-group cancellation. VM shell uses a controlling PTY with resize, ANSI, job control, Ctrl+C/D/Z and terminal restoration. Eight private, instance-pinned slots isolate concurrent sessions. Container access uses native numeric-root runtime execution; its guest Ruby supervisor distinguishes native transport failures from guest completion. Diagnostic history is not persisted by default.

Destroy now reads safely interpretable ownership independently of operational inventory versions, guest layouts, release requirements and current project configuration. `destroy --project-path /former/control-repo` and the corresponding node command select a missing repository by its former absolute canonical Git root. Host/runtime cleanup continues independent owned deletions after failures, preserves unresolved evidence, remains idempotent and never requires guest access or a live Puppetserver. Deferred public certificate fingerprints protect subsequent hostname reuse.

The four pre-existing branch commits are preserved: effective native server environment timeout 0 with explicit project overrides retained, precise mount diagnostics, direct system-SSHD user access, and the SSH-independent VM management foundation. Existing performance changes from main remain intact.

## Related issues

No issue was supplied. This implements the requested Empeira diagnostic-access and version-independent recovery work.

## Validation

- Complete deterministic RSpec: 1,767 examples, 0 failures, 93 pending (optional platform/integration gates; no tests disabled).
- RuboCop with cache disabled: 429 files inspected, no offenses.
- Both application and module-installer lockfile audits: no vulnerabilities; current ruby-advisory-db commit a6847b0651a702488f5844081e848dd1ec9dbf1d.
- Real Docker diagnostics/recovery gate: container and QEMU/KVM, 2 examples, 0 failures.
- Real rootless Podman diagnostics/recovery gate: container and QEMU/KVM, 2 examples, 0 failures.
- Native gates ran on Linux inside WSL2 with isolated disposable projects. They verify Puppet-locked root, unusable/stopped SSHD, literal argv, separated output, exits 0/6/255/127, timeout recovery, interrupt cleanup with guest PID checks, real root PTYs, resize, fullscreen top, Ctrl+C/D/Z, concurrent VirtIO sessions, VM restart, serial access without the management service, missing server/repository and incompatible-inventory recovery.
- Deterministic ownership regressions cover partial deletion, foreign IDs, symlinks, unknown future resource fields, old/unknown layouts, active session guards, stable locks and deferred certificate proof.
- CLI help, executable Bash completion, generated Bash syntax and management shell startup syntax checked; final diff whitespace check passed.
- The manual provider/VM gates were not executed on native macOS/HVF or native Linux outside WSL2; hosted Ubuntu CI and Docker smoke are reported separately. Other optional integration suites were not activated for this change. No quantitative before/after performance benchmark was run; ordinary real Puppet catalogs completed successfully.

- GitHub PR CI on Ubuntu 24.04: required `test (3.4)`, `test (4.0)` and real Docker/OpenVox `smoke` all succeeded for bd438225e689511aede04e47798cc232aa36c408. The smoke verified a real Hiera catalog, idempotence, PuppetDB and cleanup.

## Compatibility and documentation

VM management layout 2 requires explicit destruction/recreation of existing incompatible VMs; no implicit migration is performed. VM `node shell` now opens a root PTY, while `node console` retains serial guest login and Ctrl+] detach. User-facing SSH remains independent. Normal lifecycle compatibility gates remain active.

Recovery keeps native ownership labels, observed and recorded instance IDs, QEMU monitor identity, private paths/sockets, symlink checks and workspace/VM locks. Unknown or unverifiable resources remain recorded and return an error. No network ports, privileged host services, proxy grants or egress changes are introduced by the diagnostic commands.

Container exec requires the installed agent's embedded Ruby interpreter for its guest cancellation receipt. Process-init containers use SSHD as PID 1: stopping it stops the whole container, so runtime diagnostics require it to remain running; systemd-init Podman containers and VMs were tested with SSH stopped. Eight bounded VM workers add memory overhead; internal bootstrap/Puppet deadlines remain unchanged.

README, architecture, node access/recovery, troubleshooting, development instructions, AGENTS.md and completion are updated. No new dependencies, proprietary artifacts or third-party code are included.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and follows the repository's AGENTS.md conventions.
- [x] Relevant tests, linting, and security checks passed, or limitations are documented above.
- [x] Affected documentation and examples are up to date.
- [x] No credentials, production data, private keys, or sensitive endpoints are included.
- [x] Any new third-party material has documented provenance and a compatible license.

author: jeonghok
body:
quality-gates 의 `/qg` 가 사람에게 내는 글(질문 · 선택지 · 완료 표 · 합성기 첫 줄 · 시작 배너 · setup 오류 줄 · README)이 쉬운 한국어로 바뀌고, 리뷰어 지적마다 사람이 읽을 한 문장 `plain:` 칸이 생겼다.

## Summary

- 파이프라인 문구: 질문 · 선택지 라벨 · 완료 표 칸 이름 · 모델이 그대로 내는 고정 문구를 한국어로 바꿨다. 프로그램이 읽는 글자는 그대로다 — 완료 표 결과 칸의 값(`finished` · `accepted with findings iter N` · `aborted iter N`), e2e 칸 값(`pass` · `fail` 등), 개념어 Retry.
- e2e 걷기 직후 게이트: qg v10 ④(#197)가 쓴 e2e 문면이 부르는 Fix-loop 선택지를 같은 새 라벨(「고치고 다시 돌기」 · 「지금 판정으로 끝내기」 · 「멈추기」)로 맞췄다. 한 실행에서 같은 질문이 두 이름으로 불리지 않는다.
- 합성기 첫 줄: 상태 문장이다. 지적 수, 버린 지적 수, 경고가 있는지와 그 경고가 판정을 막는지를 첫 줄이 말한다. 0 인 정상 집계는 뺐고, 판단에 필요한 0(처분 줄)과 기계가 읽는 줄(`**Findings:**` · `blocking:` · `optional:`)은 남겼다.
- 표 · 시작 배너 · setup 오류 줄: 쉬운 말이 앞이고 원래 영어 토큰은 괄호에 남긴다(기존 락이 그 토큰을 잰다).
- `plain:` 칸: 리뷰어 프롬프트와 agent 정의(보안 · 비평 · 반론 · 재비판), codex 프롬프트, prepare / qg-recritic 경로, 합성기 합치기(코드 · 비코드, 비코드 adversarial `new_findings` 포함)를 거쳐 표에 먼저 보인다. 표 칸을 깨는 `|` 는 이스케이프한다. 없거나 공백 · 비문자열이면 칸을 빼고 지적은 요약으로 남는다.
- README: 소개 문구 · 첫 문단 · `## 쓰는 법` 표 · 흐름 첫 문단이 「리뷰 → 판정 → (원하면) e2e 걷기 → PR 코멘트 하나」를 말한다. SKILL 제목 버전도 올렸다.
- 버전: quality-gates 12.2.0 · spec-distill 5.1.2 (`shared/codex/codex_findings_to_yaml.py` 가 spec-distill 에 심볼릭 링크라 같이 오른다).

### 계획이 정한 것

계획: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-plain-language-pr3-quality-gates.md`. 사용자 승인은 굵게 표시했다.

| 정한 것 | 번호 |
|---|---|
| 판단에 필요한 0(처분 줄 · 배관 손실 줄)과 기계가 읽는 0(`**Findings:** 0 …` · `blocking: 0`)은 남긴다. | R1 |
| 합성기 첫 줄은 판정과 무관한 상태 문장이다. 범위 · 각도 블록 앞의 쉬운 한 줄은 블록이 있을 때만 낸다. | R2 |
| 외부 추가 리뷰어 dispatch 프롬프트 리터럴에도 `plain` 칸을 더한다. 외부 agent 정의는 건드리지 않는다. | R3 |
| 오케스트레이터가 `findings.yaml` 을 쓸 때 `plain:` 을 그대로 싣고, 없으면 키를 뺀다. | R4 |
| Codex skip 안내 · degraded 줄 · kill switch 줄은 사유 토큰이 사람에게 그대로 보여야 해서 고치지 않는다. | R5 |
| 비코드 경로에는 화면 렌더러가 없어 `kept:` 에 `plain:` 이 남는지까지 재고, 최종 보고 틀에 한 줄을 더한다. | R7 |
| 첫 줄 · 시작 배너를 golden 대신 단언으로 고정한다(0 인 등급 되살리기 변이 포함). | R8 |
| setup 의 영어 오류 줄을 쉬운 말로 시작하게 하고 영어 토큰은 괄호에 둔다. **승인** | R10 |
| 합성기 첫 줄에 버린 지적 수를 붙여 「없는 것」과 「버린 것」이 다르게 읽히게 한다. **승인** | R12 |
| README 는 설계보다 좁게(첫 문단 · 쓰는 법 · 흐름 첫 문단 · 상태도 라벨) 고친다. **승인** | R13 |
| 처분 회계 소비자에 넣는 코드는 컴프리헨션 · `break` · `continue` 없이 쓴다. | R14 |
| 완료 표는 칸 이름만 한국어로, 결과 칸 값은 게시 펜스가 읽는 기계 토큰 그대로 둔다. **승인** | R15 |
| 합성기 첫 줄에 경고 유무와 판정을 막는지를 붙인다. **승인** | R16 |
| 소개 문구 · 첫 문단 · `/qg` 행은 #196 의 게시 모양(PR 코멘트 하나)에 맞춘다. **승인** | R17 |

### 리뷰 라운드가 더한 것

| 찾은 것 | 고친 것 |
|---|---|
| 완료 표 칸을 `Outcome` 에서 `결과` 로 바꿨는데 Publish 게이트가 여전히 「Outcome 값」을 불렀다(게시 판정이 모델 추측에 기댐). | 게이트와 펜스 자리표시자가 「결과 칸」을 부르게 하고, 락을 더했다. |
| Max-iter 질문 라벨과 분기 문장이 어긋나도 락이 못 잡았다. | 라벨 ↔ 분기 문장을 함께 재는 락을 더했다. |
| 버린 지적 줄(`dropped as malformed`)의 설명이 원뜻과 달랐다. | 「목록이어야 할 자리가 목록이 아니거나 …」로 바로잡았다(기계 토큰은 그대로). |
| 비코드 합치기가 참거짓만 봐서 공백 · 비문자열 `plain` 이 코드 경로와 다르게 통과했다. | 코드 경로와 같은 술어(`_has_plain`) 하나로 맞췄다. |
| 비코드 adversarial `new_findings` 의 `plain` 이 정리를 안 거쳐 공백 · 숫자가 남고, 흡수되면 사라졌다 (최종 리뷰 I1). | 같은 규칙으로 정리하고 흡수 시 물려받되 남는 쪽의 것은 덮어쓰지 않으며, 락을 더했다. |
| 최종 리뷰 minor 여섯 중 다섯과 머리글: 재비판자에게 `plain` 이 새는지 재는 락 보강, Max-iter 「멈추기」 설명 락, README 「Stop · 중단」 → 「멈추기 · 중단」, ⑤ 충돌 표 한 줄, CHANGELOG 정리, `## qg iter N` → `## qg 반복 N`. | 모두 고쳤다(머리글은 소비자 전수 확인 뒤). 여섯째는 아래 미룬 것. |

| 단계 | 결과 |

  - 기준선과 다른 실패 하나: `test_hook_output_schema.py` (이 워크트리 안에서만 실패하고, 깨끗한 클론에서는 건너뛴다).

⑤(`2026-10-08-qg-v10-c5-differential.md`)는 아직 머지 전이다. 이 PR 이 먼저 머지되면 ⑤ 가 맞출 것이다.

| ⑤ 가 맞출 것 | 이유 |
|---|---|
| `--plan` 제거 시 `setup-qg.sh` 의 오류 줄과 「계획 파일:」 줄, README `## 쓰는 법` 의 `/qg --plan` 행, `test_plain_synth_output.sh` · `test_plain_readme.sh` 의 `--plan` 단언 · 허용 목록 · 행 개수(6 → 5)를 함께 지운다. | 이 PR 이 그 줄들을 쉬운 말로 바꿨다. ⑤ 의 `test_removed_plan_arg.sh` 는 `Plan file:` 만 재서, 「계획 파일:」도 함께 재지 않으면 부재 단언이 공허해진다. |
| ⑤ Differential test 문면의 「(최종 판정 · Stop · 중단)」을 「(최종 판정 · 멈추기 · 중단)」으로 쓴다. | 이 PR 의 라벨이 「멈추기」다. |
| 개념 별칭 스윕에 나오는 새 락 둘의 `--plan` 글자는 허용 표에 더하지 않고 단언을 지워 없앤다. | 위 행과 같은 이유. |
| 버전을 머지 직전에 다시 정한다. | 먼저 머지되는 쪽이 이긴다. |

반대로 ⑤ 가 먼저 머지되면 이 계획의 Task 0 앵커 점검이 멈추고, 계획을 그 트리에 맞춰 다시 써야 한다.

author: emef2247
body:
## Summary

Add clock-aware pitch projection for native YM2151 (OPM) VGM
conversion to X68000 MDX.

VGM files recorded with an OPM clock other than 4 MHz can now
be converted for playback on the X68000's 4 MHz YM2151.

Pitch correction is performed at the target projection stage,
without modifying the original source State or Segments.

## Changes

- Add KC/KF pitch correction based on the ratio between the
  source OPM clock and the X68000 target clock.
- Support structured, legacy and register-oriented MDX output.
- Handle KC-only and KF-only updates while preserving source
  event ordering.
- Add configurable out-of-range pitch handling:
  - `clamp` (default): use the nearest representable KC/KF.
  - `error`: reject unrepresentable pitch values.
- Record original and projected KC/KF values, pitch errors,
  and clamping decisions in diagnostic output.
- Preserve PCM playback rates and sample data when OPM and PCM
  are used together.
- Improve target timing normalization for closely spaced events,
  including ordered allocation when nearest-tick rounding fails.
- Add documentation and regression tests for clock projection
  and timing correction.

## Validation

- Verified pitch projection using public and synthetic VGM
  fixtures with different OPM clock frequencies.
- Confirmed MDX compilation and projected-state replay
  consistency in automated tests.
- Confirmed successful conversion of all 15 GENPEI tracks.
- Confirmed native playback and MMDSP animation for all 15 tracks,
  with some remaining playback/display issues.

## Known Limitations

- Pitch correction uses nominal KC/KF frequency relationships.
  Acoustic equivalence on real YM2151 hardware has not been
  independently measured.
- Out-of-range pitches may be clamped, with the resulting pitch
  error reported.
- EG, LFO, noise and other clock-dependent behavior are not
  retimed.
- Declared VGM song loops are not yet transferred to MDX song
  loops.

Native listening identified two remaining issues:
- GENPEI07 ends unexpectedly while the sound continues.
- GENPEI10 briefly stops animating before recovering.

These will be investigated separately.

## Summary

author: codetrust2025-spec
body:
### fix(resume): a refused reading can be compared field by field once confirmed as the same candidate

Reported 11 Oct: a candidate saved under a short name ("Manu") uploaded a
resume in his full name, with another phone number. The server cannot tell it
is his -- the names do not match and the phone differs -- so it refuses to fill
anything, which is right. But since the Accept/Keep review, a refused reading
also offered no comparison at all, so the operator had no way to take the
email or name from a resume they knew to be the candidate's.

Now a refused reading (one that is a resume) shows the name it gives and a
"Same person — compare fields" button. Nothing is filled before or after the
click; the click opens the existing Existing -> Resume rows for name, phone,
email and technology, each to accept or keep, and only Save writes them --
through the usual guards (10-digit phone, another person's phone, shortened
name). The candidate's id, payments and history are untouched. A file that is
not a resume offers nothing.

author: wappensc-developer
body:
## Why (#31, B2)

A creator device that saw another device's control frame learned the membership change, but not that the frame's number was taken. Its next action reused that number, and its own engine refused it as a `sequence-conflict`. Every later action failed the same way, so the device was blocked for good.

## Change (TDSP 1.2, new CTL-18 in §7)

- **Number adoption:** an engine of the creator counts creator frames it did not issue as issued, but only after an **unbroken run**. Its control state and its snapshots therefore always hold every action up to its next number. The adopted number is persisted (CTL-12).
- **Gap guard:** while it holds a creator frame numbered above that run (a frame before it is missing), it issues nothing. Its actions are refused with `sequence-conflict` and nothing is sent; once the missing frame arrives, it continues.
- **Losing a race:** a pending frame of its own, whose number another device took, is given up and reported. This also applies **mid-retry**: each attempt checks first, so it is never sent.
- **Side effect, checked deliberately:** a creator restarted without its persisted state continues if it can read every frame it sent from 1 on. If a frame is missing (bounded window, no history), it stays blocked as before. The existing security test is split into these two cases. CTL-12 says so.
- **Still a limit of 1.x:** two devices that act before either has seen the other still issue different frames under one number (CTL-17). CTL-18 says so, and an application should let the person manage from one device at a time. The resolution is D4 in TDSP 2.0.

## Tests (`control.security.test.ts`, CI role)

Desktop and tablet of one creator:
- sequential actions on both devices;
- a pending frame on the tablet whose number the desktop used;
- the same while it is being retried;
- a gap, then the missing frame arriving;
- a creator restarted without state, with and without history.

Three mutations (no gap guard, retries that never stop, no adoption) are each caught.

## For the CI role

The wire lock shows exactly `[specification] "## 7. Control state"` and `[version] 1.1 → 1.2`. Accept with `pnpm run wire:lock -- --accept specification`, then approve. Otherwise `pnpm run ci` passes. CHANGELOG.md has a TDSP 1.2 section under "Unreleased". README, CONFORMANCE.md and `docs/versioning.md` name 1.2.

Part of #31

body:
## Change

Saved mutation plans can now carry human assessments through `review list/show/record`. Assessments and revisioned history live in a separate, bounded SQLite store; stale sources and identity mismatches cannot transfer an assessment to another candidate. Execution outcomes, scores, ranking and progress remain independent. An optional validated v4 JSON report supplies execution status.

Fixes #711.

## Validation

- Rust workspace after final review fixes: 2,730 passed, 23 ignored. Review unit tests: 21 passed.
- Python 3.14: 918 passed, 29 skipped. Strict workspace/all-target/all-feature Clippy, Rust format, Ruff and ty passed. cargo clean removed 49.6 GiB (about 177 GiB free afterward).
- Three Lean model properties proved; 168 generated cases agree with Rust. Local Lean 4.34.1 and [pinned Linux Lean 4.32.2 CI](https://github.com/HayaoSuzuki/hoimin/actions/runs/38137636373/job/114464978386) passed bounded model/proof builds, generation, freshness and sensitivity.
- Dedicated JSON schema validated against actual CLI output; CLI reference generation/check and seven generator tests passed.
- Design, plan, implementation and testing each have five recorded self-reviews. A fresh reviewer found four important issues, addressed in one fix pass: saved-output errors, concurrent record responses, page-size bounds, historical execution states.
- See [implementation evidence](docs/superpowers/reports/2026-10-11-issue-711-survivor-review.md) for limits and decisions.

Latest commit CI, bounded fuzz, contracts, randomized-order tests, dependency audit, and Windows/Linux/macOS package builds all passed. [CI run](https://github.com/HayaoSuzuki/hoimin/actions/runs/38137636373), [package builds](https://github.com/HayaoSuzuki/hoimin/actions/runs/38137636397). Linux cgroup hard-mode job was conditionally skipped.

## Compatibility and migration

Adds CLI commands, review JSON schema v1 and independent review-store schema v1. Existing run/report/plan/session formats and mutation defaults are unchanged. New distributed functionality raises the version floor to **0.4.0** across manifests and three lockfiles, including the separate fuzz workspace. Existing execution sessions require no migration. Review stores bind to the canonical project root and do not automatically migrate between checkouts; old source assessments become stale. This PR does not publish a release.

## OKF

- Consulted: `docs/knowledge/design/selection-plan-verify.md`, related session/report contracts, `docs/okf-workflow.md`.
- Updated: `docs/knowledge/design/survivor-review.md`, design/audit source catalogs and design index.
- Checks: 40-page YAML/reserved-file checks, source-ID uniqueness, local paths, index reachability, updated report hashes/footnotes.

- [x] Reviewed relevant OKF claims against their sources and the affected implementation.
- [x] Updated affected concepts, source references, and indexes, or explained why no update was needed.
- [x] Distinguished checks run for this change from historical audit results.

body:
## 概要

ログイン画面まわりの不具合を2つ直しました。

1. ログイン画面を開くと、`useClerk can only be used within the <ClerkProvider />` で画面が真っ白になる
2. Google でログイン・新規登録すると、戻り先が `http://sso-callback/?__clerk_db_jwt=...` になって DNS エラーになる

## 1. `@clerk/shared` の食い違い（4839184）

`@clerk/elements@0.22.23` が `@clerk/shared@2.22.1` を固定で使っていて、`@clerk/clerk-react` が使う `3.48.0` と Context が別物になっていました。

- `@clerk/elements` を `^0.24.20` に上げ、`@clerk/shared` を 3.48.0 の1つにまとめた
- README に、依存を変えたときは frontend の `node_modules` ボリュームを作り直す手順を追記

## 2. Google から戻る先の URL（f4ac5fe）

Clerk Elements は Next.js のルーター（`next/navigation`）を前提にしています。これまでは空実装のスタブで置き換えていたため、次のように動いていました。

- 現在地が `/` と推定され、戻り先が `"/" + "/sso-callback"` = `//sso-callback` になる
- `//` で始まるとホスト名と解釈され、`http://sso-callback/` へ飛ぶ

直したこと:

- `src/lib/next-stub.ts` を2つに分けた
  - `next-compat-router.ts`：これまでどおり「Pages Router ではない」と答える
  - `next-navigation.ts`：`useRouter` / `usePathname` / `useSearchParams` を React Router で実装。Clerk から絶対URLが来た場合、同一オリジンならパスに直して遷移する
- ログインを `/sign-in/*`、新規登録を `/sign-up/*` に載せた。`SignIn.Root` / `SignUp.Root` に `path` を渡し、タブの切り替えも URL の遷移に変えた。未ログインでほかのパスに来た場合は `/sign-in` へ
- `ClerkProvider` に `signInUrl` / `signUpUrl` を指定（ログインと新規登録の間の受け渡し用）
- ボット対策用に Captcha を置いた（新規登録の start、ログインの sso-callback）
- `docs/folder-structure.md` の `lib/` の説明を更新

## 確認

- [x] `npm ls @clerk/shared` が 3.48.0 の1つだけ（ホストとコンテナの両方）
- [x] `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint` / `npm run build`
- [x] compose の frontend で `/`・`/sign-in`・`/sign-up`・`/sign-in/sso-callback` が 200
- [x] ブラウザでログイン画面が表示される（1 の修正後に確認済み）
- [ ] Google で新規登録・ログインし、登録単語一覧まで進める
- [ ] メールアドレス＋パスワードで新規登録（確認コード）・ログインできる
