author: berndhueckstaedt
body:
## What

Whoever received a transfer answers it with an emoji, and the two the transfer is between see it with the booking: in their booking lists and at the transfer's bubble in their conversation (Bernd, 11.10.2026). The second slice of the reactions, after #4123. Six emoji are a press away — 👍 ❤️ 🙏 😊 🎉 🌱 — and a "+" behind them shows all forty-eight of the wallet's own choice. Server and wallet in one PR; a migration adds a table.

- **Only the recipient reacts.** The sender reads the reaction and cannot set, change or remove it.
- **One reaction a transfer.** Another emoji takes the place of the one before; the same one again takes it back.
- **Every transfer between two members of this community** — also one made from a link or a thank-you greeting, and a payment with a thank-you card (the till is its recipient).
- **No mail and nothing unread** for a reaction.
- **The sender sees it when their list or their conversation is read the next time** — not on the chat's beat.
- **Not across the border of a community:** a transfer from a member of another community gets no reaction — the wallet does not offer one, and the server refuses it (`OTHER_COMMUNITY`). Their server holds its own row of the transfer, and a reaction has no way there yet.

## Server

- **`transaction_reactions`** (migration 0159): one row for the reaction to a transfer, hung on the recipient's RECEIVE booking and unique by it. The reaction points at the booking, not the booking at the reaction: a booking is history, on which nothing is written again. The emoji is compared byte by byte (`utf8mb4_bin`), as in `chat_message_reactions`.
- **`setTransactionReaction(transactionId, emoji)`** sets, replaces or takes back (`emoji: null`) and answers the emoji that stands at the transfer then. The transfer is named by the id of the caller's OWN RECEIVE booking, and one read says whether it is that (`dbSelectReceivedTransferOfUser`): the sender — by their row or by the recipient's —, a third member, a creation and an id without a booking all get the same `UNKNOWN_TRANSFER`. Only the wallet's forty-eight are taken (the picklist of #4123), checked before anything is looked up. Ten reactions a request at most, over every alias.
- **`REACT_TO_TRANSACTION`**, a right of its own: every member has it, and an account whose address was never confirmed loses it with the rights that act outward (`RESTRICTED_WHILE_UNCONFIRMED`).
- **A booking carries** `reaction` and `canReact`. The reactions of a page are read in one query, and only for the page's transfers between two members of this server.
- **⛔ Which booking is shown which reaction** is decided by this server's own rows (`TransactionReaction.logic`): the sender's row gets a reaction only where the RECEIVE row it hangs on names that row back — a number on the sender's row alone shows nothing —, and both rows only where the counterparty is a member of this server by their `users` row (`foreign`), not by what the booking says of a community.
- **The log** gets the booking's id and whether a reaction was set or taken back, never the emoji; the request log leaves it out by the variable's name (`$emoji`, as for #4123), to which the wallet's document is held by a test.

## Wallet

- **In the booking list** the reaction stands behind the time — on the recipient's row as their own, with the rim of gold one's own reaction has in a conversation, and on the sender's row without it. Not a control.
- **⛔ In the line that is there already, not in a line of its own:** a reaction set in the opened row changes the height of no row (measured, below).
- **The opened row of what one received** has the choice a conversation has at a message, under the word "Reagieren": the six and "+". Only where the server says the member may (`canReact`); a press in it is not a press on the row. One's own reaction is the pressed one.
- **At the transfer's bubble in the conversation** the reaction stands in the foot line, and the bubble of what one received has a menu that holds the reactions alone — by the sign beside it on a computer, by a tap on a phone. Whether the member may react is the booking's word, not the thread's about its messages.
- **For the keyboard** that menu takes the focus itself when it opens: it has no entry to stand on, and on an emoji a second Enter would set a reaction nobody chose. Tab leads into the row.
- **One module for both places** (`useTransactionReactions`): what a press sends, one reaction at a time for a booking, and the word to every place that holds the booking — a reaction set in the conversation stands in the row of the list under the window at once, and the other way round.
- **A reaction that is answered while an older page of the thread is on its way waits for it**, as a reaction to a message does: the reader keeps their place.
- **`ChatReactionChoice`:** after a press among the forty-eight the row of six is back. Seen where the choice stays open, in the booking list; a menu closes with the press as before.
- **No new texts:** the reactions' own from #4123, in the ten languages.

## Known limits

- **The sender is not shown a reaction while their conversation is open:** the transfers of a conversation are read once, when it opens.
- **A row of the booking list cannot be opened with the keyboard** — as before this PR —, so the choice there is a pointer's and a finger's. In the conversation everything goes by the keyboard.
- **An account whose address was never confirmed** is offered the choice after its grace period too, and told that the reaction could not be saved: `canReact` speaks of the booking, not of the account. As for a reaction to a message.
- **At 280 px of width** a button of the row is 29 px wide and a square of the forty-eight 27 px.
- **From the forty-eight there is no way back to the six** but choosing one, or closing the row or the menu.
- **A transfer whose two rows do not name each other** — none that today's code writes — would take a reaction its sender is not shown.
- **Measured in Chrome on a Mac.** Not tried: a real phone, Windows, Firefox, a real screen reader.

## Checked

- `database`: lint, typecheck, build; 787 tests against MariaDB in the fork's CI.
- `backend`: lint, typecheck; 2,751 tests in the fork's CI (on the master before #4125) — among them the whole way against a database: both sides read the reaction, nobody else does, every refusal, an unconfirmed account.
- `frontend`: lint, stylelint, locales, build, 8,974 tests.
- **Measured against MariaDB 10.11 in the fork's CI, with 60,000 bookings and with 5 and 7,503 reactions:** the reactions of a page of 25 bookings are read through the unique key in 0.03 to 0.08 ms (100 bookings: 0.08 to 0.17 ms, two runs), each reacted booking by its primary key; the member's own RECEIVE booking and its sender are two reads by primary key.
- **The real bundle against a stand-in server, in a headless Chrome: 170 checks** — that a reaction moves no row of the list and no bubble of the thread (set, replaced, taken back, refused, at a greeting's booking, at a transfer with a picture), windows of 1025, 768, 500 and 360 px and phones from 430 × 800 down to 280 × 653, the menu at a transfer whole in the thread or over the page, the keyboard, what a screen reader gets, the list under an open conversation, a reaction answered while an older page loads, light and dark (the rim of one's own reaction at 3 : 1 or more), the ten languages.
- **90 one-line faults put into the code, each on its own: all caught by a test** — three of them only after a test was added or corrected. Three changes to comments, as controls, leave every test green.
- **A second reader of the code before this PR:** no way found for anybody but the recipient to write a reaction, nor for anybody but the two to read one. Built from the reading: a transfer's reaction waits while an older page is on its way, the row takes the list's word by the booking it is handed, a test for the unconfirmed account, and comments that

body:
Closes #113

Rule packs group 9 of the `rule-packs` change: `php` (tier 2, adapted from ECC), `laravel` and `wordpress` (tier 1). Both reviewers end `VERDICT: PASS` after 2 review rounds each (the initial run plus 2 re-runs).

## Deviations from the task text (all from deleting what the reviewers failed)

- `rules/php/` ships `patterns.md` and `security.md` only. Dropped after review: `style.md` (strict types and the PSR-12 closing-tag bullet were judged project-wide taste, B2) and `testing.md` (its globs `tests/**` and `*Test.php` also match Pest files, so its PHPUnit-only bullets were judged too wide, B8). Also dropped: the `readonly`, `JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR` and `Throwable` bullets (B2 or untraced). Listed in the README adaptation notes.
- `rules/laravel/` has 5 files: `structure.md`, `eloquent.md`, `security.md` plus `migrations.md` and `queues.md` (split out so each file is narrowly scoped, as the django pack did). Not authored: Pint (no narrowly scoped file where it applies) and thin-controller and policy bullets (judged generic or taste by Reviewer B). Form Requests, `$fillable`, eager loading, migrations, queues and config/env are covered.
- `rules/wordpress/` is scoped to `**/wp-content/**/*.php` only. The design inventory's wider globs (`{plugins,themes,mu-plugins}`, `class-*.php`, `functions.php`, `uninstall.php`, `wp-config.php`, `theme.json`/`block.json`) were each failed by Reviewer B (B8: they also match non-WordPress PHP). The README states the large remaining gap: most plugin and theme repositories have no `wp-content/` directory, so their files get only the `php` pack. Widening is a human decision between coverage and loading these rules on non-WordPress PHP.
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`: one line added (`php`) under Adapted packs.

## Review history

- Initial run: A FAIL (2 untraced: `json_decode` flag behaviour; upload type text only in user notes), B FAIL (about 24 MUST, mostly spacing in examples that used WordPress style inside php and laravel packs, formatting bullets in wordpress/standards, wide wordpress globs).
- Re-run 1: A FAIL (1 untraced `Throwable`; 1 untraced "CSRF only" clause), B FAIL (Pest scope of `testing.md`, one lazy-loading bullet, one B3 in wordpress/security, WordPress globs B8).
- Re-run 2: A PASS, B PASS.
- All edits between runs were rewrites or deletions; no new topics were added. Reviewer A notes three bullets that passed on the loosest reading: `wordpress/structure.md#1` ("4 to 5 letters"; the page says at least 4, recommends 5), `laravel/eloquent.md#2` (the page does not forbid `$guarded = []`) and `laravel/eloquent.md#5` (derived from the documented fact that mass updates and deletes do not fire model events). A human spot-check of those is cheap.
- The reviewers ran as Opus Agent-tool subagents; Reviewer A fetched pages with curl converted to text rather than WebFetch. All 34 cited URLs returned HTTP 200.

author: gertvandenberg
body:
## Summary

Plan only, no code: [`docs/plans/legal-entities.md`](https://github.com/weldsuite/weldsuite/blob/claude/legal-entities-sharing-plan-4eaffe/docs/plans/legal-entities.md).

Today the same company is stored three times: WeldBooks `entities`, WeldHR `hr_payroll_employers` (optionally linked to WeldBooks), and the legal fields on `workspace_settings`. The plan makes the legal entity a core platform object and lets each app attach its own settings.

Decisions taken with the owner (11 October 2026):

- **Core platform object** owned by app-api (Settings → Legal entities). WeldHR works without WeldBooks.
- UI name **Legal entities / Juridische entiteiten**.
- The **workspace business profile becomes the default legal entity**.
- **Bank accounts move to the legal entity** (the account itself). Feeds, reconciliation, the ledger link and checks stay WeldBooks features on top of it.
- **Every WeldHR employee gets an employing legal entity.**
- **Per-entity access is a later phase.** v1 sends every entity lookup through one resolver where that check will go.
- **Other apps: contract only.** Commerce, CRM quotes and WeldStash follow the documented rules later.

What the plan covers:

- **Target schema.** `entities` and `bank_accounts` keep their names and ids, so the ~45 WeldBooks `entity_id` columns stay valid. It adds `legal_entity_registrations` and the WeldBooks extension tables. WeldHR employers become payroll registrations under an entity.
- **Core service.** `@weldsuite/core-domain/legal-entities`, including the `legalEntityContext()` middleware.
- **API, permissions and events.** app-api routes, `legal_entities:*` permissions with a role backfill, and entity events.
- **App changes and UI.** The WeldBooks and WeldHR changes, and the platform UI.
- **Rollout.** Release 1 only adds tables and columns, with SQL backfills and a dry-run TypeScript backfill script. Release 2 drops the old columns. Also covers tests, risks and follow-ups.

It also records bugs found during research, which the plan fixes:

- books-api doesn't validate the entity header.
- The default entity flag gets out of sync.
- Deleting an entity doesn't check for data.
- The selected entity in the web app isn't scoped to the workspace.
- Payroll silently skips the journal when the employer isn't linked.

Migrations listed in the plan still need approval before they are generated.

## Test plan

- [ ] Review the plan; no code changes

author: cuppie24
body:
## Problem
The installer's Release build would not start on a Windows 10 PC:

> Порядковый номер 1104 не найден в библиотеке DLL …\CupIsland.exe
> (Ordinal 1104 not found in the DLL)

`DCompositionWaitForCompositorClock` is a **Windows 11** API, and `dcomp.lib` links it by ordinal (1104). With a static import, Windows 10's `dcomp.dll` has no such export, so Windows refuses to load the exe before any of our code runs. The import came from the original prototype's interaction-layer follower (decision 001), which only ever ran on Windows 11.

## Fix
- **`interaction_layer.cpp`:** the function is looked up **by name at runtime** (`LoadLibraryW` + `GetProcAddress`). The ordinal is never guessed, because on another build that number could be a different function.
  - **Windows 11:** behaves exactly as before.
  - **Windows 10** (or if the name isn't exported): the morph follower waits with `DwmFlush()`, which returns once per desktop composition, the same cadence. If `DwmFlush` returns instantly because nothing is being composed, the thread sleeps 4 ms instead of spinning.
  - The log records which clock is in use: `frame clock: compositor clock (Windows 11)` or `frame clock: DwmFlush (Windows 10 fallback)`.
- **`CMakeLists.txt`:** `dcomp` is no longer linked; nothing else used it.
- **Docs:** decision 001 explains the fallback. The README states that the app runs on Windows 10 1809+ and Windows 11.

The static VC++ runtime, so the installer doesn't need the VC++ Redistributable, is already on `main` (`CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY`).

## Test plan
- [x] Core tests pass on Linux.
- [x] MinGW compile with `-Wall -Wextra` and a link of the full current app. The import table no longer contains `dcomp.dll`. The remaining DLLs (kernel32, user32, advapi32, ole32, oleaut32, shell32, dwmapi, d3d11, d2d1, DWrite, dbghelp, WinRT api-sets, plus CoreMessaging in MSVC builds) all exist on Windows 10 1809.
- [ ] Windows 11 dev machine: clicking the pill mid-morph still lands, and the log says "compositor clock".
- [ ] Windows 10 PC with a rebuilt installer: the app starts, the log says "DwmFlush (Windows 10 fallback)", and morphs and clicks behave the same.
- [ ] `dumpbin /dependents build\windows\CupIsland.exe` lists no `dcomp.dll`, `MSVCP140.dll` or `VCRUNTIME140.dll`.

author: dunca
body:
## Problem

The menu bar shows a dash instead of the usage percentage even though the popover renders both windows fine.

## Cause

The quota endpoint now labels the plan token windows `CREDIT_LIMIT` instead of `TOKENS_LIMIT`. `headlinePercentage` filters on `TOKENS_LIMIT` only, finds no rows, and the tray falls back to "—". The popover doesn't filter, which is why it still looks normal.

## Fix

- `headlinePercentage` accepts both `TOKENS_LIMIT` and `CREDIT_LIMIT`, so older and newer API responses both feed the tray.
- `displayOrder` sorts `CREDIT_LIMIT` rows the same way `TOKENS_LIMIT` rows were sorted (5-hour first, then weekly), keeping the popover order the tray headline expects.

Tested on a Lite plan where both windows come back as `CREDIT_LIMIT`: the tray shows the 5-hour percentage again.

author: tehshortbus
body:
## What changes

The indexes the client builds from each game-data set are cheaper to build. Nothing is cached on disk: after the changes no index costs enough for a cache to pay for its staleness risk.

- **The indexes built during a set switch** (monster drops, room hazards, buff strips, room spells, item names, shop stock) went from about 99 ms to 37 ms of their own time, and allocate a third of what they did. Monster drops alone: 42 MB allocated down to 7 MB.
- **Monster spawns** (background): 188 MB allocated down to 24.5 MB, several times faster.
- **Quest steps for all quests**: roughly 240 ms and 495 MB down to 50–75 ms and 45 MB. That was a pause the first time the Quest tab opened.
- **The first item window and the first room hover** no longer read the whole Rooms table on the UI thread: the item "Used on" index and the room floor-item index are built in the background right after a set loads, while Rooms is still in memory. Rooms is handed back afterwards so it is not held longer.
- The program log gains a line per set load with how long the per-set indexes took.

How: references like `map/room` in a monster's Summoned By are found without a regex or an allocation per reference; numbered field names (`Abil-1` …) are built once instead of per row; a quest's steps skip text blocks and chains that do not contain the flag's digits; the spawn index drops its per-room sets.

## Proof nothing reads differently

- A dump of the full contents of 19 indexes plus four more (spell formulas, quest steps on both axes, the spawn index's answers, every monster's summon rooms) is identical before and after for both data sets, loaded fresh and after a switch, and for a hostile hand-built set; and again on this branch merged with main.
- The new reference scanner was compared with the regex it replaces over every such cell in both sets (about 360,000 references) and 1.5 million generated strings, including non-ASCII digits and overflowing numbers: no difference.
- The quest-step filter is shown sound for any input, not only the shipped data.

## Tests

- 23 new tests. No existing test changed.
- Full suite: 16,748 passing on top of 3.179.8.

## Found in review, not fixed here

Both pre-date this change and are being fixed separately: after a set is re-imported over itself, three indexes (spawns, item sources, floor items) keep answering from the old data until a real switch; and one warm-up parses Rooms a second time on every switch.

## Not verified

Not run in a live client. Timings were taken on a busy machine; allocation figures are exact.

author: muleyuck
body:
## Summary

Replace cargo-dist with a release-please–driven flow modeled on muleyuck/turnray, so releases need no PAT and no manual tag push.

- release-please creates the tag and the GitHub release (`skip-github-release: false`).
- Jobs chained with `needs` build 4 targets (aarch64/x86_64 × apple-darwin/unknown-linux-gnu) via the reusable `build-release.yml` (`--profile dist`, thin LTO kept), packed by `scripts/package.sh` with the archive layout cargo-dist used.
- `publish` attaches the archives, renders the formula from `packaging/jqc.rb.in` with `sed`, checks it with `brew style`, and pushes it to muleyuck/homebrew-tap with a GitHub App token, as turnray does with its cask.
- Removed: dist-workspace.toml, release.yml, mark-release-tagged.yml, cargo-dist in mise.toml and renovate.json.

## Behavior changes

- **The shell installer is no longer published.** It was downloaded 3 times across v0.1.0–v0.3.0. The README now lists Homebrew, `cargo install` and the release archives, and says v0.3.0 was the installer's last release. Installers attached to past releases keep working; `releases/latest/download/jqc-installer.sh` will 404 after the next release.
- The formula's `desc` is now "Query and edit JSON with comments (JSONC) using jq" (the old one fails brew's desc rules), and the cargo-dist leftovers in the formula (`BINARY_ALIASES`, `pkgshare`) are gone.

## Before merging

- [ ] Add the `TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID` and `TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets to this repo (the same App as turnray).

## After merging

- [ ] Delete the `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` secret.
- The new flow first runs on the next real release; the publish and tap push path cannot be exercised before then.

## Verification (local)

- `make` (via the pre-commit hook on each commit): pass
- `actionlint`: no findings
- The workflow's "Render the formula" step, run locally with v0.3.0's checksums: the four sha256 match the tap's current formula, `brew style`: no offenses
- The same step with one `.sha256` missing: fails on `sha256 ""`

body:
## 무엇
설계 `docs/design/stage0-gyms.md` §2 · §7 — 모임이 여럿이어도 소식 · 출석 이벤트 · 자랑방이 섞이지 않게.

| 화면 | 광장(모임 안 고름) | 모임을 고르면 | 닫힌 모임 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 소식 | 앱 전체 공지 + 공개 모임 소식 | 그 모임 + 앱 전체 공지 | 멤버만(404) |
| 출석 이벤트 | 앱 전체 + 공개 모임 + 내 모임 | 그 모임 + 앱 전체 | 멤버만. **집계는 내가 멤버인 모임 이벤트만** |
| 자랑방 | 전체 공개 + 친구 공개 + 내 글 | 그 모임에 올린 글(멤버는 "우리 모임만"도) | 404 |
| 프로그램 신청 | 앱 전체 | 그 모임 앞으로 | 앱 전체로 받음 |

- 헤더 "지금 보는 곳"(광장 · 내 모임 · 모임 찾기). 로그아웃하면 광장으로.
- 자랑방 공개 범위 **"우리 모임만"** 추가.
- 판단은 `GymScope`(모임 보기 · 올리기) · `BragAccess`(자랑방 보기) 한 곳씩.
- 관리자 소식 작성에서 모임 고르기.

A fifth command, `report`, beside `ping`, `sync`, `restart-chat` and `morning`.

- Standard output goes to a root-only `state/report.out` while the file runs (left out of backups, removed afterwards); standard error is thrown away.
- On status 0 the output reaches the log framed: `report: begin`, every line behind `report: | `, `report: end, N lines`; at most 200 lines of 200 characters, control characters removed, non-UTF-8 bytes dropped first. On any other status one line with the status, and nothing of the output.
- Outcomes: `ok`, `failed`, `not_configured`.

```text
[07:15:02] report: begin
[07:15:02] report: | first line
[07:15:02] report: end, 1 lines
[07:15:02] outcome: report=ok
```

author: gchahal1982
body:
Track 0 guard for the `all,strict` outage (#375): lane-04b GPU run 38123946016 had 0/19 aura3d captures ready, all failing with `generated program failed to compile`. Refs #1140, #839.

## What
New job in `qr-prd01-core`: **GLSL validate (C-02 every registered chunk compiles)**.
- `tests/qr/prd01/glsl/every-chunk-compiles.test.ts` loads every lane barrel. For each pass (forward/depth/distance/velocity) it composes a generated program for **each registered ShaderFeature alone**, and one with **all features together under `$ALL,strict`**, on a lit, textured base record.
- It validates the vertex and fragment stages with Khronos **glslangValidator** (GLSL ES 3.00), installed from `glslang-tools` via apt.
- Failures quote the offending generated line, so the CI log names the chunk.
- A missing validator **fails** the test. There is no skip, and the file sits outside `tests/qr/prd01/unit/`, so only this job runs it.
- Workflow paths now include `packages/engine/src/lanes/**`, so a change to any lane's chunk triggers the guard.

## This job is RED on main today, and that is the point
Locally on main 33bb88779 (glslang 16.6.0) it finds **three** real breaks, not one:

| Feature | Stage | glslang error | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prd03.indirectFraction` | frag | `'o_color' : undeclared identifier`. Its `fragment:end` body writes `o_color` and reads `a3dIndirectRadiance`, and the generator declares neither there. | lane 03, `qr/prd03-indirect-fraction` |
| `prd10.caustics` | frag | `'uniform' : not allowed in nested scope` (`uniform sampler2D u_causticAtlas;` spliced into a body hook) | lane 10, #1143 |
| `prd10.wind` | vert | `'a3dDeform' : no matching overloaded function found`. The `vertex:deform` chunk doesn't define the canonical `a3dDeform(inout vec4, inout vec3, inout vec4)`. | lane 10, #881 |

The job goes green once those three land. It is **not** labelled ready until then, and nothing is masked.

## Splice-side rejection under strict
I didn't add it. Reliably detecting undeclared identifiers in a chunk needs a GLSL symbol table, i.e. a parser, so it isn't cheap. This CI check makes the class of bug unmergeable instead. The existing C-36 `program-compile-failed` degradation (driver log appended by #1139) still covers anything that reaches runtime.

## Local
- `pnpm exec vitest run --root . tests/qr/prd01/glsl/every-chunk-compiles.test.ts`: 3 failing tests (forward alone, forward ALL, depth ALL), each naming exactly the rows above. 5 pass.
- eslint and actionlint: clean.

author: poyrazk
body:
Milestone: hunt #9 production test loop on rc.252 (production-us).

## Found on prod
`gregale deploy --safe` (balanced 1%→10%→50%→100%) of a revision that answers **500 to every request**, with steady 5 rps traffic:
- v2 held at 1% from 11:42 to 11:48:40 — **6.5 minutes of a 100%-failing revision serving customers**.
- meterd every 30 s: `insufficient request samples (candidate=9 … 17 … 19 stable=1853; need 20 each)` — every candidate request was a 5xx.
- At 20 samples it aborted correctly (`5xx regression (candidate 95.2%, stable 0.0%; 20/21 vs 0/1998)`) and restored v1 to 100%.
- The first-window 5xx rollback (ADR-625) never applies during a canary: `ListRollbackOn5xxCandidates` only selects completed releases at 100%.

At 1% the candidate collects ~0.6 req/min per 1 rps of app traffic, so the hold scales inversely with traffic (≈33 min at 1 rps).

## Fix
`EvaluateCircuitBreaker` aborts before the 20-request floor when the candidate is failing outright: ≥5 5xx (`CircuitBreakerMinDecisiveServerErrors`), ≥50% of its requests, the stable predecessor has a full sample (≥20), and the candidate's rate clears the existing 3× factor and +5 pp delta over stable. This is the same bar docs/deploys.md promises for `--safe` ("at least 5 … 5xx, at least half its requests"). A shared outage (stable failing too) or a stable sample below the floor keeps the normal hold.

Tests: six new cases in `TestEvaluateCircuitBreaker` (prod 5/5 case aborts; 5/10 aborts; 4/4, 5/12, failing-stable and no-stable-sample hold).

No architecture change; threshold aligns the canary with ADR-625's documented bar. No migrations.

author: uuriko
body:
ackWakes opened its own lock with raw BEGIN IMMEDIATE / SAVEPOINT and closed it with COMMIT / RELEASE / ROLLBACK. Durable Object SQLite rejects those statements, so POST /api/agent-heartbeats/ack returned 500 internal_error on Workers while every Node test passed. Run the fence check and the ack UPDATEs inside store.transaction(), which is BEGIN IMMEDIATE on Node, transactionSync on a Durable Object, and a join when the caller already holds one.

Test: ackWakes issues no raw transaction SQL (red before). Test helpers that build AgentHeartbeats on a bare db now pass a transaction runner.


External-authored patch that passed independent bug-hunt review. Blobs hash-verified: 4/4.

Original author: hunt (Uuriko commit). Stacked on #2734 (branch jill/wave500-g2-reland-ack-fencing). Fixes the cloudflare CI failure on #2734: ackWakes used raw BEGIN IMMEDIATE/SAVEPOINT/COMMIT, which Durable Object SQLite rejects, so POST /api/agent-heartbeats/ack returned 500 on Workers. It now runs inside store.transaction(). Merge order: #2734, this PR, #2758, #2761. Not run by the author: cloudflare checks or real Workers; the cloudflare CI job is the proof.

author: jeffglousher
body:
Deferred Q-Block2 requests can now retain multiple initial selectors. Completion validates the complete requested union before allocating a response identity, retaining body bytes or sending output. Overlapping selections emit each payload once; invalid ranges and unions exceeding ten payloads refuse without partial output and permit corrected recovery. More than ten initial selectors cannot produce a deferred handle.

The fixed selector array adds 48 inline bytes per configured deferred row on the measured x86_64 Windows layout. Zero-row layouts and allocated byte-area requests are unchanged; there is no heap growth. The original deadline, immutable completed body and metadata, protected request owner and FETCH identity remain intact. Partial I/O and admission-ACK failure retry without redispatching application work. Deferred Observe remains separate.

Pin independently reviewed companion `c4e18441d5ccbfec29c2ef53c5aefdd37f4eb740` ([PR53](https://github.com/jeffglousher/coaptic-validation/pull/53)) for nine named initial-selector proofs and the coap-rs-client DTLS03 loss campaign. That campaign covers baseline, six individual handshake-datagram losses, permanent final-flight loss refusal and fresh recovery. body:
## Summary

Closes #199 (remaining gap). The laya-guard HTTP 403 was only enforced on `/v1/messages` (`anthropic_messages.go:149`). The primary chat API paths — **`/v1/chat/completions`** (`handleChatCompletions`, `chat_handlers.go:122`) and **`/v1/completions`** (`handleCompletions`, `chat_handlers.go:1101`) — **skipped `decision.Rejected` entirely**, going straight to `RecordRouteDecision` → `checkBackendAccess` → `switch Backend`. Jailbreak/PII/harm prompts that the laya guard flagged as `Rejected` reached fusion-mlx on these paths.

## Fix

Add the same `Rejected → 403` short-circuit (mirror `anthropic_messages.go`) to both handlers, inserted between `Decide()` and `RecordRouteDecision`:

```go
if decision.Rejected {
    body := decision.RejectDetail
    if body == "" { body = `{"dimension":"unknown","score":0,"threshold":0}` }
    slog.Info("chat|completions request blocked by laya guard", "model", ..., "detail", body)
    http.Error(w, body, http.StatusForbidden)
    return
}
```

## Tests

`laya_guard_chat_test.go` (new): mock laya httptest server returning guard-blocked JSON (`jailbreak=1.0`) + real router Engine with laya classifier wired via `SetIntentClassifier`. Asserts both endpoints return 403 with `dimension=jailbreak` in body. Config snapshot injected into request context (middleware normally does this).

- `TestChatCompletions_LayaGuard403` — `/v1/chat/completions` → 403
- `TestCompletions_LayaGuard403` — `/v1/completions` → 403

## E2E verified (real gateway + fusion-mlx, laya warm)

```
/v1/chat/completions PII → 403 {"dimension":"jailbreak","score":1,"threshold":0.5} (33ms)
/v1/completions      PII → 403 {"dimension":"jailbreak","score":1,"threshold":0.5} (26ms)
/v1/chat/completions safe → 200
```

Log confirms both new paths fire:
```
INFO chat request blocked by laya guard model=... detail={"dimension":"jailbreak",...}
INFO completions request blocked by laya guard model=... detail={"dimension":"jailbreak",...}
```

## Related

- #199 — tracking issue for E2E 403 fix (PR#198 routing bugs + PR#200 AC7 latency + this PR chat/completions gap)
- fusion-guard #20 — laya-mlx guardrails (11/11 AC)

## Problem

The pattern `(?:\s*\.(?:\s+|$)){2,}` matches two or more consecutive sentence-ending periods, but combined with `\n+` and `;` alternatives, ordinary multi-sentence tickets (e.g. 'I cannot log in. Please help.') are split into multiple chunks, so `multi_issue` becomes True for nearly any ticket with two sentences. This forces escalation in decision_engine (multi_issue path) and lowers confidence, producing wrong results for valid single-issue tickets.

author: gorillanobakaa-dot
body:
## What was wrong (each read in `speaker_loudness_setup.py`)
- **Uninstall set the default output to the first `alsa_output` card** (`hardware_sink()`), not the one you had before. Anyone on HDMI or headphones ended up on the speakers. It also did this when nothing was installed.
- **`unarmor()` ran `sudo chattr -i` on every file**, armored or not, so it could ask for a password for nothing.
- **`sudo` had no `-n`.** Without a terminal (a launcher, an agent) it waited for a password nobody could type.
- **Uninstall called `systemctl` unguarded.** On PulseAudio without systemd, `subprocess.run` raises FileNotFoundError, so it stopped before cleaning `default.pa`.

## The fix
- **The output in use before the install is recorded** in `~/.config/speaker-loudness/previous-default-sink`. It is recorded once, so a reinstall doesn't record the compressor itself.
  - `--uninstall` and a failed verification put that output back, falling back to the speakers if it's gone.
  - Uninstall leaves the default alone when the compressor isn't the default.
- **`chattr -i` runs only on files that are actually immutable.** `lsattr` checks this without root.
- **`sudo` becomes `sudo -n` when there's no terminal.** It then stops with the exact command to run by hand.
- **`systemctl` is called only when it exists.**
- The README now describes all of this.

The compressor still drives the laptop speakers, as before; that's the tool's purpose.

## Proof
Tested in Gorilla.Fieldkit (`tests/test_speaker_loudness.py`), against a pactl simulation in which absent programs raise FileNotFoundError, as `subprocess.run` does. Against the previous version, 7 of the 12 tests fail; against this one, all 12 pass.

author: realmichelduarte
body:
## Purpose
Continue M2 #48 / P0 #46 with a fail-closed **real Windows lab measurement instrument**. The existing `--probe-virtual` could accept any nonzero loopback signal; it did not verify identity of our own emitted stimulus.

## Implementation
- `LoopbackToneVerifier` accepts fragmented 32-bit float WASAPI capture PCM and calculates phase-independent 440 Hz sine/cosine projections, RMS, peak, matched amplitude and coherence, preserving frame count across callbacks.
- Lab `--probe-virtual --source-id ... --confirm-experimental` now requires the returned signal to match our sent 440 Hz tone; rejects unrelated frequencies, DC, silence and PCM errors. Never captures ordinary physical output, switches Windows defaults, installs a driver, records audio to disk or sends network data.
- `--check-loopback` runs **device-free numeric tests** for 44.1/48/96 kHz fragmented stereo positive signal and rejects 880 Hz, DC, silence, short, NaN and unaligned packets. Wired into Windows CI after native DSP/format tests.
- Updated WDK lab documentation to reflect actual prior full WDK INF/CAT CI validation, distinguishing packaging from real driver installation. Chronological project log updated.

## Strict limitations
This PR is not real driver deployment or global application audio acceptance. Actual signed driver installation in an isolated Windows machine and live virtual PCM capture must still run; subsequently prove physical output, native DSP gain, latency, callbacks, recovery and no duplicate playback. Stable v0.1.11 remains APO-backed. **No release requested** for this milestone.

## Automated gates
Windows .NET build, C++ DSP and numeric `--check-loopback` **must be green at PR head** before merge. No physical endpoint or SysVAD kernel installation is represented by a CI pass.

body:
Looking up an absent or recently deleted photo can scan the entire album after the direct ID lookup misses. That makes callers with short response deadlines time out while checking a known asset ID.

Add optional `GetPhotoRequest.DirectLookupOnly`: when true, a direct lookup miss returns explicit null with the completed response metadata and no album enumeration. Omission and false preserve existing lookup fallback. Downloads and mutations retain their existing behavior. The schema generates the public field, and the Photos guide describes the option.

The paired regression rejects every request after indexing, album discovery and direct lookup. It failed with enumeration enabled and passes with the option applied. Existing photo lookup replay scenarios also pass. Exact commit 621b9538ee764e31dd26a9567fa03fefe2df983e passed blocking CI run 38137030222: all six OS/Go matrix jobs and full SDK/CLI lint, build, race, replay, reference/schema, module and coverage gates. Documentation build also passed. Local combined non-generated SDK coverage is 87.1%; all 144 Python reference tests and the 76/76 HTTP route gate passed. A separate consumer installed the published commit with no local replacement and confirmed a deleted disposable asset absent against a real account in 1.8 seconds.

Independent reviewer inspected the implementation, generated optional public API, backward compatibility, paired regression and guide at the exact commit. Final CI approval is recorded before merge. Omission/false preserve fallback, and download/mutation defaults remain unchanged.

- `node` で直接起動（Windows 特有の `npm.cmd` による孫プロセス・ポート掴み残りを回避）。ログは `logs/pm2/` に集約。

### 4. 共通 PowerShell ライブラリ (`scripts/lib/epm-common.ps1`)
- UTF-8 BOM 付き・CRLF 改行固定（PowerShell 5.1 / 7+ 両対応）。
- 単項カンマ演算子（`return ,([string[]]$output)`）による配列アンラップ防止。
- 前提コマンド検証、DB バックアップ（SHA256 照合付き）、PM2 停止・起動・ヘルスチェック待機、アトミックビルド（`dist.next` 検証・入れ替え・復元）、ログローテーション設定など全 19 関数を実装。

### 5. ワンクリック自動更新スクリプト
- **`scripts/update-and-restart.ps1`**:
  - 名前付きミューテックスによる二重起動防止。
  - 未コミット変更チェック、`uploads/` 保護チェック、Fast-Forward 判定。
  - PM2 停止後の安全な SQLite DB バックアップ取得（既定 20 世代管理）。
  - `git fetch` & `git pull --ff-only`、依存更新検知時の `npm ci`。
  - アトミックビルド（`dist.next` にビルド・検証後に切り替え）。
  - PM2 再起動・状態保存（`pm2 save`）。
  - `try〜finally` によるフェイルセーフ自動復旧（障害検知時は直ちに `Stop-EpmApps` でプロセスを停止して DLL ロックを回避し、旧コミット・旧ビルド・DB を安全に復元して旧版再起動）。
- **`scripts/update-and-restart.bat`**: cmd.exe の更新時行ズレ暴走を防ぐ安全な 1 行ラッパー。

### 6. サービス登録・解除スクリプト
- **`scripts/pm2-register.ps1` / `.bat`**: 初回ワンクリックで依存関係チェック、ビルド、PM2 登録、ログローテーション（`pm2-logrotate`）設定、Windows スタートアップ（`shell:startup`）への `EPM - pm2 resurrect.lnk` 登録を一括自動化。
- **`scripts/pm2-unregister.ps1` / `.bat`**: PM2 登録削除、ショートカット削除（DB や画像データは安全に保護）。

### 7. 完全運用ガイド (`docs/WINDOWS_SETUP.md`, `README.md`)
- Mermaid アーキテクチャ図（LAN / スマホ ➔ Vite preview HTTPS ➔ API ➔ DB/画像）。
- 前提ソフト（Node.js, Git, PM2）の導入手順。
- 初回ワンクリック登録手順および Windows サインイン時の自動起動（`pm2 resurrect`）設定。
- デスクトップショートカットによるワンクリック更新の利用手順。
- 複数アプリ運用時の PM2 一元管理・共存の解説。
- 手動ロールバック（DB・コード・ビルド復元）手順。

---

## 検証結果
- **総合テスト (`npm test`)**: **104 件 全合格** (サーバー 76 件 + クライアント 19 件 + スクリプト静的検査 9 件)
  - `server/test/health.test.js`: PASS
  - `scripts/test/windows-scripts.test.js` (S-1〜S-8: BOM, CRLF, ASCII, PS 5.1互換, ecosystem構造等): PASS
- **Reviewer（Claude Opus 5.5）批判的コードレビュー**: 指摘対応完了の上、LGTM 承認済み

---

## 残件（マイナー指摘）
- Node.js バージョン上限（現行 18〜22 を将来的に Node 24 LTS へ緩和検討）
- 異常終了コードの精緻化（エラー終了コード 2 / 3 の区別）
- バックアップ側の付随ファイル（`-journal`）復元ケアおよび `database-failed-*.sqlite` の世代管理

body:
Stacked on #41 (it needs the new Denise ports). Retarget to `cd32-native-mvp` once #41 merges.

`rtl/sim/denise/tb_denise_scroll_copy.sv` compares where the first pixel of a bitplane fetch leaves `denise_bitplanes` against the hardware copy rule (WinUAE `drawing.cpp`: BPL1DAT arms a holding->shift copy that fires when the masked horizontal counter equals the live BPLCON1 scroll).

| | single fetch, off-grid | mid-line BPLCON1 |
|---|---|---|
| OCS FMODE 0 | matches; phase 8 one pixel early (c5ffbf9's new path) | matches |
| AGA FMODE 0 | matches | +4 / +8 / -8 px |
| AGA FMODE 1/2 | 128 of 224 cells off | -- |
| AGA FMODE 3 | 768 of 960 cells off | -- |

- **FMODE 1/2/3:** `extra_delay_f12/f3` round the load phase to 8/16 lores px, but DDFSTRT moves in 4-px steps here and in WinUAE.
- **Mid-line BPLCON1 on AGA:** still waits for the next load, which is the defect `7f93ed1` fixed for OCS only. Mutation check: reverting `7f93ed1` moves the OCS rows to exactly the AGA numbers.
- CD32 is AGA, so every CD32 title runs on the unfixed path.
- **Correction (later):** this is probably *not* MiSTer-devel/Minimig-AGA_MiSTer#158 (Turrican 2 AGA). Its developer traced that to the copper finishing a status-bar split too late, which he reproduces on WinUAE with one extra copper instruction. That's Agnus DMA timing, not this Denise copy.

On-grid cells are asserted (128 checks), the rest printed. CI step added and `check-benches-wired.py` passes (35 wired). Recorded as T28 in `docs/core-accuracy-todo.md`, with the fix shape (comparator copy for AGA and FMODE 1/2/3, ungated immediate BPLCON1). No RTL change in this PR.

Not covered: what is copied when a later fetch lands between the BPL1DAT write and the copy -- what c5ffbf9's ownership logic handles.

author: techafreshh
body:
## Problem

The app currently only runs from a Go toolchain, but the product promises one-command portable runs that work anywhere Go or Docker runs. There is no container image: no `Dockerfile` and no `.dockerignore` exist in the tree, so the deployment path described in the PRD (Phase 3) is unavailable. Issue #8 asks for a CGO-free, multi-stage image that ships the static binary on a distroless base.

## What changed

- **`Dockerfile`** — a multi-stage build. The builder stage is `golang:1.26-bookworm`; it copies `go.mod`/`go.sum` first and runs `go mod download` for layer caching, then builds a static binary with `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/server .`. The runtime stage is `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12` (no shell, no C toolchain, no source) with `WORKDIR /app`, the binary and `static/` copied in, `EXPOSE 8080`, `VOLUME /data`, `ENV PORT=8080 DB_PATH=/data/todos.db`, and a vector `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/server"]`.
- **`.dockerignore`** — keeps the build context lean by excluding VCS metadata, local SQLite files (`*.db`, `*.sqlite`, `todos.db`, `data/`), build artifacts, the Docker files themselves, and planning/harness docs (`.agents/`, `harness/`, `MISSION.md`).
- **`main.go`** — names the container-facing runtime contract as constants (`envPort = "PORT"`, `envDBPath = "DB_PATH"`, `indexFile = "static/index.html"`) and uses them at the `PORT`/`DB_PATH` reads and the UI serve. The values are unchanged, so behavior is unchanged; the constants give the `Dockerfile`'s literals a single owner to bind against.
- **`docker_test.go`** — `TestDockerfileBindsRuntimeContract` reads the `Dockerfile` and binds the two sides: `ENV PORT`/`ENV DB_PATH` to the keys `main.go` reads, the `WORKDIR`-relative asset `COPY` destination to the path `main.go` serves, and the directory of `DB_PATH` to a declared `VOLUME`. A rename or reorg on either side fails `go test` instead of silently 404-ing the UI or routing the DB into the image layer while `/healthz` stays green.

Behavior after this change: the image starts the HTTP server with `PORT`/`DB_PATH` defaults, answers `GET /healthz` with `200 {"status":"ok"}`, serves the UI from `static/` (copied because `main.go` resolves it relative to the working directory), and persists state to the `/data` volume rather than baking a database into an image layer.

## Validation

Docker CLI is not available in this environment (documented in PRD §15), so `docker build` / `docker run` / `docker image inspect` cannot run here and remain a Docker-host acceptance step. What actually ran on this checkout:

- `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w"` succeeds; the stripped binary is 10.5 MB (unstripped was ~15.5 MB), comfortably under the 30 MB ceiling given the ~2 MB distroless static base.
- Simulated the container runtime contract in an `/app`-shaped directory (binary at `/app/server`, `static/` at `/app/static`) with `PORT=<free port> DB_PATH=/data/todos.db`: `GET /healthz` → `200 {"status":"ok"}`, `GET /` → `200` serving `static/index.html`, and `POST /api/todos` → `201` with `GET /api/todos` returning it and the SQLite file created at `DB_PATH`.
- `go vet ./...` — clean.
- `go test ./...` — `ok github.com/techafreshh/todo-app-go-sqlite`.
- `gofmt -l .` — no files reported.
- No aggregate command (Makefile / task runner / CI workflow) is defined by the project, so `go vet` and `go test` are the applicable checks.

Docker-host follow-up for a reviewer: `docker build -t todo-app .`, `docker run --rm -e PORT=8080 -e DB_PATH=/data/todos.db -p 8080:8080 todo-app` then `curl localhost:8080/healthz`, and `docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' todo-app` (< 30000000).

Closes #8

body:
## 1. 概要

sf-init で作った実際のリポジトリが、実際の組織に対して正しく動くことを確認する機能と、その周辺の改善。

### 1.1 sf-verify.sh（新規・管理者向け）
- 実際のリポジトリ・組織で、Hello World の Apex を、各段階（develop → staging → main）にリリースして、削除する
- 診断 → 実行内容の表示 → Enter で確認 → リリース → 削除（組織のクラスと、リポジトリのファイルの両方）
- 段階ごとに、JWT ログイン・ほかの段階のログインが skipped・接続ユーザー・クラス名を確認する
- `--plan`（何も変更しない）・`--cleanup`（削除のみ）。失敗時は、残った段階と `--cleanup` を案内する
- 検証用と同名のクラスのファイルがすでにあれば、実行しない

### 1.2 セットアップの診断（`sf-init.sh --status`）
- リポジトリ・ブランチ・ワークフロー・Secrets・Variables が、そろっているかを、✓ / ✗（直し方つき）/ ！ / ？ で表示する（読み取りのみ）

### 1.3 sf-init の改善
- init フォルダの削除の質問を廃止し、管理者用フォルダとして残す（完了画面に案内）
- 完了済みのプロジェクトで再実行したときは、接続の確認／最初からやり直す、を案内する
- Token の入力を `*` で表示し、受け取った文字数を表示する

### 1.4 e2e（開発者向け）
- `--layout 1|2|3`: 層数に応じて、段階ごとに PR → 検証 → リリース。意図した組織にだけ入ること、wf-propagate、削除が他の段階に及ばないことを確認する
- `bootstrap.sh --add-orgs`: staging・develop のテスト用組織を追加（重複を検出し、確認後にまとめて保存）
- 部品を `lib/sf-verify.sh` に共通化（sf-verify.sh と共有）

## 2. 検証
- `bash tests/run_tests.sh` 全件 PASS（1485 件）
- 実機: `sf-verify.sh` を、実際のリポジトリ（3 層・Developer Edition 3 組織）で実行 → 60 件成功。3 つの組織に、クラスが残っていないことを直接確認
- 外部レビュー（Codex）を 4 回実施し、最終回は「問題なし」

author: kitsu-agent
body:
## What this does

An offline snapshot of the W3Schools C# tutorial, cleaned of everything that only made sense on the live site. Five commits, each a self-contained block of work.

**1. `5d2c524` — internet-only nav and footer blocks.** Removed `#pagetop` (top navbar), `#subtopnav` (per-lesson sub-navigation) and `#spacemyfooter` (deep footer) from all 71 pages, each as a whole element - 3,170,822 characters.

**2. `5ae16a4` — the other-language asset folders.** Deleted `www.w3schools.com/c/`, `html/` and `python/`. Each held one image embedded by C# pages, so every reference was handled rather than left broken:
- `c/col-row.png` -> moved to `cs/col-row.png` (the 2D-array illustration)
- `html/img_cert_html.jpg` -> the C# exam/quiz/index pages were showing an *HTML* certificate; repointed to `cs/img_cs_certificate.png`
- `python/syllabus-webinar.png` -> a Python-academy banner on the C# study-plan and syllabus pages; banner and its link removed, the "Watch Demo" CTA kept

**3. `4b42851` — empty nav wrappers, reclaimed top space, dead scripts and cert images.** Removed `#top-nav-bar`, `.topnavbackground` (the empty 33px dark band), `.topnavcontainer`, `#tnb-search-suggestions` and the ~4 kB inline subtopnav scrolling script per page; `#main`/`#right` margin-top 90px -> 0 and `#leftmenuinner` padding-top 87px -> 0 in `lib/w3schools/main.v1.0.5.css`; guards in `lib/w3schools_footer.js` and `lib/topnav/main.v1.0.144.js` where they dereferenced the removed markup; the cs_quiz/index/exam certificate pickers now resolve to the local C# certificate.

**4. `2414400` — adventure banner, ad slots and socials column.** Removed `div.advb` (the Adventure-Mode/account promo: XP, streak and league stats, app-store badges, sign-in CTA - 8,324 chars/page), `div#right` (socials, skyscraper ad slot, "remove ads" promo - 3,078 chars/page) and `div#mainLeaderboard` (the empty 90px leaderboard slot). `#main` now takes the full row width with the column divider dropped, which is what the site's own ad code does when it removes that column. Guards added in `lib/uic_prov.js` (unguarded `stickySkyscraper.remove()`) and `lib/w3schools_footer.js` (two click handlers bound straight to `#right`).

**5. `41b33aa` — the consent popup and the leftover bottom placeholder.** Each page carried both halves of the FastCMP consent manager: a 2,278-char inline TCF/`__tcfapi` stub and an async loader from `https://static.fastcmp.com/fast-cmp-stub.js`, which built a full-viewport backdrop plus the iframe "W3Schools seeks your consent..." dialog that opened on every first visit. Both gone. `div#wrappercontainer` - a red 100px box declared in its own inline CSS, wrapping nothing but a `#footerwrapper` of dead CSS - is gone too, along with the empty `#footer` shell (`<hr>` plus the empty `#bottomads` slot) next to it. Guard in `lib/uic_prov.js` for its unguarded `bottom.length` teardown.

## Verification

- Through every element removal: tag counts checked on comment-, script- and style-stripped markup, equal opening/closing tags removed, no removed ID left in the repo, no `<script>` swallowed by a cut.
- All relative `href`/`src` references in the repo resolve to a file that exists.
- Headless Chrome with the HTTP cache disabled - and storage cleared before each load so the consent dialog could appear if anything still triggered it - at 1265px and 685px viewports over 15 pages: **zero console errors, zero unhandled rejections, no consent elements in the DOM, no horizontal overflow, trailing gap below the content 0px**.

A lesson page: 219,215 -> 35,259 bytes of HTML (-84%).

## Known leftovers (deliberate)

- Dead CSS for removed blocks (`#subtopnav`, `.topnavbackground`, `#mainLeaderboard`, `#right`, `#skyscraper` rules, etc.) is still present in each page's inline `<style>` blocks. Inert; straightforward to strip next.

author: fiftyeightcoins
body: ## Title fix(presale): correct timezone detection in organizer calendar ## Description Fixes multi-timezone detection in the presale organizer calendar views (`CalendarView`, `WeekCalendarView`). `add_events_for_days` and `add_subevents_for_days` were reading `event.settings.timezones` / `s.timezones` (plural), which is not a valid setting key. The correct key is `timezone` (singular). The code now reads `.timezone` and adds it to the set only when a timezone is configured. This PR also binds the loop variable in `OrganizerIndex.get_context_data` using `lambda e=event: e.settings.timezone` to resolve Ruff lint rule B023. ## Motivation and Context The calendar template displays a notice when `len(timezones) > 1`: > Note that the events in this view are in different timezones. Because the incorrect setting key always resolved to `None`, the set contained only `{None}`. Consequently, the notice never appeared, even when an organizer had events across multiple time zones. As a result, organizers could misinterpret event times without being warned about timezone differences. ## Behavior Change **Before:** The multi-timezone notice never appeared on the organizer calendar or week calendar. **After:** The notice appears when the displayed events or subevents span more than one time zone. Calendars with a single time zone remain unchanged. The B023 fix has no runtime effect. ## How Has This Been Tested? Added unit tests in `app/tests/tickets/presale/test_organizer_page.py`: - `test_add_events_for_days_populates_timezones` - `test_add_subevents_for_days_populates_timezones` Added the integration test `test_calendar_multiple_timezones`, which verifies that the notice renders when events in different time zones are present. Testing performed: - Ran `pytest tests/tickets/presale/test_organizer_page.py` against a local PostgreSQL instance on port 5432, with `pg_trgm` enabled in `template1`: **21 passed**. - Ran Ruff checks on the modified files. ## Types of Changes - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) ## Checklist - [ ] My code follows the code style of this project. - [ ] I have read the CONTRIBUTING document. - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [x] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [x] All tests in `test_organizer_page.py` passed. ## Summary by Sourcery Fix organizer calendar timezone detection and ensure users are warned when displayed events span multiple timezones. Bug Fixes: - Correct multi-timezone detection in organizer calendar and week calendar views so notices appear when displayed events or subevents use different configured timezones. Enhancements: - Bind the organizer calendar timezone lookup to each event to satisfy closure-safety linting. Tests: - Add unit and integration coverage for timezone collection and rendering the multi-timezone calendar notice. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Organizer calendar pages now account for the configured time zones of events and subevents. When public events use different time zones, the page displays a notice to help attendees understand the schedule. * Time zone information is now retained accurately across multiple events, preventing one event’s time zone from being used in place of another’s.

author: lioreshai
body:
## What a player sees differently

ABATOIR CORE is the one sector that looked like a toy rather than a place. Standing at its arrival camera, the room is a wet red interior — salmon fibre walls, a red cracked deck, a pale tendon ceiling — and then the minority wall face, one face in five, is **quilted violet panelling** with a magenta filament seam. Turn a corner and a salmon fibre face meets a purple one. It is not a loud thing, it is a wrong thing: a technical panel in the colour of a different level, in the one level whose whole idea is one organic interior.

After this change the same camera shows one grimy red room with **one** thing in it that is deliberately loud — the green lamp field overhead, which the level already authored as its accent. The purple is gone; the quilt, the seams and the darkness stayed.

## Why it happened

Each level authors four independent material choices plus a lamp colour, and nothing asks whether the families belong together. ABATOIR's `wall2` is `WT.TECH2`, picked for contrast, and `WT.TECH2` is purple. #369 fixed this level's *value* collision (its walls were wearing the deck's own generator) and deliberately held mean albedo — it never looked at hue. #416 bounds brightness and grain. Neither instrument can see a colour.

## The change, and the term it is made at

`WTEX.TECH2` is worn by exactly one level, so this is a palette re-tone inside one painter (`js/10_assets.js`):

- the albedo is an oxblood over the same quilt, authored at the **violet tile's own Rec.709 luma**, so no surface changes brightness;
- the seam stops being a magenta filament and becomes an amber one — still emissive, at the same emissive area;
- the dust wash goes from violet to rust.

No `alb`, no `amb`, no `spec`, no bump, no grain, no per-level bias, no lamp, no height. The structure is untouched on purpose: a lined, drained cutting room would really be panelled, and the issue's acceptance is an area rule about which colours carry a frame, not a demand to repaint the geometry.

## Validation at b13adc4

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `node tools/view.js matband` | main's verdicts — wall spread 131.2/90.5 = 1.45x, floor 136.0/94.5 = 1.44x, ceiling mean 68.8 below every face |
| `node tools/view.js exposure` | `EXPOSURE ok`, exit 0 — seeded medians **74 / 69 / 67 / 92**, every roll list unchanged |
| `node tools/view.js flatparity` | ok, exit 0 — L2 PARITY and L2 LOCK re-keyed, **both means hold to the tenth** (37.5, 59.0); L0/L1/L3 byte-identical in the same run |
| `node tools/view.js refs` | ok — `refs.lock` re-recorded with the repo's own `refs --record` |
| `node tools/smoke.js` and `VERT=1 node tools/smoke.js` | `SMOKE PASSED`, exit 0 both lanes |
| `node tools/view.js scene 2 0` before/after | the room reads as one interior with one loud thing in it |

A frame moving while its mean does not is the signature of a hue change and not of a relight, and the three levels that do not wear this tile are byte-identical — that is the control that makes this a re-record rather than a widening. No threshold, tolerance or vacuity floor was moved.

## What is *not* done

The issue's census named three sectors; this PR fixes the one in its title. Still open, and measured in the issue:

- **RING TRANSPORT carries no accent at all** — 99 % of its chromatic pixels sit in two adjacent cool buckets, so nothing in it is deliberately loud. Adding one is not a palette edit: every lever that would make a RING surface disagree with its own room (its lamp colour, its deck) is a light or value term and moves a recorded median.
- **THE STACK's stone deck contributes a yellow-green family of its own** to a grey vault — the moss mottle in `FLOORS.STONE`. That tile is shared with ARCHIVE SUBLEVEL, so quieting it is a two-level change with two recorded medians behind it, not one literal.

Both are stated rather than half-done because a palette change that moves a level's median is being made at the wrong term, and this cycle had neither the time nor the measurements to do them at the right one.

Refs #466

author: uhbyxer
body:
## Summary

Fan a PR out to a chosen set of agents in parallel, group them into one `multi_agent_run`, and compare results in Columns/Tabs with a deterministic "Where agents disagree" block. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-07-08-multi-agent-review.md`, plan: `docs/plans/multi-agent-review.md`, mockups: `docs/design/`.

```text
AgentPicker (PR page) ─┐
                       ├─ POST /pulls/:id/multi-agent-run
ConfigureRun page ─────┘     createMultiAgentRun
                             N × agent_run (multi_agent_run_id)
                             run-executor: Promise.allSettled   <- was sequential
GET /pulls/:id/multi-agent
  listRunsForMultiRun -> columns
  computeConflicts (pure: same file + overlapping lines, done runs only)
  -> MultiAgentRun { columns, conflicts, totals }
```

```diff
 server/src/modules/reviews/
+├── conflicts.ts          # pure cross-agent grouping
 ├── run-executor.ts       # sequential -> parallel fan-out
 ├── service.ts            # startMultiAgentRun, getMultiAgentView
 client/src/
+├── app/multi-agent-review/         # Configure run + [multiRunId] results
-├── .../_components/RunReviewDropdown
+├── .../_components/AgentPicker
 └── components/run-trace-drawer     # moved from the PR route, shared now
```

- Migration `0017`: nullable `agent_runs.multi_agent_run_id` (FK, cascade) + index.
- `GET /agents` now carries `est_duration_ms` / `est_cost_usd` / `has_history`; the summary (time = max, cost = sum) is computed on the client.
- Out of scope: Compose review, other GLOBAL nav items, functional Learn/Reply/Turn into eval (disabled placeholders), reviewer-core, `ci/`, `agent-runner/`.

## Evidence

- **Before:** one-or-all `RunReviewDropdown`; sequential executor; no multi-agent page.
  **After:** server non-IT tests 278 pass; client 149 pass, `tsc` clean; `multi-agent-run.it.test.ts` passes against Postgres. Ran locally: Configure run and the Columns result for a 4-agent run render with real data.

```text
computeConflicts: same file + overlapping range -> one group
  Security flags api.js:18-28, others silent
  -> takes: Security=CRITICAL, rest="ignored" (did not flag)
```

Known: server `pnpm typecheck` shows pre-existing errors outside this feature's files (reviewer-core deps were not installed in my worktree).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive nullable column and new routes; the old `POST /pulls/:id/review` still works. Reverting is a code revert (the column can stay).

**Blast Radius:** executor + PR header

- `executeRuns` is now parallel for **every** caller (`{all:true}`, MCP, CI). With many enabled agents this can trip provider rate limits (no concurrency cap).
- The PR page's run control is replaced by `AgentPicker`: disabled agents are not offered, and every manual review now navigates to the multi-agent page.
- `startMultiAgentRun` is not fully atomic: a failure inside the per-agent `createAgentRun` loop can leave an orphan `multi_agent_runs` row.
- A failed start can show both the inline error and the global mutation toast.

author: iliaal
body:
## Summary
Embed the OpenCode hook runtime with Bun's text loader so a built CLI can install hook-enabled plugins outside the source checkout. Previously installation failed with ENOENT while reading `../runtime/opencode-hooks.ts` relative to the bundled executable.

## Failing-path audit
All production callers of `writeOpenCodeBundle` go through `targets.opencode.write` in `src/targets/index.ts`:
- `convert --to opencode`: primary target write in `src/commands/convert.ts`.
- `convert --to codex --also opencode`: secondary target write in the same file.
- `install --to opencode`: primary target write in `src/commands/install.ts` (local and resolved GitHub plugin paths share this write).
- `install --to codex --also opencode`: secondary target write in the same file.
All four CLI routes are covered by new regressions. The existing direct-writer integration test remains covered. No install/convert caller to this failing sink is left unfixed.

## Validation
- Before the fix, all four new tests failed with ENOENT at the runtime read.
- Bun 1.4.2: locked dependency install, full `bun test` (73 tests / 258 assertions), and `bun build src/index.ts --target=bun` passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Each new regression builds the CLI into a temporary directory, runs it outside the repository, deletes the source plugin, then executes the installed hook and verifies its copied resource is readable. Spaces in source/output paths are exercised.
- Independent review repeated the full test suite and build; no blocking findings.
- Remote commit `7cff75daff2424ee0ba5c0b91a52921d5339a12d` was fetched and its entire content/mode tree matched the final tested local tree `8aafdeb453bf6c0c739b70cd3377bc282f05fc62` before opening this PR.
- Exact-head [CLI regression checks](https://github.com/iliaal/whetstone/actions/runs/38137033398) completed successfully for `7cff75daff2424ee0ba5c0b91a52921d5339a12d`: one run, one test-and-build job, with dependency install, CLI tests, and build all successful (none skipped). Run/check/job listings have total_count 1 and were fully enumerated with per_page=100. No legacy commit statuses. No new workflow or dependency added.

## Limits and scope
- Optional TypeScript 5.9.3 `tsc --noEmit` still reports the same four baseline errors on both master and this branch: hook-fixture typing at `src/parsers/claude.test.ts:93,109`, and missing js-yaml declarations at `src/utils/frontmatter.ts:1` and `src/utils/frontmatter.test.ts:2`. No new diagnostics. Bun's text-loader import uses a narrowly explained `@ts-expect-error` because TypeScript treats the file as a normal TS module. No lint script is configured.
- Separate existing bundled `cleanup` limitation is unchanged: `src/commands/cleanup.ts` resolves both pluginRoot and runtimePath relative to its own file. Repro: `bun build src/index.ts --target=bun --outfile=/tmp/whetstone-cli.js`, then `bun /tmp/whetstone-cli.js cleanup --target opencode --output /tmp/whetstone-cleanup-repro` fails before cleanup with ENOENT for `/plugins/whetstone/skills`. This PR fixes installation/conversion, not cleanup ownership discovery.
- Live open-PR listing was empty before edits and publication, so there are no sibling file overlaps. No Unreleased section exists; AGENTS.md reserves changelog/version/count changes for releases.

## What changed

- Reuse that same in-memory history across all five OOS windows and seven body thresholds.

## Why
The previous loop fetched history again for each threshold and window. That caused redundant API requests and allowed threshold variants to be evaluated against slightly different snapshots if the exchange data changed during a run. This change improves efficiency and apples-to-apples comparability.

## Safety
- Research-only script change; no production signal logic, BUY thresholds, target policy, execution, leverage, withdrawals, or SPOT enforcement changes.
- Historical candle data remains read-only.

## Validation
CI should run tests and production-readiness checks. The OOS research workflow should be rerun to confirm the report is produced from the cached snapshot.

author: remzfx
body:
## Problema y alcance
Datos dinámicos se interpolaban directamente en HTML de Admin, Registro y Auxiliar. Un nombre/archivo/fecha podía generar etiquetas; las comillas podían alterar atributos y la justificación escapaba únicamente comillas dobles, dejando que entidades HTML cambiasen su valor al volver a leerlo.

Base: main posterior al PR #72, `69cbe868189b7e7e9238bca92e8561120f4fdac3`. Solo protección de presentación: se mantienen las plantillas estructurales, estilos, handlers, datos originales y contratos.

## Sinks corregidos
- **admin.html / renderDocentes**: escape de nombre/usuario/nivel, descripción de grados/áreas/asignaciones/aulas, tutorías/aportes y texto de clave. `data-doc-id` conserva el ID original tras la decodificación normal de atributos; Editar/Eliminar siguen usando la delegación existente.
- **admin.html / listarPlantillasSiagie**: nivel, bimestre, grado, sección y filename se muestran como texto codificado. La consulta no cambia.
- **registro.html / renderFinales**: nombres de alumnos y encabezados de competencia codificados. Notas, calculados, conclusiones y controles mantienen su lógica.
- **registro.html / renderStudents**: nombres y textos de competencia/capacidad de la grilla codificados.
- **registro.html / renderAsistencia y renderSesiones**: nombres, horas, fechas visibles y atributos de fecha codificados; datasets recuperan el valor original.
- **registro.html / fillComps, fillCaps, renderAreas, llenarAulasPadron, onGrado**: textos y valores de selects/contexto relacionados codificados. Identidades URI existentes y handlers no cambian.
- **auxiliar.html / renderLista**: nombres, numeración, horas y motivos; escape completo de `value` y de atributos basados en la identidad URI. Se conserva P/F/T/J, búsqueda, edición y selección del estudiante.
- **auxiliar.html / onNivel y onGrado**: escape de texto/atributos de opciones de grado/sección vinculadas a los estudiantes.

Se reutilizan `escapeConsulta` y `escapeRegistro`; Auxiliar incorpora un helper local equivalente. El escape ocurre al renderizar, nunca al almacenar. Las entidades literales como `<` se conservan como tales en el valor original, sin doble decodificación.

## Archivos y pruebas
Productivos: `admin.html`, `registro.html`, `auxiliar.html`.
- Nuevo `tests/frontend-html-escape.test.cjs`: **18 regresiones** ejecutan los renders reales y comprueban su salida, atributos recuperados y handlers. Tildes, ñ, apóstrofos, comillas, &, <, >, etiqueta sintética inerte, nombres/archivos SIAGIE, justificaciones, fechas, dataset, edición de notas en Letras/0–20 y solo lectura.
- Nuevo `tests/html-escape-snapshot.cjs`: lista cerrada de las transformaciones exactas de presentación aprobadas aquí, exclusivamente para snapshots históricos; no normaliza código productivo ni las nuevas pruebas de seguridad. Cualquier otro cambio continúa fallando las comparaciones.
- Fixtures/snapshots relacionados actualizados: layout-shells, registro-academic-model, registro-layout, registro-session-layout-pr67, registro-transversales-integracion y students-client. No se eliminan assertions funcionales.

## Validación
Head: `a2e29d9734848cad0e0c7cf689fa6bce9b8fd9aa`.
- Pruebas específicas: **18/18 aprobadas**.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive bot permission validation and event-loop latency monitoring to prevent silent failures and improve diagnostics for Discord interaction timeouts.

## Key Changes

### Bot Permission Validation (`utils/bot_permissions.py`)
- New utility module for checking bot permissions at guild and channel levels
- Defines `BASELINE_BOT_PERMISSIONS` (view_channel, send_messages, read_message_history, use_external_emojis) required by all message-sending modules
- Implements `missing_guild_permissions()` and `missing_channel_permissions()` that report **all gaps at once** (never short-circuit) so admins see every missing permission in a single message
- Provides `format_missing()` to render permission gaps with localized permission names and channel mentions
- Integrated into `/config` command to validate module requirements before opening config screens

### Module Permission Declarations
- Updated all modules to declare `REQUIRED_BOT_PERMISSIONS` (module-specific only; baseline merged automatically)
- Added `SENDS_MESSAGES` flag to modules that don't post (auto_role, bot_customization)
- Added `channel_requirements()` classmethod to modules that use specific channels (altguard, interserver, logs, tickets, etc.)
- New tests (`test_bot_permissions.py`) verify no module requires Administrator and all baseline permissions are properly declared

### Ticket Service Permission Clamping (`services/ticket_service.py`)
- Discord rejects channel create/edit with overwrites allowing/denying permissions the bot doesn't hold (unless Administrator)
- New `bot_permissions_for()` computes bot's effective permissions in a category or guild
- `clamp_overwrite()` and `clamp_overwrites()` strip permissions from overwrites that the bot cannot grant
- Ensures tickets open even when staff roles request permissions the bot lacks (staff keep what the bot can give)
- Tests (`test_ticket_permissions.py`) verify clamping behavior and core permission validation

### Interaction Latency Monitoring (`utils/loop_monitor.py`)
- Heartbeat task measures event-loop lag every 250ms and warns when exceeding 1.0s
- Watchdog thread detects when heartbeat stalls while loop is blocked and dumps the main thread's stack (exact line hogging the loop)
- `observe_interaction_age()` called from `bot.on_interaction` distinguishes "interaction delayed by gateway/loop" from "our callback was slow"
- Minimal overhead: one timer wake-up per 250ms + one thread polling every 500ms
- Tests (`test_interaction_latency.py`) verify expired-interaction detection and loop monitoring

### Expired Interaction Handling (`cogs/error_handler.py`)
- New `expired_interaction_kind()` unwraps exception chains to detect 10062 (unknown_interaction), 10008 (unknown_message), 10015 (unknown_webhook)
- `log_expired_interaction()` warns (never errors) about expired interactions, counts them, and samples to Sentry (at most once per kind per 10 min)
- `BaseView.on_error` swallows expired interactions without user-facing error messages (the channel is gone anyway)
- Prevents noise that hides real bugs while keeping diagnostics visible

### Incognito Preference Caching (`utils/incognito.py`)
- In-process cache for user's DEFAULT_INCOGNITO preference (60s TTL, max 4096 users)
- Bounded lookup timeout (0.8s) ensures DB round trip never eats into Discord's 3s ack window
- Integrated into slash commands (preferences, reminder, saved_messages, invite, moddy, ping, user) to defer before reading DB
- `resolve_default_incognito()` falls back to default on timeout or DB error

### Global Sanctions Lookup Optimization (`utils/global_sanctions.py`)
- Single-flight deduplication: concurrent callers share one DB query per subject
- Bounded lookup timeout (1.0s) for interaction paths
- Prevents pool starvation from eating the 3s ack budget

### Ticket Closure Timing Fix (`utils/ticket_views.py`)
- New `close_then_answer()` helper ensures interaction response is sent while

author: nitr57
body:
## Problem

Discord *bugs-and-issues*, "Flat wizard with Gemini flat lite now not working" (Fraser, Nikon Z via libgphoto2, native NEF): the flat wizard's auto brightness overexposes, and the preview turns black above a certain brightness. Astro cameras and the same Nikon under Windows/TNS work. A histogram target of 3% gave flats at about 50% in Photoshop.

**Cause:** LibRaw pixels are not scaled, but their range came from the profile's camera bit depth (16 by default). A 14-bit NEF therefore read 4× darker than it is, a 12-bit NEF 16×. The wizard drove the panel into saturation.

**Black preview:** A clipped flat is nearly uniform, so its MAD is about 0. With a median below half the assumed range, `GetStretchMap` sets `shadows = median` and `midtones = MTF(t, 0) = 0`, which maps every pixel to black.

**Second bug:** `AutoBrightnessFlat`, `AutoExposureFlat` and `SkyFlat` compared the mean of the converted image against `image.BitDepth`, the profile bit depth carried by the `IExposureData`. Since #306 RAW honours bit scaling. With bit scaling on (the default) and a bit depth below 16, the pixels are scaled to 16 bits but measured against e.g. 2^14, so flats came out 4× too dark.

## Changes

- **`LibRawConverter`:** The reported bit depth is lowered to what LibRaw's white level and the brightest pixel actually reach.
  - The white level comes from `libraw_get_color_maximum`, a C getter, so no struct offsets are needed.
  - Pixel values and saved files are unchanged.
  - The bit depth is only ever lowered: a too-low profile setting is still raised while copying, and a pixel above the white level keeps the bits needed to hold it.
  - Without the getter or a white level, the old behaviour stays.
- **`AutoBrightnessFlat`, `AutoExposureFlat`, `SkyFlat`:** The histogram target is measured against `imageData.Properties.BitDepth`. `AutoExposureFlat` and `SkyFlat` already used that value for their percentages. For non-RAW cameras both bit depths are identical, so nothing changes there.
- **Docs and changelog:** The bit depth contract is documented in `NINA.Image/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and there is a CHANGELOG entry under *Unreleased*.

## Impact

- **Affected paths:** Only RAW frames (all formats via LibRaw, from libgphoto2 cameras and opened RAW files). Astro, INDI and ASCOM paths pass their bit depth through unchanged.
- **Visible changes for RAW:**
  - The preview stretch and histogram now span the real range, e.g. 14 instead of 16 bits.
  - Histogram targets that were lowered to work around the bug (such as 3%) need to go back to normal values.
- **Unchanged:** Saved FITS/XISF pixel values, so calibration frames taken before and after stay compatible. Native RAW files are written byte for byte, as before.

## Verification

- **New tests:**
  - `LibRawConverterBehaviorTest.GetDataBitDepth_*` covers the 16-bit default, 12-bit data, no white level, a white level filling 16 bits, a pixel above the white level, bit scaling with 14- and 12-bit data, a too-low profile bit depth and an overflowing white level after scaling.
  - `AutoBrightnessFlatTest` and `AutoExposureFlatTest` each get a regression test where the exposure says 14 bit and the converted image 16 bit.
- **Updated tests:** The existing `AutoBrightnessFlatTest` cases now set up `IImageData.Properties`, which the item reads now.
- **LibRaw check:** I ran the converter's steps (`open` → `unpack` → `raw2image` → `libraw_get_color_maximum`) through ctypes against LibRaw 0.22.1 with sample RAWs:
  - The two 12-bit Nikon D3S NEFs report a white level of 4095, which gives 12 bit.
  - The Canon 5D Mark II CR2 reports 15600 (brightest pixel 16383), which gives 14 bit.
- **Not done locally:**
  - The .NET SDK and NuGet were not reachable from this environment, so I could not compile or run the tests here. CI (`build-and-test.yml`) has to confirm both.
  - Not tested on hardware.
  - Still to try: Fraser's saved NEFs (dark, ~50 %, saturated) through PINS, checking that the pixel hashes stay the same and only the bit depth and stretch change.

author: poyrazk
body:
Milestone: hunt #9 production test loop on rc.252 (production-us).

## Found on prod
h9-canary (`max_concurrency 1`): a `--safe` canary v2 was aborted by the circuit breaker at 11:48:40 (live, traffic 0%, `rollout_state=aborted`). Its instance stayed `running` until 11:58:07. The next deploy (v3) primed at 11:54:41, and its hosting smoke then got **165 × 429 on `/healthz` (11:55–12:00)**, because the stable instance plus the aborted candidate's instance filled `max_concurrency + RolloutConcurrencyGrant`. v3 only went live after the idle reaper parked both (11:58:09).

## Fix
`enrichReaperEnvironmentPolicies` treats a live, 0%-traffic aborted canary candidate (`state.AbortedCanaryCandidate`, already used to keep it out of rollback targets for H5-62) like a superseded revision, so `drainSupersededReaperRows` parks it on the next tick **with** a snapshot (an operator `rollouts recover` can still wake it). A completed release later rolled back, a staged 0% revision without a canary, and an aborted candidate still carrying traffic are untouched.

Tests: `TestRunReaperDrainsAbortedCanaryCandidate` (MemStore: canary woken, aborted via `RecoverRolloutForDeployment(abort)`, reaper parks it with one snapshot, stable still wakes), `TestReaperAbortedCanary` (predicate table). Ran locally: `go test ./pkg/sched -run 'Reaper|AbortedCanary'` ok.

No architecture change; no migrations.

body:
## Problem

`commands/manager-loop.md`'s `waiting-on-human` bullet told a manager to **post the decision to the attention board**, and stated only later in the same bullet that a closer-line `pick` must never be posted. The instruction preceded its own exception, so a top-down read reached the wrong action first and had no reason to keep reading.

Measured 2026-10-11 in a live manager session: a tracked worker's closer-line `pick` was carded, the operator answered it on the board **and** in the worker's own pane, and two task-creators were dispatched for one one-clause change before a peer message caught the duplication.

## Change

The gate class test now precedes every gate-acting instruction in the bullet, so a reader who reaches the post instruction has already passed the routing rule.

The three exceptions are unchanged **byte-for-byte** — only their position moved.

## Why the diff looks the way it does

Both anchors previously resolved to the **same physical line** (275 — the whole bullet is one physical line, 6740 characters), so a line-number before/after cannot express this change; it is a reorder *within* the line.

Diff shape: 1 removed region (576 chars, the exception block at its old position) and 1 added region (780 chars, the class test plus the block at its new position), 1 hunk.

- `make precommit` passes. (A fresh worktree needs `npm install --no-audit --no-fund` **inside `server/`** first — the Makefile documents that trap.)
- The three exception sentences are byte-identical to the pre-change revision.

author: 55kamiryo
body:
closes #17403 <!-- Add the related issue number here. Repeat this line for each additional issue it closes -->

<!-- Explain the goal of the PR, why it is needed, and what has been changed to achieve that goal -->

SvelteKit renders `<link rel="stylesheet">` and the `rel="preload"; as="style"` Link header without `crossorigin`. Vite's preload helper and SvelteKit's own `load_css` request the same stylesheets with `crossorigin`. If `paths.assets` is on another origin and its server sends CORS headers only for requests with an `Origin` header, the browser can reuse the cached no-cors response for the CORS request and block the stylesheet. The issue has a reproduction.

This PR adds `crossorigin` to both. Without it on the Link header, the browser fetches the preload in no-cors mode and reuses that response for the `<link crossorigin>`, so the CSS fails on a full page load.

Tests: `test/apps/options` checks the SSR stylesheet links with a cross-origin `paths.assets`, and `test/apps/options-2` checks the `Link` header with `linkHeaderPreload`. Both fail without the change.

After an upgrade, browsers reuse stylesheets cached by the previous version (without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`) for the new `<link crossorigin>` until the file names change. Vite changed all CSS hashes once to handle this (vitejs/vite#18367). Should this PR do the same?

AI disclosure: Claude helped with the investigation, drafted this change and the tests, and helped with the English. I reviewed and tested everything myself.
