author: skalaliya
body:
First of the alerts phase (P4). **Merge this before the "Rules today" PR and the EXP-0023 PR, which are built on it.**

## What

On a session day the host's `options-live` job also works out where each of the four probation rules stands so far, and sends it with the positions as version 2 of its document.

- **Same rule code.** It replays the rules with `wt.options.rules`, the code the after-close run uses, on the feed's half-hour bars cut into the hours the broker cuts (`wt.options.intraday`), against levels built from the feed's own daily bars.
- **Provisional, and it says so.** The feed runs 16 minutes behind and its bars can differ from the record's by cents. The block carries states, the time of the trigger and R so far. No prices.
- **Alerts ship in log mode.** `rule_alerts` in `config/options_desk.yaml` is `log`: a rule that triggers is written to the job's log. `phone` pages once per name and rule a session, naming the stock and the rule and saying it is a paper rule on probation, not a signal to trade. That switch is the owner's, after a week of logs.
- **Never at the positions' expense.** The block is sent only to a dashboard that reports it accepts version 2 (asked once an hour). If the site refuses it anyway, the positions are sent again without it. A fault reading the bars is named in `problems`.
- The site's schema accepts the block from this PR (`OPTIONS_LIVE_ACCEPTS` 2). Nothing draws it until the next PR.

## Checked

- A read-only run against real market data for Friday 9 October: ten names, seven hourly bars each at the close, states for all forty name-and-rule pairs, one second, a 3 KB block that passes the schema.
- Independently reviewed before opening. A 4,000-session fuzz found the mid-session trick (a repeat-of-last-close bar so the latest hour can trigger) never creates, hides or changes a result against the finished-session replay. Its ten findings are in the second commit; the main one was that a site rollback could stop positions for up to an hour.

## For the owner after merge

`wt-deploy deploy` on the VM. Code only, no unit install. Rule states start flowing on the next session day once the site's deploy of this PR is live.

## Known and left

- `rule_alerts: phone` alerts are filed under the stocks desk's alert list (title: stock and rule label) until the day rolls over. Worth a look before flipping the switch.
- A name whose daily bars fail the engine's checks (a gap, a suspected split) is skipped every run and only counted, not explained.

## Summary

This stacked draft PR builds on `feature/student-explore-smart-domains-fonts` and improves the Android student Explore experience based on the provided visual reference and emulator feedback.

### Visual redesign
- Use a pure-black Explore canvas and black-to-neutral-graphite gradient, without blue/purple cast in the page background.
- Reserve violet for brand and selected states; remove neon-style icon halos.
- Replace the flat XML vector placeholder artwork with a bundled **glossy 3D raster sprite atlas** (`drawable-nodpi/domain_art_sprite.jpg`). The atlas contains 20 illustrated domain images and crops the matching image for recommended-domain tiles, the full domain picker, selected-domain chips, and job-card category badges.
- Normalize visible category labels and deduplicate aliases (including Mobile Apps / Mobile Development).
- Keep the currently selected domain visible in the horizontally scrollable row, even when it is one of the recommended domains.
- Match the opaque floating navigation dock to the black theme and reserve Explore viewport space above it to reduce content overlap.

### Filter and card improvements
- Filter edits remain drafts until Apply; dismissing the dialog discards pending edits, and choosing a domain inside Filters returns to that panel.
- Scope required skills to the selected domain and remove incompatible skill choices after a domain change.
- Present required skills as compact wrapping selectable chips, display the selected-skill count, shorten the search label, and return all matching search results.
- Wrap job-card skill tags on narrow screens.
- Sanitize and validate budget ranges; keep unknown budget values from passing active ranges or sorting ahead of known values; preserve domain selection during keyword search; keep Clear all from changing the feed tab unexpectedly.
- Use a restrained category color and neutral dark surfaces, and display the fixed-budget/hourly-rate caption correctly.

### Navigation and refresh
- Preserve the route stack in saveable state, push detail/workspace routes on top of the current page, keep the parent root tab selected, and provide in-app and Android Back behavior.
- Refresh Home, job/gig Explore, Orders, Chat, Profile, and Notifications on return and when re-selecting a bottom tab; add pull-to-refresh to job and gig Explore feeds.
- Keep cached order/chat/notification/gig results visible when a refresh fails, surface retryable errors, and avoid showing empty/error states before initial loading starts.
- Preserve unsaved profile edits during automatic refreshes; invalidate stale order-selection, payment-verification, and checkout responses; prevent duplicate escrow/order actions; and allow Back to cancel an inline order load.
- Show the global Back arrow only on pushed detail routes; avoid duplicate Back controls in the order workspace.
- Remove the static notification dot because it was not connected to real unread state.

### Web marketplace reference
The Android filter set is based on the React source at `apps/web/src/pages/StudentMarketplacePage.jsx`, which exposes keyword, budget range, project type, skills, location, language, sorting, and pagination. The deployed Vercel page was not visually verified in this review.

### Verification status
- Static source audit across the changed Kotlin files found balanced delimiters and no duplicate imports; navigation callbacks, artwork references, loading defaults, and filter state paths were checked.
- API repositories used by the refreshed screens now propagate coroutine cancellation rather than converting it into ordinary request failures; request-generation guards prevent older responses from replacing newer selections.
- **The latest head still needs `testDebugUnitTest` and `assembleDebug` plus emulator interaction testing.** No Android CI run is configured for this branch, and the user's most recent successful APK predates these changes.
- Resume-derived skill extraction is not included because the current profile model does not expose parsed resume text or extracted skills.

_Requested by **Koen** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01UY2d6TtbJmsRKNAXTAtkTe?thread=cmsg_01UY2d6TtbJmsRKNAXTAtkTe1rWp88urzecJuJvaLCm72P)_

Before: even with the Slack secrets set, `/deliverybot` commands always failed. The signing secret was never read, so every command got a 400. The `/slack/*` pages were caught by the `/:owner/:repo` dashboard routes. Sign in also used Slack's legacy `oauth.access`, which new Slack apps can't use.

After: you create a Slack app, set `SLACK_CLIENT_ID`, `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET` and `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET`, and `/deliverybot login` and `/deliverybot deploy owner/repo@ref target` work. Linked accounts keep working after the GitHub App's 8-hour user tokens expire.

How:
- `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` is read in `packages/run/src/config.ts` and passed through the Deploy workflow. `SLACK_LOGIN_URL` is gone because the authorize URL is now built from `SLACK_CLIENT_ID` and `BASE_URL`.
- The Slack app is registered before the dashboard so its routes aren't shadowed.
- `/slack/install` starts an `oauth.v2.access` flow with the `commands` scope and an OAuth `state` kept in the session. Without the state, a forged callback could link the attacker's Slack user to the victim's GitHub account.
- The GitHub login callback keeps the refresh token and expiry in the session. The Slack link stores them, and `freshToken` refreshes an expired token before running a command.
- The login button for unlinked users now has a URL. It was previously passed the team id instead of the context.
- Removed the unused duplicate `auth` app from the slackbot package. Setup steps are in `packages/slackbot/README.md`.
- Added `packages/app/test/apps/slack.test.ts`, covering the full link flow, forged state, bad signatures, unlinked users and token refresh.

本地产物只 mock 已知只读启动 API，阻断其它外部请求和 API 写入。项目直链预置一个隔离的 IndexedDB 项目，不预加载应用模块。检查工作台/画布挂载、启动遮罩移除、JS 异常与必需 JS/CSS 加载；固定 Playwright 运行时放在仓库外，不改 workspace lockfile。

## Evidence

- **Before:** 在 macmini2 独立快照构建实际事故提交 `0ff43cf2`，构建成功；新检查立即以非零退出，捕获与线上一致的 `Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'Activity')`，堆栈指向 `react-vendor-pzdp9nkm.js` 与 `zustand-BaN3tIGL.js`。
  **After:** 回滚基线上的公开版和 `private.lock` 钉住的收费版真实 dist，首页与项目直链全部通过。
- 12 个测试通过：真实 ESM 循环初始化、缺失 JS/CSS、残留启动遮罩、直链失败、画布未挂载、离线可选字体、凭证跨域匿名启动、API 写请求拦截，以及最终检查失败后不调用 Wrangler。
- macmini2：`pnpm exec biome check --write .`、`pnpm lint`、全包 `pnpm typecheck`（含 overlay）、`pnpm lint:sh` 通过；本地 `actionlint`、`git diff --check` 通过。独立静态代码评审无阻塞项。
- 启动检查不替代登录、真实云项目数据和生成业务验收；本次不调用付费生成。

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

可通过回滚恢复发布脚本，无数据库或协议变更。合入 test 使用 merge commit，以保留 main 祖先，满足测试部署的分支守卫。

**Blast Radius:** release

启动异常将提前阻止前端上传，生产现有产物保留；浏览器安装和检查增加 CI/发布耗时。此 PR 的目标是 test，验收前保持 main 不变。

author: davidmundackal
body:
## Why
A concurrency audit (2026-10-11) found a problem when the notch windows are rebuilt for a display or resolution change.

- `tearDownAllWindows` reuses the same `KannuViewModel` but never clears its scroll-gesture and auto-close suppression tokens, or its popover flags.
- Those are only released by the views' `onDisappear`, which the view model's own comment calls unreliable for these panels.
- So if the pointer is over a suppressing view (the timer ruler, the side column, the name field), or a popover is open, at the moment of the rebuild, the notch afterwards never auto-closes, or stops reacting to scrolling.

## What this changes
- New `KannuViewModel.resetTransientInteractionState()` clears both token sets and every popover flag that `hasAnyActivePopovers()` reads.
- `tearDownAllWindows` calls it after the old window is closed and released, so no `onChange` on the old view runs against the cleared state.
- New `NotchTeardownRulesTests`, a source scan with planted offenders, checks two things:
  - the teardown calls the reset;
  - the reset clears every flag `hasAnyActivePopovers()` reads, so a new flag can't be added to one without the other. The flag scan also matches `@Published private(set) var`.

## Testing
- The full suite passes (855 tests) and the app compiles, with compile steps for `KannuApp.swift` and `KannuViewModel.swift`.
- Not tested on a real display change; this is in the local test build.

body:
Every settlement poll previously scanned all Orders, Outbox and Charges and fetched two PITR bookmarks. Payment polling now uses indexed Payment Key reads; runner setup/teardown use exact persisted Run IDs. Full ledger/bookmarks require an explicit operator request. Missing or ambiguous scopes refuse instead of falling back to full scans.

Nullable Run ID columns and indexes preserve legacy Key readback without guessing ownership from key prefixes. Native SQL cursor rowsRead is exposed for the three readback SELECTs only; it is not whole-account metering. Queue idempotency and unknown-outcome readback remain intact. The runner repeats a same-key observation if separate DO snapshots briefly yield incomplete PAID evidence.

Validation: 22 Node/source-SQL/local-workerd controls, 3 site controls and verify-medium doctor passed; local workerd proves scoped cursor reads stay constant as unrelated rows grow. Existing interface and DR controls remain green. Wrangler config and Free subscriptions unchanged; no paid resources or preview production bindings added.

Matching-head CI passed: https://github.com/ed3c/medium-compiler/actions/runs/38154849462 on 08c8fde8c9f198519b638c66d7d1ffbdbc76ea46. Native Workers Builds succeeded on main 545b4298e199684e4d8bdcb22da771988b10b8d8 (build 4bfac958-353f-4631-86ed-fc3d73ba6a2b); version 0034619b-5724-459b-95aa-3b7008e2c38b serves 100% and API v3 was observed in the owner browser.

Native controls: on the same 52-order ledger, full readback consumed 156 SQL cursor rows, exact 4-order Run consumed 28, Key consumed 3. Legacy keys remain readable. Missing/ambiguous scope refused; prefix-neighbor Run stayed isolated; Lost Reply was observed as PENDING with one persisted charge, then PAID after redelivery/readback. Duplicate admission published zero additional messages; changed amount/Run returned 409.

Native bounded baseline (PAID latency includes polling/network delay):
- Before, 1 arrival/s x 4s: 4/4 PAID; p50/p95/p99 3.6895/4.2144/4.28208s.
- First after: 4/4 PAID; 6.0155/6.3115/6.3511s; 59 readback cursor rows.
- Warm after: 4/4 PAID; 3.7955/3.96435/3.97767s; 51 readback cursor rows.
- Burst, 2 arrivals/s x 8s: 16/16 PAID; 8.9375/13.18525/13.36585s; 274 readback cursor rows. Observed completion rate 0.7651 PAID/s across settlement, not sustained 2 PAID/s.
All runs: one matching charge and one publish per order, zero failed/dropped iterations. Small samples do not establish a latency SLO or a statistically significant speedup.

Actual Cloudflare minute metrics (two DO namespaces, not just readback): old-run 00:08–00:09 Taipei window 1953 rows read/52 written; warm 00:24 window 714 read/60 written. Warm window includes nearby manual observation/alarm activity; first after includes index migration. These are observed platform windows, not isolated per-payment attribution. Queue Last-24h counter moved 281→374 operations during this task; final backlog 0. Account Free subscriptions were freshly read; no paid upgrade occurred. Last-24h totals do not prove today's remaining quota or a whole-account $0 invoice.

Remaining cost risk: existing Outbox COUNT/MIN queries scan history, so the 98.1% Key-readback reduction does not apply to total application rows or scale linearly with history. Queue's 10k operations/day yields only an ideal 3333 small, retry-free messages/day, before other usage. Real sustained capacity, Queue outage/DLQ recovery and PITR restore were not proven by this smoke.

Migration note: old Provider code used positional INSERT; after the nullable column is added, rollback code must use explicit column names. Worker rollback does not reverse SQLite schema.

author: zy4
body:
Item 1 of the gaps list: the CLI could check packages but not produce them. This PR adds the package side; creating signed evidence statements is the next PR.

```sh
verified issue draft.json --trust trust.json -o package.json
verified sign package.json --key-id my-issuer-key --key issuer.key --trust trust.json -o signed.json

# Or keep the issuer's key elsewhere (HSM, KMS, another machine):
verified sign package.json --signing-input-out input.bin
verified sign package.json --key-id my-issuer-key --signature-file signature.txt --trust trust.json -o signed.json
```

## What each command does

- **`issue`** reads a draft: the library's `Draft` as one JSON file, documented in the new `docs/sdk/issuing.md`. It holds the contract, the claim, the signed evidence with its bodies, and the times. There's **no member for a decision**: it's computed. The command writes what `verified_verifier::issue` returns, and that function returns a package only if a verifier holding your registry reproduces its decision. Anything else exits 1 and writes nothing.
- **`sign`** adds an issuer signature through `countersign`, in one of two ways:
  - **External** (`--signing-input-out`, then `--signature-file`): the key never touches this machine, as decision 0007 prefers.
  - **Local** (`--key`): a PEM PKCS #8 Ed25519 key, the form `openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519` writes.
    - Only that exact form is read; an encrypted or other key is refused.
    - The key is held in memory that's wiped when dropped (`zeroize`, plus `ed25519-dalek`'s `zeroize` feature).
    - Nothing read from the file is ever printed, which a test checks.

  Either way, the signed package is written only if the signature counts under your registry. An evidence key can't sign a decision (`ISSUER_SIGNATURE_INVALID`).
- **Neither command overwrites an existing file.**

## Tests

- Issuing an example's draft gives `supported.json` back **byte for byte**. Signing that with the test issuer key gives `supported-issuer-signed.json` back byte for byte, both with `--key` and with a signature made externally over `--signing-input-out`.
- **Refusals write nothing:**
  - evidence whose body doesn't match its statement exits 1 with no file;
  - signing with the evidence key exits 1 with no file, and the key isn't echoed.
- **Bad input means the command couldn't run (exit 2):**
  - an existing output file is kept;
  - a draft with an extra `decision` member is refused.
- I also tried a key generated with `openssl genpkey`: it's read correctly, and refused only because it isn't the issuer key in the registry.

The full suite passes (256 tests), and the library API is unchanged: the API check against `v0.1.1` passes.

## Decision 0013 is amended

It said "No command" and "No keys". The amendment records the two commands and what still holds:

- the library takes no key;
- a draft has no decision member;
- nothing a verifier would refuse is written;
- external signing is the preferred route.

## Dependency

Adds **`zeroize` 1.9.1** (Apache-2.0 OR MIT) and enables `ed25519-dalek`'s `zeroize` feature for the CLI. `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` is regenerated, and its CI check will confirm that.

This PR and #36 (`verified trust`) both touch `cli.rs`, `main.rs` and the README. Whichever merges second will need a small rebase, which I'll do.

- **App gửi lại sau lỗi mạng ghi trùng**: bán nhanh / thu tiền báo "quá lâu" mà máy chủ đã ghi, bấm lại là thêm đơn / phiếu. Thêm mã lần gửi (`maGhi`): máy chủ nhớ kết quả 10 phút.
- **App, màn "Đã bán"** vẫn hiện "Còn nợ" + nút Thu tiền sau khi đã thu → thu trùng.
- **Phiếu trả lại tiền khách** (số âm): mở trên web rồi Lưu biến thành phiếu thu dương (lệch công nợ, sổ quỹ gấp đôi). Máy chủ giữ số âm; in ra Phiếu chi.
- **Trả máy sửa chữa / khách trả hàng gửi hai lần** → hai đơn, hai phiếu thu / nhập kho, trả tiền hai lần. Giữ chỗ trong khóa. **Lưu phiếu sửa chữa từ bản cũ** ghi đè trạng thái "Đã trả khách" → đọc lại trong khóa.
- **Lịch trả góp**: thu / hủy nhầm đợt khi lịch vừa đổi; **phiếu của đợt** xóa / đổi tiền được ở màn Thu tiền → chặn.
- **Điện thoại bị đăng xuất từ xa** có thể được cấp lại phiên → dựng lại phiên trong khóa.
- **Ngày theo giờ Việt Nam trên web và app** (máy để múi giờ khác: sau 0 giờ VN đơn mới bị lọc mất, phiếu thu app ghi ngày hôm trước).
- **Khách trùng** khi nhập '+84 …', '+84 0…' hoặc hai số cách nhau ' - '.
- **Email / thông báo sáng gửi mỗi ngày** vì máy cũ bán hết (tồn 0) nằm mãi trong "Hàng sắp hết". Phiếu thu trống hình thức bị sổ quỹ tính vào ngân hàng → mặc định tiền mặt.
- Đơn đã hủy đang gắn với phiếu thu / hợp đồng: lưu là mất liên kết. Tổng tiền màn hình cộng cả dòng không tên.
- Nợ nhà cung cấp tính nhầm khách; kiểm kho nhận nhầm mã lạ; nhãn phiếu trả hàng; nhân bản hợp đồng bỏ sót CCCD; app ghi đè số mới bằng số cũ; thử thông báo báo "đã gửi" sai.

## Lỗi giao diện
- **Logo cửa hàng chỉ còn một chấm** (cả web thật). "₫" rơi dòng. Màn soạn trên điện thoại: một hàng nút vuốt ngang. Bảng dòng hàng vừa 1280 px. App: ô "Giảm giá" co lại.

## Mượt hơn
- Danh sách dài vẽ dần (chuyển màn nhanh ~2×), nút **Hiện thêm** khi quá 300 dòng.
- Máy chủ: lệnh từ web đọc mỗi trang tính một lần, nhớ dòng tiêu đề (lưu đơn 20 → 14 lần đọc…). Màn "Khách còn nợ" của app chỉ đọc 3 trang. Hẹn giờ sáng đọc dữ liệu một lần cho cả email và thông báo. Xóa mã thông báo hết hạn trong một lần khóa.

## Cố ý chưa làm (cần chủ cửa hàng quyết / ghi chú)
- Hoàn tiền khi trả hàng có thu máy cũ; định nghĩa "Đã thu hôm nay" (app, email) khác sổ quỹ.
- Trả hàng cùng mặt hàng nhiều dòng giá khác nhau; trả hàng, lưu lịch trả góp, ghi máy cũ chưa nguyên tử; hai quầy cùng thu một mẫu máy cũ có thể tạo hai mặt hàng; bán nhanh lỗi xuất kho để lại khách mới; quản trị giới hạn cửa hàng vẫn thấy điện thoại mọi cửa hàng (hiện chỉ 1 cửa hàng); app tự tính lại công nợ Tổng quan sau khi ghi.
- Mã xác thực chữ ký: **không đổi** (đổi sẽ làm mọi chữ ký cũ báo không hợp lệ).

## Kiểm tra
- `node dev/kiem-tra.js` (gồm API app, dữ liệu thử): đạt; mỗi sửa có kiểm thử, các sửa chính đã thử bỏ thì kiểm thử báo lỗi.
- `dev/kiem-trinh-duyet.js` 29/29 và `dev/kiem-trinh-duyet-app.js`: đạt (web/app đã chạy ở UTC, America/Los_Angeles, Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh).
- `mobile`: `npm run kiem-tra`, `expo lint`: đạt.
- Review mã 8 lượt, phủ mọi file (#11, PR này, HopDong.gs, Api.gs, Code.gs, Index.html, mobile/src, DichVu/SoQuy/EmailSang); không thấy lỗ hổng chèn mã.

author: paradispartiet
body:
## Kvalitetsrevisjon av 46 eksisterende Aalesund-profiler

Rotårsak: P1 klassifiserte én vellykket kamphandling som varig `strengths`, og motoren tolket det som direkte dokumentert spillerstyrke med attributtløft.

### Faktisk endring
- **32** tidligere styrkeposter flyttet til `P1_NEW_EVENT_ONLY`: spillere, historiske kamphandlinger, kilder og gamle tokens bevares; `strengths` er tom i runtime.
- **14** beholdes som mer varig dokumenterte kvaliteter med `evidenceKind` og konkret `playingStyle`.
- Tor Hogne Aarøy: `heading`, `hold_up_play`, `combination_play`, kilde fra Aftenposten 2008.
- Michael Barrantes: `vision`, `simple_passing` fra VG-lupen 2014 i stedet for isolert dødballhendelse.
- Fredrik Ulvestad: `set_pieces` med presis **straffespark**-avgrensning fra VG 2014; innleggs-/avslutningshendelser gir ikke lenger automatisk styrke.
- P1-audit utvidet med kildekategori, eksklusiv identitet, event-til-strength-sperre og fordelingsintegritet.
- Dekningsrapport viser hendelsesbelegg og `playingStyle` separat uten å telle hendelseskilder som styrker.
- [Metode og full revisjon](https://github.com/Paradispartiet/HistoryGo-FootballManager/blob/quality/aalesund-p1-evidence-vs-strengths-20261011/docs/AALESUND_P1_EVIDENCE_QUALITY_REVIEW.md).

**Korrigert Aalesund P1-status:** 14 dokumenterte varige styrkeprofiler + 32 historiske hendelsesprofiler + 23 foreløpig uten kvalifiserende kilde = 69 eksklusive identiteter.

Ingen endringer i spilleridentiteter, stillinger, råkatalog, klassehøyder eller spillmotorens vekter. Event-only registeret er ny datakategori i P1-overlegget, og krever derfor **full CI** og relevante regresjonstester før merge.

author: zhangshenghang
body:
## Purpose of this PR

This PR fixes a batch of real documentation bugs found by auditing the docs against the Java source code on the current `dev` branch. All fixes are backed by code evidence; no formatting-only or cosmetic churn is included.

## Documentation issues found and what was changed

### Clickhouse connector (wrong type mappings)

- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/source/Clickhouse.md`: the doc claimed `DateTime -> TIME`. The source converter (`TypeConvertUtil`) maps ClickHouse `DateTime` (object class `LocalDateTime`) to `LOCAL_DATE_TIME_TYPE`, i.e. `TIMESTAMP`; `LOCAL_TIME_TYPE` is never produced. Also split the over-lumped integer row to match the actual object-class mapping (`Int8` -> `TINYINT`, `Int16`/`UInt8` -> `SMALLINT`, `Int32`/`UInt16` -> `INT`, `Int64`/`UInt32`/`UInt64` -> `BIGINT`), verified against the clickhouse-client 0.3.2-patch11 `ClickHouseDataType` object classes.
- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/sink/Clickhouse.md`: the doc claimed `TIME -> DateTime`. `ClickhouseTypeConverter.reconvert` maps `TIME` to `STRING` (this converter generates the `${rowtype_fields}` DDL used by `save_mode_create_template`). Added the missing `TIMESTAMP -> DateTime64` and `BOOLEAN -> Bool` rows, split `TINYINT -> Int8`, `SMALLINT -> Int16`, `INT -> Int32` per the converter, and fixed the example that used Kafka's port `9092` for a ClickHouse HTTP host (everything else in the doc uses `8123`).

### File connectors

- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/source/ObsFile.md`: the STS example used `hadoop_obs_properties`, an option that does not exist anywhere in the codebase (`ObsFileBaseOptions` defines only `access_key`/`access_secret`/`endpoint`/`bucket`, and `ObsConf` maps exactly those three into the Hadoop config). Rewrote the example to use the real options and documented that no extra Hadoop OBS property pass-through (e.g. session token) exists. Also removed a duplicated `sheet_name` row in the zh table.
- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/sink/OssFile.md` and `docs/zh/connectors/sink/CosFile.md`: the CDC schema-evolution example block used the wrong plugin name `LocalFile` for an OSS/COS sink (silently misleading for copy-paste users). Changed to `OssFile` / `CosFile` with the connector's required credential options, aligned with the correct en CosFile example.
- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/source/LocalFile.md`: `file_format_type` was marked required, but `LocalFileSourceFactory` registers it as `.optional(...)` (only `tables_configs`/`path` are exclusive-required). Marked it optional.
- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/sink/{CosFile,OssJindoFile}.md`: added the `enable_header_write`, `schema_save_mode`, `data_save_mode` option rows that every sibling file-sink doc documents and that the shared base sink (`FileBaseSinkOptions`, read unconditionally by `BaseMultipleTableFileSink`) supports.
- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/sink/ObsFile.md`: added missing shared sink option rows (`tmp_path`, `filename_extension`, `encoding`, `csv_string_quote_mode`, `enable_header_write`, `schema_save_mode`, `data_save_mode`), limited to the formats the doc claims for this connector.
- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/sink/BosFile.md`: added 10 missing shared sink option rows (excel/csv/cdc/save-mode options), matching `FileBaseSinkOptions` defaults.
- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/source/OssFile.md`: added `archive_compress_codec` (enum `zip`/`tar`/`tar.gz`/`gz`/`none`, default `none`), `enable_file_split` (default `false`, text/json/csv/parquet per `FileFormat.supportFileSplit()`) and `file_split_size` (default `134217728`) rows that other file-source docs already document.

### CDC production cookbook

- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/cdc-production-cookbook.md`: the MySQL-CDC examples used `exactly-once = true`, but the option key is `exactly_once` (underscore, no fallback keys in `SourceOptions`), so the documented config silently runs at-least-once. The Postgres-CDC example used `schema-names`, but the Postgres connector option is `schema-name` (`PostgresIncrementalSourceOptions.SCHEMA_NAME`); the Oracle example correctly keeps `schema-names` (its code key is plural).

### Engine docs

- `docs/{en,zh}/engines/event-listener.md`: the `EventType` table documented `READER_OPEN`, `READER_CLOSE`, `WRITER_OPEN`, `WRITER_CLOSE`, which do not exist in `org.apache.seatunnel.api.event.EventType` (there is no `WRITER_OPEN` at all). Replaced them with the real `LIFECYCLE_*` values and added the undocumented enum values (`SCHEMA_CHANGE_CHANGE_COLUMN`, `SCHEMA_CHANGE_RENAME_TABLE`, `SCHEMA_CHANGE_ALTER_TABLE_COMMENT`, `SCHEMA_CHANGE_ALTER_COLUMN_COMMENT`, `SCHEMA_CHANGE_RESTORE`, `READER_MESSAGE_DELAYED`), each mapped to the event class that actually returns it. Fixed the example imports (the classes live in `org.apache.seatunnel.api.table.schema.event`, `org.apache.seatunnel.api.source.event`, `org.apache.seatunnel.api.sink.event`, not `org.apache.seatunnel.api.event.*`) and the `switch` case labels.
- `docs/{en,zh}/engines/zeta/stain-trace.md`: documented `stain-trace-sample-interval` as the engine parameter, but the canonical key is `stain-trace-sample-rate` (`ServerConfigOptions.STAIN_TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE`); the `-interval` spelling is only a backward-compatible alias in `YamlSeaTunnelDomConfigProcessor`. Now documents `-rate` as primary and mentions the alias.

### Others

- `docs/{en,zh}/connectors/source/Iceberg.md`: the `table_list` row now documents the per-item split tuning keys `splitSize` / `splitLookback` / `splitOpenFileCost` supported by `SourceTableConfig` (deserialized with a default Jackson mapper, so camelCase); the zh table's three Kerberos rows used `no` instead of `否` in the required column.
- `docs/{en,zh}/transforms/sql.md`: `plugin_input` was typed `string`, but it is `List<String>` (`ConnectorCommonOptions.PLUGIN_INPUT`) and `SQLTransform` reads element 0; fixed the type and clarified the multi-table behavior.

## Were both English and Chinese docs checked?

Yes. Every fix was applied to both `docs/en` and `docs/zh` where the same content exists in both languages. 30 files changed in total (15 en / 15 zh).

## Duplicate check (last 7 days)

Checked all open docs PRs before starting: #12709, #12693, #12679, #12641, #12621, #12615, #12602, #12570, #12514 (another author), #12459. Several initially planned fixes were already covered by those PRs (e.g. PostgreSQL-CDC `schema-name`, SqlServer-CDC `connect.timeout.ms`, MongoDB-CDC `format`, `engine-jar-storage-mode` `enable` key, `security.md` `enable-http` default, `telemetry.md` endpoints, `user-command.md` checkpoint options, `state-storage-and-recovery.md` checkpoint keys/CLI/IMap names, `rest-api-v2` /log port). All overlapping fixes were dropped from this PR; every remaining fix above was verified not to overlap with the diffs of those PRs.

## Verification

- Verified each claim against the source before editing: type converters (`TypeConvertUtil`, `ClickhouseTypeConverter`, plus the `ClickHouseDataType` object classes decompiled from clickhouse-client 0.3.2-patch11), option definitions (`ObsFileBaseOptions`, `FileBaseSinkOptions`, `FileBaseSourceOptions`, `SourceOptions`, `ServerConfigOptions`, `EventType`), factory option rules (`LocalFileSourceFactory`, Obs/Oss/Jindo sink factories) and event-class-to-EventType mappings.
- Ran a table-structure check over all 30 changed files (column-count consistency per table): 0 issues.
- Ran a relative-link check over all changed docs: 0 broken links.
- Grepped the changed files for the old wrong keys/values (`exactly-once =`, `hadoop_obs_properties`, `stain-trace-sample-interval:`, port `9092`, `LocalFile {` in OSS/COS examples): no leftovers.
- Did not run the full Docusaurus build (pnpm install/build) because the changes are markdown-only and the table/link checks above cover the syntax surface touched; happy to run it if reviewers prefer.

author: adammiribyan
body:
`superfind show --json` gives each commit in `outcomes` a `body`: its message after the subject. It's masked like the turns before it's cut to 2,000 bytes, with `…` where it was cut, and never cut inside a `[masked …]` placeholder or a character. The bodies share 12,000 bytes or half of `--max-bytes`, whichever is less, newest commit first; `--max-bytes 0` lifts that. A body is empty for a pull request, and for a commit that a squash merge carried after its branch was deleted. `outcomes.go` already read `%b` for every commit, so there's no extra git pass. Plain `show` text is unchanged.

Why: on coachspect, squash merges land with bare titles, so the reasons live in the branch commits' messages, and `git log origin/master` never shows them (sfd-evidence: 22 of 22 in-commit citations were branch-only commits).

## Measured

18 coachspect keepers, read-only through a scratch HOME and cache, judged by reading the masked output.

- **Frozen path** (`blame FILE`, then `show ID --json`, all within 12 KB): **no change**. Within that frame `--max-bytes` gets small. With many commits, half of it spread over the bodies leaves most of them `…`. Example: H22's session has 19 commits.
- **The skill's recipe, `show ID --json --tail 1`** (not frozen; I added it after the frozen run, so treat it as indicative): bodies state the finding for **3 keepers**:
  - H1: the text lockfile needs Bun ≥ 1.2; 1.1.8 → 1.3.14.
  - H13: the draft broadcast is still in flight when the test clears the composer.
  - H22: Capybara's `reset!` wipes cookies while a response can still re-set them.

  On main, the outcomes state none of the three: H22 had one of its two terms, from a subject. The outcomes JSON grows accordingly. Example: 5.8 → 13.0 KB for H22's 19 commits, and 11.5 → 19.2 KB for the largest session, at the default `--max-bytes`.

Limits: the body is git's, so it can be wrong or stale like any commit message. A commit found only inside a squash gets no body. The squash body's per-commit section could be split out later; not done here.

## Tests

- `tests/test_outcomes.py`:
  - All three vendors' commits carry their bodies.
  - A key placed across the 2,000-byte cut is masked first. A clip-first build leaks a key fragment and fails this test, as does main, which has no `body`.
  - Eight commits share the budget, newest first, also at `--max-bytes 3000`. This test caught a negative-budget panic during development.
- Go: a rune-boundary cut, no cut inside a mask, invalid UTF-8.
- `test_llms` checks that `llms-full.txt` documents `body`.
- `go vet`, `go test ./...`, and the 401 Python behavior tests all pass.

## Reviews

- **Codex.** Fixed:
  - `scripts/llms.py`'s field list lacked `body`, which broke the reference and the release asset.
  - A duplicate `[Unreleased]` heading.
  - Invalid UTF-8 could exceed the cap after JSON encoding; it's now replaced before masking.
- **Fable.** Fixed:
  - Bodies had no total bound. A 40-commit session took a `--max-bytes 1000` show to 83 KB; hence the shared budget tied to `--max-bytes`.
  - A cut inside `[masked …]`.
  - An untested rune backoff.
  - Inconsistent wording across README, help, CHANGELOG and llms.
  - Double `TrimSpace`; `BodyBytes` was exported needlessly.
- Left for later (Fable's design notes): recovering a squashed commit's own section from the squash body, and a `body` for pull-request outcomes.

author: lhaseparth2610
body:
## What & why

A Gemini CLI agent can't write to its own hive folder. Gemini's file tools refuse any path outside the workspace (`Path not in workspace`), and the agent's folder (`hive/agents/<id>/`, which holds its `memory.md` and inbox) and the hive root sit outside its working folder. Claude agents get these folders through their settings file and Codex agents through `--add-dir`; Gemini agents got nothing. This is gap 4 of "Make a second engine (Codex first) ready for an office" in `TODOS.md`.

This change gives Gemini the same folders `sandboxWritableDirs` gives Codex, in two places:

- **`context.includeDirectories` in the per-agent settings file.** Gemini CLI up to 0.59 reads it, and merges it with the owner's own include directories.
- **`--include-directories` on the command line,** which every version reads. This is needed because **Gemini CLI 0.60.0 and later skip a system settings file in a folder the user owns**, and the per-agent file lives in the agent's folder. The flag splits values on commas, so `geminiIncludeDirArg` passes a path with a comma (an office inside "Acme, LLC") relative to the agent's cwd, which Gemini resolves against.

Gemini keeps workspace folders in a set of real paths, so a folder named in both places counts once. Gemini isn't in `BUILD_ENGINES` yet, so nothing changes for owners today; this removes one blocker to offering it.

Closes #183

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Build / CI

## Before and after

**Tested live with a real Gemini API key** (`gemini-2.5-flash`, real Gemini CLI). The agent is built by `HiveManager.ensureAgent` from this branch, with the office at `Acme, LLC/Office` and the agent in `Acme, LLC/Support`. The model is asked to save a note to the agent's `memory.md`.

| Gemini CLI | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.63.0 (current) | ❌ `write_file` refused: `Path not in workspace ... resolves outside the allowed workspace directories` | ✅ `write_file` succeeded, `memory.md` holds the note |
| 0.59.0 | ❌ `write_file` refused: `Path not in workspace` | ✅ `write_file` succeeded, `memory.md` holds the note |

The model had only `write_file`, `read_file` and `list_directory` (no shell or web tools), in throwaway folders with an isolated Gemini home.

<details>
<summary>Offline repro anyone can run (no key needed), and why the settings file alone isn't enough</summary>

Gemini CLI's own `--fake-responses-non-strict` test mode replays a canned model turn that calls `write_file` on the agent's `memory.md` and on a note in a folder the owner listed in their own `~/.gemini/settings.json`. Variant A is `main`, B is the settings file alone, C is this PR.

```
| Gemini CLI | Variant          | memory.md written | "Path not in workspace" | settings file skipped | owner note written |
|------------|------------------|-------------------|-------------------------|-----------------------|--------------------|
| 0.59.0     | A. main today    | no                | yes                     | no                    | yes                |
| 0.59.0     | B. settings only | yes               | no                      | no                    | yes                |
| 0.59.0     | C. this PR       | yes               | no                      | no                    | yes                |
| 0.63.0     | A. main today    | no                | yes                     | yes                   | yes                |
| 0.63.0     | B. settings only | no                | yes                     | yes                   | yes                |
| 0.63.0     | C. this PR       | yes               | no                      | yes                   | yes                |
```

On 0.63.0 the settings file alone (B) is still refused, because Gemini prints `Security Warning: Skipping system settings file ...`. That's why the folders also go on the command line. The owner's own include directory works in every run, so their setup isn't disturbed. The script is in the linked issue; it isn't added to the repo because it downloads Gemini CLI.

</details>

## How I tested it

- **OS:** Windows 11 Pro (x64) 10.0.26200, Node 24.19.0
- **New tests** in `test/auto-mode-sandbox.test.cjs`: a Gemini agent whose office sits in `Acme, LLC` gets its folders in the settings file and the comma-free ones on the command line as relative paths, with the protocol seed still last. `geminiIncludeDirArg` has its own test. Both fail on `main` and pass here.
- **Updated test** in `test/hive-hook-node.test.cjs`: the Gemini spawn test no longer assumes `-i` is the first argument.
- **Live** with a real Gemini API key on Gemini CLI 0.63.0 and 0.59.0 (table above), on this branch rebased onto `main` at 303b620b.
- **`npm run typecheck`** passes.
- **`npm run test:focused`:** no new failures. 24 tests fail locally both with and without this change (an identical set on the unchanged base commit). They look specific to this Windows setup, mostly symlink tests. I expect CI to be green.
- **Not run:** `npm run build`, and the full app with a Gemini team member (Gemini isn't offered in setup yet).

## Notes for review

- **Access stays level across engines.** A Gemini agent's workspace now holds the same folders Claude and Codex agents can already write to (agent folder, hive root, memory palace), nothing more.
- **Related, not fixed here:** on Gemini CLI 0.60+ the per-agent settings file is skipped as a whole, so Gemini agents' hooks never load, and an untrusted folder blocks auto mode. Filed separately as #ISSUE2_NUMBER to keep this PR to one change.
- **No overlap with #176**, which adds a background-task runner and doesn't touch the spawn path.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test:focused` passes. (No new failures; the local failures are identical on the base commit. Relying on CI.)
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds. (Not run locally.)
- [x] This PR is **one change**. Unrelated fixes belong in their own PR.
- [x] I read the diff myself before opening this, and there is no debug output, commented-out code, or unrelated formatting churn in it.
- [x] Any new UI derives from `DESIGN.md` / `tokens.ts`. (No UI changes.)
- [x] If I added art, it's my own or compatibly licensed. (No art.)

author: niksedk
body:
Review of both features after [VideoHelp thread 419443](https://forum.videohelp.com/threads/419443-is-there-an-AI-tool-for-automatically-fixing-the-timing-of-the-lines), tested on Friends S01E01–E02 (retail SRT from the MKV, Canary CTC aligner, Parakeet check).

### Improve time codes
- **Mistimed overlaps survived.** Any overlap in the input counted as "on purpose" (`Tidy`, `Settle`, `RoughSync.Apply`), so after a correct re-time 80–100 overlaps (median 0.2 s) were left per episode. Now only an overlap of ≥ 0.5 s *and* half the shorter line (two speakers at once, a sign over dialogue) is kept (`SubtitleRetimer.OverlapsOnPurpose`). Measured: 82/102/90/100 → 0/4/0/0, start accuracy unchanged (offset +3 s: 90% within 0.1 s of the clean-input result).
- **Song lyrics** (line starting/ending with ♪/♫, or wrapped in `#`), **positioned signs** (`{\pos}`/`{\move}`) and **ASSA comments** are no longer aligned as speech.
- **Frame mode:** moved lines are snapped to frames, keeping the minimum gap (`SubtitleRetimer.SnapToFrames`).

### Import plain text
- **Ends too short.** `ApplyTimeCodes` used min(speech, reading time), so quick speech vanished with seconds of silence after it. Ends are now held for the maximum CPS, room permitting: lines over max CPS 46 → 17 on E01, none of the 17 with room after it.
- **Alignment can be cancelled** (Cancel/Esc, closing the window); OK and both align buttons are disabled while it runs, so lines still being written to can no longer be handed to the main window. ffmpeg's output is now read (a full pipe could stall the dialog).
- **The "estimated lines" warning never fired** (`UnalignedLines` was always 0). `Result.EstimatedLines` now counts lines placed by reading time; new language string.
- **The dialog's Gap (ms) was ignored** by both align modes; it is now passed to `ForcedAligner` and `ScriptSyncService`.
- Unexpected errors (ffmpeg/engine missing, I/O) are logged and shown instead of escaping the command.

### Not included
The forced aligner's `accept == 0` skip-ahead is unreachable. I tried two ways of making it fire when the script lacks a scene, tested with a 3-minute scene cut from the script. Neither measured better than leaving it alone: the narrow version was slightly worse on the missing scene; the broad one hurt complete scripts (lines over 0.5 s off: 25 → 32 on E02). So it is left as is.

`English.json` was regenerated by the build and also picks up 4 TTS keys missing on main from #15930.

### Tests
New unit tests for the overlap rule (they fail with the old rule), frame snapping, lyrics/sign detection, the max CPS hold and the gap parameter. 1144 related tests pass.

body:
Adds a standalone Hakha Chin (`cnh`) speech-to-text prototype using Meta `facebook/mms-1b-all`, alongside the existing Whisper apps. Browser PCM capture sends 2–5 second chunks to the local model backend, flushes the captured remainder on Stop, skips quiet input before inference, and shows timestamps and decode latency. Start/Stop/Clear, a bounded queue, CPU/CUDA selection, pinned dependencies, noncommercial attribution, privacy disclosure, and local/Mac/Colab setup are included.

The recorder keeps audio in memory and sends it only to the model backend (through Gradio's tunnel when `--share` is explicitly selected). `MMS_REALTIME.md` includes a reproducible comparison procedure using the same consented recordings and the exported V6 model, with verbatim outputs and CER/WER when human references exist.

Validation:
- All 24 regression tests pass, including normalization/resampling, silence bypass, chunk order, partial flush, errors, and HTTP input validation.
- Real MMS revision `3d33597edbdaaba14a8e858e2c8caa76e3cec0cd` loaded on CPU; model adapter and tokenizer both selected `cnh` with matching vocabularies.
- Empty/silent input skipped inference and returned empty text. A synthetic tone exercised both real model inference and the final HTTP endpoint; this is not recognition accuracy evidence.
- Headless Chromium with a synthetic microphone and fake decoder verified full windows, final partial audio, ordered timestamps, Clear during an active request, and a phone-sized viewport without JavaScript errors.
- Python/JavaScript syntax, dependency compatibility, documentation snippets, and diff checks pass.

No consented native-speaker recording, reference transcript, exported V6 model, GPU, or physical phone was available. Native speech accuracy, CER/WER, paired benchmark results, GPU behavior, and Mac/Colab device deployment remain unverified. Meta's MMS weights are CC BY-NC 4.0; the prototype is for noncommercial evaluation.

Refs #24.

author: pontussandberg
body:
Follow Through could chain to ~3.8 hits/s: each landed hit cut the next windup by 72% and the cooldown by as much.

- **Follow Through** now gives the **next attack only** +100% attack speed if started within 1.5 s of a hit; a miss loses it. Chained hits: 30-tick swings, ~2.1 hits/s (base 1.07).
- **Attack speed is the windup.** `cooldown_ticks` is removed from attacks (every class had it equal to `windup_ticks`), and so is `AttackState::ready_at`. The next attack starts the tick the last goes off, so the attack and its animation can't diverge. "+X% attack speed" divides the windup by (1 + X).
- `follow_up` takes `attack_speed` instead of `faster`; the `{follow_up_speed}` placeholder replaces `{follow_up_faster}`. README, `classes.ron` docs and the stat frame are updated.

Targeted shared tests pass (attack, follow-up, class file); the full suite hasn't been run.

author: dw021213
body:
Closes #199

## 요약

봇은 모든 회의를 `.env` 의 `BE_WORKSPACE_ID` 하나로 보내서, 다른 팀이 웹에서 서버를 연결해도 그 연결을 보지 않았습니다. 이 PR 은 `/record` 때 BE 의 서버 조회(#197)로 워크스페이스를 찾아 매니페스트에 고정하고, 회의 생성·발화 저장·추출 등록·유사 검색이 그 값을 쓰게 합니다. `BE_WORKSPACE_ID` 설정은 지웁니다. 결정 기록 0021, 진행 로그 `ai/docs/basis_for_decision/member/2026-10-12-guild-workspace.md`.

**BE 계약 문서 `backend/docs/contracts/backend-ai-contract.md` 를 같이 고쳤습니다.** "봇 미구현" 이라 적힌 곳과 봇 설정 줄입니다. @wkddnjswns 확인 부탁드립니다.

## 바꾼 것

### 1. 서버로 워크스페이스를 찾아 고정 (`handoff.Handoff.workspace`, `/record`)
- 전: `/record` 때 `.env` 의 워크스페이스를 매니페스트에 적고 그 값으로 BE 회의를 만들었습니다
- 후: 서버 ID 로 조회해 매니페스트 `workspace_id` 에 고정하고 그 값으로 BE 회의를 만듭니다. 비어 있을 때만 묻고, 한 번 정하면 바꾸지 않습니다
- 어떻게: BE 회의를 만든 뒤 워크스페이스가 바뀌면 추출 등록이 400 `WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` 라서 다시 묻지 않습니다. 처리할 때 비어 있으면(조회가 실패했던 회의) 그때 다시 묻습니다

### 2. 연결 없는 서버 (409)

| 모드 | 전 | 후 |
|---|---|---|
| 봇 모드 | `.env` 워크스페이스로 들어감 | `/record` 때 연결 안내, 전사까지 해 채널에 회의록, BE 단계는 멈춤 |
| 워커 모드(운영) | 같음 | `/record` 때 연결 안내, 연결될 때까지 전사하지 않고 기다림, 기다리는 회의는 "앞에 N건" 에서 뺌 |

PM 이 웹 온보딩의 디스코드 연결 단계에서 서버를 연결하면, 봇·워커가 끝나지 않은 회의를 다시 집을 때 BE 에 다시 물어 이어서 처리합니다. 다시 묻는 간격은 1분입니다(봇 복구 루프 60초, 워커 루프는 10초지만 기다리는 회의는 1분에 한 번만 묻습니다). 운영(워커 모드)은 봇이 녹음만 저장하고 처리는 디스코드에 접속하지 않는 워커가 해서, 연결 전에 전사해도 채널에도 웹에도 보일 곳이 없습니다. 그래서 워커 모드만 연결될 때까지 전사를 미룹니다.

### 3. 조회 실패
- 일시 실패(연결 실패, 5xx)는 발화 저장 단계의 실패로 세어 기존 재시도 규칙(1·2·4·8분, 5번째 포기)을 따릅니다
- 401 은 설정 문제라 BE 단계를 건너뛰고 결과 보고에 적습니다

### 4. 판단 경로의 유사 검색 (`judge_path.build_extractor`)
- 전: 설정의 `BE_WORKSPACE_ID` 로 검색했습니다
- 후: 추출기가 회의의 `workspace_id` 를 인자로 받습니다. 없이 불리면 `/workspaces/None/...` 으로 가지 않고 오류로 멈춥니다

## 용어

| 용어 | 뜻 |
|---|---|
| 연결 | 웹 온보딩에서 디스코드 서버를 워크스페이스에 붙인 것. BE `Integration(provider=discord)` 에 서버 ID 가 남습니다 |
| 연결 없음 | 봇은 서버에 있는데 BE 에 연결이 없는 상태(웹에서 연결 해제, 온보딩 밖 초대 링크 등). 조회가 409 `INTEGRATION_NOT_CONNECTED` 를 줍니다 |
| 워커 모드 | 봇은 녹음만 저장하고 처리는 디스코드를 모르는 워커가 하는 운영 방식(`MM_PIPELINE_MODE=worker`) |

## 테스트

- 서버 조회와 고정, 연결 없음·일시 실패·토큰 거절, 연결 없는 회의가 멈췄다가 연결되면 이어짐, 판단 추출기가 회의 워크스페이스를 받음, `/record` 의 고정과 안내, 워커의 연결 대기와 대기열 제외
- develop 을 합친 뒤 전체 992 통과

```
cd ai && .venv/bin/python -m pytest        # 992 passed
```

## 배포

- 운영 BE 에서 팀 서버를 조회하면 지금 `.env` 와 같은 워크스페이스가 나옵니다(10/10 확인). 바꿔도 팀 회의가 들어가는 곳은 같습니다
- 배포 뒤 서버 `.env` 에서 `BE_WORKSPACE_ID` 와 `DISCORD_GUILD_ID` 를 빼고 봇·워커를 다시 띄웁니다. 팀 서버 1분 녹음이 같은 워크스페이스로 가는지, 명령이 모든 서버에 보이고 팀 서버에 두 번 보이지 않는지 확인합니다

## 이 PR 밖

- 연결 없는 서버는 테스트로만 확인했습니다
- #208 도 `judge_path.extract` 와 `recorder` 를 고칩니다. 나중에 머지되는 쪽이 충돌을 맞춥니다
- 이름 힌트를 BE 멤버 이름으로 바꾸는 일은 BE 에 봇용 멤버 조회가 생긴 뒤에 합니다

author: pabloguilherme01
body:
## Problema
A Central de Serviços executava busca completa e reconstrução da listagem no mesmo ciclo de renderização da digitação. Em celulares modestos, o campo podia competir com cálculo dos resultados e cartões. Não havia estado de processamento para distinguir contagem ainda desatualizada.

## Mudança restrita
- Usa `useDeferredValue` **apenas na consulta textual** da listagem oficial, mantendo teclado/campo responsivos. Categorias, recursos (contato/rota/online), salvos e links selecionados continuam imediatos.
- Mantém paginação vinculada ao termo efetivamente filtrado, reduzindo travamentos e saltos visuais ao mudar consulta.
- Durante a atualização de texto, exibe `Atualizando resultados…` em vez de contagem errada, marca resultados com `aria-busy`, e evita expor o estado vazio e botão Mostrar mais desatualizados.
- Sem dependências, caches novos, modificações de fontes, GPS, maps, API, PWA, worker ou offline.
- Teste Vitest de digitação, correspondência, restauração e filtro online; teste E2E Android Chromium / iOS WebKit em 320px, cobrindo zero resultados, recuperação, continuidade de busca com filtro Premium, sem overflow.
- Requer CI completo, E2E, smoke Pages, Responsive, Mobile QA, Security e CodeQL verdes no head antes do merge.

## Segurança e rollback
Mudança puramente de renderização, preserva dados locais/privacidade. Reversão via squash revert, sem migrações. Não há números de FPS sem medição física.

author: dany-fedorov
body:
## What

First bounded delta of WBS 080.20, Twilight Navigator (OpenSpec change `twilight-navigator-plan-reference`):

- **Burokrat contracts** declare `plan-reference` and `progress-receipt` v1 (`contracts/navigator-records.ts`): undeclared keys refused, embedded canonical-JSON SHA-256 digest verified on decode; `contracts/canonical.ts` (`canonicalJson`, `digestOf`, `verifyDigest`). `twib validate` accepts both kinds.
- **`twilight-navigator`** app (`apps/twilight-structure/twilight-navigator/cli`, binary `twin`), with the same layout as Dash's first slice:
  - `twin plan-reference`: WBS v6 plan export + requirements file → `tasks.json` + `plan-reference.json`, created exclusively with mode 0600, no clock, byte-stable; prints the digest.
  - `twin receipt-to-commands`: progress receipt + plan reference + task export → one WBS command batch (`setProgress`, `setMeasure`). Nothing is applied: records, not calls.
- Registration: `@twilight-burokrat/contracts` alias; Navigator `eslint.product.mjs` allowing exactly that alias and `@wbs/contracts`; tool-devsync name exception, inventory, graph-oracle pairs, `RESTART_PATHS`, effective-lint test; `LLM_README.md` line.

## Why

Navigator and Dash exchange records, not calls, but until now no record existed in code. Without one, every planning agent invents its own shape.

## Review fixes (Fable, "MERGE AFTER FIXES" @643d67e7) at 0aae0947
- **F1:** the forwarded organization cookie is now proven with a real selection binding (`gateway-browser-selection.controller.db.test.ts`):
  - own project: 204
  - foreign project: 404, the same as an absent one
  - removed member with their own still-valid cookie: 403 `not_a_member`
  - another user's genuine cookie pasted in: 403 `no_active_organization`, not `not_a_member`, because the cookie is bound to its owner's credential
- **Honest production behaviour:** be-01 still composes `NO_BOUND_ORGANIZATION`.
  - Before activation, every authenticated socket is granted every project. This is legacy access, identical to HTTP reads.
  - After activation, unless the selection binding is wired, every subscribe would be refused `no_active_organization`.
- **F2:**
  - A lease round now checks every held project at once.
  - At most one round is queued.
  - A test with 5 held projects and a 1.4 s be-01 asserts the ≤4.5 s bound and that a subscribe issued mid-round completes.
- **F3:** one transport failure is retried inside the same 1.5 s deadline. A deadline or an aborted check is never retried.
- **F4:** the batch route `POST /internal/gateway/browser-access {projectIds}` is recorded as a follow-up. Today's cost is about 83 req/s at 50 sockets × 5 projects.
- **F5:** `ws-ping.ts` now documents what the 1008-counting hop no longer proves: it does not prove `/internal/resume` reads the log for a real principal, and a be-01 with a wrong session key also passes.
- **Proofs:** five new faults, each watched fail (added to `verify.md`).
- **Reruns:** gw-01 152 pass; tool-smoke 46 pass; be-01 gateway and mounted suites 205 pass; lint:fast and typecheck green for gw-01, be-01 and tool-smoke; openspec validate and prettier clean.

## Assumptions

- Change name follows the design (`twilight-navigator-plan-reference`).
- `PlanReferenceRecord` adds `tasksDigest` (binds the task export) and `referenceDigest` (its own digest). `createdAt` = the export's `exportedAt`, so no clock is read.
- WBS ids use their own grammar (UUIDs may begin with a digit), not Burokrat's `OpaqueId`.
- **Receipt entries map to `setProgress` (step scope), not `setStatus` (work-item scope, which marks every step done).** This is flagged as DECISION NEEDED in the lane record.
- The export is validated with WBS's `planDocument` under deep undeclared-key rejection.
- The batch is checked against `postApiProjectsByIdCommands`' params/body shapes in tests. A runtime check would have no way to fail, because the batch is built from `PlanCommandWire`.
- Exit 2 for usage refusals (raised before any read), exit 1 for every other failure.
- The v6 fixture was written by WBS's own exporter over a memory source and contains no real data.

## Tests and proofs

Commands, results and the 26 watched faults are in `openspec/changes/twilight-navigator-plan-reference/verify.md`. Each fault has an adjacent `Proof:` comment. Observed results:
- `nx run-many -t test lint typecheck -p twilight-navigator --skip-nx-cache`: exit 0, 29/29 tests.
- `twilight-burokrat`: `test` 813 pass / 0 fail. `lint:source` and `typecheck` pass, uncached.
- `tool-devsync` test (395/395), lint and typecheck pass uncached. The first CI run caught an alias scope that was not a product and a broken README link; both are fixed in 50f15262.
- `check-indexes working`: exit 0. OpenSpec `validate --all`: 161/161. Prettier is clean.

## Not run

- Host gate `bin/h2puni-gate.sh <sha>`: the orchestrator runs it.
- The unreadable-input proofs need a non-root runner.

body:
**Merge after #42, #44, #45 and #46** (this branch builds on them).

## The new logo

> "Use this for logo inspiration, replace any and all occurrences of the previous logo with this one."

- **The wordmark.** Your image is redrawn as SVG paths (`Logo` in `components/icons.tsx`, and `docs/brand/arc-wordmark.svg`): heavy, slanted letters, the A a solid triangle with an arrow at its foot. One colour, navy on paper or white on navy.
- **Where it replaced the old tile-and-arc mark:**
  - the app's rail;
  - the sign-up and log-in header;
  - the landing page's header and footer;
  - the welcome chat's header;
  - the README.
- **The A alone, where only a square fits:** the phone bar, the chat's avatar, and the favicon (white on a navy tile). At those sizes the full wordmark can't be read.
- It's drawn from the image, not traced from a source file. If there's a vector original, its paths drop straight into `icons.tsx`.
- ADR-0034.

## Landing: reps that reach the goal line

> "On landing the ROM doesn't hit the target line at all."

- **The reps.** The hero's reps peaked at 122–134° against a 140° goal. Every rep now reaches 140–146°.
- **The line.** The goal line sat at a fixed 34% of the stage height, nowhere near the goal. It now runs from the goal tick on the figure's arc to its label: the 3D scene reports where the tick lands on the canvas, so it lines up on every screen size.

## Checked

- **Tests:** the web app's 295 pass (serially) and the typecheck is clean. The hero's test now checks every rep's top reaches the goal.
- **In a browser (scratch stack):**

body:
### What

`scePthreadRwlockUnlock` called `unlock_shared()` whenever the caller was not the write owner, which is undefined behaviour on the host for a lock nobody holds or one write-held by another thread, and returned 0. It now returns `EPERM` in both cases, as FreeBSD libthr does ([`thr_rwlock.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/lib/libthr/thread/thr_rwlock.c), releng/11.4). Fixes #3096.

Carries @husseinkad's two commits from `husseinkad:fix/pthread-rwlock-unlock-unowned` (earlier PRs #2679 and #3615 were closed by intake limits), rebased onto current `main` with authorship kept. `main` already counts readers since #2978, so only the unlock path and the test change.

### Tested

Windows 11 Pro 26200, WinLibs GCC 15.2.0 r7, Release, NVIDIA RTX 4060 Laptop.

- `guest_pthread_rwlock` passes 10/10 with the change and aborts (`0xc0000409`) with `main`'s `Rwlock.cpp` and the new test.
- Full `ctest`: 827/836 pass, 5 skipped. `guest_kernel_sys`, `windows_exceptions` (#3411), `agc_driver_emulated_color_compare` and `guest_filesystem` fail the same way with `main`'s `Rwlock.cpp` on this host.
- `tools/check_conventions.py --base origin/main` passes.

author: rahul9046
body:
A cycle day's position may occupy `1..=day_count`. Most of that was already true in the repository — this closes the gaps and makes the interface say so *before* a user meets a refusal.

## What was already enforced, and what wasn't

Worth separating, because the honest answer is "most of it":

| Requirement | State before | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No duplicate positions | `UNIQUE (cycle_id, ordinal)` → `DuplicateValue{field:"position"}` | none; now tested |
| Position > `day_count` | `check_ordinal_within_cycle` | none; now tested |
| Shortening below an occupied day | `highest_cycle_day_ordinal` guard in `update_cycle` | none; now tested |
| No auto-delete or renumber | nothing did | none; now tested |
| **Position zero** | **only the schema `CHECK`** | **fixed** |

Position 0 *was* rejected — `cycle_day` carries `CHECK (ordinal >= 1)` — but it arrived as *"that cycle day has a value the project does not allow"*, which is what `translate` makes of any `CHECK` failure because it cannot tell which constraint fired. True, and useless: it names no field and suggests no fix, and the form has nowhere to attach it.

The range is now checked in full before the insert, so the refusal reads *"a cycle day's position counts from 1, so there is no position 0"*. The `CHECK` stays as the backstop it always was — belt and braces is right for a rule whose violation would put a day in a cycle that has no such position. A test asserts the generic message no longer reaches the caller.

`update_cycle_day` shares the same check, so a direct IPC call cannot move an *existing* day out of range either — `setup_cycle_day_update` is as direct a route as `create`.

## The frontend

`CrudSpec` gains `addBlockedBy`, deliberately distinct from the existing `blockedBy`: that one **hides the table**, which would be perverse when the reason you cannot add is precisely that all the rows already exist. The table stays, the Add button is disabled, and the reason shows **as visible text as well as the button's `title`** — a disabled button is not focusable, so a tooltip alone is unreachable by keyboard and by touch, i.e. invisible to exactly the users most likely to need it.

**"Is this cycle full?" is answered, not computed here.** It reads `CycleCoverage.missingOrdinals`, which `evara_core::time` worked out and the backend handed over. Comparing a row count against `dayCount` in the view layer would be the same rule implemented twice, in the layer `CLAUDE.md` forbids it in. For the same reason the range is **not** added to `validateCycleDay` — `validation.ts` explicitly names "whether an ordinal fits the cycle's declared length" as belonging in `evara-db`. The field hint names the positions actually free ("From 1 to 10; still free: 4, 7" beats "From 1 to 10" on a cycle whose only gap is 7), the form pre-fills the first gap, and the repository's refusal is what gets shown if one slips through.

## A bug found while testing

**Lengthening a cycle did not refresh coverage.** `loadCoverage` is keyed on the selected cycle's *id*, which an edit does not change, and the cycle panel's `onChanged` only reloaded the cycle list. So after following the instruction *"Increase the cycle length to add more days"*, the message stayed on screen and the button stayed disabled — the one action that message tells you to take did not work. Fixed, with a test driving the whole edit-then-add path.

I also caught my own first test helper asserting the button's **loading** disabled state rather than its **limit** state: three tests were passing for the wrong reason. The helper now waits for the panel to settle, and the full-cycle tests wait for the explanation to appear before asserting `disabled`.

## Tests

`npm run check` exit 0 (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, **303 Rust tests**, `types:check`, tsc, vitest). Production frontend build exit 0. Frontend suite **517 → 530**.

`tests_cycle_day_limit.rs` is new (16 tests) and covers every case in the brief plus:

- **a gap in the middle** of a cycle, not at the end — the case a "count the rows" implementation gets wrong
- the **shorten-to-exactly-the-highest-day** boundary: a 6-day cycle with days up to 4 may become 4, but not 3
- `i64::MIN` and `i64::MAX` positions, and a one-day cycle
- the limit is **per cycle, not per school** — a full weekly cycle does not constrain a fortnight beside it
- one test runs *every* refusal in sequence against a materialised six-day grid with a calendar mapping, then asserts timeslots, mappings, day IDs and `rev`s are all byte-identical afterwards

No migration touched, no schema change, no IPC contract change.

## Remaining issues

- **Two "Add cycle day" buttons exist when the list is empty** — the panel head and the empty state both offer one. Both now respect the limit (I guarded the empty-state action too), but it is a pre-existing duplication in `CrudPanel` that the tests had to accommodate. Unreachable for cycles in practice, since `day_count >= 1` always leaves a free position when there are no rows.
- **`addBlockedBy` has exactly one caller.** A general mechanism added for a single screen; justified by the alternative being a bespoke panel head, but it is new surface area.
- **The note's placement is visually unverified.** It sits between the title and the button in `.panelHead`'s `space-between` row with `max-width: 44ch`. `npm run dev` was not run, so it may wrap awkwardly on a narrow window.
- **`beyondDeclared` is not part of this gate.** A day numbered past the declared length cannot be created, but a project repaired by hand could hold one, and `cycleFull` reads only `missingOrdinals` — so such a cycle would still offer adding. Not silent: `CoveragePanel` already reports `beyondDeclared` separately.

author: henrygoldsmith07-wq
body:
Tenth autonomous audit-and-implement pass. **Base: `main`** (PR #47 is merged, so this PR is not stacked).

## Product assessment
The ninth pass left two honesty gaps that matter more than new content. I re-checked both against the code before building anything.

1. **The offline/rubric marker credited short wrong answers (confirmed, real).** With no AI provider, or offline, `markPart` credits a scheme point when at least half its content words appear in the answer. On a two-word point, one word is enough. "Pulmonary artery, right atrium" scored **2/2** on the pulmonary-vein question. The marker also passed "b² + 4ac" for "b² − 4ac", "< 0" for "> 0", "centre (−3, 2), radius 25" for "(3, −2), radius 5", "nucleophilic" for "electrophilic", "proton acceptor" for "proton donor" and "both alleles are **not** expressed". It told students wrong answers were right, and those marks fed practice feedback, recovery and Today's ranking. I found three further causes while tracing it:
   - The **authored-answer shortcut** canonicalises term order, so "cos 2θ = 1 − 2cos²θ" matched the model's "2cos²θ − 1".
   - The **symbolic layer** pulls a fragment out of prose points, so it called "b² + 4ac" *equivalent* to "Discriminant = b² − 4ac". Its "equivalent" verdict overrode every other check.
   - `pointCoverage` missed a short scheme term when it carried the answer's final full stop. "E(X) = np." scored 0 against "E(X) = np", so correct answers lost marks.
2. **Readiness showed "Proven" beside "8 marks lost and not yet recovered" (both signals right, scoped differently).** "Proven", "Secure" and the ledger's "improved on new questions" claim describe a topic as a whole. `buildMarksAtRisk` counts specific lost marks that haven't been won back yet. Neither signal is wrong, and hiding either would be dishonest. The screen just never said how they relate. No proof predicate is involved, and nothing was marked proven that isn't.

## Improvements implemented
### 1. The offline marker rejects answers that contradict the scheme (`src/domain/marking-contradiction.ts`, `marking.ts`)
- A new pure module asks one question of each scheme point: does the answer assert something the point contradicts? Six narrow checks:
  - **Opposite term** next to the point's subject: ~40 groups, e.g. artery/vein, left/right, atrium/ventricle, oxidised/reduced, anode/cathode, endo/exothermic, nucleophilic/electrophilic, addition/substitution/elimination, donor/acceptor, α/β, insulin/glucagon, aerobic/anaerobic, high/low, positive/negative, once/twice, thin/thick, increase/decrease.
  - **Negation** of one of the point's own words ("not constant", "not independent").
  - **Flipped sign** in an expression ("b² + 4ac", "u² − 2as"), plus same-left-side equations whose signed terms differ ("cos 2θ = 1 − 2cos²θ").
  - **Flipped inequality** ("b² − 4ac < 0", "x < 2" against "2 < x < 3").
  - **Different coordinate or named value** (centre, radius, roots, gradient…), only when the scheme's value appears nowhere in the answer.
  - **Different chemical formula** with the same elements (NH₂⁻ for NH₃).
- Each check fires only when the scheme's own term or value is **absent** from the relevant part of the answer. A contrast like "the vein, not the artery" is left alone. **The checks can only remove credit.**
- **Clause-aware.** Proximity never crosses a clause boundary. A point is read against the clause it is about, and the grammatical subject wins ties. "M is reduced…; N ions are oxidised…" cannot borrow the right word for M from the clause about N. When clauses tie, a veto needs all of them to contradict, so sentence order never changes a mark.
- **Scope, chosen by measuring false positives on every model answer in the bank:**
  - The wording checks run on answers of up to 40 words, and across the whole answer only up to 15.
  - Physics parts already have their own reversal and result guards and long multi-claim answers. They get the general veto only up to 15 words.
  - A negation inside a conditional ("If substrate runs out, the rate need not double") is a qualification, not a reversal.
- `markPart` applies it after the existing polarity check. The authored-answer shortcut now refuses an answer that contradicts a point, though the verbatim model answer always keeps it. The symbolic layer's "equivalent" stays decisive only for a point that is a bare expression.
- **It says why.** Evidence reads "Not awarded: your answer says “artery” where the mark scheme needs “vein”."
- **Provisional instead of awarded when unsure.** A credited point whose answer hedges between the right term and its opposite ("the pulmonary vein or the pulmonary artery") is marked `contested`. `assessDeterministicMark` then labels the whole mark *provisional*, with its own failed `answer-evidence` check, instead of presenting it as firm.
- `pointCoverage` strips a trailing full stop from words. The anti-recitation cap still reads `tokenise` unchanged, so it is not loosened.

**Regression set:** `tests/fixtures/marking-contradiction-set.ts` covers 27 real bank questions: the 18 recall probes plus 9 bank items across Maths, Biology, Chemistry and Physics. It has 74 answers: 27 model answers, 9 paraphrased-correct, and 38 contradictory. Each has a hand-judged examiner mark. These marks are my own judgement against the question's scheme, **not human-moderated marks**.

| Regression set | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Contradictory answers over-credited | **30 / 38 (35 marks)** | **5 / 38 (7 marks)** |
| Contradictory answers marked exactly right | 8 / 38 | 33 / 38 |
| Contradictory answers under-credited | 0 | 0 |
| Correct paraphrases at full marks | 8 / 9 | **9 / 9** (the full-stop fix) |
| Model answers below full | 3 / 27 | 3 / 27 (keyword coverage gaps, not contradictions) |

Across the whole bank, submitting each of the 4,845 authored model answers fires the veto on **1 of 13,288 scheme points**. That one is a short Physics answer whose "first-minimum angle" sits next to the scheme's "central maximum". Before scoping, the same check fired on 74.

**The 5 remaining over-credits are documented in the fixture as known gaps:**
- "two new strands" vs "one original strand": counting.
- "broken down into its elements" vs "formed from": no opposite word.
- "each atom provides one electron" vs "both from the same atom": quantifiers.
- "diffusion distance" satisfies the one-word point "Diffusion" in an answer that names osmosis.
- A 31-word Physics answer, outside the Physics scope.

**Not changed:** copied-mark-scheme detection (`textOverload`), the anti-recitation cap, proof predicates, review gates and trust gates. The AI marking path is also untouched (see limitations).

### 2. Readiness explains "Proven" next to unrecovered marks (`progress-summary.ts`, `ProgressSummaryPanel.tsx`)
- `buildProgressSummary` adds three things:
  - `losing.inStrongTopics`: topics shown as Secure or Proven, or with a ledger-proven gain or a proven/holding lifecycle, that still have open lost marks.
  - `losing.scopeNote`: one plain sentence when they overlap. Example: "5 of these marks are in Topic t1, which shows as strong or proven. Both are true: that label is about the topic as a whole, while each lost mark is a specific question you have not yet got right again."
  - `strong[].openMarks`.
- The panel shows "N lost marks here still to win back" beside the badge, and the scope sentence under the total. No stage, proof rule or total changed.

## Strategic impact
Without an AI key, the rubric marker *is* the product: it marks first submissions offline and feeds recovery, Today's ranking and practice feedback. Telling a student "Pulmonary artery, right atrium" is worth 2/2 undermines the whole recommendation loop: a loss that never registers can't be repaired. This makes the deterministic floor honest about contradictions and honest about doubt. Readiness no longer reads as self-contradicting, which matters for trust once teacher approvals make "Proven" re

body:
> **Builds on #8 (rivals).** Merge #8 first; until then this diff also shows #8's commit.

## Line Up
A four-in-a-row game, named so it doesn't borrow a trademarked name. It has a new **LINE UP** tab.
- **VS CPU (Easy, Medium, Hard):** the computer looks 2, 4 or 7 moves ahead. Every level takes a winning move and blocks yours, so Easy never looks broken. Hard takes about 0.3s per move at most.
  - In 10-game matches: Hard beat Medium 5–2 (3 draws) and Easy 9–1, and Medium beat Easy 9–1.
- **Pass & play** on one device.
- **Private online rooms:**
  - invite links (`?lineup=CODE`) and the phone share sheet
  - live moves with a drop animation on both screens
  - reactions, a match score where the loser starts the rematch, turn alerts while the tab is in the background
  - **head-to-head rivals** with REMATCH, from #8
- **Feel:** discs drop with gravity and a bounce, a ghost disc follows your pointer, and the winning four pulses for 1.5s before the result screen. Keyboard works too (← → Enter, or keys 1–7). Sounds, a how-to-play panel and a per-device record.
- It fits on phones without a special layout.

## Backend
- `PoolRoom` gets an optional **`game`** field (`'pool'` or `'lineup'`). Both games share the room table. Renaming the model would replace the table, so it keeps its name.
- Rooms made before this have no `game` and are treated as pool rooms.
- A code typed into the wrong game redirects to the right one.

## Also
The small label above the result title now fits the situation ("GAME OVER", "RACK OVER", "WAITING FOR A PLAYER") in both games. It used to always say "THE TABLE IS RACKED" or "THE GRID IS EMPTY".

## Testing
- Engine: wins horizontal, vertical and diagonal; second-player wins; full columns rejected; no moves after a win; real draws (full board, no score change); the computer takes wins and blocks losses; level-vs-level matches.
- Browser (headless Chrome, mock backend):
  - **vs CPU:** a full game to the end, with the record updated.
  - **Online:** desktop host and phone guest via invite link. "FIRST GAME VS Rival" toast. The host's vertical four gives "YOU WIN!" / "YOU LOSE". The winning line stays visible before the result screen. Both rival lists updated, and the loser starts the rematch.
  - A pool code typed into Line Up redirects to `?room=`.
- Neon Cue regression: rivals, gameplay and the phone full-screen view still pass.

## Push notifications
Not in this PR. #5's notification function will be updated for Line Up (wording and `?lineup=` links) once this is merged.

body:
## Teller-Rollen: vier neue Rollen, Herkunft je Zeile, Neu-Zuordnung mit `--alle`

**Anlass:** Probelauf 2 auf demo war grün (0 ungültige Rollen). Zwei Lücken, beide entschieden von Dominique am 11.10.

### 1. Neue Rollen (Regel `gericht.teller_rolle`, Migration, Aktiv-Status bleibt)
- **Neu:** `hauptkomponente`, `eis`, `frucht`, `traeger`, mit Labels Hauptkomponente, Eis, Frucht, Träger.
- **Neue Anrichte-Reihenfolge** (Reihenfolge der Werte): traeger → basis → protein → hauptkomponente → beilage → frucht → sauce → crunch → eis → saeure → aroma → garnitur. Gepflegte Labels, Aliase und Zusatzwerte bleiben.
- **Bedeutungen** (in der Regel-Notiz):
  - hauptkomponente: Hauptelement ohne Protein
  - eis: Eis, Sorbet, Granita
  - frucht: Kompott, frische oder marinierte Frucht, Röster
  - traeger: Bun, Cracker, Tartelette, Löffel-Basis, Brot bei Fingerfood
- **Pairing:** Die vier haben **bewusst kein Gewicht** (Rückfall 1,0), bis Dominique Werte nennt. So steht es in `pairing.rollen_gewicht`.
- Der Regel-Block zieht die Werte automatisch. rolleWillSub: Die neuen Rollen werden Basisrezept, außer Kleinstmengen.

### 2. Herkunft der Teller-Rolle: `recipe_ingredients.role_source` (ki | kaskade | migration | manuell)
- **Rückfüllung:**
  - Rolle = `role_v21` → migration.
  - Rolle ohne Quelle, mit **belegtem** vk.rollen-Call nach der Umstellung, und Zeile seither geändert → ki (die Probeläufe: 1373, 1374, 1378, 1382, 1398).
  - Alles andere bleibt **unbekannt**. Kein erfundenes Etikett.
- **Gesetzt von:** Generator (ki, geerbt vom Basisrezept: kaskade), Editor (manuell), MCP `recipe_ingredients.PUT` (ki; optional `role_source: manuell` nur bei ausdrücklicher menschlicher Vorgabe), `acceptRollen`/vk.rollen/Bulk (ki).
- **`syncIngredients`:** Eine unveränderte Rolle behält ihre Quelle. Nur eine Änderung übernimmt die mitgegebene Quelle, ohne Angabe ist sie unbekannt.

### 3. `foodalchemist:teller-rollen-klassifizieren --alle`
- Ordnet leere Zeilen und Rollen aus migration/ki neu zu. **Manuelle Rollen und Rollen unbekannter Herkunft bleiben** und werden gezählt („x Zeilen bleiben geschützt“).
- Im --alle-Modus bekommt die KI die zu überschreibenden Altwerte **nicht als Echo**, sonst bestätigt sie z. B. „Olivenöl [beilage]“ eher. Manuelle Rollen bleiben als Kontext sichtbar.
- Die Kosten-Schätzung kommt aus gemessenen Calls.

### Tests
`TellerRollenTest` erweitert:
- neue Rollen in Reihenfolge, mit Labels und Gewicht 1,0
- neue Rollen werden Basisrezept
- Rückfüllung migration, belegt ki, ohne Beleg unbekannt
- Quelle je Schreibweg (Generator, geerbt, Editor-Änderung, unverändert, MCP)
- MCP `role_source=manuell` wird übernommen, andere Werte abgelehnt
- `--alle` überschreibt leer, migration und ki, lässt manuell und unbekannt, ohne Altwert-Echo

`Spec81PflegeseiteTest` an die neue Werte-Reihenfolge angepasst.

**Gegenprobe:** Jede geänderte Datei sowie die Rollen- und die Quellen-Migration einzeln zurückgesetzt, jedes Mal wird ein Test rot.
**Volle Suite:** 5.480 bestanden, 5 übersprungen, 0 rot.

### Nicht ausrollen
Nach dem Deploy macht die Kuratorin einen Probelauf mit `--alle --limit=5` (Dessert und Fingerfood dabei) für Dominique. Ausgerollt wird erst nach ihrem Go.

develop → release の [#1721](https://github.com/ISCProduct/soc-ai-agent/pull/1721) がコンフリクト（DIRTY）・198ファイル扱いになっている件の対処です。

## 原因

#1717 と #1719 を release へ**スカッシュ**でマージしたため、develop と release の共通の祖先が #1711 の時点のまま残っています。GitHub はそこからの差分を PR として見るので、取り込み済みの変更まで「未反映」に見え、同じファイル（`student-bottom-nav-auth.test.tsx`）が両側で新規追加された扱いになってコンフリクトしていました。

release を develop へマージし、コンフリクトは develop 側（「プロフィール」）を採用しました。**ファイルの中身は develop と完全に同一**で、変わるのは履歴だけです。
