body:
## What

The second step after [#4128](https://github.com/gradido/gradido/pull/4128): the words a member wrote in a conversation and did not send now lie on the device, so they outlast a reload, a closed tab and a session that ran out (Bernd's choice among three, 11.10.2026). Until now they waited in memory and were gone with the page.

Wallet only; nothing changes at the server.

## What lies on the device, and what does not

- **The words only**, under `chat-drafts:<gradidoID>` in `localStorage`, by conversation, each with the time it was last written. Outside the vuex store, which is written whole on every mutation.
- **Never the picture and never the box "also by e-mail".** They wait in memory as before: a chat picture is not put into the device's storage, and comes back for as long as the wallet runs in the tab.
- **The device says what the words are.** Another tab of the same member may have sent them or written on. Memory says only where the device takes nothing (storage switched off, or full) — an emptied field included.

## Whose they are, and how long

- **A member's words lie under that member's key**, and are read and written only while that member is signed in. Another member on the same browser finds an empty field and has a key of their own.
- **"Abmelden" takes them off the device** — the member's own word, in a menu or in the question before a session ends.
- **A session that ran out leaves them there**, as does a session that could not be extended and every other sign-out the member did not ask for: whoever signs in again finds what they had written. What waits in memory — the picture, the box — goes with every sign-out.
- **Words nobody touched for fourteen days are let go**, for every member of the device, with the next sign-in or sign-out there: a member who does not come back to a shared computer does not leave them there for good. A time ahead of the device's clock counts as now, so a clock that was wrong does not keep words young.
- **Thirty conversations at most** keep their words on the device, the ones written in last.

## How the sign-out learns whose word it is

- `SessionLogoutTimeout` sends `{ ranOut: true }` with `logout` where the clock ends the session (time ran out, renewal failed); its button "Abmelden" sends nothing.
- `DashboardLayout.logoutUser` tells the store `{ byOwnWord, member }`: whose word it is, taken with the press. The server is asked before the store hears of the sign-out, and a sign-out that got ahead — the clock ends the session while "Abmelden" is on its way — has cleared the store by then.
- The store's `logout` hands `forgetChatDrafts(member, { fromDevice })` the member the word names, or the one it read before clearing the state. Its `login` lets old words go as well: a wallet closed with its tab runs no sign-out.
- Every other caller of `logout` (the guards, a token the server refused, the way into the admin area, the friends page handing the device to a guest who registers on it) says nothing, and nothing said leaves the words on the device.

## Known limits

- **The words lie in the device's storage in the clear**, as the theme, the session and the map's settings do; whoever can open the browser's storage of this device can read them. Fourteen days and the member's own "Abmelden" bound that.
- **The picture does not outlast a reload or a sign-out**, on purpose.
- **Two tabs of one member** share the words through the device; a field that is open in the other tab does not change under the member's hands, it shows them when it is next opened. Where the same conversation stands open in both tabs at once, the bar changed last says what the words are.
- **Where the device refuses a write** (its storage is full), the newer words wait in memory only. What the device took before is an older state, and that is what comes back after a reload.
- **A sign-out pressed in the admin area is not the wallet's.** The way there signs the wallet out without a word, so the words stay on the device, for up to fourteen days.
- **utils/chatReturn still notes the words while the page is out of sight** (#3999). With the words on the device that is a second copy; taking it out is a change of its own.
- **Measured in Chrome on a Mac** and in the tests' DOM.

## Checked

- `frontend`: lint, stylelint, locales, build, 9,168 tests.
- **The real bundle against a stand-in server, in a headless Chrome: 45 checks** — those of #4128 again, and: the words on the device under the member's key and nothing else there, a page loaded anew, a session that ran out in the running wallet (the member is signed out by the clock, signs in again: the words are there, the picture is not), a session that ran out while the wallet was closed (opened again, the guard sends the member to sign in: the words are there), "Abmelden" (the words are off the device), another member on the same browser (an empty field, a key of their own, and the first member finds theirs again). Against a bundle of #4128 exactly the checks of the device are red.
- **108 one-line faults put into the code, each on its own: all caught by a test.** Two changes to comments, as controls, leave every test green.
- **A second reader of the code before this PR**, seven points. Built: who said "Abmelden" is taken with the press (two sign-outs under way at once left the words on the device; found here as well before the report came); old words are let go with a sign-in too; a time ahead of the device's clock; a refused write, where an emptied field could bring back what the device still held; and tests that run the store with the real drafts and the layout with the real clock, where each side had been held by a name of its own. Not built and named above: the same conversation open in two tabs, and the admin area's sign-out.

body:
Refs #558. This is the report-date-filter slice, revived from #711 onto today's schema. The Additional information and Ministry report "Submitted on or after/before" filters, their exports and the Ministry packet now take days in the viewer's browser time zone (Administrator decision, 2026-10-04). **Stacked on #1045** (base `pr/stewardship-463-family-timeline-export`, 0063), because migration PRs merge in number order. Review only the top four commits.
**Re-derived SQL, frozen migration 0064.** #711's SQL copied the report functions as they were before 0040 and 0045, so I rebuilt it from today's latest bodies. Each new function is copied whole from its latest twin with only #558's change: the `zone` filter key and a predicate from local midnight of the first day to local midnight after the last, each bound computed once.
- `stewardship_browser_day_start_v1(day, zone)`: new, unchanged from #711's reviewed version, including the Havana repeated-midnight rule.
- `stewardship_information_report_v2`: from 0045's `information_report_v1`.
- `stewardship_ministry_report_v3`: from 0045's `ministry_report_v1`. #711's "v2" name is taken by 0040's actor wrapper.
- `stewardship_ministry_report_v4`: from 0040's actor-scoped `ministry_report_v2`, calling v3. The page calls v4, so SQL still derives the reader's scope (#389 L3).
- `stewardship_information_export_capture_v2` (from the baseline) and `stewardship_ministry_export_capture_v2` (from 0045): zoned filters call the new selections, filters without a zone call v1, and a packet's zone must be blank. Both capture triggers are re-pointed with `CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER`.
- None of these is SECURITY DEFINER, and each keeps its twin's attributes, so there is no `ALTER ... SECURITY DEFINER` to repeat. The DO block refuses unless each copy matches its twin's `prosecdef` (false), volatility, language, return type, `proconfig`, `proacl`, owner and arguments and carries the change. The helper must place Havana's repeated midnight correctly, and both triggers must call the v2 captures.
- Earlier versions stay installed. Grants are unchanged: the new functions keep their twins' default EXECUTE.
**Checklist.**
- Digest pinned (`85da90b9c2df…`); both `.dockerignore` files list the file; schema baseline regenerated on #1022 plus this.
- Django `stewardship_reports.0016_report_local_days` depends on `reports.0015_timeline_exports` (#1045, installs 0063), so the files apply in prefix order with a single leaf. It is in the users swap's closure; the swap tests register its six functions in CLOSURE_CREATED and `swap_pending` restores the two capture triggers on the v1 captures (`before_report_local_days`). No `runtime_grants` entry: it creates no granted table or definer routine.
- **Expected failure:** `test_frozen_files_form_one_consecutive_sequence` fails until 0057–0063 land.
**DO block and copies tested:** new `test_report_local_days_migration_postgresql.py` (11 tests).
- Each of the five copies contains every unchanged line of its latest twin, in order, and grows by fewer than 20 lines.
- The check passes on an installed database. It refuses the database before 0064 (new functions gone, triggers on v1), a copy given definer's rights, a lost `jit` setting, changed grants, and a trigger left on v1.
**Application** (from #711, conflicts resolved against today's main):
- Both filter forms carry a hidden `zone` field that `ui-v1.js` fills, a note naming the zone, and Apply held with a plain hint while a date is entered without a known zone. The button now uses the shared `{% button %}` tag.
- The labels lose "(parish date)", and the About text no longer mentions campaign-zone days or a UTC fallback. The export time zone choice stays, as the recorded exception.
- `InformationQuery` and `MinistryQuery` carry `zone`; a date without a catalog zone is refused with a "reload the page" message. A retained export captured before 0064 is retried with its zone-less filters.
- The ui-conventions date rule names this as the fourth #558 page group, and the reports spec is updated.
**Local evidence** (macOS; one PG pair, removed afterwards; disk was at 17 GB free):
- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`: clean. pymarkdown on the three changed specs: clean. test_traceability: passed.
- Unit: test_report_zone_refusals (fixed for main's NAV-11 campaign check), test_information_followup, test_ministry_reports, test_ministry_packets, test_build, help guards, button guard, in-place controls, page names, date format and browser-local times: 1332 passed. The one failure is the expected sequence check.
- PostgreSQL:
  - test_report_local_days (13, including SQL equal to Python's day start across DST and odd offsets) and test_report_jit: 24 passed.
  - test_schema_baseline (regenerated), test_upgrade_parity, test_storage, information access, exports and follow-up, Ministry exports, follow-up, packets and reports, and test_load_check: 103 passed.
  - test_report_local_days_migration: 11 passed.
- Browser, `--require-no-skips`: test_report_local_days, 16 passed across Chromium and WebKit. The Ministry route pattern moved to `/joining/`. Chromium: test_information_followup, test_ministry_followup and test_ministry_reports, 27 passed.
**pk-local checklist** (Administrator or Staff)
- Reports → Additional information: under the date filters, a note names this computer's time zone. Enter "Submitted on or after" and Apply: the table refreshes in place with requests submitted from local midnight of that day, and the address and paging keep the filter.
- With the browser's time zone set to one where a request falls on a different day than in the parish zone, that request moves in or out of the list accordingly.
- Clear the dates: Apply works with no zone message.
- Ministry requests (Joining) for one Ministry: the same date filters and note. Queue an export after applying dates; the file has the same rows.
- The Ministry follow-up packet still exports, with no dates.
- About panels mention only "your computer's time zone" for the filters, with no "parish date" or UTC wording.


**Review fixes (445fc7c3f, after rebasing onto #1022's e8e0223e5):**
- **MEDIUM:** `pk-admin report information` and `report ministry` take `--zone`, required with `--start`/`--end` as `logs` does, and checked by the pages' own parsers. Their printed `filters` gain `zone`.
  - New CLI tests: both commands with a valid date range in a zone match the page's count, and both refuse dates without a zone (exit 1, `invalid`).
  - The golden documents now include `zone`.
  - The automation guide covers the report options and the exports' `--filter zone=…` (required with `start=`/`end=`), and has an Output changelog entry.
- **LOW:** the UX conventions spec again lists report day buckets among what stays in the campaign zone, since the participation chart still buckets by campaign time.
- Evidence:
  - PostgreSQL: test_admin_report_cli plus test_schema_baseline, 22 passed.
  - Unit: test_admin_cli, test_admin_report_reads and parity, 148 passed.
  - ruff, pymarkdown and traceability: clean.



**Rebase onto #1045 (dd893077d), 2026-10-11:** the two #558 commits rebased linearly; the frozen 0064 file is unchanged (none of 0057–0063 replaced the functions it copies from 0045, 0040 and the baseline, so its digest stands). Added: reports.0016 re-chain plus users-swap closure registration, and a schema baseline regenerated on 0057–0064. Local evidence: unit tests (migration files and frozen digests, traceability, date format including #1096's compact table-cell guard, restore check, #1047's units) 201 passed; PostgreSQL (schema baseline, upgrade parity, users swap and upgrade, report local days and its migration, Ministry reports, report JIT, storage, admin report CLI, timeline exports) 154 passed; Chromium (report local days and the follow-up/history in-place tests that use the changed component helpers) 39 passed; `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` clean. #1069's data-order-hint fix ap

author: tchouhanjsm
body:
## Outcome

Improve backup observability and failure handling before the owner relies on recovery: record duration and receipt-copy workload on successful runs, show those measurements in owner Settings, and email the owner once when a backup failure incident begins.

## Acceptance criteria

- Record elapsed time for the backup pass, including lock wait and retention pruning.
- Record the count of copied receipt files and the sum of source receipt file sizes when every size can be measured. If any size is unavailable, report the total as unknown rather than a partial sum.
- Persist the three metrics as one timestamped record and expose them only when their completion timestamp matches the current recorded last success.
- Keep telemetry-write failures non-fatal to an otherwise completed snapshot and never turn incomplete/unknown bytes into zero.
- Send one owner email for the first failure in a continuous failure incident; do not repeat on each subsequent failed run. Reset the incident only after a successful backup.
- Keep email delivery failure separate from the underlying backup failure, preserve the original error and allow a later backup attempt to retry the alert.
- Expose backup failure as an assertive accessible status in owner Settings and show last successful duration, receipt count, known payload size and any email-delivery issue.
- Add seeded mock workload coverage for 0, 10, 100 and 500 receipts, plus regressions for unknown receipt sizes, consecutive-failure deduplication, recovery after success and mail-delivery failure.
- All three required workflows must pass on one exact final PR head.

## Verification evidence

Base/main SHA: `4082503cf96bf08a2aa6408bde14fbd0bef14d2c` (PR #82 merge).

CI, Browser E2E and Full Flight Test will be checked against the final exact PR head. The seeded workload is a deterministic mock benchmark and its harness wall time is not a real Apps Script/Drive performance measurement. No local test run is claimed because there is no local checkout available in this session.

## Security and failure review

- The email recipient comes from the existing `OWNER_EMAIL` Script Property; the message contains the bounded backup error and no voucher rows, receipt contents, tokens or Drive IDs.
- `MailApp.sendEmail` introduces an Apps Script mail-sending authorization scope. The owner must review/authorize it in the intended project before live email notifications can work; no authorization or deployment is performed in this PR.
- Backup failure remains the primary state even if notification delivery fails. Delivery errors are stored separately; a failed mail attempt clears the incident marker so a later attempt can retry.
- A success status and workload metrics are not evidence that a snapshot opens or can be restored. Metrics are tied to the recorded success timestamp to avoid displaying stale measurements.
- Seeded timings exercise instrumentation and proportional work only. They do not establish an execution-time, quota or storage threshold for production.

## Release boundary

Backend backup orchestration/telemetry, owner-only status display, mock fixtures, regression tests, test scripts and backup/release docs only. No merge, Apps Script `setup()`, `clasp push`, deployment, production-data mutation, live backup trigger, live failure injection, or restore operation.

## Residual risks / not verified

- Live Apps Script authorization of MailApp and actual owner email delivery are not verified by CI; deployment approval is still required.
- A seeded mock cannot measure real Drive copy latency, daily workload growth or Apps Script quota behavior. Collect live metrics after an owner-approved release before setting thresholds.
- The owner still must observe a real scheduled backup and witness restoration into a separate recovery Sheet/folder, validating row counts, numbering, receipt copies and manifest references.
- Existing structural backup inspection remains distinct from a restore drill. Production readiness remains unverified.

## Session handoff

PR #82 is merged at `4082503cf96bf08a2aa6408bde14fbd0bef14d2c`. PR #83 addresses the next roadmap phase: measure successful backup work, alert the owner on a new failure incident and add seeded regression coverage. Do not merge or deploy on the owner's behalf. After code review, the remaining P0 is the owner-authorized live backup/alert check and isolated restore drill.

## Summary
- Add passkey registration, password-free sign-in, and owner-scoped removal while retaining password sign-in.
- Verify user presence and user verification, signatures, origin, relying party ID, user handle, and single-use browser-bound challenges.

- `prek run -a` passed.
- `npm run check` and `npm run build` passed.
- Chrome virtual-authenticator test passed: registration, incorrect password, expired challenge, invalid signature, sign-in, replay rejection, and removal.

- `npm run test:training:postgres` passed (12 tests).
- `npm run db:migrate -- --name passkeys` applied all migrations successfully on disposable PostgreSQL; both passkey tables were verified.
- Final browser checks used an isolated SQLite database on port 8785 because another test process owned port 8784. The test server was stopped.

## Production requirements
- Apply the included database migration.
- Use HTTPS and set `PASSKEY_ORIGIN` to the exact public origin in the app process environment.
- No production services or deployment configuration were changed. Physical biometric devices and cross-device synchronization were not tested.

author: ilya-kozyrev
body:
## Что и зачем

Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`) имеет настройку effort (`low|medium|high|xhigh|max`, adaptive thinking). Claude Code >= 2.1.296 резолвит алиас `haiku` в неё (2.1.289 давал Haiku 4.5). Код предполагал «у Haiku нет effort» и выбрасывал effort для любой модели с `haiku` в имени; с Haiku 5.5 effort оставался неуправляемым. Теперь Haiku решает effort тем же путём, что и все модели.

## Что изменено

- `agent spawn --model haiku`: `--effort`, иначе запись `AGENT_HUB_EFFORT_DEFAULTS`, иначе `AGENT_HUB_DEFAULT_EFFORT`, иначе `high`. Флаг уходит в CLI, пишется в `meta.json` и строку старта, учитывается `--reason` и `AGENT_HUB_EFFORT_RULES`. Нового default для Haiku не добавлено.
- `hub reviewer`: стартовая строка haiku-ревьюера несёт `--effort`.
- `hub succeed` / autopilot: преемник на Haiku получает effort как любой (унаследованный от хаба, либо отказ, если прочитать нельзя). Параметр `model` у `successor_effort` стал не нужен и убран.
- `session_effort`: логика не менялась (условие «запись Haiku без effort» уже различает 4.5 и 5.5), исправлены докстринги и текст отказа («recorded no effort»).
- Документация: `docs/reference.md`, `docs/reviewers.md`, `docs/install.md`, `skills/hub/SKILL.md`, `bin/agent` (шапка и `--help`), комментарий у `MIN_CLI_VERSION`. Алиас `haiku` = Haiku 5.5 только с CLI 2.1.296, до него Haiku 4.5; минимум (2.1.287) не поднят.
- `docs/examples/subagent-policy.json`: по политике владельца Haiku работает на `high` (допустим `medium`), на `low` запрещён; добавлено правило deny для low перед allow для Haiku.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: запись в Unreleased.

## Что показал замер (CLI 2.1.296, 2026-10-11)

`claude -p --effort low` при унаследованном `CLAUDE_EFFORT=xhigh`, с хуком PreToolUse, пишущим вход, и командой Bash `echo $CLAUDE_EFFORT`:

| | запись ассистента | вход хука | `$CLAUDE_EFFORT` в Bash |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-haiku-5-5` | `effort: low`, `perTurnEffort: low` | `effort.level: low` | `low` |
| `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | поля `effort` нет, `perTurnEffort: null` | нет | `xhigh` (унаследованное) |

Оба запуска с `--effort low` завершились с кодом 0: на Haiku 4.5 флаг принимается и не действует, поэтому его безопасно передавать на любом поддерживаемом CLI. Субагент Haiku 5.5 (general-purpose) в сессии Opus на `high` унаследовал `effort: high` (транскрипт реальной сессии).

## Проверки

- `git diff --check origin/main`: 0
- `bash tests/run_all.sh "$(mktemp -d)"`: 0 (3403 проверки, 0 падений)
- `claude plugin validate .claude-plugin/plugin.json --strict`: 0
- Отрицательный контроль: новые тесты против кода origin/main падают на всех haiku-проверках (spawn_policy 6, cli_models 8, reviewers 2, autopilot 6, effort 1, agent 1, discipline 1: запрет low в примере политики); на коде ветки проходят. Положительные контроли: `--model haiku --effort <x>` доходит до CLI на 2.1.295 (Haiku 4.5) и 2.1.296 (Haiku 5.5), запись effort Haiku 5.5 читается через env и транскрипт, Haiku 4.5 по-прежнему считается моделью без effort.
- `tests/fake_claude.py` теперь резолвит `haiku` по `FAKE_VERSION` (>= 2.1.296: Haiku 5.5, иначе 4.5), как настоящий CLI.
- `tests/t_agent_runs.sh`: проверка «без слэша» в строке agent-top ловила `/` из ячейки MODEL (`haiku-…/hi`, теперь у Haiku есть effort); заменена на проверку отсутствия пары `run/total`.

## Ограничения

Файлы и код этого PR к `jwait` не относятся, локально `t_jwait` проходит в полном прогоне; похоже на гонку теста, перезапуск не делал.

body:
Follow-up to #1 (stacked on `feature/mono-hq-app`). This is visual only: no server, API or behaviour changes. Merge #1 first, or retarget this PR to `main` afterwards.

The branch merges #1's head (b0fa147, the pre-merge audit fixes) in 029c56e, so this PR's diff against `feature/mono-hq-app` holds only the visual work below.

## Commits

### 66ab283: lo-fi night office look
A new `web/src/ambience.css`, loaded after `styles.css` (which stays under 500 lines), plus a small markup tweak in `Office.tsx`:
- **Calmer surfaces.** Flat frosted-glass panels, 1px hairlines, a faint film grain (inline SVG; the CSP allows `data:` images), and more breathing room.
- **Big calm numbers.** Tabular stat values with small soft labels.
- **The wall.** A deeper night sky with six slowly drifting stars, a moon halo, a slow-breathing neon "MONO HQ" sign, and a warm wall sconce (hidden on phones).
- **The floor and desks.** Warm amber lamp pools. Idle desks rest slightly dimmed and undim on hover and on keyboard focus. Working desks breathe a slow mint halo.

### ece57c2: after-hours studio type, night-shift header, lights-on boot
- **Type.**
  - Karantina, a condensed Hebrew poster face, for display: the greeting, titles, numerals, nameplates and the neon sign.
  - IBM Plex Sans Hebrew for text.
  - Both are self-hosted via `@fontsource` (OFL-1.1), Hebrew + Latin subsets, because the CSP allows same-origin fonts only.
  - Latin capitals are tracked; Hebrew and numerals are not.
- **Night-shift header.**
  - A time-of-day greeting for Asia/Jerusalem ("משמרת לילה" from 21:00 to 05:00) on the start side.
  - A condensed clock on the end side.
  - On the office page the bar title steps back to a quiet label.
- **Office stats.** A ruled strip sized by a container query: 2 columns, or one row of 5 from 760px. The sidebar never causes a 4 + 1 wrap.
- **"Lights on".** The first office view per page load waits for live state, then:
  - the veil fades;
  - the neon flickers once (under 3 flashes/s);
  - lamps rise desk by desk in reading order;
  - failed desks stay dark.

  Everything rests in its final state under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Fixes:** the loading overlay sits above the desks, and spend labels stack above the numerals.

### bd60cb4: fonts satisfy the CSP
Vite inlined the smallest font files as `data:` URIs, which the CSP (`default-src 'self'`) blocks. That produced console errors, although the text still rendered from the woff2 files. `vite.config.ts` now sets `assetsInlineLimit: 0`, so every asset is a same-origin file.

## Verification
- **CI on bd60cb4: green.** `tsc` clean, **147/147 tests**, build OK, `found 0 vulnerabilities`, `secret-scan: 81 tracked files clean`.
- **Isolated build of bd60cb4:** all 12 font files ship as `/assets/*.woff2`, and no `data:` font URIs remain in the CSS or JS.
- **Lo-fi look (66ab283),** checked in the built app at pane width and on a 375×812 phone:
  - all 7 routes render with no horizontal overflow;
  - no failed requests;
  - demo mode shows working desks and stops cleanly.
- **Independent a11y/performance review of 66ab283:** no blockers. Changed text contrast is 5.1–6.7:1 (AA), and every new animation stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **ece57c2:** reviewed by an independent design/a11y reviewer and approved after two rounds.

## Not done
- Motion can only be turned off through the OS reduced-motion setting. There is no in-app motion toggle.
- The `.bubble::after` arrow is about 14px off-centre in RTL. This predates the PR and was left untouched.

author: magior
body:
**Problem**

Since 71e1560 ("Time can now be set", 2025-03-19) `COMMAND_TIMER` expects a 27-byte body.
The CP Plus sends 24 bytes in the `18 3D` timer status buffer, and the layout before that
commit (like the 2022 one) was 24 bytes too. `TrumaCommand.parse()` raises
`bitstruct.Error: unpack requires at least 216 bits to unpack (got 192)`; the exception
leaves `Lin.loop_serial`, `TrumaService._loop_step` and `miqro.Service.run` (no handler),
so the service exits at the first timer download.

On a CP Plus C3.00.00 the timer buffer is downloaded right after the box has registered
(and again after an init request), so the service dies about 10 s after registration.
Other panels send `18 3D` in normal operation (see the WomoLIN `cp_plus.log`).

Two more things fall out of the same definition:

* the write buffer was 27 bytes with `cid_write 0x3C`; the real box sends 17 bytes
  (`11 3C`): the 12 settings bytes, then active, start minutes/hours, stop minutes/hours;
* `timer_heating_mode` and `timer_el_power_level` had no entry in
  `STATUS_CONVERSION_FUNCTIONS`, so `get_all()` would raise once a timer buffer parsed.

**Fix**

* `COMMAND_TIMER` read layout = esphome `StatusFrameTimer` (24 bytes): heater settings
  (same 12 bytes as `14 33` / `0C 32`), 7 unknown bytes, active, start, stop.
* New optional `TrumaCommand(..., data_elements_w=...)` for commands whose write buffer is
  not a prefix of the status buffer; used for the 17-byte timer write. Default behaviour
  unchanged for the other commands.
* Conversion entries for `timer_heating_mode`, `timer_el_power_level`, `timer_energy_mix`.

**Tests**

`tests/test_timer_buffer.py` (pytest, `pytest tests`), 7 tests. The buffers are real bus
data, not derived from the command definition: captures from a CP Plus C3.00.00 + Combi 6
H5.00.00 (status 5 °C / boost / 40 °C / 01:00–05:00; a write that the panel acknowledged
with error 0 and that the re-read timer matched) and one of the examples quoted in
esphome-truma_inetbox. One test feeds the 7-frame BB transfer through `Lin.loop_serial`.
On master 6 fail, on this branch all 7 pass.

**Evidence**

Captured on the LIN bus (sniffer + emulated iNet Box, 2026-10-04). Timer status after
the write below, as the panel sent it:

```
00 1f 00 1e 00 00 22 ff ff ff 54 01 18 3d 00 b5 5e 0b 01 00 00 00 02 0d 00 00 01 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 00 02 1e 03
```

Write uploaded by the box (counter 0x12), acked `02 0D 12 … 00`:

```
00 1f 00 1e 00 00 22 ff ff ff 54 01 11 3c 12 ab 5e 0b 01 00 00 00 02 0d 00 00 01 01 01 00 02 1e 03
```

The panel showed the timer icon and the timer as 02:00–03:30, 18 °C, eco, water 60.

Is 24 bytes panel-specific? The WomoLIN logs say no: `18 3D` (length byte 0x18 = 24) is the
only timer buffer in the C4.01.01 init logs (`Log Truma CP Plus init mit AC`, `… mit Combi 6`)
as well as in the C3.00.01 logs (`cp_plus.log`, `cp_plus-combi_6d_e-inet_box.log`); a 27-byte
buffer would be `1B 3D`, which no log contains.

## Summary Architecture-review candidate #5. It also fixes two fields that real users never saw. **User-visible fixes:** - **Series:** the user-books query never asked for `featured_book_series`, so the detail pane always showed "Series —". It now requests `featured_book_series { position series { id name } }` and shows e.g. "Dune #1" or "The Expanse #2.5". The position is a `float8` in Hardcover, so it's now `float64`. Field names were checked against the hardcover-docs schema source. Existing caches pick up the series on the next sync. - **Genres:** `cached_tags` was saved to the cache but never read back, so the Genres row never appeared for real users. It does now. **Refactor:** - `internal/app/hardcover_map.go` is now the single place where Hardcover data becomes model data, with one date parser. `convert.go` is gone. `api` returns only wire types: `SearchBooks` returns `[]api.TypesenseBookDoc` and `GetBookRatingsByIDs` returns `map[int]api.APIBook`. - New model types: `BookDetail`, `BookJournalEntry`, `GoalInput` (which now owns `Validate`), `RatingBucket` and `ParseRatingDistribution`. `internal/tui` no longer imports `api`, and `internal/cli` imports it only for wiring and auth symbols. - The store has one scanner per row type, and `GetLatestRead` uses the same ranking as the joined queries. No nested queries inside row loops, and no pool cap. ## Compatibility - `goals --json`, `journal --json` and `book --json` are pinned byte-for-byte to the old output, which was captured with the old types before the change. - `list --json` now also fills in `CachedTags` and `FeaturedSeries`. - Goal validation moved from `api.SaveGoal` to `App.SaveGoal`. It runs at the same point with the same messages. ## Tests - **`TestUserBookSurvivesSyncAndCache`:** realistic Hardcover JSON goes through sync, the mapper and the store, then is read back three ways, and every field is compared. It fails if a fixture field is left empty, and it was checked to fail with the series mapping or the tags scan removed. - **api:** an httptest checks that the query requests the series fields and that positions 1, 2.5 and null decode correctly. - **model:** tests for the new types, plus updated app, api, tui and cli tests. `go build`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` and `-race` on app, tui and store are green locally. author: rhawk117
body:
## Ticket

Closes #20.

## What changed

python-harness goes to 0.2.0.

- The MCP server has eight tools. `survey` and `gate` join the six it had. Both read the project at `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` and take no arguments. `gate` runs the project's ruff, ty and pytest checks, so it is the one project tool without the read-only hint. When the project has no ruff or ty configuration, the gate uses the files the plugin ships inside the gate package, and its report says which was used in `ruff_config_source` and `ty_config_source`. `ruff check` runs with `--no-fix`, so the check does not rewrite files in a project whose ruff config enables fixing.
- The plugin has a `ruff_version` option, default `0.16.9`. A project that does not declare ruff has its ruff checks run with that version. A project that declares ruff runs its own.
- `collect_python_facts` and `map_python_calls` take `detail` (`full`, `summary` or `counts`) and `budget` (default 4000 tokens, minimum 256). Their default output is now a summary inside an envelope, where 0.1.0 returned the whole document. A response that does not fit the budget steps down a level and sets `degraded`. The `what-would-ryan-say` skill and the `pylens` agent ask for `detail: full` with a budget of 20000.
- Every project tool's document carries workspace diagnostics under `workspace`: `source_roots`, `fallback_diagnostics` and `unindexed_packages`.
- Source roots come from the members of a uv workspace, read with `uv workspace list --paths --offline --color never` under a five-second timeout. If that fails, the tool answers from the project root's `src` directory and records the cause as a diagnostic. A module under more than one source root takes its name from the deepest one.
- Four data commands print YAML reports: `alert-budget`, `paired-compare`, `profile-data` and `size-check`. They run as `bin/python-harness-data <subcommand>`. The launcher pins duckdb, msgspec, numpy, polars, pyyaml and scipy, and the six also sit in a `data` extra. `bin/python-harness` and the hooks are unchanged. `.mcp.json` gains one environment entry, which carries the `ruff_version` option to the server.

Outside `plugins/python-harness` the diff touches `CHANGELOG.md`, the root `README.md`, the marketplace entry's version, the root `pyproject.toml` (the dev environment now installs the `data` extra) and `uv.lock`.

## Verification

Run at `52e035b`, after the second round of review fixes.

```
make sync                                                exit 0
make lint                                                exit 0, 2273 passed, "quality checks passed"
claude plugin validate --strict plugins/python-harness   Validation passed
claude plugin validate --strict .                        Validation passed
bin/python-harness-data <subcommand> --help              exit 0 for each of the four
bin/python-harness-data with no or an unknown subcommand exit 2, usage line on stderr
```

The 0.2.0 server was also started from a clone of this branch and called through an MCP client. It lists eight tools, and a `gate` call left the clone's tree unchanged.

## Review notes

- The review covered the security surface: `gate` starting the project's test suite from a tool call, workspace discovery starting `uv`, `profile-data` building SQL from column names, and the data launcher's six third-party packages. Its findings and their outcomes are in the three review comments on this pull request. One is documented and not fixed: a gate check still running when the MCP server is terminated keeps running (README, Limitations).
- One suppression is added: `# noqa: S603` on the call that starts `uv` for workspace discovery, in the same form as the existing `git` call.
- Two tests are missing. None starts the data launcher through `uv` (the launcher tests load the file and check its pins against `uv.lock`). None runs `gate` over stdio against a fixture project that has its own `.venv`.
- `uv workspace list --offline` was tried on uv 0.11.29 only. It created no `.venv` and no `uv.lock`, and left a stale `uv.lock` unchanged.
- The `ruff_version` option has not been set through Claude Code's option dialog. The server was run with the unexpanded `${user_config.ruff_version}` from `.mcp.json` and used the default. `uvx ruff@<version>` resolves through the project's own uv settings, with no `--exclude-newer` and no hash.
- On this repository `gate` reports all four checks failed while `make lint` passes. pytest fails collection because `uv run --isolated` does not install the workspace members that `uv sync --all-packages` does. The cause of the ruff difference was not established.
- The CLI's `inspect gate` passes no ty fallback. Only the MCP `gate` does.
- `check_citations` reads a cited source once for the project index and once for the check. The other project tools read each file once per call.
- Two commits on the branch have a red CI run, `7749137` and `36fa395`. The commits after each fix the cause, and the head is green.
- Debt left alone: `bin/python-harness` has no `--exclude-newer` while `.mcp.json` and the data launcher have one, and the README's Limitations sentence that begins "As of 0.1.0" stays as written.

## Summary

With metrics scraping on (`--monitoring` / `metricsScrapeEnabled: true`), `process_metrics.py` adds aggregate statistics to `processed/pod_startup_times.json` (`aggregate`) and `processed/replica_status.json` (`aggregate_ready_replicas`). `metrics_processor` embeds both files into the v0.2 report under `results.observability`, where they are `Statistics`. That model requires `units`, which the repo's own fixture `br_v0_2_legacy_example.yaml` uses as `units: s`. `_compute_stats`, however, keys the unit as `unit`. results.observability.pod_startup_times.aggregate.units                Field required [... 'unit': 's'}]
results.observability.replica_status.aggregate_ready_replicas.units   Field required [... 'unit': 'count'}]

Two other things in these files still fail validation. Fixing them takes a schema decision, so this PR leaves them alone:

## Validation

author: nestorcolt
body:
Closes #2623

Swarm task t425. A swarm tick keeps its controller lease through a slow agent launch. A Codex launch whose harness does not start inside its start timeout fails fast and is recorded against the launch, not the tick.

## Incident
On 2026-10-11, 17:07 to 17:19 local, three ticks each spent about 182 s in `HerdrRuntime._launch` (journal: `_launch wall_s 182.67` and `182.59`, outcome error), then ended with `SwarmError: the controller lease is stale` before the intent pass. Launch records for engineer 1108, 1109 and 1110 stayed `pending`; 1111 recorded `mounted profile canary did not validate before timeout`. The 182 s were the route wait (90 s) plus the binding wait (90 s), after the 30 s start timeout had passed.

## Acceptance against the task
- **"A launch that outlives the lease renews it, so one slow spawn never aborts the other tick steps."** Every fenced runtime call, spawn and resume included, runs inside `lease.kept`, which renews the controller lease once per tick until the call returns. Test `test_a_launch_slower_than_the_lease_keeps_the_intent_pass_in_the_same_tick`: a spawn that advances the controller clock 600 s (over three lease lives) while the tick runs; the lease stays at epoch 1, the tick completes, `last-tick` is written and the intent pass runs after the launch in the same tick. On dev this test fails with `the controller lease is stale` (red run 38151785043).
- **"A Codex launch that does not start inside its start timeout fails fast."** The swarm gives a Codex launch its 30 s start timeout for the terminal to run the launcher, as before. It now also gives the Codex harness the same 30 s to start, measured by its route report (`--route-timeout 30` for Codex; Claude keeps 90). Across 141 recorded Codex launches, the harness started within 4.1 s at most. When the harness has not started inside that timeout, init-agent fails the launch at once with `the harness did not report its route within 30s`. A failed route fails with `the harness route is failed: <error>`. Neither case waits the 90 s binding timeout that made the incident 182 s, so a stuck Codex launch now ends in about 60 s. Tests: `test_a_codex_launch_must_start_its_harness_inside_the_start_timeout`, `test_a_codex_launch_that_never_reports_its_route_fails_without_the_binding_wait` (Codex, exit 3, binding wait never called) and `test_a_profiled_launch_with_no_route_report_fails_at_the_route_timeout`. The lease is kept through the launch either way.
- **"Recorded against the launch, not the tick."** Test `test_a_slow_launch_that_never_starts_is_recorded_against_the_launch_not_the_tick`: a slow launch that raises the init-agent route failure leaves the swarm `launches` row as `failed` with that exact error. The tick still runs the intent pass and keeps lease epoch 1.
- **"Done when a test with a launch slower than the lease keeps the intent pass running in the same tick, and the pull request merges."** The first test above, green in Tests 38155567032. The merge is this pull request.

## What is not weakened
No fencing is relaxed: a lease taken by another controller stops the heartbeat, and the next fenced write still refuses (`test_beat_stops_once_the_lease_is_lost`, `test_a_tick_whose_lease_was_stolen_stops`, `test_run_tick_stops_between_steps_when_another_controller_took_the_lease`). The only launches that now fail sooner are ones that could never validate. Either the harness never reported a route, or it reported a failed route and had already exited 3 before starting the agent.

## How the phase uses it
Tier 5 runs the swarm controller on Anton capacity, where spawns go through the same `FencedRuntime` in the distributed deployment, with Kubernetes placement as well as herdr. `lease.kept` wraps that path unchanged, so a slow Pod or herdr launch no longer drops the controller lease or skips the intent, merge and health passes of that tick. The fencing contract is unchanged: a lease another controller took stops the heartbeat, and the next fenced write still refuses (`test_beat_stops_once_the_lease_is_lost`, existing `test_a_tick_whose_lease_was_stolen_stops`). `tests/swarm/test_controller_placement.py` and `tests/test_swarm_v2_controller.py` pass on this head.

## Change
- `lease.beat` / `lease.kept`: a thread renews the controller lease once per tick (`lease.beat_s`) while a fenced runtime call runs; it stops on a lost lease and keeps going through a Redis error. `FencedRuntime` wraps every runtime call and `spawn` in it.
- `HerdrRuntime.resume` runs its launch as a tick step, so the tick lock is refreshed before it, as for fresh spawns.
- `HerdrRuntime._argv`: a Codex launch passes `--route-timeout 30`, its start timeout, so its harness must start inside the start timeout.
- `init_agent._route_reported`: a profiled launch whose harness reported no route, or a route outside routed, bare and direct, fails at the route timeout instead of waiting the binding timeout too. The swarm records that `SpawnError` on the launch row as `failed`.

## Evidence
- Red: Proofs 38151785043 on tests only commit 68f865692: 7 failed, the slow launch tests with `the controller lease is stale`.
- Green: Proofs 38152059859 on 93dc43478: 444 passed. Tests 38155567032 on head 1e50d95da: every unit shard, mutation and the required gate pass.
- Mutation: two earlier rounds found a surviving resume argument (killed by a resume terminate test) and a heartbeat loop mutant that spun on a set stop event (the loop now checks the stop flag first).
- Review: Standards and Spec readers, three rounds. Standards closed all findings. Spec closed all; the start timeout wording was settled by amending the issue to the route timeout reading.

**Phase Swarm v2, tier 5: scale on Anton capacity, masters scale:** Tier 5 of 8 of Swarm v2, ordered so the swarm can run on Anton compute first. ASG capacity reuse, checkpoints for Spot, several masters with a private channel, health and controls for a distributed swarm. Spec for every task here: /home/iamroot/dev/tcc-ecosystem/agentihooks/Swarm-v2.md, one section per work package. Authorized repos: agentihooks, agentibrain-kernel, antoncore.

**Task t425, Swarm tick keeps its controller lease through a slow agent launch and a stuck Codex launch fails fast:** Parent: the Anton push, every task in tiers one to five merges through the tick's intent pass. Observed on the eleventh from 17:07 to 17:19 local: three ticks in a row spent 182 seconds in the herdr launch of a Codex engineer, then ended with the controller lease is stale, aborting the whole tick before the intent pass, so a ready pull request's draft intent verdict was never refreshed and its merge queue was refused. author: ninjudd
body:
The `windows` CI job fails on every run of `main`, and every branch cut from `main` inherits the failure, so a red windows check says nothing about the pull request it sits on. The failures come from `main`'s own tests meeting Windows, not from any open pull request. This change fixes the 12 tests that fail on every windows run, and the inventory-cache test that failed in 7 of the 22 failed windows runs I read on 2026-10-11 (main's newest run and every failed branch run back to 2026-10-11 04:39 UTC). It also gives `clone.test.ts`'s heavy setup hook room to finish. It changes test files and one plan note, and no product code.

- **The voice host's process tests** (`src/keys/voice-host.test.ts`, 7 tests). They start an extensionless Node script with a `#!` line as `FIELD_SCLANG`. Windows cannot start that, and `sclangCommand` refuses it there with "which Windows cannot start directly" before anything spawns. They now skip on win32, the way `src/graph/build.test.ts` skips its `#!/bin/sh` sclang stubs. The missing-binary refusal in the same block still runs everywhere, and `src/generators/supercollider.test.ts` covers the Windows lookup rules on every platform.
- **Instrument resolution** (`src/keys/voice-host.test.ts`, 3 tests). `instrumentPath` resolves a program against the project root with `path.resolve`, so on Windows it answers `D:\p\shared\instruments\pad.scd`, and `resolveInstrument`'s refusal names that path. A program is a file to open, so a native path is correct; only project-relative paths that are data stay slash-separated. The product code is right and the expectations now build native paths with `path.resolve` and `path.join`.
- **MIDI take cleanup** (`src/commands/record-midi-daemon.test.ts`, 2 tests). The `afterEach` kills the daemons and calls `rmSync` on the temp project at once. On Windows a killed daemon keeps the project as its cwd until it exits, so the removal failed with `EPERM`. It now goes through `removeTempProject` (`src/testing/temp.ts`), as the other daemon test files do.
- **The inventory cache** (`src/audio/plugin-hosting.test.ts`, "serves an unchanged file from cache and re-reads a changed one"). Every failure was at the same-size rewrite: the third read returned the cached second object. That write follows the previous one at once, and on Windows it can land in the same timestamp tick, so no timestamp moves and the size and file index match. The test now waits 50 ms on win32 before that write, as its sibling test already does. The tick is the inferred cause, as the sibling's comment says; it was not measured.
- **The clone tests' setup** (`src/commands/clone.test.ts`). Its `beforeEach` builds the source project, commits it, clones it bare, and pushes its LFS objects, one git or git-lfs process after another. On the windows runner that takes 2 to 3 s, judged by the file's tests that do nothing beyond it, but process starts there stall now and then, and on this pull request's first windows run one stall pushed the hook to 10.6 s, past vitest's 10 s default. The hook measures nothing about `clone`, so it now gets 30 s.
- **The Windows plan** (`docs/projects/windows-portability/readme.md` §7.2). Its guard census now counts the seven voice host tests beside `build.test.ts`'s two.

Two kinds of intermittent failure remain, and this change leaves both alone because neither is a test defect.

- **Loop takes in `src/commands/punch-daemon.test.ts`**, now #203, failed in 6 of the 22 runs: "timed out waiting for three passes to land", `loop_takes` missing from status after three takes landed, `missed` at 1, and once "field-audiod stopped answering mid-take". Reading `serviceCapture` and `recordAudioBlock` in `native/audiod/src/player.cpp` shows two loop handoff races that a slow message thread opens, which fits these symptoms; I have not reproduced them. First, a wrap that arrives before the heartbeat has serviced the previous pass ends the loop for good, because that path does not request a new start. Second, a wrap that arrives while `serviceCapture` is finalizing, before the next standby is open, counts a missed pass. If the heartbeat then runs before the callback adopts the late standby, `capture` stays null, status loses `loop_takes`, and the following pass's `serviceCapture` dereferences a null `finished`.
- **Runner stalls** outside `clone.test.ts`: a 10 s `beforeEach` timeout twice in `src/model/project.test.ts`, whose hook only creates a project, and a 5 s test timeout once in `src/audiod/live-session.test.ts`. A hook that only creates a project does not take 10 s, so these read as the runner stalling rather than as tests to change.

## Testing

From the root of a checkout of `windows/ci-green`, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and a native build (`cmake -S native/audiod -B native/audiod/build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` then `cmake --build native/audiod/build --parallel 8 --config Release`):

```sh
pnpm typecheck
FIELD_AUDIOD=$PWD/native/audiod/build/field-audiod_artefacts/Release/field-audiod pnpm exec vitest run src/keys/voice-host.test.ts src/commands/record-midi-daemon.test.ts src/audio/plugin-hosting.test.ts src/commands/clone.test.ts
FIELD_AUDIOD=$PWD/native/audiod/build/field-audiod_artefacts/Release/field-audiod pnpm test
project check
```

On macOS you should see `tsc --noEmit` print nothing, then `Tests  57 passed | 1 skipped (58)` for the four files, then `Test Files  81 passed (81)` and `Tests  1026 passed | 1 skipped (1027)` for the suite, then "Project plans are valid." The one skip is "refuses to arm for MIDI where there is no MIDI source", which runs only where there is no MIDI service, such as Linux without `/dev/snd/seq`. On macOS and Linux these changes leave every changed test running, so a failure in "resolving an instrument" there would mean the native-path expectations broke POSIX. The commands leave the native build in `native/audiod/build`, and the tests remove their own temp projects.

The real check is this pull request's `windows` CI job, which cannot run by hand here. In its `pnpm test` step the seven "the voice host process" tests should report as skipped, and the three "resolving an instrument" tests and both MIDI take tests should pass. Any `FAIL` line for `src/keys/voice-host.test.ts` or `src/commands/record-midi-daemon.test.ts`, or an `EPERM` naming `field-record-midi-`, shows the change is wrong. A `punch-daemon.test.ts` loop take failure there is the daemon race above (#203), not this change, and a `beforeEach` timeout in `clone.test.ts` would mean a stall longer than 30 s.

author: jmmana
body:
## Summary
Extends `GET /api/v1/usage/rollup` with an opt-in `include=latency,failures` parameter: nearest-rank p50/p95 latency and failure-rate/error-kind breakdowns per group and in `totals`, computed by pure functions shared between the memory and SQLite stores. Omitting `include` reproduces the exact pre-existing response, byte-for-byte.

This is the server half of #89, split out per `.claude/agent-policy.md` (the issue has two independent deliverables: the server rollup extension and the Model Ops UI). Sub-issues: #285 (this PR) and #286 (UI, depends on this one). #89 stays open until both land.

## Changes Made
- `server/usage/reliability.ts` (new): pure, store-agnostic `nearestRankPercentile` (deterministic nearest-rank, `sorted[ceil(p*n)-1]`), `summarizeLatency`, `summarizeFailures`, `computeFailureRate`, `failureErrorKindKey`.
- `server/usage/types.ts`: `RollupInclude`, optional `failedCalls`/`attempts`/`failureRate`/`failures`/`latency` on `UsageRollupTotals`, `include` on `RollupQuery`.
- `server/usage/rollup.ts`: `include` parsing/validation in `parseRollupQuery` (reuses the endpoint's existing `400 invalid_filter` shape, not `/api/v1/events`'s `validation_failed` — see note below); memory-mode accumulation of latency samples/missing and per-`errorKind` failure counts; new SQLite sidecar queries (`buildGroupLatencySql`/`buildGroupFailuresSql`/`buildTotalsLatencySql`/`buildTotalsFailuresSql`), no percentile computed in SQL (none exists).
- `server/index.ts`: one `RollupQuery` literal (the export-scope helper) updated for the new required `include` field.
- `docs/integration.md`: new `include` row and a "Latency and failure rates" subsection in the rollup reference.
- Tests: new `tests/reliability-rollups.test.mjs` (pure-function cases incl. ties/unsorted/0-sample/seeded-random property test, memory/SQLite parity, the "totals differ from either group's own p95" rule with a hand-verified fixture, dedup-by-`requestId` honesty, no-model grouping); extended `tests/integration-api.test.mjs` (HTTP `include` combinations, 400 on an unknown value, byte-for-byte unchanged when absent) and `tests/server-rate-limit.test.mjs` (the ingest limiter's own 429 never increments `rateLimitCount`); two pre-existing `RollupQuery` literals in `tests/usage-export-format.test.mjs` updated for the new required field.

## Notable deviations from the issue text (verified against the real shipped code, not the issue's own stale sketch)
- The real `LLM_ERROR_KINDS` enum value is `rate_limited`, not `rate_limit` as the issue's example shows.
- The endpoint already has its own `400 { error: "invalid_filter", issues }` contract for every other bad parameter (`groupBy`, `limit`, `asOfSeq`, ...); `include` reuses it rather than introducing `/api/v1/events`'s `validation_failed` shape onto one parameter of an endpoint that otherwise never uses it.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched: `tests/docs-versions.test.mjs` enforces that `## [Unreleased]` stays empty between releases in this repo; the entry belongs in the release PR, not here.
- Dedup by `requestId` (#48) already happens at ledger write time, keyed on `(provider, requestId)` without the event type; by the time a rollup query runs, `usage_ledger` already holds at most one row per that pair, so there is nothing further to deduplicate inside this feature itself. A genuine failed-then-successful retry is only both-counted when the provider assigns a new request id to the retry (the realistic case, since it's a new provider-side call) — covered by a dedicated test.

## Verification & Commands Executed
```bash
npm run lint                                             # tsc --noEmit, clean
npx tsx --test tests/reliability-rollups.test.mjs tests/integration-api.test.mjs \
  tests/server-rate-limit.test.mjs tests/usage-rollup.test.mjs tests/usage-export-format.test.mjs
# 202 passed, 0 failed
npm run test:node                                        # full server suite: 1277 passed, 1 pre-existing skip, 0 failed
```
`npm run build`/`test:unit`/`test:golden` were not run: no frontend, library or SDK file changed (demo-app/Model Ops is the separate #286).

## Checklist
- [x] Code follows project conventions (English codebase and docs).
- [x] No secrets or real user credentials included.
- [x] Tests added or updated for all changes.
- [x] Verified on local environment.
- [ ] Golden reconciliation suite (`npm run test:golden`) not run: no reconciliation-relevant figure changed by this PR (the new fields are additive and opt-in).

Closes #285
Refs #89

author: josh-complex
body:
P1-15 part 1: the homomorphic tally of ADR 0002 (option B) and ADR 0003 (option C), with ADR 0015 deciding what the tally publishes. It covers cell aggregates, trustees' summed shares and their check, and the combination of `k` valid summed shares into each cell's opening. The tally transcript (part 2), destruction statements (part 3) and regional cells (part 4) follow.

## What changed

- **`docs/adr/0015-tally-publication.md`** (`Accepted (agent) — owner may veto`, option C, listed under Decisions to review). Trustees exchange summed shares privately under the hybrid KEM. Summed shares never go on the board, IPFS or the archive. Only each cell's opening `(V_j, R_j)` is published. The rejected options:
  - Option A, publishing summed shares, leaks per-seat values. Combined with posted shares, those values can complete a ballot after a classical break (`crypto-review`'s finding on this PR).
  - Option B, re-randomising the sums with zero-sharings, closes a corrupt trustee's view only against coalitions of fewer than `k − 1`.
- **`docs/spec/tally.md`** (new page):
  - aggregates;
  - summed shares and the trustees' summed-share check;
  - combination of the `k` lowest passing seats by Lagrange interpolation at 0;
  - the verifier's opening checks: `tally-missing`, `tally-opening`, `tally-range`, `tally-conflict`. An opening is attributed only when it carries a signature binding the definition hash, the cell and `m`;
  - coarser totals, derived by adding cells and never opened;
  - residuals.
- **`docs/spec/verifier.md`:**
  - 7.2 checks the published opening.
  - 7.4 treats a disclosed summed share as unattributable: it is reported against its sender or any recipient, never against its signer alone.
  - 8.2 counts, per cell, the counted ballots with fewer than `k` valid posted shares.
- **`packages/crypto/src/tally.ts`:** `aggregateCell`, `sumShares`, `checkSummedShares`, `lagrangeAtZero`, `openCell` (a trustee's combination), `checkOpening` (the verifier's check) and `deriveTotal`.
- **Vectors:** `docs/spec/vectors/tally.json` and its independent generator, `packages/crypto/scripts/tally-vectors.py`.
- **Threat files:** T-14, T-15, T-16, T-29 and T-54. T-15's Status and Mitigation are updated, and the adversary is now A-11.
- **Status:** `docs/status/P1-15.md`, and a Decisions to review entry in `docs/STATUS.md`.

No new dependencies. No new domain-separation tags.

## Threats

- **T-15 / T-16:** publishing only openings keeps the tally record information-theoretically hiding beyond each cell's count, even against an adversary who later breaks the posted shares' classical encryption. Ballots with `k` or more posted shares are readable after such a break, as ADR 0002 already states. They shrink the cell's anonymity set, which 8.2 reports.
- **T-29:** a wrong opening fails `tally-opening` and is attributed to its signer. A wrong summed share is caught by the other trustees but is no longer publicly attributable (stated as known-weak).
- **T-54:** any `k` passing seats give the same opening. Fewer than `k` gives `tally-quorum`.
- **T-14:** a corrupt or seized trustee sees every seat's summed share. This residual is stated and not mitigated.

## How it's tested

- **Vectors:** 11 cells, 16 published openings checked by the verifier, and a derived total. The vectors come from an independent Python implementation, which finds openings by Gaussian elimination and cross-checks them against Lagrange coefficients. TypeScript reproduces every aggregate, summed share, verdict, combined set, coefficient, opening and opening verdict.
- **fast-check properties,** passing at `FC_NUM_RUNS=1000`:
  - honest sums from any `k` or more seats open each cell;
  - any other `k` seats give the same opening;
  - any changed summed share is excluded;
  - a sum that leaves out one ballot fails at every seat.
- **Unit tests and mutation checks:** dropping the summed-share check or the range check fails tests.

## Independent review

In-session subagent reviews ran three passes over the ADR 0015 fix. They covered framing through a disclosed summed share, the option B bound, multiple openings per cell, and attribution only with a binding signature. All findings are resolved; the details are in `docs/status/P1-15.md`. `crypto-review` failed on the earlier head (published summed shares leaked), and that failure is fixed at the root by ADR 0015. `crypto-review` and `claude-review` now pass on this head.

## Known-weak

- Nothing sends, posts or signs summed shares or openings yet (part 2), so verifier 7.3 and 7.4 and signer attribution are still missing.
- A corrupt trustee sees every seat's summed share (T-14, T-15).
- `tally-conflict` is specified, but `checkOpening` takes only one opening. Part 2 implements the rule.
- A wrong summed share isn't publicly attributable (T-29).
- No published vectors exist for this composition (T-36).
- Scalar arithmetic in JavaScript `bigint` isn't constant time.

**npm:** nuxt 4.6.0 → 4.6.1, @tauri-apps/api 2.12.1 → 2.12.3, @tauri-apps/cli 2.12.1 → 2.12.2, plugin-dialog 2.8.1 → 2.8.2, plugin-shell 2.4.0 → 2.5.0, plugin-updater 2.13.1 → 2.13.3, vue-router 5.3.1 → 5.4.0, vite 8.3.3 → 8.3.4, @playwright/test 1.63 → 1.64, @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.9 → 6.0.10, vue-tsc 3.3.12 → 3.3.13, @iconify-json/lucide 1.2.140 → 1.2.142

## Held back
- **keyring `=3.6.3`** (latest 4.2.0): v4 turns `keyring` into a sample/CLI crate. Apps are meant to use `keyring-core` 1.x plus a store crate per platform. Migrating means rewriting `credentials.rs` and verifying that hosted OS probes can still read entries written by 3.6.3. That work is security-sensitive, so it is left as a follow-up.
- **typescript 5.9.3** (latest 7.0.2): the TS 7 npm package no longer exposes the classic JS API that vue-tsc/Volar need. 6.0.x is an optional intermediate step.
- **@types/node 22**: it matches the Node 22.22.3 pin.
- Node and Rust toolchain pins are unchanged.

## Follow-up changes (commit 2)
- **Shell → opener:** removed `tauri-plugin-shell` (Rust + npm, `plugins.shell` config, `shell:allow-open`) and added `tauri-plugin-opener` 2.7.1. The new grant is `opener:allow-open-url`, scoped to exactly `https://github.com/calebsmithdev/wowthing-sync/releases/latest`. `UpdateBanner.vue` now calls `openUrl`, and the process-spawning shell plugin is gone from the binary.
- **Updater `PreviousAppNotRestored`:** when the macOS swap can't restore the old app, the banner now reads *Reinstall Needed*. It explains that the previous copy was kept as "(previous version)" and offers a **Download** action. The raw error stays under Technical details. A unit test covers this.
- **Notification click:** a native `on_action` handler (`tap`) opens the main window through the tray's existing `show` dispatch. Only production builds register it; the smoke/integration builders are unchanged.
- **base64:** set to `default-features = false, features = ["std"]`, which drops the SIMD `unsafe` engine from the CLI verifier.
- **Nuxt workaround removed:** dropped `nitro.externals.inline: ['nuxt/internal/']`, since Nuxt 4.6.1 (21657c6fc) inlines its dist through a matcher that normalizes path separators. `scripts/nuxt-runtime.test.mjs` now reads Nuxt's shipped `NUXT_DIST_RE` matcher and runs Nitro's real externals plugin on a Windows-style resolved ID. If Nuxt stops normalizing, the test fails with instructions to restore the workaround. **The Windows CI job is the real confirmation here.**
- AGENTS.md security notes are updated: opener grant, notification click, and the requirement to bump minisign-verify together with the updater.
- No action needed for tauri 2.12.2/2.12.3 or fs 2.7: their fixes arrive with the version bump.

## Changelog report
### Breaking changes (none affect this repo)
- **minisign-verify 0.3**: the API is unchanged. It now rejects non-canonical Ed25519 `S` values and removes some `unsafe` code. `updater_fixture.rs:74-78` matches `tauri_plugin_updater::Error::Minisign(minisign_verify::Error::InvalidSignature)`, which only compiles while our direct version matches the updater's. Both are on 0.3.0 now; keep them bumped together. Updater 2.13.3 also changes the error message text, but nothing in the repo asserts the old string.
- **base64 0.23**: `general_purpose::STANDARD` and `Engine::decode` (`bin/signature-check.rs`) are unchanged. MSRV is now 1.71 and SIMD is on by default.
- **notification 2.6**: the JS `onAction` callback type changed. We don't import the JS plugin, and the Rust builder use in `sync_service.rs` is unaffected.
- **Playwright 1.64**: `screen` is now forwarded from device descriptors. Our config sets its own viewport.
- **vue-router 5.4**: the only breaking change is in the experimental router.

### Recommended changes
- **Move from shell `open` to `tauri-plugin-opener`.** Shell `open` has been deprecated since 2.1, and 2.5 still marks it deprecated. Our only use is `UpdateBanner.vue`. Moving to `openUrl` with an exact-URL `opener:allow-open-url` scope removes a process-spawning plugin from the binary.
- **Updater 2.13.2 macOS atomic swap**: adds the new `Error::PreviousAppNotRestored`. Show it in plain language in the update controller instead of as a generic install failure.
- **tauri 2.12.2/2.12.3**: macOS `process::restart` now goes through LaunchServices, which should make relaunch after an update more reliable. Also fixes a `once`-listener panic and keeps Channel messages delivered after a handler throws. The NSIS downgrade block doesn't apply because `allowDowngrades` keeps its default.
- **fs 2.7.0** (transitive) brings symlink-scope and `customFlags` security fixes. The frontend has no fs grants, so this is defense in depth only.
- **Dependency advisories**: `npm audit` reports 15 advisories (7 critical, 7 high, 1 low). All are in build/dev tooling: nuxt devtools → simple-git, nitropack → listhen → node-forge, braces/micromatch, and esbuild's dev server on Windows. None ship in the app bundle, and none has a non-breaking fix (`npm audit fix` changed nothing). `cargo audit` finds no vulnerabilities, only 2 upstream GTK3-stack warnings (proc-macro-error unmaintained, glib 0.18 unsound).

### Improvements / opportunities
- **Nuxt 4.6.1** fixes inlining of the nitro runtime on Windows paths, so the `externals.inline` workaround in `nuxt.config.ts` may no longer be needed (check on Windows CI). Its dev-handler changes are covered by the `test:native:dev` run.
- **Notifications**: Rust `on_action` now works on desktop. Clicking the batch summary could focus the window or open Status.
- **base64**: `default-features = false, features = ["std"]` would drop the SIMD `unsafe` code from the CLI-only verifier.
- **@tauri-apps/api 2.12.2**: `onFocusChanged`/`onDragDropEvent` now return awaitable cleanups. We don't use them today.

## Validation (macOS ARM64, Node 22.22.3, Rust 1.97.1)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm ci`, lint, typecheck | ✅ |
| `test:unit` | ✅ 44 tests (after commit 2) |
| `generate` | ✅ |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | ✅ |
| `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -D warnings` (default + `integration-test`) | ✅ |
| `cargo test --locked` | ✅ 42 passed, 1 ignored (nightly endurance) |
| `cargo check --locked` (default, smoke-test, signature-audit, os-integration-test) | ✅ |
| `node --test scripts/*.test.mjs` | ✅ 31 passed, 3 platform skips |
| `node scripts/release-metadata.mjs verify` | ✅ 1.1.1 |
| Browser e2e smoke (`test:e2e`) | ✅ 2 passed |
| Native WKWebView smoke (`test:native`, after commit 2) | ✅ `errors:[]`, saved=1, synced=true |
| `cargo audit` | ✅ 0 vulnerabilities, 2 warnings |

I did not run `test:integration` locally, and nothing ran on Windows, Linux or Intel macOS. All checks above were rerun after commit 2. CI must cover them, especially the updater install path and the minisign error identity.

author: jonsandruck
body:
Two things, found one after the other while testing translucent tiles. The first adds support for see-through surfaces. The second fixes a gap in the physical model that glass made obvious but that affects every surface.

## See-through surfaces: `glass`

Making a surface's background translucent made its grain louder and lighter. Surface mode isolates the element so its layers can sit under the content, but `mix-blend-mode` only blends inside its own stacking context. As the background went transparent the grain had nothing to blend with and quietly turned into plain alpha compositing — the same failure room mode already handles on `<body>`.

**`--cast-grain-z` for surface mode.** Room mode had it; surface mode hard-coded `z-index: -1`, so the fix couldn't be expressed at all. The default changes nothing: the full demo page was pixel-identical to main in both themes.

**A `glass` modifier**, `data-cast="surface glass"`, which sets seven things:

```css
isolation: auto;
--cast-surface-z: 2;
--cast-grain-z: 9999;
--cast-edge-lit: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cast-light-color) 50%, transparent);
--cast-edge-shade: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45);
--cast-edge-overhead: var(--cast-edge-lit);
--cast-grain-blend: soft-light;
```

- **Dropping isolation alone is not enough.** Layers at `-1` then paint behind the element's own background; on an opaque tile the sheen measured 0.00. Both layers come up as well.
- **A stronger rim**, because a see-through face no longer outlines itself. Tuned to match an opaque card: lit side +80.2 against a card's +76.5, up from +55.0.
- **`soft-light` blending.** Under `overlay`, the library default, `glass` barely helped (grain RMS 3.07 → 2.80). `overlay` is loud over mid-tones, which is what most photos are. Since glass can't know its backdrop, it takes the blend whose worst case is half the other's.
- **One class of specificity**, via `:where()`. It still beats the library defaults, but an author's own class now overrides it. The first version used two attribute selectors and beat `.panel { --cast-surface-z: 1 }`; confirmed against that commit before fixing.

Grain's own contribution as the background goes from opaque to clear, `soft-light`, mid-grey backdrop: RMS 1.01 → 3.05 without `glass`, 1.00 → 1.36 with it.

**Not tuned by theme.** The demo first tinted its glass tiles with the theme's surface colour, which made them +18.1 L\* in light mode and −6.4 in dark. Behind glass the surface is the backdrop, which doesn't change with the theme. The tiles are now clear and skip the page's dark-mode overrides: +2.4 and +2.6.

The demo has a live example over a photograph of patterned window glass from Unsplash, credited in the README.

## Faces stay lit under the lamp

As the light moved over any surface, its sheen and rim faded to exactly zero. A clear glass tile's lit rim ran +24.7 far away and 0.0 under the light, while room mode's pool was brightest in the same spot.

This was half of the obliqueness change from #8. Directly overhead, neither side of a face is brighter, so the directional effects should fade there — that part was right. But nothing replaced them, so "no direction" became "no light".

**`--cast-overhead`** (`1 − obliqueness`) hands the directional effects over to even ones:

- **Face:** a uniform wash of the light's colour, at the sheen's strength and falloff.
- **Rim:** an even ring in the new `--cast-edge-overhead`. On a solid object the rim is a bevel tilting away from an overhead lamp, so it gets cos 45° = 0.71 of the face's light and sits just *darker* than the face — 29% of the shade colour by default. On glass, light through the pane lights the edge from inside, so `glass` sets it to the lit colour.

Rim against the face, light moving in, mid-grey backdrop:

| light distance | solid | glass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| far | +9.2 / −21.1 | +24.7 / −21.2 |
| 300px | +1.9 / −14.0 | +20.5 / −0.9 |
| on the tile, before | 0.0 / 0.0 | 0.0 / 0.0 |
| on the tile, now | −6.7 / −6.7 | +22.6 / +22.6 |

A first version drew the lit ring on everything, which put solid edges brighter than their faces under the lamp. That's corrected in the last commit.

## What changes on an existing page

- **Light far from an element:** nothing. With the light off to one side, all 18 viewports of the demo were pixel-identical in both themes, apart from one small box that also differs when the same code is run twice.
- **Light mode, pale card under the lamp:** the face can't brighten (no headroom), but the edge now survives: +0.4 before, −8.7 now. That was a known limitation.
- **Dark mode, card under the lamp:** face +7.4 L\*, edge just below it. Code chips keep their own background, so they stand out a little more there.
- **Reduced motion / no JavaScript:** the static fallback sits inside 45°, so it picks up a little of the overhead terms — +1.1 L\* on a dark card's face.

## Known, not fixed

- CSS clips an element's own drop shadow to outside its box, so a clear tile never shows its shadow through itself the way real glass would.
- `glass` does not frost. Add `backdrop-filter` for that.
- Over the window photograph, the ridges hide most of the grain difference between the two example tiles. The measured numbers come from a flat backdrop.

No browser-floor change: `:where()`, `min()`, `clamp()`, `color-mix()` and plain `calc()`, all already required or older.

author: tobert
body:
`kaibo configure` stopped at `consult`, so a user with an OpenRouter key was never told about `decide`, and one with a Stability key never about `generate`. This adds a step 7 to the shared configure steps (MCP and CLI both get it; the end step is now 8) mapping keys to tools, and says what the caller must do: `decide` needs its own `judge` cast and `cast = "judge"` on every call, because the default cast cannot decide. `generate` needs its own provider key; OpenRouter does not staff media.

The guide gets a key-to-tool table and a paragraph on Jev: a fast classifier, probabilities and no text, about 32k tokens of state, a fraction of a cent per call. The template comment says the `openrouter/` prefix is the backend's name.

A new test checks the step is present on both front doors. The old prompt had none of its needles. The CLI prompt must not name `kaibo://` resources, so the step says "the example config".

## Summary
Supersedes #50 via #63. Preserves candidates' authentic uploaded CVs (.pdf, .docx, .doc) via private Supabase Storage instead of re-synthesizing them into generic ReportLab layouts.

Branch created directly off `origin/main` containing exclusively the changes for Issue #63.

### Key Changes
- **In-Memory Streaming & Storage (`jobs/apply/cv_storage.py`)**: Stateless retrieval of candidate resumes directly into `io.BytesIO` buffers with zero temporary disk writes, fulfilling Constitution §1.2. Generates SHA-256 audit snapshots for `applications.resume_snapshot`.
- **Zero-Dependency Document Security Scanner (`jobs/apply/cv_security.py`)**:
  - Enforces 2 MB file size cap and extension whitelist (`.pdf`, `.docx`, `.doc`).
  - Scans PDF Action dictionaries to block weaponized executable payloads (`/S /JavaScript`, `/S /Launch`, `/EmbeddedFiles`) while permitting legitimate developer GitHub URLs and skill text.
  - Inspects DOCX ZIP archives to block Word macros (`vbaproject`, `.exe`, `.vbs`) while permitting legitimate embedded charts (`.bin`).
  - Rejects legacy DOC files with OLE macro streams.
- **Database Schema Migration (`db/schema.sql`)**:
  - Adds `resume_storage_path`, `resume_filename`, `resume_content_type`, and `resume_uploaded_at` to `users`.
  - Configures private `resumes` bucket with 2 MB cap and allowed MIME whitelist.
  - Adds Row Level Security (RLS) policies on `storage.objects` restricting users to `resumes/<auth_user_id>/*`.
- **Auto-Derive Storage URL (`config.py`)**: Automatically resolves `https://<ref>.supabase.co` from direct or pooler `DATABASE_URL`.
- **Constitution (§1.2)**: Updated architectural invariant to mandate in-memory candidate CV streaming from Supabase Storage instead of ReportLab PDF compilation.

## Verification & Testing
- 24 new unit tests in `tests/test_cv_security.py` and `tests/test_cv_storage.py`.
- Full test suite passing: 219 passed, 1 deselected in 0.29s.
- `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy`, and `python -m scripts.validate_seed_schema` passing 100%.
- Verified against live Supabase staging: database schema applied, bucket configured, test resume uploaded, downloaded in-memory, security scanned, and audit snapshot verified.

Closes #63

author: zyrona-labs
body:
## Bug
The controller creates a CSI `VolumeSnapshot` per volume and does not tie it to the `MachineSnapshot`. The self-test's cleanup deleted the MachineSnapshot, restore and claims, but not the VolumeSnapshots, so **every `full` run on a CSI cluster left a snapshot (and its data) behind**. I found four of them on the lab host while cleaning up after the session.

## Fix
- `kube.Client.DeleteVolumeSnapshot`.
- The snapshot-restore cleanup reads the MachineSnapshot's `status.volumeSnapshots` names and deletes those VolumeSnapshots before deleting the MachineSnapshot.
- kairon-ui's ClusterRole gains `get`/`delete` on `volumesnapshots` (chart and `deploy/rbac.yaml`) so the dashboard-started run can clean up too.
- The simulated controller no longer cascades the delete, so a leak fails the tests (verified: the assertion fails with the fix reverted).

## Test plan
- [x] `go vet`, `go test -race ./internal/selftest ./internal/kube`; RBAC-coverage script; `helm lint`
- [x] golangci-lint v2.14.0 over `./...` (run on the lab host): 0 issues
- [x] Real lab cluster (CSI hostpath): `selftest --only boot,snapshot-restore` passes, and no machines, claims, VolumeSnapshots or VolumeSnapshotContents with `selftest` in their name remain afterwards
