author: lucamartinetti
body:
Custom inspectors can now say which phases they inspect, so a request-only plugin no longer forces every response onto the buffered path.

## The problem

`plugin.rs` answered `inspects_responses() = true` for every loaded wasm plugin, and `Chain::inspects_responses()` is the streaming switch in `flow.rs`. Loading `header-policy` (requests only) made the egress buffer every response whole, under the per-body cap: downloads past 256 MiB failed and LLM token streams lost their streaming.

## Compatibility mechanism

The world moves to **`agentcage:inspector@1.1.0`** and gains one optional export and its type:

```wit
flags phase-set { request, response, websocket }   // in `types`, @since(1.1.0)
export phases: func() -> phase-set;                 // in the world, @since(1.1.0)
```

- **The egress does not instantiate through the `inspector` world.** Generated `instantiate` type-checks every export the world declares, so a 1.0.0 component, which has no `phases`, would be refused. Instead `wasmtime::component::bindgen!` gets a small host-only inline world, `agentcage:egress-host/base`. It holds the three exports every 1.x component has (`configure`, `inspect-request`, `inspect-response`) over the live `types`. The loader instantiates with `Linker::instantiate` plus `Base::new`, then looks `phases` up by name with `Instance::get_func`:
  - export missing (a component built against 1.0.0): the plugin is treated as inspecting every phase, exactly as today;
  - export present: it is typed with `Func::typed::<(), (PhaseSet,)>` and called once, under the fuel budget, right after `configure` succeeds;
  - wrong type, or a trap: the load fails (`inspector <name>: phases failed: …`), so the chain keeps its previous config (fail closed).
- **Why this is sound in the component model.** Record, enum and flags types are checked structurally. A 1.0.0 component's `context` and `verdict` therefore match the 1.1.0 ones even though its `types` import is `@1.0.0`, and a world export is a plain name, not a versioned one. It also works the other way: a 1.1 plugin on an older egress just has an extra export nobody asks for.
- **Why the call comes after `configure`.** The answer can depend on the config: `dlp-regex` declares `response` only when `responses: true` is set. Each instance gets the same config, so the first instance's answer is the plugin's.

## Loader and chain

`Plugin` stores the declared `Phases`:
- `inspect_request` runs only for a declared `request` (HTTP) or `websocket` (an outbound WS message).
- `inspect_response` runs only for a declared `response` (HTTP) or `websocket` (an inbound WS message).
- `inspects_responses()` is true only for a declared `response`.

WebSocket messages never depended on `inspects_responses()`. The chain runs on every message and the plugin filters by `websocket`. No change to `chain.rs` or `flow.rs` was needed: the chain now streams whenever no live inspector declares responses.

## SDK

- `Phases` (a `REQUEST`/`RESPONSE`/`WEBSOCKET` set with `const fn union`/`contains`, plus `|`).
- `Inspector::phases(&self) -> Phases`, defaulting to `Phases::ALL`. Rust cannot reliably tell at compile time which `inspect_*` methods a type overrides, so the SDK does not guess. A plugin is never silently skipped for a phase it implements unless it declares so.
- The export macro implements the new export.
- Examples: `header-policy` declares `REQUEST`. `dlp-regex` declares `REQUEST | WEBSOCKET`, and adds `RESPONSE` only with `responses: true`.

## Tests

- `tests/plugins.rs`:
  - per-phase dispatch for every declaration (misbehaving fixture, `config.phases`);
  - a trapping `phases` fails the load;
  - `header-policy` is called for requests alone;

## Implemented
- Add PostgreSQL adapter implementing the error-aware `core.Repository` introduced in #7; keep the existing JSON demo unchanged by default.
- Add `db/migrations/0002_workspace_documents.sql`: one transactionally versioned JSONB snapshot per previously provisioned organization, with forced row-level security.

- Reject superusers, schema owners and `BYPASSRLS` runtime roles. Validate organization UUID and existence at startup.
- Use transaction-local organization context, SQL parameterization, fresh read-only transactions, serializable row-locked write transactions, and bounded serialization retries. Persist source data and historical reconciliation evidence together.
- Pin MIT-licensed `github.com/lib/pq v1.12.3` in go.mod/go.sum; update Docker build to download the dependency.
- Add live PostgreSQL integration tests using a separate least-privilege runtime login for two pre-provisioned organizations. Tests confirm data isolation, durable state across handles, mutation rollback, missing-org rejection and failed-read propagation.
- Document migration-owner versus runtime-user privileges, private workspace setup, SSL best practices, existing-data migration limitations, and requirements still blocking multi-tenant SaaS launch.

## CI
Latest branch run: https://github.com/savisaluwadana/RevenueLeak-OS/actions/runs/38168010552 (PostgreSQL integration and Docker jobs passed; remaining browser suite in progress at PR creation). Go tests/race, browser, Docker and Postgres isolation all required.

## Critical limitations
- **NOT multi-tenant SaaS authentication**: one configured workspace UUID per server process, one admin login, no OIDC/memberships/RBAC.
- Uses an organization-scoped JSONB document as a transitional persistence adapter; the normalized relational contract/invoice/usage tables from 0001 are not the API's source of truth yet.
- Does not migrate existing JSON pilot data, add backup/restore, encrypted connector vault, durable queues or enterprise finance audit guarantees.
- Not approved for shared-customer production or unreviewed real financial records. Remains tracked in #5.

## Next build
Normalized relational repositories and data migration from pilot snapshots; OIDC/RBAC with end-to-end tenant-scoped HTTP access; durable ingestion, finance approvals and restore/load validation.

author: stringnick
body:
## Summary

A visible document whose text layouts slightly exceed the 8 MiB cache budget can evict its own paragraphs during each sequential redraw. On the next redraw every paragraph is shaped again.

Retain recently used layouts for eight global frames, bounded by 64 MiB. Preserve the 4096-entry limit, 8 MiB single-layout admission limit, immutable layout ownership and font-generation invalidation. Excess cache memory is reclaimed after subsequent unused frames; there is no wall-clock idle timer. Completely idle applications can retain the larger working set, and frames from another window age the shared cache.

## Testing

Regression tests reproduce the first-redraw cache miss on the original implementation and cover reuse, aging, hard limits, clearing, alternating windows, parameter changes and font-generation invalidation. Independent peer review found no blockers.

Six 500 ms samples with identical warmed workloads on Apple M1 Pro / macOS arm64 / Core Text. Each operation requests all paragraph layouts sequentially and ends a frame; setup and warmup are excluded. Before is upstream `9653c25`, with an overlay to compile the identical benchmark.

| 200-paragraph working set | Before median | After median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Time | 21.806 ms | 0.0225 ms |
| Shaping calls | 200 | 0 |
| Go allocations | 5,202 | 0 |
| Go allocated bytes | 4,185,548 | 0 |
| Estimated retained cache bytes | 8,380,974 | 9,011,800 |

The 40-paragraph Core Text control remains allocation-free: 4.301 → 4.032 µs, unchanged estimated cache size. A deterministic stub workload also reproduces the cache cliff. Small control timing differences are noisy; unrelated processes were active on the shared host, while our workers' heavy work did not overlap measurements.

These measure layout retrieval/shaping, not whole-frame rendering. Cache sizes are conservative accounting estimates, not RSS, and Go allocation metrics exclude native Core Text allocations. Working sets above the hard limits or unused for eight global frames can still reshape; caller-held layouts can also outlive cache eviction.

All checks passed with `CGO_ENABLED=0`: targeted cache tests; `go test ./...`; macOS/Linux/Windows builds and vet; production `mygo_noinspector` vet; js/wasm vet excluding CLI; `git diff --check`. GUI E2E and Bun checks were not run for this text-cache-only change.

## AI disclosure

- Tool and model: Codex; GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`, medium) workers for investigation, implementation, tests, benchmarks and independent review; GPT-6 orchestrator for integration and this description.
- Used for: code, tests, benchmarks, review, validation and PR description.
- [x] A human read every line of this change and can explain it.

author: slayerjain
body:
> **Draft.** Review round 4 open: cleanup of hold links after a swap that died; on Fedora/RHEL 9/10 run the distro's own update-ca-trust extract -o into staging; exact-match fallback elsewhere. Being fixed.

## Describe the changes that are made

### What was wrong

Two native keploy runs on one Linux machine — parallel CI jobs on a shared runner, two services recorded side by side — share the system trust store, and each agent installs its run CA there. On `main` they break each other in three ways, and on Fedora every single agent start or stop breaks the machine for a few seconds. All of it was reproduced with the real install code and the distros' real trust stores (see "Reproduction" below).

1. **A starting agent removed every running agent's CA.** `sweepRunLeftovers` deleted every `keploy-mitm-*.crt` that was not the starting agent's own, taking "not mine" to mean "left by a crashed run", and the bundle regeneration that follows dropped those CAs from the bundle. An application of the earlier run that reads only the system store then failed its next handshake with keploy's proxy:
   `curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`.
2. **Agents that start at the same moment failed CA setup.** Each ran the distro's tool with no coordination — at start and again at stop — and the tools are not safe to run two at a time. On Fedora `update-ca-trust` deletes the certificate directory's hash links and recreates them with a plain `ln -s`: `ln: failed to create symbolic link '/etc/pki/tls/certs/002c0b4f.0': File exists`. On Debian `update-ca-certificates` builds the new bundle in one fixed file that every run appends to, moves away and deletes: `mv: cannot stat '/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt.new': No such file or directory`. Either way `SetupCA` returned an error and that run had no working TLS interception.
3. **On Debian the same overlap destroys the machine's CA bundle.** When the runs do not fail, the shared temp file leaves `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` with most of its certificates missing — the machine's own roots, not keploy's. Six agents starting together on `main` left a 150-certificate bundle with 0 to 4 certificates in 5 runs out of 5. Every process on the machine that verifies TLS against the system bundle fails until something regenerates it.
4. **On Fedora every regeneration empties OpenSSL's default certificate directory.** `update-ca-trust` deletes every link in `/etc/pki/tls/certs` before it extracts anything and recreates them after the last extraction: 1.6 to 3.9 s per run with no certificate in that directory. Fedora 44 has no `/etc/pki/tls/cert.pem`, so that directory is the only default source of OpenSSL and of everything that uses its defaults — Python's `ssl` module and `urllib`, Node (Fedora builds it to use them), Ruby, PHP, `openssl` itself. Every keploy start and stop ran the wrapper, so every one of them made every such client on the machine fail for that long, keploy's own CA and the public roots alike; with several agents the gaps came back to back. And because the install ran the wrapper under the run's context, a run cancelled at the wrong moment SIGKILLed it half-way and left the directory empty until something ran it again.

### The fix

**A run's anchors are kept for as long as its agent lives, and the kernel is what says so.** Each agent creates a claim file for its run, `/run/keploy/ca-runs/<run id>`, and holds an exclusive `flock` on it for its whole life (`claimRun`). The sweep removes a `keploy-mitm-<run id>.crt` only when that run's claim can be taken (`runIsLive`): then no process holds it, and the claim is cleared too. The kernel releases a `flock` when the holding process is gone, however it went — clean exit, crash, `SIGKILL`, OOM kill — so no pid is recorded (none to be reused), no start time compared and no age guessed. An anchor with no claim — a crashed run's whose claim was already cleared, one written by a keploy from before this change, one from before a reboot (`/run` is a tmpfs) — is swept as before. The claims directory is `0700` and each claim `0600`, both root's, so no other user can open a claim and so keep a dead run's anchor in the store; the anchors themselves are plain `0644` files again and a lock on one means nothing. Two store paths that are one directory get one file, written twice, which is fine.

**One agent at a time changes the store, and the lock outlives the agent while its tool runs.** Every change keploy makes to the machine's trust state — sweeping, writing an anchor, importing into the JDK keystore, regenerating, removing it all again at stop, and the legacy-CA sweep's anchor removal, regeneration and `keytool -delete` — happens under one machine-wide `flock` on `/run/keploy/ca-trust.lock` (`0600`, root's). Every command started under it inherits the lock as an extra file descriptor (`storeCommand`, `cmd.ExtraFiles`). The kernel frees a `flock` only when every descriptor of it is closed, so an agent killed in the middle of a regeneration keeps the store locked until the tool it started has exited, and the next agent never regenerates beside it. The tool's output goes to an unlinked temporary file rather than a pipe back to the agent (`runStoreCommand`), so the agent's death does not kill the tool either: through a pipe it would get `SIGPIPE` at its next write, and `update-ca-certificates` writes one after it has replaced the bundle and before it runs its hooks. The wait for the lock has no time limit — a holder finishes or dies — is cancellable, and logs the pid it is waiting for. Once the lock is held the run's context no longer stops anything (`context.WithoutCancel`): a regeneration or keytool import that has started runs to its end.

**On Fedora, RHEL and Amazon Linux keploy no longer runs `update-ca-trust` on the live store; it swaps a staged copy into place.** keploy first fills a staging directory under the store with exactly what the wrapper would write, and only then puts that in place:

- where the wrapper can write its output elsewhere — `update-ca-trust extract -o DIR` on Fedora, RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 — keploy runs the distro's own wrapper into the staging directory. That output is the wrapper's by construction: on `fedora:44`, UBI 9 and UBI 10 it is byte for byte what a live run writes under `/etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted` (450, 452 and 450 entries, RHEL 9's two compatibility links included), and the `-o` run does not touch `/etc/pki/tls/certs`. What a live run alone does — empty `/etc/pki/tls/certs` of its hash links and fill it with one absolute link per hash link of `directory-hash` — keploy does itself, but only if the wrapper's live-only blocks are exactly those lines; `DEST_CERTS` without its fill loop, another line in such a block, or any other use of `DEST_CERTS` hands the job back to the wrapper;
- where it cannot — RHEL 8 and Amazon Linux 2023 — keploy reads the wrapper (`readP11KitLayout`) and runs its extraction lines into the staging directory itself, with the wrapper's tool and `P11_KIT_NO_USER_CONFIG=1`, and adds its compatibility links. Every line that uses `$DEST` must then be one keploy does: a known output with its known arguments, once, or a known `ln -s` link. Another output, other arguments, the same output twice, `ln -s -f`, an extraction through a variable or a function, a `cp`, `rm`, `restorecon` or `openssl rehash` into the store: the wrapper is run instead;
- either way `DEST` must be set exactly once, to a plain path, and no line may name the store's path itself;
- and what the staging directory holds must be something keploy can put in place exactly as a live run leaves it: only the store's own directories and `directory-hash`, no file output the store has and the staged output lacks (a live run would have removed it, or left it — nothing tells which), no regular file under a hash link's name in the store. A staging run that fails hands the job to the wrapper too: it fails the same way, or works wh

author: patrob
body:
Closes #1702

## Summary
Talk over a quiet music underscore now gets its own Analyze state, **Speech + bed**. Before this change, the binary Music/Speech classifier flipped between the worship and speech targets.

- `ProgramModeTracker` (SoundBuddyKit) now has a third state, `speechOverBed`, as a pure state machine:
  - Over a 3 s evidence window, if the speech-frame share is below 0.3 it reads Music.
  - Otherwise, a music-frame share of 0.2 or more reads Speech + bed, and anything less reads Speech.
- Switching is stickier:
  - A challenger needs 6 s of consistent evidence before the state changes.
  - After any switch the state holds for at least 10 s.
  - All of these are named constants (`switchEvidenceSeconds`, `minimumHoldSeconds`, `speechPresenceFraction`, `bedPresenceFraction`, `evidenceWindowSeconds`).
- In Speech + bed:
  - Coaching covers only the voice bands (low mid, mid, high mid, roughly 250 Hz to 4 kHz), judged against the speech curve.
  - Sub, bass, presence and brilliance tips pause, because those bands belong to the bed.
  - `BandDeviationCoach.deviations(for:in:)` level-matches over that subset only.
- In the UI:
  - The chip reads `Speech + bed`.
  - The auto target stays on `Speech / podcast (auto)` for both Speech and Speech + bed, so the curve no longer swaps.
  - VoiceOver says "speech over a music bed".
- Any state switch resets the coaching stabilizer from #1695.
- A manually chosen target is still never auto-switched.
- DEBUG only: launching with `-speechBedDemo` feeds a deterministic speech-over-underscore source. That is how the simulator proof below was captured. Release builds are unaffected.

## Tests (written first, commit e57ae28)
- New: `SpeechBedScenarioTests` uses the analyzer's own feature extraction on synthetic signals (`SpeechBedSignals`). It checks that:
  - speech over a pad and speech over a quiet band stay in Speech + bed for 60 s with no flip-flop
  - pure music stays Music
  - pure speech stays Speech
- `ProgramModeTrackerTests` (rewritten) checks that:
  - transitions need 6 s of consistent evidence
  - no change happens inside the 10 s hold
  - evidence restarts when the challenger changes
  - silence holds the current state
- `AnalyzeSpeechBedTests` checks that, with a bed-heavy mix, only voice-band tips appear and the target stays on speech.
- `BandDeviationCoachVoiceBandTests` covers subset level matching.
- `swift-test.sh`: 613 tests in 69 suites pass on the Mini after rebasing onto 78f181c (run at 1fd503f).
- CI fix: the fake PEM fixture in `apps/ios/scripts/test_testflight_signing.py` (from #1729) tripped the key-material guard in `app/electron/licensing.test.ts`. Its BEGIN/END armor is now assembled at runtime, and a new `SecretFixtureTests` case checks it is still a well-formed private-key block. The Python suite passes 26/26 on the Mini, and a replica of the guard scan over all 1365 tracked text files finds no offenders.

## Proof (iOS simulator, `-speechBedDemo`)
- iPhone 17:
  - `docs/screenshots/1702/iphone17-01-music-before-switch.png`: Music chip, worship target
  - `docs/screenshots/1702/iphone17-02-speech-bed-chip.png`: chip switches to Speech + bed
  - `docs/screenshots/1702/iphone17-03-speech-bed-mid-tip-only.png`: `Target · Speech / podcast (auto)`. Only a Mid tip shows, while sub +14 dB, bass +12 dB and brilliance +10 dB are not coached.
  - `docs/screenshots/1702/iphone17-04-speech-bed-steady.png`
  - `docs/screenshots/1702/iphone17-speech-bed.mp4`: about 69 s recording; the chip stays on Speech + bed with voice-band-only tips
- iPad Pro 13 (M5):
  - `docs/screenshots/1702/ipad13-01-speech-bed-chip.png`: Speech + bed chip, `Target · Speech / podcast (auto)`
  - `docs/screenshots/1702/ipad13-02-speech-bed-mid-tip-only.png`: 40 s later, still Speech + bed; the only tip is Mid (500 Hz to 2 kHz) 4.7 dB below target, and the loud sub, bass and brilliance bed is not coached

## Why On PAR Dev's Software Factory skipped this
#1662 and #1665 both carry `factory:order:24`. Ordering throws on duplicate positions, so every analysis-lane cycle ends with no work picked. That blocks #1702 and everything behind it in the lane. The duplicate label is still in place; fixing it is a separate call. `factory:queued` was removed from #1702 before this work started, and no claim existed.

body:
## Scope

Fixes #3277.

Whole-stack `down` now retains both space-scoped and legacy delivery credentials until every required component stop succeeds. Standalone and selective delivery teardown retain their existing stop-then-delete behavior, including loud deletion errors. Process-identity checks, broker-last ordering and stop refusals are unchanged.

The final candidate is `b4c5c33d1e49f573890f611d7857584ba7cbf83c`, based on main `a64403efacfd4ebbc0d6fe37552e871908f7f897`. Its nine changed files contain only the shutdown repair, 14-cell regression suite, two mutation definitions, progress metadata, suite registration, documentation and CLI patch changeset. It does not include the general-endpoint feature branch or the separate instrument-fixture repair in #2793.

## Reproduction and observed repair

- Exact-main CI run `38117604075`, job `114405534091`: the original `smoke:clean` assertion `down: keeps control-plane artifacts` fails after a refused broker stop. Delivery credentials had already been removed during the earlier delivery stop.
- The unchanged assertion passes with the repair in jobs `114554761046` and `114567276777`.
- Job `114567322724`, on measured predecessor `701b41809a221815f591c7ba5abdaee3a70683c9`, reports a **green 14-mark baseline**, then kills both named cleanup mutations:
  - DRM01 restores early deletion and fails DR01, retaining zero preceding PASS marks.
  - DRM02 omits successful final deletion and fails DR07, after six preceding PASS marks.
- Both kills passed the maintained original-source restoration, full rebuild and restored-suite success gates. Separate per-restoration 14-cell stdout transcripts are not claimed.

The hermetic suite drives the shipped command and helper with real temporary filesystem credential storage. Only process stopping is mocked; process signals and liveness probes are forbidden. The terminal marker is emitted after cleanup even when a named assertion throws.

## Exact final-source join

All nine changed files on `b4c5c33d1e49f573890f611d7857584ba7cbf83c` are byte-identical to the measured 701b versions. The only successor action restores the CI workflow and unrelated instrument fixture to their exact main/412149 contents. The temporary ordinary base/head observation job has served its diagnostic purpose and is not added permanently to every PR. Its evidence and the separate fixture correction remain preserved in commit history.

Independent review accepts the measured cleanup proof for this unchanged cleanup source. This is an explicit source join, not a claim that b4 itself was executed before publication.

## Other completed failures remain visible

The earlier workflows were **not wholly green**:

- The ordinary explicit-space startup test failed on both exact main and 701b with the same manager-exit-before-readiness class; its deeper daemon cause remains unknown.
- A TLS refresh route passed on 412149 but failed on 701b despite unchanged relevant declared sources. That transition is unresolved, not labeled a flake or proven non-regression.
- The separate instrument mutation baseline completed 59 passing and two failing counter checks before mutation; it is not a mutation kill or a 61-cell green result.
- The cleanup proof's overall shard failed because a separate pin-recut mutation had a stale source anchor. That row executed no mutation; the two cleanup targets independently passed.
- Existing census/TLS and plural-eviction smoke failures are retained separately.

The sole intended closing reference is #3277 for premature credential deletion. Issue #2793 and the other failures remain outside this PR's scope. Release readiness and Cloud deployment remain unproved.

Independent exact-head review has accepted the narrow source change and required cleanup proof with the unresolved runtime failures above explicitly retained. No review blocker remains for this scope; normal repository merge checks still apply.

author: sjevans1
body:
## X4b-2 / W03: provider-scoped back-channel logout

Closes the W03 isolation gap: revocation keyed on issuer + sid/subject could not
separate two providers sharing an issuer with different clients.

Frozen head: `1cca27d17720522940c36a666ba9fd78b8b379d6` (implementation `77c65bd`),
based on accepted `main@6634033`.

### Scope

- `infrastructure/migrations/025_oidc_logout_provider_lookup.sql`: narrow
  `SECURITY DEFINER` issuer lookup, activated/unrevoked providers only, granted to
  `workspace_app`.
- `infrastructure/migrations/026_session_provider_provenance.sql`:
  `sessions.oidc_provider_id` plus fail-safe legacy-OIDC invalidation.
- `packages/auth/index.ts`: `createSession` persists provider provenance.
- `apps/api/src/app.ts`: issuer selects candidates, each candidate verifies the
  token with its own configuration, exactly one validation context is required,
  revocation is provider-scoped, W02 callback persists `pending.provider_id`.
- `tests/integration.test.ts`: native acceptance.
- `docs/W03_PROVIDER_SCOPED_LOGOUT_ACCEPTANCE.md`: acceptance record.

### Native acceptance

- issuer selects the candidate providers; unknown issuer fails at the not-configured
  boundary;
- active candidate that cannot verify the token fails closed at validation;
- disabled and revoked providers are never candidates;
- same issuer with different clients: A validates only through A, B only through B;
- SID-scoped revocation; subject-only revocation remains provider-scoped;
- overlapping issuer/subject/email does not weaken the boundary;
- replay is deduplicated and revokes nothing additional;
- tenant+tenant ambiguity fails closed with no session deletion, no accepted JTI,
  no audit event;
- deployment+tenant ambiguity fails closed with the same zero side effects;
- migration 026 upgrade regression: legacy OIDC sessions invalidated, local/password
  preserved, no issuer-only backfill, no guessed provider id, nullable column, no
  provider FK, both indexes present, migrator re-run a clean no-op;
- W02 session provenance through the real creation path: tenant-bound records the
  exact provider id, deployment records NULL, local records no OIDC provenance.

Focused runs, both orders from a clean state: 6/6 (W02 then W03 then migration) and
3/3 (W03 then migration), exit 0. Typecheck green.

### Real-provider acceptance

Keycloak 26.7.4 over HTTPS, API trust via `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, no API TLS
verification bypass, `ignoreHTTPSErrors` only in the disposable browser context.

- genuine authorization-code flows through the live start route and the Keycloak 26
  login form, with invitation-backed provisioning, same verified email in both
  realms with distinct issuer+subject identity;
- genuine Keycloak-emitted signed Logout Tokens via admin session termination
  (204); no manufactured tokens;
- A logout revokes only A; B stays valid; local break-glass stays valid;
- B logout subsequently revokes B and not A or local;
- exactly one `auth.oidc_backchannel_logout` audit event per affected tenant, none
  for the unaffected tenant;
- three genuine Logout Tokens per issuer, with duplicate delivery producing no
  additional revocation;
- tenant-provider sessions removed, local/password sessions preserved;
- `workspace_runtime` and `workspace_app` remain `rolsuper = false`,
  `rolbypassrls = false`.

```
before          A=200  B=200  local=200
terminate A ->  204
after A logout  A=401  B=200  local=200
terminate B ->  204
final           A=401  B=401  local=200
```

### Known non-blocking limitation

The optional same-realm / two-client real Keycloak topology was not executed. The
permanent native suite proves that exact isolation model cryptographically (two
providers on one issuer with different clients where only the matching client
validates and neither revokes the other), and the real two-issuer lane proves the
genuine protocol integration. No real-provider proof was fabricated to remove this
note.

### Not included

No W02 or W04 semantic change beyond the provider provenance W03 requires. No RLS
weakening, no new broad privilege, no debug or instrumentation, no secrets or
credentials. W04, W27/W28, W29/W30, SMTP and OpenJM integration are untouched.

author: aitoncumbi
body:
Second Phase 3 item: check responses against the API's contract.

## What changed

**Configuration.** A collection or folder can name an OpenAPI 3.x / Swagger 2.0 document. A request can name a JSON Schema file or opt out. The nearest setting applies:

```yaml
# collection.yaml
contract:
  openapi: ../openapi.yaml   # relative to the workspace; may sit next to the service's code
# a request: contract: { schema: schemas/order.json }  or  contract: { off: true }
```

**Checks (`trax-core/src/contract.rs`).** After the post-response scripts, the runner adds one test per response, `contract: GET /users/{id}`. It fails with every violation found:
- an undocumented path or method
- an undocumented status (exact code, then `4XX`, then `default`)
- an undocumented content type
- a missing required response header
- no body where one is documented
- schema errors (the first five, each with its JSON pointer)

Because it's an ordinary test, it shows up in the app, MCP results and CLI reports, and fails runs, with nothing extra.

- **Matching:** strips each server's path prefix (or Swagger's `basePath`), then tries without one. Supports partial templates (`{name}.{ext}`). Prefers the template that documents the method, then the longest prefix, then the most literal characters. So `/users/me` beats `/users/{id}`, but `DELETE /users/me` still finds `DELETE /users/{id}`.
- **Validation:** `jsonschema` 0.58 with default features **off** (no HTTP or file retrieval), so only local `$ref`s resolve. OpenAPI 3.0 and Swagger 2.0 are validated as draft 4, with 3.0's `nullable: true` rewritten to allow `null`. 3.1 is validated as 2020-12, and a standalone schema file by its own `$schema`. Formats aren't checked.
- **Loading:** specs are parsed once and cached until the file's mtime changes. A missing or unparseable file fails the contract test with the reason.

**Merge/diff.** `merge.rs` and `diff.rs` list fields explicitly, so both now handle `contract`. Without that, a semantic merge would silently drop it. The diff shows "Contract added/changed/removed".

**UI.** A Contract tab on collections and folders (spec path, plus an "off" switch for folders). Request settings get a "Check the contract" switch with a note saying which contract applies and where it's set, and a JSON Schema field.

**MCP.** `upsert_collection` and `upsert_request` accept `contract` (`{openapi}`, `{schema}`, `{off: true}`, `false`, or `null`).

**Docs.** README (feature, plus a workspace-format example), DESIGN.md ("Contract checks" and request execution steps), ROADMAP item checked.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` (Linux, plus `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` for core and MCP), and `cargo test` all pass.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass.
- New tests:
  - core (`contract.rs`): template matching, status/header/body checks, Swagger 2.0 `definitions`, `nullable` rewriting, nearest-contract precedence, file loading and errors
  - runner: a contract test runs after the scripts against a wiremock server, and a request can opt out
  - merge: a contract added on one side survives a merge
  - diff: "Contract added" is reported
  - MCP: an agent sets a contract, sees the violation, and opts a request out
- I also clicked through the UI in the browser preview against the mock backend: set a spec on a collection and saved it, saw the request's note pick it up, and toggled the request off.

## Notes for review

- **Dependencies:** `jsonschema` brings in 25 pure-Rust crates (fancy-regex, referencing, num-*, ahash, ...). Its default features (reqwest, rustls, aws-lc-rs, idna) are off.
- **No `FORMAT_VERSION` bump:** the field is optional, which matches how earlier optional fields were added. An older app that rewrites `collection.yaml` would drop `contract`.
- **Not in this PR:**
  - importing an OpenAPI spec doesn't wire up the contract automatically
  - external `$ref`s (other files or URLs) don't resolve
  - no script-level `toMatchSchema` assertion

author: miricoder
body:
Makes Project Kit installable and testable on **macOS, Linux and Windows**, which it was not before.

## The three things that blocked terminal testing

1. The terminal `claude` on the author's machine is 0.2.56 with **no `plugin` command** — terminal testing was impossible and the failure mode was confusing.
2. All four skills emitted **bash-only syntax** (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-...}`) and 23 hardcoded `python3` calls, which fail where `python3` is not the command.
3. The README had **no terminal, PowerShell or Windows guidance** at all.

## Approach

**One tested Python module, two thin wrappers.** `setup.sh` and `setup.ps1` only locate a Python 3 and hand off to `scripts/doctor.py`. Writing the same checks twice in two shell languages would drift within a week and double the test burden.

**A `pk` launcher** (`bin/pk`, `bin/pk.ps1`) resolves the interpreter and plugin root, so SKILL.md reads `pk gate phase design` on every platform — and costs fewer tokens than the old four-line path preamble.

## The doctor refuses to flatter

Two deliberate honesty fixes, both found by running it against this machine's genuinely broken state:

- **Plugin check no longer asks a broken CLI.** It looks on disk first and reports *present-but-unverified* rather than a false "not installed".
- **`--live` probes each seat.** "Configured" only means a key exists. On this machine `--live` correctly reports `2/3 working`, catching a Moonshot account suspended for insufficient balance that the default check shows as a filled seat. Transient 5xx is retried and classified separately from billing failure, so an overloaded model is not reported dead.

It also diagnoses the specific trap here: a stale install outside the current npm prefix, where a plain `npm i -g` loses the PATH race and leaves two installs.

## Verification

- 77 unit tests pass (25 new), covering the classifier and the panel rules — duplicate families fill one seat, Anthropic is excluded as the authoring family
- `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes
- `./setup.sh` run end to end: correctly reports the known-bad CLI and exits 1
- Docs regenerate; CI staleness gate green

**Not yet verified:** the PowerShell path and Windows behaviour. That needs a real Windows box — the author's test is what confirms it.

author: jonny5509
body:
## Problem
Hikvision event callbacks commonly send XML with a charset parameter, such as `application/xml; charset=utf-8`. The notification handler compared the full Content-Type header against a few exact strings, so valid XML requests with different casing or charset formatting could be incorrectly passed to the multipart decoder. A missing Content-Type header also caused an AttributeError instead of a useful validation error.

## Changes
- Normalize the media type independently of parameters and casing for direct XML requests and multipart parts.
- Handle a missing Content-Type header with a clear validation error.
- Add regression tests for common XML charset variants and missing headers.

## Verification
- Regression tests were added but have not been executed in this environment.
- CI status was checked after creation; no passing result is claimed without check data.

author: spiesdan
body:
## Duas ideias roubadas, adaptadas ao nosso desenho

### 1. Laboratório (do [vocero-crm](https://github.com/kevinrivm/vocero-crm))

Seis personas simuladas testam a campanha **antes dela falar com gente de
verdade**: o decidido, o perguntão de preço, o irritado, o que pergunta o que
não sabemos, o que exige humano e o que escreve errado. A conversa roda em
**sandbox com o gerador real de abordagem** (nada é enviado — estruturalmente
impossível: o módulo não importa o sender, e um teste quebra se importar). Um
**juiz dá nota 0-100 com achados e evidência**, e o histórico mostra o **delta**
entre rodadas (só vale entre rodadas de mesmo `config_hash`).

**Diferença do original:** personas com **roteiro determinístico** em vez de
LLM. O roteiro custa zero, não varia entre rodadas (delta significa "o agente
mudou", não "o simulador estava de bom humor"), e cada persona existe por um
defeito nomeado. O único gasto LLM por rodada é o juiz (6 chamadas) + até 36
gerações — com gate `manager` e contagem na resposta.

### 2. Raio-X do site (do [ProspectOS](https://github.com/nando0x/ProspectOS))

O score sabia `temWebsite` booleano (+10). Agora: `sem_site`, `site_ruim` (sem
HTTPS, 5xx, >8s), `site_simples` (construtor pronto ou sem mobile), `site_ok` —
pesos 10/6/2/0 no lugar do 10/0. `POST /prospecting/prospects/[id]/raio-x`
analisa, grava situação+detalhes+carimbo; o score da leitura seguinte já usa.

Com **SSRF guard de verdade** (só http/https, portas 80/443, DNS resolvido e
conferido contra faixas privadas antes de cada request, redirects seguidos à
mão com revalidação). Cada bloqueio é um teste.

### O que NÃO veio

- Do vocero: API de bot externo, agenda, atribuição de anúncios, guia de
  onboarding (nada disso é o nosso buraco).
- Do ProspectOS: scraping de Maps/Instagram, PDF de diagnóstico, sessão de
  prospecção (temos OSM, follow-up e Meu Dia — não duplicar).

Ambos MIT. Nenhum código copiado — só as ideias, reimplementadas no nosso
desenho (outbox de testes, mutação provada, apêndice no baseline junto).

## Validado

- 17 (lab) + 4 (lab route) + 17 (raio-x) + 4 (raio-x route) + 9 (workflows parse)
- `test:unit` 770/8180, `test:db` 146/1342, mobile e2e 4/4
- Migrations 0264+0265 com apêndice no baseline + MANIFEST + seed RLS
- Tela `/app/laboratorio` no registry (sem sidebar, porta via ⌘K)
- `typecheck` e `eslint` limpos

author: mpscholten
body:
Subagents can suspend until a timestamp without occupying an active worker, then resume through the runtime scheduler or earlier steering input. Suspension commits only after the tool result is durably recorded; failed persistence does not acknowledge a successful sleep. Hosts can restore sleeping children across process restarts.

`withSubagentRuntime` owns trees across root turns, wakeup scheduling, idle retirement and joined shutdown. The library also owns durable recovery and reconciliation, transcript persistence and tool-result deduplication, child loop execution, and coalesced parent notifications. Typed host callbacks supply storage, authorization, provider codecs and domain settlement. Notification adapters must serialize delivery and commit the message and parent wake request in one transaction.

Adds bounded, paginated agent listings and status support in CLI/dialects. The CLI does not gain an automatic durable scheduler from this change.

Child tool effects can append native image/document inputs to the durable transcript and yield for user input. Added inputs survive continuation and recovery. Child execution brackets preparation and cleanup across successful completion, failures and cancellation; cleanup also runs when preparation fails after resources were acquired. Focused tool-effect/transcript checks and all six child-execution tests pass.

Durable cancellation is reconciled before ordinary recovery. Closing a child joins its supervisor before persisting closure and releasing ownership; persistence failures retain the cancellation marker for retry. The latest recovery and suspension suites each pass 11 tests, including cancellation ordering.

Validation: 53 focused suspension, child lifecycle, collaboration and status tests and 12 scoped-runtime lifecycle tests passed earlier in this branch. The extraction adds 21 passing tests covering recovery, transcripts, child execution and durable parent notifications. The consuming application's three transcript tests pass and its child runner typechecks. Full CI remains required; the application's local dependency build encountered macOS nested sandbox failures in existing shell-execution tests.

author: kovtcharov-amd
body:
The TUI could send the user's AMD gateway or Fireworks key to a Lemonade that isn't GAIA's. The gateway screen posted the token to whatever answered on port 13305 or 8000. The `/provider` panel fell back to 13305 whenever GAIA's Lemonade state file was missing, which is exactly what happens while the daemon restarts it. Now the TUI follows the same rule as the Python side (#4999). A key goes only to GAIA's own running Lemonade, to the server in `LEMONADE_BASE_URL`, or to the system Lemonade when GAIA's own isn't installed. If GAIA's Lemonade is restarting, the TUI waits for the daemon to bring it back. If it's still down, the TUI shows "GAIA's Lemonade Server is restarting and is not back yet" and sends nothing.

## Test plan
- [ ] `cd tui && go test ./... && go vet ./...`
- [ ] New tests use a test-port `httptest` server that accepts keys as a stand-in for someone else's Lemonade. They check that, with GAIA's Lemonade installed but stopped, neither the `/provider` panel nor `/gateway` sends any request anywhere (default port included). They check that the key reaches GAIA's server once the daemon brings it back, and that an explicit `LEMONADE_BASE_URL` still receives it. They also check that the agent the TUI launches is not pinned to a probed port during a restart. Files: `internal/lemonade/credential_test.go`, `internal/ui/gateway/target_test.go`, `internal/client/subprocess_provider_test.go`.
- [ ] On a machine with GAIA's embedded Lemonade, stop only the embedded `lemond`, then open `/gateway` and submit a token right away. The screen either connects to GAIA's restarted server or shows the restarting message, and nothing reaches port 13305.

author: aikido-autofix[bot]
body:
This patch addresses a command injection vulnerability in the CVE triage workflow where untrusted user input from `workflow_dispatch` events was being interpolated directly into shell commands. The fix eliminates shell-based validation and moves all input handling to Python, which reads the issue number directly from the environment variable without shell parsing. Changes were made to `.github/workflows/cve-triage.yml` to remove the shell conditional check and to `scripts/triage.py` to accept and validate the issue number as a string with proper sanitization before type conversion.
✅ 1 issue fixed by this PR
| Issue | Severity           | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | 
[CodeAudit#728780096](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/single/728780096)
| 
HIGH
| The workflow embeds `${{ inputs.issue_number }}` directly in shell source both in the `if` condition and in the `--issue` argument. This is textual script generation rather than argument passing. A dispatch value containing shell syntax can therefore alter the shell program; Python's downstream `type=int` validation only occurs after the shell has parsed and potentially executed the injected commands. The `type: number` declaration is not a shell-escaping boundary, particularly for callers using the workflow-dispatch API rather than the browser form. The affected step exposes the job's write-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, so a user permitted to dispatch the workflow can execute code in the job context and exfiltrate or misuse those credentials. Pass the input through `env` and use a quoted environment-variable expansion instead. |

author: leaf-agent
body:
The [public release journey](https://github.com/max-sixty/leaf/actions/runs/38166862461) failed when its triage-board comment received HTTP 400. [#2416](https://github.com/max-sixty/leaf/pull/2416) made event admission compare the page's serving identity with the running Leaf. That identity included `sys.version`: CI built the page with Python 3.12, while [the website container](https://github.com/max-sixty/leaf/blob/36d09d7abc691768ed67ea1c7a00261185630d25/Dockerfile.website) runs Python 3.14. The first comment therefore looked like a write through another Leaf's contract.

The serving identity now hashes the Python serving files and dependency manifests, which define the vendored event contract, without the interpreter's version string. A focused regression reproduced the HTTP 400 before this change and now verifies that a page remains current under `page init --dry-run` and accepts the comment after the Python version changes. The existing checks for changed serving files and manifests, and for genuinely foreign runtime and server identities, also pass (6 focused tests total).

The hosted Chrome journey cannot run in this sandbox because Chrome aborts at startup when it cannot create a socket; the public deployment check will exercise the full route after landing.

author: iloveeyjafjalla
body:
## Why

Captured request start/end instants contain nanoseconds, but native ATIF export
formats both with whole seconds. An ordinary 300 ms request is consequently
reported as zero or one second by the existing performance consumer.

## What changed

Use Chrono AutoSi in the existing formatter to retain fractional precision
when present. Add public converter → shared ATIF serde → actual performance
integration fixtures for both 300 ms shapes, exact nanosecond roundtrip, and
unchanged whole-second strings. One production line; no new schema or dependency.

## Related issue

closes #7094

## User / Agent impact

Exported measured instants retain their original precision. Model and wall
duration statistics can use the recorded fraction; whole-second spelling stays
compatible. This does not invent missing timing or change tool attribution.

## Risk and compatibility

- [x] Public CLI, API, configuration, or documented behavior changed
- [ ] Privileged or security-sensitive behavior changed
- [ ] Cross-component contract changed
- [ ] Migration or rollback guidance is needed

RFC3339 timestamp strings may now include their measured fractional seconds.
The existing shared schema and consumer already accept them. Integer-second
exports remain byte compatible; no storage migration, route, configuration,
privileged behavior or dependency change.

## Validation

Official main `a91ba949de298e1e2dd97ed1ff7788557727f114`, WSL Ubuntu 22.04,
Rust 1.89.0, locked dependencies and private native build tools:

- Normally compiled original four-case integration: 3 real failures / 1
  whole-second control passed. Same assertions with fix: 4/4 passed; final
  rustfmt-formatted test also 4/4 passed. Only formatting changed between versions.
- `cargo +1.89.0 fmt --all --check`: passed.
- `cargo +1.89.0 clippy --locked -p agentsight --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo +1.89.0 build --locked -p agentsight`: passed.
- `cargo +1.89.0 test --locked -p agentsight`: library suite 2648 passed, 1
  failed, 1 existing ignored. Failure is in the unchanged tokenizer fixture
  `configured_cache_size_governs_manager_capacity` (temporary JSON EOF); its
  cause is not established. No full-package success or later suites claimed.
  Test compilation used debug=0/strip=debuginfo for agentsight only; assertions
  and test selection were unchanged. This failure was not suppressed.
- Independent implementation review on a separate clean tree: original 125 ms /250 ms cases both failed, integer two-second control passed; same three public converter/serde/performance fixtures all passed after the one-line fix and normal recompilation. No author binary was substituted. The unchanged tokenizer test also passed in isolation; this does not erase the full-suite failure or establish its cause.

Only synthetic in-memory event/trajectory data; no live trace, tool execution,
external model, credentials or host/network/security-setting change.

## Documentation and rollback

This restores measured precision inside the existing RFC3339 timestamp format.
No new command, setting, page or interface is added. Revert the commit to restore
seconds-only formatting.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation and
tests (`codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`).

author: atherkel-agent-app[bot]
body:
Closes #243. Clears the last open blocker of #170.

## What this changes

- **`load_configuration` refuses a category whose ID is `transfer`, `adjustment` or `unknown`.** It reports one problem per offending category, in file order, beside the category's other problems:

  ```text
  taxonomy.toml: category "transfer": the ID is a transaction type that carries no category
  ```

- **`classification.md`**: *Configuration errors* now lists the rule. In *Taxonomy*, the identifiers bullet says no category may be named `transfer`, `adjustment` or `unknown`, and the income-and-expense sentence is guidance, not a requirement ([L62-L68](https://github.com/ATherkel/budget/blob/ce559594fae54593984e9d2d6d7200b8e77edf8d/docs/architecture/classification.md?plain=1#L62-L68)):

  > This is guidance, not a configuration error: money no category rule matches stays `unknown` and is raised as an `unclassified` review item.

## Decisions

Both rules follow the owner's decision on #243. These choices were reviewed in the session:

1. **The rule covers category IDs only.** A group is never allocated, so a group ID can't be confused with a transaction type. IDs are already lowercase only, so `Transfer` can't occur.
2. **Only the types that carry no category are refused.** `income`, `expense` and `refund` are transaction types too, but a category may still take those names. The docs, the problem wording and the loader's `_UNCATEGORISED_TYPES` all name exactly the three refused types.
3. **No new test for "a taxonomy without income loads".** `test_the_documented_examples_load` already pins it: the `operations.md` example has only expense groups.
4. **A test guards against drift from Gold's `TransactionType`.** `inputs` must not import `gold`, so the loader keeps its own copy of the three names. `test_the_refused_ids_are_gold_transaction_types` asserts they are all among `TransactionType`'s values, so renaming or removing a type fails loudly.
5. **No `format = 2` test.** `read_document` refuses any format other than 1 for the whole file, before any entry is checked. `test_accounts.py` already covers that.

## Verification

- Red: `test_a_transaction_type_is_not_a_category_id` failed with `DID NOT RAISE ConfigurationError`. Green: it passes. After review, the expected wording changed and failed against the old message before the rename made it pass.
- `uv run pytest`: 520 passed, 297 subtests passed.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check` and `complexipy` all pass.

body:
Merge train 136: villager-jobs-1 (783e2e982, on master 8639feab8). Land 1 milestone #21 (partial).

User: "Does a fisherman (disciple or not) have a fishing rod and animation?" and "Do villagers chop wood on land 1? I get a sense they don't due to no buildings. Confirm?" Handover: bw1-decomp `docs/openblack/villager/villager-jobs-1_handover.md`; research in `villager/jobs.md` §8.

**The answers:**
- **Rod and animation:** yes. A fisherman, disciple or not, walks to his town's fish farm with the rod, steps off the farm's own spot to a spot in its map cell, plays the fishing clip and catches fish (37 a catch). When the next catch wouldn't fit, he carries the bag home.
- **Land 1 wood:** no villager chops in the opening, but not for lack of buildings. Villagers fetch wood only when their town wants it. The settings give a minimum of 500 and a maximum of 5000, scaled by abodes/10:
  - Norse store 30000 against a target of 17000 (34 abodes): wood desire 0. Its abode and civic desires are negative (−0.58, −1.0), which holds wood at 0 even with an empty store (checked against the disassembly).
  - Aztec store 10000 against 8500 (17 abodes): wood desire 0, until the store falls below its 850 minimum.
  - Food is the same (Norse food desire 0.0003 with 20000 stored), so no one fishes in the opening. Disciples work regardless.
- **The creature empathising with the wood desire** only happens in states v1.20 never enters, so there is nothing to implement.

**This PR:**
- Pure rules in `src/ECS/VillagerWorkRules.*` (17 tests in `test_villager_work`).
- **Foresters:** choose the store, a forest or a big forest; walk out with the axe; fell the nearest forest tree; watch it land; pick the wood up through the wood reaction (the "wood catches the eye" rule is in, and working foresters react to wood again at once). Big forests shrink as wood is taken (`TakeBigForestWood`), and the log shown follows the tree kind.
- **Fishermen:** the town's want of food weighs fish farms, fields and taking food home. They walk to the farm's cell, move to a spot, fish and go home with the bag. A deleted farm sends its fishermen back to deciding (0xA3).
- **Disciples:** forester and fisherman disciples work instead of waiting at the town centre.
- **Towns count what their people are doing by state**, as vanilla does; otherwise every villager offered took the same job.
- Fallen trunks and big forests give up their wood when taken from. `living.town_desires` reports raw desires, doing-now counts and the wood targets.

**Checked on Land 1** (stores lowered or disciples added through the inspector):
- 5 fishermen, one per Norse farm, with rods and bags; the 8 farms of the empty neutral town get none, as in the game.
- A Norse forester disciple took 250 wood from the big forest to the store.
- Aztec foresters chopped with axes and carried wood home once their store was emptied.
- Screenshots in `E:\openblack\screenshots\villager\jobs\`.
- `villagers_1000`: mean 3.7–5.0 ms, p95 5.5–7.0 ms; one 16 ms spike in one of three runs on the shared machine.
- Locally (GitHub CI is off): Debug and RelWithDebInfo build with no warnings; full ctest 382/382.

**Still to do:**
- Footpaths.
- The forester's look-ahead re-targeting (undetermined).
- Temporary pots for towns without a pit.
- Farmers and shepherds (a field can win the food choice but nothing follows; flocks aren't weighed).
- Confirming the chop and fishing sounds sample by sample.

author: iperev
body:
> Stacked PR 5/8 — base: #59 (`fix/release-attempt-identity`). Do not merge yet. Review only the top commit.

## Context
CI-054/CI-058 lane C.
- F-19: after the cleanup deadline, the Actions JWKS provider could start its first transport
  close when its cache drain absorbed the deadline cancellation.
- F-13: forward append compared descriptor hashes only with the previous revision, so retiring
  and later re-adding a capability could change its meaning.
- F-17: the profile declares a computable advisory-key derivation, but admission did not check it.
- F-11: no test covered a child task calling commit.

## What changed
- The JWKS provider starts its transport close only when the closing task has no pending
  cancellation; it re-raises an absorbed cancellation. A transport close that has already
  started remains retained.
- Forward append rejects any proposed capability ID whose descriptor hash differs from a
  retained row for that ID. The read is bounded and happens before attestation. Re-adding with
  the original hash is allowed. Replay and runtime admission are unchanged.
- The DB16 mutant is re-anchored to the unique adjacent attestation/insertion statements; it
  still removes only the attestation. Selector, witness, mutant count (36) and budgets are
  unchanged.
- Profile admission requires the code-owned key domain and declared derivation and recomputes
  the lock pair from that domain only, never from the profile digest.
- Added unit and PostgreSQL tests (runtime fence, JWKS provider, child-task commit,
  write-once capability identity, fence key derivation) and updated the owner documents.

## Expected result
- No transport close starts after the deadline; a close already in progress may still finish.
- The rebinding countermodel r1{(A,h1),(B,hB)} -> r2{(B,hB)} -> r3{(A,h2),(B,hB)} is rejected,
  and the current migration history is accepted.
- An edited fence domain, derivation or pair is rejected.
- The mutation applicability preflight passes.

Non-claims:
- No deployment or provider evidence.
- Behavioral, PostgreSQL and mutation tests were not run locally; they run in GitHub CI.
- No change to GitHub/Keycloak close ordering, and no guarantee of physical resource release.
- Only static checks and the mutation applicability preflight were run locally.
```
Audit dispositions: F-19 confirmed narrow source-level fence violation; F-11 oracle gap (no product defect); F-13 owner decision — enforce the existing lifetime immutability norm at append; F-17 adopted because the profile declares a computable derivation. A related observation (GitHub/Keycloak retained closers) is recorded as an owner wording question, unchanged. Independent review: gpt-6-astra (xhigh), one blocker (DB16 mutation anchor) fixed.

author: greluc
body:
## What

Plan item P4-3 of `docs/DOMAIN_MODULARISATION_PLAN.md` (§7.6): the twelve refinery types that P3-8b left in the layer packages move into the refinery module. Behaviour, DTO/OpenAPI schema, 403/404, queries and statement counts are unchanged.

1. **Inversion.** `LocationService` asked `RefineryOrderRepository` and `ShipRepository` whether a location is in use. The catalogue now owns a read SPI, `catalogue.api.LocationUsage` (`position`, `users`, `isUsed`), implemented by `hangar.internal.ShipLocationUsage` (10) and `refinery.internal.RefineryLocationUsage` (20), `MANDATORY` in the delete's transaction. The first usage that reports the location in use names the refusal; both messages, their order and the 409 are byte-identical.
2. **Probe, not a guess.** A class-dependency graph over the compiled classes (ArchUnit import, nested and generated classes folded onto their source type, one node per first package segment, the twelve types reassigned to `refinery`) found exactly one edge that closes a cycle before the SPI, `LocationService -> RefineryOrderRepository`, and none after it. The second edge named in P3-8b (`UserDeletionService`) was already gone with P4 slice a.
3. **Move.** `RefineryOrder`, `RefineryGood`, `RefineryOrderStatus`, the repository with `RefineryMissionProfitAggregate`, the mapper with `RefineryOrderMissionLookup` and the two request records go to `refinery.internal`; the three order DTOs go to `refinery.api`. `REFINERY_ORDER_SCOPE_TRIPLE` is now a constant of `RefineryAccessPolicy`, spliced into the same four queries with the same text.
4. **Operation.** The operation ranks above the refinery, so its finance and payout classes read the orders through the new refinery-owned `refinery.api.RefineryOrderFinanceReader` (figures, lines with the order DTO, profit per mission), implemented by `RefineryOrderFinanceReads` with the same repository calls and the same mapper. The payout path takes figures only, so it builds no DTO and costs no statement more.
5. **NullAway** covers the moved tree: nullable entity fields, DTO components, the repository's search pattern and the id setter's parameter carry `@Nullable`; the generated MapStruct implementation is the first one inside a checked tree, so the compile gets `NullAway:TreatGeneratedAsUnannotated`.

## Baseline and gates

- Module baseline **38 → 36** (`catalogue -> hangar`, `catalogue -> refinery`, both from `LocationService`), rewritten by `ModuleBaselineTest`, not by hand. (The P4 slice a entry said 43; the file already held 38.)
- Architecture test model-code floor 344 → 343; the domain map loses the class rule of `RefineryMissionProfitAggregate` and the name rule `^(Refinery|ImportIssue|ImportSuggestion)`, which assign no class any more.
- Tests of the moved types moved into the matching test packages.

## P4-4 feasibility (not started)

Still blocked. With the seven operation types reassigned, the probe finds exactly three class edges entering the operation from inside the cycle: `MissionDto -> OperationDto`, `MissionListDto -> OperationDto` and `MissionMapper -> OperationMapper`. `MissionPeerRedactor` no longer reads `OperationDto` (the plan said four classes). The wire shape is the blocker, not a missing inversion: the plan records it under §7.6.

## Verification

- `LocationDeleteInUseIntegrationTest` (Postgres) written first, green on `c042014ee`, red when the two checks swap.
- Targeted tests green locally: architecture classes, `ModuleBaselineTest`, `ModularityTest`, `DomainMap*`, `*Refinery*`, `*Location*`, `*Operation*`, `*Mission*`, OpenAPI and contract tests, N+1 tests, the differential verdict test. The full suite runs in CI.
- `spotlessApply`, `checkstyleMain`, `checkstyleTest`, `spotbugsMain` clean.

## Docs

Plan §7.6 (dated entry with Corrections, baseline before/after, P4-4 result), arc42 §5, `module-boundaries.md`, `data-persistence.md`, `refinery-notifications.md`, spec index. No user-visible change, so no CHANGELOG entry, no wiki change, no new monitoring or audit surface.

author: arigsela
body:
Retires `homelab-agent`, the LangGraph BYO kagent agent. This is Task 5.2 of `docs/plans/kagent-1-0-on-k8s-1-37-implementation-plan.md` (Phase 5 cutover). `kagent-langgraph` doesn't implement kagent 1.0's BYO contract (gRPC A2A, TaskStore), and on 2026-09-26 the owner decided `homelab-knowledge` stays the single knowledge agent.

**Merge order:** merge only after Task 5.1 (the off-cluster `pg_dump` of `homelab_agent`) is done. The ECR repository goes in a separate Terraform PR (`chore/retire-homelab-agent-ecr`), applied by Atlantis before that PR merges.

## What changes

**Deleted (Argo CD prunes them):**
- `base-apps/kagent/`: `agents/homelab-agent.yaml`, `homelab-agent-serviceaccount.yaml`, `homelab-agent-external-secret.yaml`, `homelab-agent-secret-store.yaml`, `eso-homelab-agent-serviceaccount.yaml`, `homelab-agent-db-external-secret.yaml`, `homelab-agent-db-secret-store.yaml`, `eso-homelab-agent-db-serviceaccount.yaml`
- `base-apps/postgresql/`: `init-homelab-agent-db.yaml` (Sync hook, nothing live to prune), `homelab-agent-db-external-secret.yaml`, `homelab-agent-db-secret-store.yaml`, `eso-homelab-agent-db-serviceaccount.yaml`

When Argo CD prunes the `Agent`, the kagent controller deletes its Deployment and Service. The ExternalSecrets use `creationPolicy: Owner`, so their target Secrets (`homelab-agent-secrets`, `homelab-agent-db`, `homelab-agent-db-credentials`) are garbage-collected with them.

**§V.72 consumer grep** (`homelab-agent`, `homelab_agent`, `homelab-agent.kagent` Service DNS) across the repo: no other manifest, script, test, catalog entity, workflow, Renovate rule, admission policy or dashboard references it. Only docs did. No agent delegates to it. It called `k8s-reader`, `agent-docs-mcp`, Backstage MCP and Ollama, but none of them called it back.

**`scripts/provision-homelab-agent-vault.sh`:** kept, because `provision-donetick-vault.sh` cites it as the per-consumer pattern. The header now says it was retired on 2026-10-11, and a guard makes it exit 1 so nobody recreates the roles. The header also lists the one-time manual cleanup (Vault + Postgres + Anthropic key, below).

**Docs** now describe the end state: kagent `docs.md`/`runbook.md` (agent table, BYO section, secrets tables, provisioning how-to, symptom entry), postgresql `docs.md`/`runbook.md`, ollama `docs.md`, backstage `docs.md`/`runbook.md` (MCP token copy), system-upgrade-controller `runbook.md` (affected workloads), `docs/platform/external-secrets.md`, `index.md`, `recovery/CLUSTER-RECOVERY.md`, and `CLAUDE.md` (Vault-role example is now `agent-audit-web-db`). `sources:` lists no longer name deleted files. `base-apps/index.md` and the TechDocs copies were regenerated. `SPEC.md` and `docs/plans/**` are left as historical records.

## Manual cleanup after merge (owner; not done here)

Run once Argo CD has pruned the ExternalSecrets, so ESO doesn't log 403s against deleted roles in the meantime.

```sh
# Vault, inside vault-0 with an admin token
vault kv metadata delete -mount=k8s-secrets homelab-agent
vault kv metadata delete -mount=k8s-secrets homelab-agent-db
vault delete auth/kubernetes/role/homelab-agent
vault delete auth/kubernetes/role/homelab-agent-db
vault policy delete homelab-agent
vault policy delete homelab-agent-db

# Postgres: the pgvector `postgresql` Deployment, not CNPG. Dump off-cluster first (Task 5.1)
kubectl -n postgresql exec deploy/postgresql -- sh -c \
  'pg_dump -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d homelab_agent -Fc' > homelab_agent.dump
pg_restore --list homelab_agent.dump >/dev/null && shasum -a 256 homelab_agent.dump
kubectl -n postgresql exec -it deploy/postgresql -- sh -c 'psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"'
#   DROP DATABASE homelab_agent;
#   DROP ROLE homelab_agent;
```

Then revoke the agent's dedicated Anthropic key in the Anthropic console. The `backstage-token` in `k8s-secrets/homelab-agent` was a copy of Backstage's MCP token. `kagent-backstage-mcp` still uses that token, so deleting the Vault key is enough and nothing needs rotating.

## Validation (local)

- `python scripts/gen-okf.py --repo-root . --check` and `python scripts/gen-techdocs.py --repo-root . --check`: in sync
- `validate-agent-docs.py` (24 apps, 0 warnings), `validate-catalog-refs.py`, `validate-agent-identity.py` (7 agents), `validate-agent-capability.py`, `validate-eval-corpus.py`: OK
- `pytest` suites `agent-identity` (15), `agent-capability` (23), `okf` (21), `catalog-refs` (5), `techdocs` (6), `agent-docs` (35), `agent-audit` (105), `eval-corpus` (63), `appset` (12): all pass
- `yamllint` on `base-apps/kagent` and `base-apps/postgresql`: only pre-existing line-length warnings
- `sh -n` on the script, and a run confirms the guard exits 1

## Impact

- **Deployment:** the `homelab-agent` pod, Service and A2A endpoint go away, with no in-cluster caller. Its Backstage entity should drop out on the kubernetes-ingestor's next run.
- **Secrets/IAM:** the Vault roles, policies and keys stay until the manual cleanup above. Nothing reads them after the prune.
- **Data:** the `homelab_agent` database stays until it is dropped by hand. Nothing in git drops it.
- **DNS:** none.

body:
Tem Script? | Novas Env Vars
-- | --
Não | Não

> :warning: **NOTA**
> - **Mudança de comportamento (#507):** o `SubjectGraph` deixa coluna `LargeBinary` fora da exportação por padrão. `exclude_binary=False` volta ao comportamento anterior.
> - **#493:** um `session_factory` que é função geradora passa a ser registrado como `Depends`. O callable sem argumentos de antes continua funcionando, e os 1282 testes de auth e api passam sem mudança.

## Problema

Três melhorias de desenho de API, a partir de contornos que o 7rc/homework_api precisou escrever:

- **#508:** fora o `actor_id`, coluna de domínio na tabela de auditoria (o titular do evento, o tenant) exigia sobrescrever `new_entry` e passar o valor escondido no `context`.
- **#507:** o `SubjectGraph` exportava coluna binária em base64. Além disso, ele não alcançava dado do titular sem chave estrangeira: o convite enviado **ao** titular aponta para quem mandou. Com isso, a prova de exclusão dava `0` com o e-mail ainda no banco.
- **#493:** as dependências de JWT e de rate limit exigiam o objeto pronto no import. O `make_auth_router` chamava `session_factory()` direto, sem passar pelo FastAPI, então um `get_session` com sub-dependências não funcionava e o `dependency_overrides` dele não alcançava as rotas de auth.

## Solução

### #508 — `columns=` na auditoria
`new_entry`, os `for_*`, os `*_audited` e o `record_event` aceitam `columns: Mapping[str, Any]`. Cada chave vai para a coluna de mesmo nome. Chave sem coluna levanta `ValueError` e reverte a transação; medido, nem a linha de negócio é gravada. Chave em `AUDIT_RESERVED_COLUMNS` (as colunas do SDK e o `actor_id`) também é recusada.

### #507 — `SubjectGraph`
- `exclude_binary=True` por padrão.
- `value_matches={"invites.to_email": "email"}`: `condition`, `export` e `count` recebem `values=`, e o filho de uma linha casada por valor também é do titular.
- `erase()` apaga as linhas casadas e a raiz, sem commit, e devolve o `count`.
- `violations()` acusa entrada fora do fecho ou com coluna inexistente.
- Medido: sem `values`, o `count` diz `invites: 0` com o convite no banco; com `values`, 1; depois do `erase`, 0, e o convite de outro titular fica.

### #493 — recursos criados depois do import
- `make_jwt_user_dependency`, `make_bearer_token_dependency`, `make_role_dependency` e `make_permission_dependency` aceitam `(request) -> JWTUtils`.
- `make_rate_limit_dependency` aceita `(request) -> RateLimitStore`.
- `make_auth_router` registra o `session_factory` gerador como `Depends(session_factory)`.
- Medido em `tests/api/test_lazy_dependencies.py`; os 4 testes falham no código antigo:
  - dois apps com segredos diferentes e a mesma dependência de módulo recusam o token um do outro;
  - cada app conta o rate limit no seu store;
  - o router de auth funciona sobre `get_session(database=Depends(get_database))`;
  - o override é chamado no `/auth/login`.

Não se aplica — backend.

- Receitas `audit-trail`, `subject-data`, `http` e `auth-flow` (PT/EN), com exemplos completos executados; referência; CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`.

author: oddharsh
body:
Item 3 of the [2026-10-11 dependency digest](https://github.com/oddharsh/site/issues/1144#issuecomment-6115140939): playwright-core 1.64 (#1272) added [`page.webmcp`](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.64.0), which lists the tools a page actually registered.

## The gap

`contract-webmcp-one-door-onto-the-browser-catalog` reads source: no Lens page tool shares a `/mcp` name, and nothing reaches `document.modelContext` around `webmcp.js`. It can't see the result. The browser's catalog is shared and append-only, so a duplicate name, a rejected schema, or a registrar that never boots all leave the page working while the tool is silently gone.

## What this adds

- **`bun run webmcp:check`** (`tools/webmcp-catalog.ts`). It loads pages in Chrome with `--enable-features=WebMCP` and polls `page.webmcp.tools()` until the catalog stops growing, since registration happens on idle. It then diffs the live catalog against what should be there:
  - every page: whatever the origin's own `/mcp` answers `tools/list` with, read live so a production run can't fail on deploy skew;
  - `/lens`: those plus the 6 page tools in `lens-webmcp.js`.

  Exit 0 on a match, 1 on a diff, 2 when the instrument fails. `ORIGIN=` points it at a local or preview Worker. It defaults to production and samples `/`, `/lens`, `/whoareyou` and `/garage`.
- **`tools/lib/webmcp-catalog.ts`** holds the pure half: the Lens name scanner (moved out of the source contract so both read one list), the expected set per route, and the diff.
- **`tools/contract-webmcp-live-catalog-probe.test.mjs`** pins that pure half. It checks that the scanner reads 6 names and refuses a missing array, that only `/lens` adds page tools, and that the diff reports a dropped tool and an unexpected one.

It doesn't gate CI, for the same reasons as `check-agent.ts` and `csp-sweep.ts`: it needs a WebMCP Chrome and a reachable origin.

## Measured, with both controls

Chrome 155.0.8059.40, production:

```

author: virtusrickandmorty
body:
The owner asked (Oct 12, 2026) that restocking a ready-stock website item go to the production board, and that other work can be added by hand: rework, and changing items into something the website can sell. The owner's choices:
- **On sale only when finished:** pieces go on sale only once production finishes them.
- **Change covers three sources:** website stock, a job order's leftovers, and other pieces.
- **Rework takes pieces off sale** until they are fixed.

## What it does
**From a product's Stock window** (new choices beside "Pieces came in" and "I counted the shelf"):
- **Restock: make more**: type pieces per size and colour, then choose the due days, rush and a note → it goes to production.
- **Send for rework**: pieces that need fixing come off sale now → they go to production.

**The new Shop work tab** (Website shop):
- Lists the shop's open work orders with pieces, pieces in stock, and pieces **finished and waiting**.
- **Put into the shop's stock** records the finished pieces, and from then on they are for sale. When every piece is in, the job order is done (Released).
- **Put back on sale** returns pieces taken off sale that were not worked on after all.
- **+ Change items**: pieces become a website item. Each line chooses where they come from:
  - **website stock**, taken off sale now;
  - **leftovers of a job order**, naming it;
  - **other pieces**, with a note.

## How
- Each work order is a **₱0 job order** on the shop's own customer, *Virtus website shop (own stock)*, made on the first one. It goes on the **production board like any other**: steps, workers' pieces and rates, rework.
- It is copied from the TPL restock design and uses the same JO hooks: `onForStockCheck`, so a release slip is refused, and `onJobOrderEdited`, so an edit stays shop work and pieces off sale move with it.
- **Migration SHP/0010:**
  - new tables `shp_work_customer`, `shp_work`, `shp_work_lines` and `shp_work_moves`, all insert-only with triggers;
  - `stockOf` adds the work moves (taken off −, given back +, put in +).
- **New permission `shp.work`** (encoder, owner). Making one records a job order, so it also needs `jo.post`. Putting pieces in uses `shp.stock`.
- Pieces only, **no journal**: periodic inventory, PLAN D2. No posting code, and the engine, JO and PRD are unchanged.

## Tests
- `SHP/tests/work.test.ts` (4):
  - **restock:** a ₱0 job order for the shop, on the board, refused on a release slip, nothing in stock until finished, put in partly then fully → Released, and one shop customer only;
  - **rework:** off sale, give back, only the pieces still out come back;
  - **change:** from stock, from a job order's leftovers, and from other pieces;
  - **refusals:** no source, same item, size not offered, over what is on hand across lines, made-to-order items, and no `shp.work`.
- Full suite: 1,887 passed. Only the known Windows line-ending failures remain locally.
- Checked in a browser on the practice shop:
  - restock from the Stock window, then on the production board under the shop's name;
  - put into stock from Shop work;
  - the change window.
