Current head: `cc019f683884c7d4c88544ea1dd47cef2c2921db`. PR is open, non-draft and **unmerged**.

- [PR CI run 38191148668](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38191148668): all **9 jobs completed successfully** on this head: Python 3.10/3.12/3.14, Windows/macOS core portability, Docker integration, intentional negative evidence and both collectors. Python 3.12: **95 passed, 5 skipped**.
- The previously pending [macOS job](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38191148668/job/114623984906) completed successfully at 01:16:11 UTC; [final collector](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38191148668/job/114624228437) completed successfully at 01:16:23 UTC. [Negative collector](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38191148668/job/114624075966) also succeeded.
- [Follow-up review](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/pull/2#pullrequestreview-5485895428) confirms the prior short-write/output-cap blocker is resolved on this exact head: `read1(min(4096, remaining + 1))`, plus stdout/stderr cap+1-flush-then-sleep regressions. No further fix was requested for that finding.
- A separate [new Copilot review run](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38230395421) is in progress at this checkpoint; its outcome is not included in the successful test-CI claim.

Known limits remain: immediate-child termination only, no process-tree guarantee; persistent bidirectional sessions unverified; no crash-durability/fsync guarantee; filesystems without hard-link support fail closed; Windows symlink assertions depend on symlink permission. No automatic consumer promotion.

Earlier verification checkpoints below are retained as history; their draft/pending language is superseded by this section.

## Scope

Cross-repository review of CLI argument/process patterns in Ironmate, flutter_navigation_basic, browser-test-kit, mcp-toolcall-lab, web-ui, markdown, the parent repository, gh_identity and yourself (excluding Aoi). Preserve the **single-file, stdlib-only Python 3.10+** core.

The most reusable missing contract was **stdin on run_command**: Flutter's JSON-stdin workers and browser-test-kit's child probes repeatedly need it, while cli_args currently classifies Git NUL-safe stdin pathspec as only construct-only.

### Implementation
- Add optional `stdin: str | bytes | None` to `run_command`: strict UTF-8 encoding for text, exact bytes for binary, no implicit newline, shell=False, one-shot buffered subprocess invocation.
- Type/encoding validation also occurs in dry-run, without running a subprocess or showing input contents. Preserve existing return-code, timeout, stdout/stderr UTF-8 replacement policy and compatibility for existing calls.
- Python 3.10+ / Windows/macOS core test for text, invalid UTF-8 output replacement, NUL records, disallowed stdin types, dry-run.
- Real Git NUL-safe `--pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul` test with Unicode/leading-hyphen filename. Long-lived interactive/bidirectional `git cat-file --batch-command` remains construct-only.
- README documents the new contract and cross-repo evidence/limits.

No modification to Aoi, gh_identity, yourself, or other consumers; they can adopt after this standalone CLI contract is reviewed and verified. No dependency upgrades or deployment changes.

## Historical verification
[CI run 38185941819](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38185941819) ran against code head `ce1717fbca53a62b747676382e62b358879f07b6`: Python 3.10/3.12/3.14, Windows/macOS core portability, Docker integration, negative failure lab and negative collector are successful. Python 3.10/3.12 each reported **83 passed, 5 skipped**; general failure-identity collection also completed successfully. All 9 jobs passed. At that checkpoint, head `1a1da71a47dfaabd152b505334ea04725c70c633` changes **README only**, correcting the documented NUL escape; CI's `paths-ignore: docs/**, README.md` intentionally does not rerun for README-only changes. Keep Draft / unmerged for review. Related to parent vendor release-train #46 only as a future recommended baseline candidate, not automatic promotion.
## Additional cross-repository test evidence (follow-up)

- Real finite Git `cat-file --batch-command --buffer -Z` round trip (stored blob body includes an embedded NUL). This upgrades the previously construct-only argv test; **persistent bidirectional sessions remain unverified**.
- Stdin + nonzero exit/stderr, empty input, timeout + partial diagnostics regressions.
- Updated README and CLI argument-pattern documentation to reflect only the measured support.
- [Follow-up CI run 38186226523](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38186226523): Python 3.10/3.12/3.14 passed on follow-up code head; Python 3.12 and 3.14 each **85 passed / 5 skipped**. Full OS/container/collector job conclusions need same-head confirmation before asserting all green.

## Added in the same PR: safe output + output-size cap

- `write_output(..., overwrite=False)` uses exclusive file creation and refuses existing targets, symlinks and dangling symlinks without unlinking. Existing `overwrite=True` behavior remains default. Uses a private staging directory next to the destination, writes the complete UTF-8 content first, then atomically publishes by an exclusive same-filesystem hard link. Refuses existing files and symlinks (including dangling symlinks); never removes the destination. Filesystems lacking hard-link support fail closed. Crash durability/fsync is not guaranteed.
- `run_command(..., max_output_bytes=N)` uses two concurrent pipe readers and a shared stdout+stderr *raw byte* budget. Exceeding the cap terminates the immediate child (not a whole process tree), keeps at most N bytes, and sets `CommandResult.output_limited=True` and `returncode=None`. Limit is opt-in; legacy JSON encoding omits the false status to preserve compatibility.
- `examples/run_cli.py` exposes `--no-overwrite` and `--max-output-bytes`, with dedicated exit **125** for overflow (existing timeout 124 preserved). Tests cover exact cap, zero cap, combined stdout+stderr, runaway child, dry-run validation, stderr/timeout, invalid types, and example CLI. Windows symlink-specific assertions run when symlink creation is permitted.
- Retains Python 3.10+ / stdlib-only, no external runtime dependency or automatic promotion to consumers.

Historical source/test head: `61e98579d14685e56dd7325c68e7108bbcdb48d9`. [Same-head CI](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38186542809) is still being checked. PR remains Draft / unmerged.

### Follow-up after Windows test feedback

Early CI found that Windows can follow dangling symlinks even with `open('x')`. This was treated as a real safety issue, not a test skip: fixed using an explicit existing-path check plus complete staging and exclusive hard-link publication, and added a fail-closed simulated link failure regression.

[Historical verification run 38186649903](https://github.com/myon-bioinformatics/cli_args/actions/runs/38186649903) targets head `f745c9701748cedbf44f2161410eaa311522e9ae`. author: hernanmec
body:
## Alcance FE-02

Implementa el recorrido de identidad Angular contra las rutas Go existentes: términos versionados, registro y preferencia inicial, verificación/reemisión, acceso, consulta de sesión, logout, recuperación y cambio de contraseña. Separa adaptador HTTP, estado de sesión y componentes; reutiliza el SDK OpenAPI generado.

El Bearer queda en memoria. No se guarda en localStorage/sessionStorage ni se incluye en URL/logs. Logout y cambio de contraseña limpian estado privado; las respuestas de sesiones anteriores se descartan. Navegación y modo restringido usan exclusivamente roles/modo confirmados por Go. Preferencia ofrecer/arrendar no deriva permisos. Identidad y cuenta son CSR/noindex. Go mantiene sus rutas; el mock continúa disponible.

## Respuesta a revisión

- Recuperación de contraseña ahora se coordina por `IdentitySession`; al confirmarla Go se invalida el Bearer, la sesión y el estado privado que pudo revocarse.
- `IdentityPage` registra y libera la limpieza de los formularios sensibles, resetea contraseñas/tokens, invalida operaciones pendientes y descarta sus avisos tardíos. Logout limpia localmente incluso si Go no responde y la app sale de la vista privada.
- Logout captura la generación de sesión. Una respuesta tardía no cambia avisos ni navegación después de un nuevo login.

## Validación

- `npm test -- --watch=false`: 26 pruebas en 7 archivos. Incluye los escenarios previos y las dos regresiones solicitadas en la última revisión: login desde IdentityPage con IdentitySession real que confirma sesión y navega a `/mi-cuenta`; recuperación A pendiente → logout → login B → respuesta tardía A, con revalidación de B y conservación de Bearer, roles y avisos; recuperación anónima vigente aceptada que limpia tokenId, token y contraseñas del formulario.
- `npm run api:check`: regeneración desde OpenAPI y compilación TypeScript.
- `npm run build`: build CSR/SSR y prerender de las tres rutas públicas; identidad permanece CSR.
- Recorrido M01 con cuenta sintética y Mailpit en stack Compose temporal y volumen PostgreSQL desechable: términos, registro/preferencia, duplicados, correo no verificado, verificación/reemisión/replay, login/sesión/logout, recuperación anti-enumeración, token inválido/replay, cambio/revocación/relogin, CORS y mock separado. Escaneo de logs sin secretos.
- `go test ./internal/openapicontract ./internal/platform/health`, `go build ./cmd/api` y `npm audit --omit=dev` (0 vulnerabilidades).
- Evidencia visual: [sesión escritorio](planning/frontend/evidencia/FE02_sesion_escritorio.jpg) y [registro móvil](planning/frontend/evidencia/FE02_sesion_movil.jpg).

El SDK generado no fue modificado. Su orden de construcción no adjunta Authorization a las llamadas protegidas de M01; el adaptador provee el header en memoria explícitamente y una prueba HTTP fija ese contrato.

## Límites

Los términos locales disponibles son códigos/versiones/hash, no texto legal; la UI declara el alcance sintético y no afirma aceptación legal. Catálogo/explorar, gestión de anfitrión y administración muestran solo destinos pendientes FE-03/06/11. No se inicia GCP ni proveedor real y no se retira el mock. Recuperación y cambio de credenciales pasan las pruebas de integración API/Mailpit; no se automatizó el ingreso de nuevas credenciales desde la UI del navegador.

author: mcncl
body:
## Why

Buildkite agent users should be able to run a GitHub Actions workflow without installing a separate `buildkite-gha` binary and plugin:

```sh
buildkite-agent pipeline upload --format github-actions .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

That needs the agent to import this module as a Go package. Today the only entry point is `internal/cli.Run(args)`: the agent would have to shell out, parse argv-shaped strings, and still depend on a `buildkite-agent` binary on `PATH` for artifacts, metadata, pipeline upload, and secrets. `internal/` packages also cannot be imported at all.

## What

The root package `github.com/buildkite/buildkite-gha` is now the stable embedding API. The agent supplies its own Buildkite effects and credentials instead of subprocesses:

```go
import gha "github.com/buildkite/buildkite-gha"

client := gha.Client{Version: version, Backend: agentBackend, Credentials: agentCredentials}
err := client.Upload(ctx, gha.CompileRequest{WorkflowPaths: paths, EventPath: eventPath})
```

| Entry point | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Client.Compile` / `Client.Upload` | Hosted upload preparation, then verified artifact and pipeline upload. |
| `Client.UploadStage` | Deferred expansion from a stage digest and producer. |
| `Client.RunJob` | Plan execution with the authoritative exit code, including `78` for tolerated failures. |
| `RunCLI` | Dispatch for the argv forms generated pipelines invoke, including the private container process helper (`gha.ContainerProcessHelperCommand`). |

`Backend` and `Credentials` are interfaces for artifacts, pipelines, annotations, metadata, step updates, secrets, redaction, and Git credential helpers; `Client.AgentAPI` optionally injects an `http.RoundTripper` for job-scoped Agent API calls. Plans, stage records, and pipeline bytes stay opaque and version-bound.

The CLI is unchanged for users. Its implementation moved from `internal/cli` to `internal/command` so the executable adapter and the shared orchestration are separate packages; the Windows CI workflow now targets the moved tests and drops the step for the secrets migration tests removed in #592.

The generated command protocol an embedder must dispatch (`run-job`, `upload --stage-digest`, and the container helper) is documented in `doc.go` and [docs/development.md](https://github.com/buildkite/buildkite-gha/blob/bm/exported_package_api/docs/development.md#embed-the-go-package). `api_test.go` covers the contract end to end with in-memory `Backend` and `Credentials` implementations.

Consumer: the agent branch at buildkite/agent `feat/github_actions_pipeline_upload` already builds against this API and has run jobs on a local macOS queue. After merge this needs a `v0.103.0` tag so the agent can pin a release instead of a pseudo-version.

author: tonksthebear
body:
The structural fix of the FLAKY result `botster-core-sys::slow_process a_spawned_child_matches_its_identity_and_dies_by_the_group_kill` (#287 gate on `27cb2cc4`, mutation stage 2), under BUILD.md Testing rule 9. Record: `~/botster-sessions/shared/core-stage1/handoffs/flaky-a-spawned-child-matches-its-identity-and-dies-by-the-group-kill-27cb2cc4.md`.

## The failure

Attempt 1 failed and the one retry passed. The test body passed. The panic came from the guard's drop:

```
thread 'a_spawned_child_matches_its_identity_and_dies_by_the_group_kill' panicked at crates/botster-core-sys/tests/common/process_guard.rs:113:17:
the group guard's cleanup failed (Ok(ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(9)))):
```

The anchor (the process that holds the group) ended by SIGKILL and wrote no report. The mutant of that run (`real/route.rs`, testkit) is not in the `botster-core-sys` test binary (`cargo tree`). So the failure is a flake of the test itself.

## Cause (from the source and the retained output; no reproduction campaign)

1. `spawn` in `tests/slow_process.rs` returned as soon as the child existed. It did not wait for the child's shell prefix to register its group with the anchor.
2. The test then sent SIGKILL to the whole group.
3. Two orders were possible:
   - The kill came first. The anchor was not in the group, so the guard guarded nothing, and the test passed.
   - The registration came first. The test's own SIGKILL ended the anchor, and the guard's drop panicked (attempt 1).

Neither order is the designed state, which is "the anchor is in the group before the body runs".

## The fix

- `spawn` (slow_process) waits for a FIFO line that the shell writes after the registration and before the body. So the anchor is always in the group when the body runs. The FIFO helpers `fifo` and `told` are the existing code of `the_worker_control_signal_reaches_the_worker_handler`, moved. The 10 s deadline value does not change.
- `GroupGuard::drop`: a SIGKILL of the anchor with no report is a group kill from outside the guard. The drop then waits for the group's last members with no signal (`await_group_end`), as `PayloadGuard` does. `await_group_end` moves unchanged from `payload_guard.rs` to `guard_cleanup.rs`. The registration thread now gives the group's pid, so that the drop knows which group to wait for.
- No retry. No timeout value changes.

## The other users of the guard

`process_guard.rs` is also compiled into the tests of `botster-core` (`ScriptWorker`) and `botster-worker` (`slow_cli`, the driver observer in `tests/common/session.rs`). `slow_payload` (`dropping_the_payload_reaps_its_leader`) uses it too. In each of them, the shell prefix blocks until the anchor confirms that it joined the group (`register_worker` reads the anchor's ready byte). So no body runs before the registration. An outside kill before the registration ends only the shell and its `register_worker` helper, and nothing is left behind. An outside SIGKILL after the registration was the failing path, and the new drop rule now accepts it for every user.

## Proof

- Mac pool evidence job on `1a9ba675cd6f51afd88e657649d22ec525d32f44` (Darwin 27.0.0), exit 0. Log: `~/botster-sessions/gates/botster-core-stage1-p6-group-guard-order-1a9ba675-pool-20261011-165612-58346.log`. Script: `prebuild-worker`, then:
  - `botster-core-sys` (`slow_process`, `slow_payload`): exit 0. `slow_process` 23 passed, `slow_payload` 28 passed.
  - `botster-core` (`slow_facade_worker`, `slow_real_core`, the `ScriptWorker` users): exit 0. 19 and 27 passed.
  - `botster-worker` (`slow_cli`, `slow_session`, the guard and the driver observer): exit 0. 17 and 41 passed.
  - Reversal in the same job: the new drop rule off (`if false && killed`), the FIFO wait kept. The kill test fails with the gate's attempt-1 message (`the group guard's cleanup failed (Ok(ExitStatus(unix_wait_status(9))))`), exit 101. So the order is now certain, and the drop rule is what makes the test pass.
- Full Linux pool gate on `1a9ba675cd6f51afd88e657649d22ec525d32f44`: msa1, exit 0. The gate base `BOTSTER_CI_BASE_REF` is `v1` `f6025aed4cdf7da836e835e0040fc128b7e8f32f`. All 10 steps PASS. The kill test PASS (`slow_process a_spawned_child_matches_its_identity_and_dies_by_the_group_kill`). No FLAKY result. The diff changes only test code, so the gate lists no mutant of it. Log: `~/botster-sessions/gates/botster-core-stage1-p6-group-guard-order-1a9ba675-pool-20261011-164959-15401.log`.
- Two earlier gates of this branch failed, and the fixes are commits of this PR:
  - `5f667383`, clippy: `await_group_end` moved into the shared `guard_cleanup.rs`, so its `Instant::now` calls reached the tests of botster-core, which disallow them (Core TM-1). `4c22e277` makes it read `platform::real_now()`, as `end_group` does.
  - `4c22e277`, taint: the `mkfifo` call that moved into `fifo` waited with no bound, and the process-check entry of its old function allowed no site. `1a9ba675` runs it through `OwnedChild::spawn(..).status()`, as `slow_facade_worker`'s `marker_fifo` does, and removes the stale entry.
  - Logs: `...-5f667383-pool-20261011-163751-35206.log` and `...-4c22e277-pool-20261011-164042-57342.log`.
- The branch merged `v1` `f6025aed` once (`5f667383`), before its first gate.
- Final flow (lead SLOT): the branch merged `v1` `f7eeced64e652700f2f78fc063e4896832134233` once (pure, no conflict): head `07f5db488e71f5da46d845ee9663a5a7e6863ec5`.
  - `cargo xtask base-merge-check 1a9ba675 07f5db48`: PASS (both ancestry checks and conditions (1) to (4)); none of the 20 paths that changed on the base is in the pull request's 5 paths; the own diff is byte-identical (sha256 `7d706be6d1560e1c0760501d74bd022772a0fda93df267df622922aa9c8a3012`). author: zacxdev
body:
## Mechanism

Every `run:` block in `.github/workflows/publish-image.yml` is `set -euo pipefail`. The three anonymous-pull proof steps printed a preview with `echo "$out" | head -20`, where `$out` is `skopeo inspect`'s JSON. That JSON has one `RepoTags` entry per tag the package has ever carried, and this workflow adds one per published commit, so it grows without bound.

While the output fits in the kernel's pipe buffer (64 KiB) the writer finishes into the buffer and never learns the reader left. Past that size `head` exits while `echo` is still writing; `echo` gets a broken pipe and `pipefail` fails the step. This happens **after** the image was pushed and the inspect succeeded, and it aborts every later leg of the job. It is deterministic from the crossing onward: every earlier run passed, every later one fails.

## Fix

Every site of the shape in the file (8 lines in 4 steps):

| step | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Go / Python / UI proof — preview | `echo "$out" \| head -20` | `sed -n '1,20p' <<<"$out"` |
| Go / Python / UI proof — digest | `printf '%s' "$out" \| sed -n '…p' \| head -1` | `sed -n '…p' <<<"$out" \| sed -n '1p'` |
| UI control — loaded ref | `docker load … \| sed -n '…p' \| head -1` | `… \| sed -n '1p'` |
| UI control — refusal preview | `echo "$out" \| head -20` | `sed -n '1,20p' <<<"$out"` |

A here-string has no writer process to break, and `sed -n` with no `q` reads to end-of-file. The digest line was not the measured failure, but `skopeo inspect` prints a `Digest` line per layer below the manifest's, so `head -1` left a writer behind it too.

**Not consolidated into a shared script, deliberately.** The existing guards read the workflow text: `test_every_inspect_is_anonymous`, the per-package absent-tag count, `test_each_anonymous_proof_inspects_ITS_OWN_package` and the whole-body pins. Moving the proof into a script would leave those reading three call lines and nothing about what the proof does. The "one place" for this rule is the reader ledger below, which covers every step in the file.

## Guards

- **Behavioural** — `test_the_anonymous_proofs_survive_an_inspect_larger_than_a_pipe_buffer`: extracts each proof step's own shell, substitutes the `${{ … }}` expressions, and runs it against a stub `skopeo` (absent tag refused, otherwise a synthetic manifest). Parametrised over 3 steps × 2 sizes (3 tags; 3701 tags ≈ 208 KiB) × 2 SIGPIPE dispositions (ignored, as on the runner; default). Asserts exit 0, the manifest's digest (not a layer's) on the `digest:` line, and a preview rather than the whole manifest.
- **Structural** — `test_no_pipeline_reader_can_exit_before_its_writer_finishes`: every command reading from a `|` in any step, pinned by set equality (fails on grow and shrink), plus a predicate naming the four early-exit shapes (`head`, `grep -q/-m`, `sed …q`, `awk … exit`). The predicate is a closed list; the equality is what forces the decision for a new reader.
- **Mutants** — six rows added to `tests/publish_workflow_mutants.py`.

## Matrix

`pytest tests/test_publish_workflow.py -k pipe` (13 cases), same tests, workflow file varied:

| workflow | result |
|---|---|
| as at `74f826f` | **7 failed, 6 passed** |
| this branch | **13 passed** |

The 7 reds at `74f826f`: the reader ledger, and all six `large` rows — `echo: write error: Broken pipe`, exit 1 with SIGPIPE ignored (the failure the publish run showed); exit 141 with it at default. The six `small` rows pass there, which matches the history.

Mutant battery: `30 mutants, 0 problem(s)` over a 37-test baseline. The three `reintroduce-head-20-in-the-{GO,PYTHON,UI}-proof` rows are killed by the behavioural test; `reintroduce-head-1-on-the-digest`, `reintroduce-head-20-in-the-UI-control` and `pipe-the-preview-into-an-UNLISTED-reader` by the ledger. Each `head` mutant was separately checked to land in the step its name states.

## Not verified

- **The real workflow.** It runs only on push to `main` (and `workflow_dispatch`), never on a PR, so nothing here executes the fixed steps against ghcr. The first real evidence is the publish run after merge.
- **`cairn-ui` at `74f826f` is still unpublished.** This PR does not publish it; the merge commit's own run publishes all three images at the new sha.
- The UI control's two changed lines have no behavioural test (no `docker` stub); they are covered by the ledger and the whole-body pin only.
- The stub is not skopeo: its layout is hand-written to match (one key per line, per-layer `Digest` lines), not captured.
- A harness finding worth knowing: the step must be run with a minimal environment. A nix dev shell exports a variable named `out`; reassigning it keeps it exported, the 208 KiB manifest lands in every child's environment, and the step dies of `Argument list too long` (126) — a red unrelated to the pipe. The test pins a minimal env and says why.

author: fclairamb
body:
This adds SolidPing as a DietPi-Software title. I'm the author of SolidPing.

SolidPing is a self-hosted uptime monitoring tool: HTTP, TCP, DNS, ICMP, TLS, database and other checks, status pages and alerting. It is a single Go binary with an embedded SQLite database. Source: https://github.com/fclairamb/solidping (AGPL-3.0).

## Implementation

- Software ID `solidping`, category System Stats & Management, next to Uptime Kuma.
- arm64 and x86_64 only. Upstream does not build ARMv6, ARMv7 or RISC-V binaries.
- Install: the release binary `solidping-linux-$arch.gz` is extracted to `/opt/solidping/solidping`.
- Data: `/mnt/dietpi_userdata/solidping` (SQLite database and uploaded files), owned by a `solidping` system user.
- Config: `/mnt/dietpi_userdata/solidping/solidping.env`, created on first install only, so a reinstall keeps it. It sets the port, `SP_BASE_URL` from the local IP, and a random `SP_ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY` used to encrypt stored check and integration credentials.
- Port 4002. SolidPing's default is 4000, which NoMachine already uses in DietPi.
- Service with the same hardening as other titles. ICMP checks need no capability, since `97-dietpi.conf` sets `net.ipv4.ping_group_range`.
- First login: `admin@solidping.io` / `solidpass`, SolidPing then requires a new password.
- Uninstall asks before removing the data directory, like Uptime Kuma.
- `update_urls.bash`: bumps the fallback URL and watches for armv7 and riscv64 builds.

## Testing

- Ran `.github/workflows/dietpi-software.bash -s solidping` from this branch on an arm64 host (privileged Debian trixie container with systemd), for aarch64 trixie and aarch64 bookworm. Both passed: service active, port 4002 listening, `/api/mgmt/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.
- x86_64 was not run through the test script, I have no x86 host. The amd64 binary was started under emulation with the same environment: health check and login OK.
- The `update_urls.bash` entry, run alone against an older fallback URL, replaced it with v0.38.3.
- shellcheck: no new findings compared to `dev`.
- Unprivileged ICMP checked under the service hardening (`PrivateUsers`, `NoNewPrivileges`) with DietPi's `ping_group_range`.

Docs: https://github.com/MichaIng/DietPi-Docs/pull/1238

author: freeperro
body:
The commit-time guard read session.new/dirty at before_commit, so any
handler that flushed first committed an inconsistent invoice unchecked, and
an edit to lines alone never checked the header at all. An after_flush hook
now records every touched invoice - written directly, through a new, dirty or
deleted line, or as the invoice a line was moved away from - and the commit
checks that record. Savepoints keep their own record: a release checks what
was written inside it and hands it up; a rollback (explicit, exception, or
failed flush) discards it. That keeps the QuickBooks per-row loops and the
closeout autodraft contained, and create_invoice's GL savepoint does not see
the half-built header. The docstring no longer claims flush-time enforcement.

No migration; no stored row changes. Strict mode is unchanged;
GDX_INVOICE_INVARIANT=log remains the escape hatch. Test seeds that committed
inconsistent invoices now restate their headers; two tests that pin paths on
inconsistent rows run in log mode and say why.

## VERIFICATION MANIFEST

**The Delta:** gdx_dispatch/core/invoice_invariants.py (flush-time record,
savepoint record stack, commit/release check, active_history on
InvoiceLine.invoice_id); new test_invoice_invariant_flush_tracking.py (20
tests); fixture seeds in 8 existing test files. Full matrix (7 shards):
10527 passed, 347 skipped, 5 xfailed, 0 failed; --scans green. The new tests
fail against the old guard (8 against HEAD; the savepoint and moved-line
cases against earlier drafts of this fix).

**The Assumption:** prod holds few unlocked, line-bearing invoices whose
total disagrees with their lines - a read-only count earlier in this work
found 4 (all paid, created 2026-03-29) and 0 on demo. Any write that touches
one of them without restating its header is now refused.

**The Blind Spot:** the Postgres arm was not tested locally (347 skips, all
environmental; CI runs it). I haven't checked the QuickBooks pull adoption
path against real QBO payloads, and I don't know how often prod writes touch
the 4 legacy rows. POST /api/jobs/{id}/line-items adds a line without
restating the header and is now always refused in strict mode; it has no UI
caller and was not changed here.

**The Test Gap:** no test drives a real HTTP handler through the
flush-then-commit shape; the guard is exercised on direct sessions and
through create_invoice. The active_history listener guards a shape no
production code currently produces (no line reassigns invoice_id).



## Notes

- **Postgres arm not run locally:** 347 skips, all environmental. CI's Postgres jobs are the first run of that arm.
- **Before merge (audit ask):** count, on prod and demo, unlocked non-deleted invoices with live lines whose total disagrees with `Σlines + tax` by more than 0.005. An earlier count found 4 on prod, 0 on demo. Each such row now refuses any write that does not restate its header.
- Issues: parent GDXA-679, this PR issue GDXA-684.

## Scope and compatibility

Preserves `sbd.shop.v1`, `system-by-dave.shop.v1`, the unchanged pure model, all four reviewed legacy imports, quantities and retained originals. Optional validated stored views and guarded draft/layout recovery use the existing console engine. Apply, Save and export remain explicit; layout operations never infer readiness or synchronize another app's records.

Applied text edits now trim surrounding whitespace. Worklist warnings and the summary agree for empty blockers, including old plans, without rewriting untouched saved values. No new dependency, shared-engine redesign, legacy retirement, inventory accounting, hardware control or specialist absorption.

## Verified

- Typecheck, eight existing plus twelve native model tests, generated build parity and source contracts passed.
- Preserved legacy browser checks passed on the candidate and live: quantities/partial/zero/unknown, preview/cancel, stale/repeated/malformed source rejection, old backup, explicit Save/reload/export/restore, source preservation, damaged-save recovery, themes, keyboard, five viewports and print.

## Retained failures and limits

Original review P2 remains in history. Its regression failed against the old build with one blank blocker warning and passed after correction. Initial regression label lookup was corrected before exercising that product assertion.

Retained CI failures: exact HTML count 147 versus 148 (`38185943733`), domain key count 73 versus 75 (`38186219804`), and immediate error-visibility check before scheduled scroll (`38186219653`). Corrected inventory assertions explicitly include the new Shop assets/keys; error visibility now waits for the same containment predicate and retains the original assertion. Earlier probe timing and real 320×256 clipping failures are retained; no warning assertion was removed.

Windows domain staging qualification gaps were not hidden or bypassed; full Linux CI/publication passed. The previous Show Control LED first-attempt failure and unchanged-source retry remain historical evidence, not a fix claimed by this PR.

Physical touch, virtual keyboards, operator rehearsal and actual process/power interruption are **not tested**. This is The Shop's bounded technical release, not whole-suite completion. The existing private Next Steps Board was unavailable; no replacement was created or synchronization claimed.

body:
## PR-8 (EG-6) — vdesk-clientes, qa-alert e qualidade param de reler tabela para comparar

Três edges baixavam linhas só para compará-las e jogá-las fora. A comparação vai para o banco (mesma receita da EG-2) e a edge recebe só o resultado, em **jsonb escalar** (o `max_rows = 1000` do PostgREST não corta).

### Medido (edge_logs 10–11/10/2026, 24h; bytes crus estimados pelo JSON das mesmas linhas no PROD em 11/10)

| Leitura | Rodadas/dia | Por rodada antes | Depois | MB/dia antes → depois |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vdesk_clients?select=id,nome,source_hash,status` (3 páginas) | 96 | ~154 kB | 42 B | ~14,8 → ~0 |
| qualidade: fila inteira com `custom_fields` | 143 | ~50 kB | ~455 B | ~7,2 → ~0,07 |
| qa-alert: 33 itens em desenvolvimento com `state_history` | 144 | ~29 kB | 2 B | ~4,2 → ~0 |
| qa-alert: ~156 filhos pré-carregados para o cartão | 144 | ~35 kB | 0 (sob demanda) | ~5,0 → ~0 |
| qa-alert: abertos + `select state` e `select id` por item | 144 | ~13 requisições | 2 | ~2.000 → ~290 req/dia |

**~31 MB/dia → ~0,1 MB/dia.** No dia medido: 95 rodadas ok do vdesk gravaram 0 linhas; a qualidade teve 0 candidatos; o qa-alert não tinha nenhum item com evidência sem evento aberto.

> A tabela do briefing citava `pbi_stage_config` / `pbi_health_thresholds` / `devops_lead_area_map` a 288/dia: essas leituras são do `devops-sync-all` e já estão atrás da fila de lifecycle desde a EG-2 — hoje são **3/dia**. Ficaram de fora.

### O que muda

**Migration `20261011130000_eg6_vdesk_qa_qualidade_rpcs.sql`** — 4 funções STABLE, SECURITY INVOKER, `SET search_path = public`, REVOKE de PUBLIC/anon/authenticated, GRANT a service_role. Nenhuma escreve.

- `rpc_vdesk_clientes_diff(text[], text[], text[])` → `{gravar, inativar, na_base}`. Regra copiada da edge (`IS DISTINCT FROM` = `!==` com NULL). Inativação calculada antes do upsert, como a leitura `existentes` era; a edge continua dona de quando aplicar.
- `rpc_qa_retorno_candidatos(text)` → itens sem evento aberto e com **possível** evidência.
- `rpc_qa_eventos_abertos()` → abertos com `existe` e `state` do item; a edge decide com o mesmo `toLowerCase().includes(...)`.
- `rpc_qualidade_fila(uuid, text[], boolean)` → `{fila, tags_suspeitas, candidatos}`.

**Superconjunto + regra original = resultado original.** Onde a regra depende de JavaScript (`toLowerCase`/`toUpperCase` de Unicode, `new Date()` de texto), o banco não imita: devolve um superconjunto (a prova está no comentário de cada função) e a edge reaplica a regra de sempre. Casos que no JS lançam exceção (ex.: `state_history` objeto, elemento nulo) voltam para a edge, que faz o que sempre fez.

**Edges**
- `vdesk-sync-base-clientes`: `diffClientes()` chama a RPC. Nome não-texto vai como NULL (nunca casa, como `Map.get(123)`); status não-texto é forçado como "mudou" na edge.
- `devops-qa-alert`: candidatos e abertos pelas RPCs; filhos do cartão lidos sob demanda, só para o item alertado (mesma leitura `lerEmLotes`, mesmo filtro). O dedupe por item continua antes do insert.
- `devops-sync-qualidade`: `carregarFila()` chama a RPC; `precisaRevisitar`, a contagem de AVIAO e o sort/teto continuam na edge.
- Todas caem na **leitura antiga** se a RPC não existir (`PGRST202`), com log explícito de "migration EG-6 ausente".

### Validação
- **PROD (read-only)**: corpo de cada função rodado inline contra a regra antiga sobre os dados reais. vdesk com carga perturbada (3 nomes fora, 2 hashes trocados, 1 status virado, 1 novo, nome numérico, status numérico): gravar/inativar iguais; carga = base → `{gravar:[], inativar:[]}`. qa: detecção igual; evidência ignorando abertos igual (6 itens); resoluções iguais. qualidade: fila 119, avioes 17, candidatos 0 iguais; com `force`, 119 iguais e `custom_fields` idênticos.
- **DEV (transação desfeita por RAISE)**: migration + 20 casos de borda (hash/status nulos, nome nulo, reativação, `state_history` objeto/`[null]`/`[1,"x",[]]`/jsonb null, oldValue numérico, evento aberto, item sumido, carimbo inválido/numérico/outro formato/sub-ms, `changed_date` nulo, tags `AVıAO`/`Ação`, force, carga vazia, grants). `RESULTADO OK`.
- `npx vitest run`: 658/658. `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json`: 9 erros (os de base). esbuild das 3 edges ok.

### Diferenças conhecidas (todas fora do caso normal)
- As leituras antigas de candidatos (qa) e da fila (qualidade) não paginavam e seriam cortadas em 1000 linhas; o jsonb não corta (hoje 33 e 119).
- Ordem: as leituras antigas não tinham ORDER BY; as RPCs devolvem por id. Só afeta a sequência de alertas na mesma rodada e o desempate do sort por `changed_date` no teto de 200.
- qa-alert: no caminho antigo, erro na leitura de `state` de um evento virava `wi` nulo e **fechava** o evento; com a RPC não há leitura por item. O fallback legado mantém o comportamento antigo.

### Publicação (não feita neste PR)
1. Aplicar a migration no PROD.
2. Publicar as 3 edges (com `verify_jwt` atual = `true` nas três):
   - `vdesk-sync-base-clientes`: `index.ts`, `_shared/cors.ts`
   - `devops-qa-alert`: `index.ts`, `_shared/cors.ts`, `_shared/leitura.ts`
   - `devops-sync-qualidade`: `index.ts`, `_shared/cors.ts`, `_shared/devops.ts`

A ordem não quebra nada (fallback `PGRST202`), mas a economia só aparece com as duas partes.

body:
## Summary

Qualify an additional finite Local D25 filesystem-pressure profile for #682. Actual kernel ENOSPC on one private 512 MiB APFS image exercises capture admission, retained-object publication and exact materialization, followed by source preservation, recovery, GC and exact owned cleanup.

Delivery head: da514eb230edeaa89ca33b9420e4ea0ea9d696b5. Tested source: f2c28c55a9a7e296652d6e9c1a425b088d5a4345. Exact evidence: 6a3f37414f1b8c2390db1b9725e996304c6d2797. The final merge carries reviewed parent qualification documentation only.

## Contract

- One private single-writer image, bounded native clients, independent recovery journal, host-headroom admission and exact image/mount/device ownership checks. No forced eject or global sweep.
- Preserve the production 256 MiB capture floor. Full-volume capture refuses admission without acknowledgment; this does not qualify mid-capture journal exhaustion. CAS and materialization observe actual storage failures after a separate raw kernel ENOSPC witness, without a valid object, usable inputs or artifact.
- Source remains reconstructable. Release only the owned pressure entry, recover idempotently, materialize exact bytes and remove the eligible orphan through real retained CAS GC. Images, source repositories and journals are preserved on every attempt.
- Cleanup requires exact owned eject and independent image, native-device and mount absence observations. Ambiguous mutation outcomes remain unconfirmed and require reconciliation.
- The pre-unlink inode check is qualified for this private single-writer fixture, not atomic concurrent path replacement. This profile does not qualify full host/daemon/backend pressure, power loss, native build/verifier authority or whole Local Q3/Q4 completion.

## Test plan

author: gaurav-kunal
body:
Card #485 (INF 6), **part 3 of 5**: the rollout across the fleet (canaries, then waves sized to the org's Actions jobs, pause, resume, roll back) and its Admin API for Engineer on call and Super admin.

**Stacked on `#485/task/upgrade-bot-2` (part 2, #656)**, so the diff below is this part only. No migration of its own.

## What's built

**The tick** (`saas/fleet/rollout.ts`, in the every-minute cron before the outbox relay, so the stores it starts go out the same minute)
- **Enrolment**, on a rollout's first tick: every store not closed whose live build is on an older core (and with no passed major at or past the version waiting). Five, by a hash of the store and the rollout, are the **canaries** (`position` 0); every other gets a place from 1 to 100.
- **Starts** pending stores, lowest place first, marking each running and queueing `storefront.upgrade` (part 2's Workflow), while upgrades running across every rollout stay under **`GITHUB_ACTIONS_JOBS`** (new optional variable, 20 = the Free plan): half of it for an upgrade, so merchants' own publishes keep the rest, **all of it for a security fix**, which so goes ahead of automatic publishes (LIVE-SHOP §8, §10).
- **Canaries first**: once they end, one pinned or on the baseline **pauses the rollout** (`core_rollout.paused`, `canary_failed`) for an engineer; otherwise **waves** reach 10, 25, 50 and 100 stores in a hundred, each once the one before ended, then the rollout is `done`.
- **Roll back** puts back, twenty a minute, each store it took live: the pointer moves back to the build before the upgrade (`rollBackLive`, the same move as the regression rule's; `storefront.rolled_back` with `core_rolled_back`), and a passed major's waiting upgrade is dropped; a store whose live build moved on since keeps it (`moved_on`).

**Admin API** (`apis/admin/fleet.ts`, `saas/fleet/admin.ts`; SAAS §13 "Fleet": Engineer on call, Super admin)
- `coreRollouts(first, after)`, `coreRollout(id)` (each with its stores counted by state) under the new **`fleet.read`**; `startCoreRollout(version, security, reason)`, `pauseCoreRollout`, `resumeCoreRollout` and `rollBackCoreRollout(id, reason)` under **`fleet.manage`** (ACCESS §5.4 updated, with the role-table test). Each write is audited as `core_rollout.*` with the staff member, the reason and the state before and after (staff only). One rollout at a time (`ROLLOUT_ACTIVE`); unknown version `NOT_FOUND`; a blank reason `INVALID_INPUT`; a move the state doesn't allow `WRONG_STATE`. Schema regenerated.

## Decided here
- **A rollout is a `core_rollout` row moved by the cron, not a `job`** (SAAS §10 said "a platform-level job"); the per-store work is part 2's Workflow. Updated in SAAS §10.
- **Five canaries; waves of 10, 25, 50, 100 per hundred**; a canary that ends pinned or on the baseline pauses the rollout rather than going on. Resuming it, once its canaries all ended, means the engineer accepts them: the first wave starts.
- **Waves are sized by how many upgrades run at once**, not by a store count: half the org's jobs for an upgrade, all of them for a security fix.
- **Roll back moves pointers, never rebuilds**: a store that published or rendered a page since keeps its live build and is marked `moved_on` (suggested follow-up below).
- **`GITHUB_ACTIONS_JOBS`** defaults to 20 until #287 decides the org's plan; documented in THIRD-PARTY-ACCESS §8 and `.env.example`.

## Tests
- `tests/core-rollout.test.ts` (integration): Engineer on call **starts, pauses, resumes and rolls back**, each audited with its reason; a second start, a wrong move, Support, Read-only, a signed-out caller, a blank reason and an unknown version are refused; **canaries first, then each wave once the one before ended, then done**, one store at a time on two jobs; a **pinned canary pauses** the rollout with a job-actor entry; **resuming after that pause starts the waves** and doesn't pause again; **a security fix takes every job**; **roll back** puts a store back on the build before the upgrade, leaves one that moved on, drops a waiting major, and then leaves the rollout alone.
- `src/auth/permissions.test.ts`: the role table with `fleet.read` and `fleet.manage`. `src/index.test.ts`: the minute's cron runs the rollouts before the relay.

## Gates
- `pnpm turbo run build typecheck lint test --force`: 33 of 34 passed; `@dripfunnel/sandbox#test` lost one browser-driven publish check to a timeout while other agents' gates loaded the machine; run alone: **apps/sandbox 6 files, 46 tests passed**. (The first run caught `api#typecheck` in the scripts' project: the Admin API imported the fleet module's index, which reaches Workers types; it now imports `saas/fleet/admin` and both projects typecheck.)
- `pnpm --filter ./apps/api test:integration`: 122 of 126 files passed; `build-uploads`, `platform-branding` and `shop-worker` timed out in their hooks under the same load and pass alone together with `core-upgrade` and `core-rollout` (**5 files, 65 tests**); `store-webhooks` fails the same 2 delivery-count tests as on dev's parts 1–2, untouched by this card.

## Suggested follow-up
- Roll back stores whose live build moved on since the upgrade, by rebuilding their code on the previous core.

## What's left on the card
Part 4 (the migration agent, the baseline fallback with the merchant's notice, the draft's rebase at publish), part 5 (the image retirement rule and its job).

author: astrosteveo
body:
Closes #37

A session used another session's GitHub data only for the same branch and active issue, so parallel sessions on different branches each read GitHub.

- `remoteQuery` in `hooks/snapshot.ts` no longer depends on the branch or the active issue. It fetches the 30 most recently updated open pull requests with their branches and checks, the 20 most recently merged pull requests, the 30 newest open issues and the board items. `rateLimit(dryRun: true)` puts its cost at 2 points, the same as the old query. `gh run list` now fetches 20 runs instead of 6, so each branch's latest run is more likely to be among them.
- `GhRemote` holds data for the whole repository. `buildSnapshot` picks the branch's open pull request, its merged pull request and the active issue out of it.
- An active issue that isn't among the listed open issues is read with one REST request, again only when the active issue changes or on a fresh refresh.
- A github refresh in any session uses saved data for the same repository that is less than 30 seconds old, whatever its branch. `isRemote` ignores data that an older version of the mod saved in the old shape.

### The `$.store` experiment

Two `claude -p` sessions with a probe mod showed that a running session reads another session's `$.store` write within 25 ms, and that both keep all their keys when they write different keys at the same moment. So the shared data stays in `$.store`, and the fallback file in the git common directory isn't needed.

### Tests

- Five tests, each one session on its own branch, share one store and start 5 seconds apart. Only the first sends the refresh query, and each finds its own pull request.
- A session on another branch uses saved data and finds its pull request and active issue in it.
- An active issue older than the listed open issues is read with one REST request, once.

The wiki page Refreshes and GitHub requests describes the change.

author: luofang34
body:
What a host draws over the map's finished image, such as text and icons,
cannot be depth tested with the frame, and following a line of sight
across the terrain for each of them costs about 22 µs: 1,750 labels and
handles over hills took 35 ms each time they moved.

A host now sets DepthProbes (a pixel and the depth of the point there)
with HeadlessMap::set_depth_probes. A small pass after the overlay draws
one point per probe into its own texel, comparing the probe's depth,
with the overlay's DEPTH_BIAS, against the frame's nearest depth at its
pixel, and the answers are read back without waiting: the host takes
them with depth_probe_results a frame or two later. One request is in
flight at a time, the latest probes replacing waiting ones; requests
over MAX_PROBES answer the first MAX_PROBES. It uses vertex attributes
and texture loads only, so WebGL2 runs it too.

Test: probes at ground points on a grid over hills at 80° pitch answer
in sight for at least 99 % of those in sight and for at most 5 % of
those well behind hills, against all of them with the comparison
removed; the overlay's own test shares the points.

Its tests are headless pixel tests (features `headless thread-safe-futures`); they pass locally on Metal. CI runs that feature set only once #48 lands.

body:
Fixes #1096
Fixes #1098

An agent on the bridge could not make a trigger, a door or a button, so the wiring most levels need first could not be built. And a wire could only be taken back with `hf_undo` while it was still the agent's last step.

**#1098, brush entities**
- `hf_set_brush_entity` (brush_id, entity_class, optional name) goes through `tie_brushes_to_entity()`, the dock's Tie to Entity, as one undo step scoped to the brush. The class must be one the definitions mark `is_brush_entity`; a refusal lists them all. A cut is refused. With no name the brush keeps the one it has, so a `trigger_once` made a `trigger_multiple` still answers to the wires aimed at it.
- `hf_add_entity_output` takes `brush_id` as its source in place of `entity`, one or the other. A plain brush is refused and pointed at `hf_set_brush_entity`. Outputs are checked against the brush class, as they are for a point entity.

**#1096, removing a wire**
- `hf_remove_entity_output` (entity or brush_id, index) goes through `remove_entity_output()`. An index the source does not have is refused with how many it has, and changes nothing.

Both new tools work in `hf_batch`, and `$N.brush_id` reaches a brush made an entity earlier in the batch.

author: nezhinskiy
body:
`git_answer` read different faults as one `ran=False`, and every refusal built from it said "check that `git` runs here" without naming a checkout. Among them:

1. a question that outlived `git_run`'s five-second bound: a loaded machine, not a broken `git`;
2. a question asked in a directory that no longer exists. `git -C <gone> --version` exits 128 before it reads `--version`, so the usability probe called it a broken `git`;
3. a `git` a signal ended (a negative exit, the OOM killer's). It fell through to "git said no", and `main_checkout` then answered the worktree itself, the silent no-op it exists to prevent;
4. a `git` that genuinely cannot start or run, the only case the message described.

## How it was found

`stayfixed attach --store … --yes` in a repository with 65 worktrees failed on every run for a stretch of time with `` `git` could not answer which checkout owns this worktree in this checkout; … — check that `git` runs here ``, then succeeded unchanged.
- The machine's load average was 19 / 59 / 142 (1 / 5 / 15 min), with a parallel mutation-oracle run on it.
- The link timestamps that one failing run left show it stopping at one worktree after a 17-second stall over two others. The same `rev-parse` there took 0.03 s once the load fell.
- A `git` earlier on `PATH` that sleeps 7 s for that one `rev-parse` reproduces the message verbatim, exit 1, on the released 0.2.0.

## What changes

- **`gitenv._ask` is the one place a `git` process starts.** It returns `(code, stdout)` or why there was none (`_NoAnswer`: unlaunchable, timed out, unencodable input). `git_run` flattens that to `(-1, "")`, so its callers and `NO_ANSWER` are unchanged.
- **`git_answer` reads the cause where it is known, not by inference.** The cause is an `Unasked` enum whose values are the refusal sentences, each ending in its remedy:
  - `TIMED_OUT` and `ENDED`: run the command again;
  - `NOT_STARTED` and `BROKEN`: check that `git` runs;
  - `GONE`: the worktree went away.

  A positive exit is still told apart by a `git --version` probe, and only after `git` exited on its own. The probe reads its own timeout as `TIMED_OUT`, not as a broken `git`.
- **`GitAnswer`** is `value` plus `cause`; `require` appends the cause to the caller's words. `GitUnavailable.cause` carries it. `GitAnswer.ran` had no readers and is gone.
- **The refusals name the checkout**, through `printed.quoted`: `memory.store.main_checkout` and `_registered_worktree`. The latter now asks its second question only after the first is answered. In hooks these still surface only as the fixed "could not ask" line, so no path reaches the model.
- **`attach` skips a worktree removed mid-walk** (`_link_everywhere`), as `_worktrees` already skips a `prunable` one. `main_checkout` is `link`'s first call, so nothing was written there. Any other cause still fails the run.
- **Tests.**
  - `git_that_cannot_run` stubs `git_program`, the seam `_ask` starts `git` through, instead of `git_run`, which `git_answer` no longer calls.
  - `tests/outbound/policy.py` declares `_ask` as the root `git` launcher; `git_run` and `git_answer` are derived from it.
- **Unchanged:** the five-second bound (`GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). A retry on timeout was considered and declined: it would double the worst case of every `SessionStart` hook that asks the same question.

On the reproduction, this branch prints `` `git` could not answer which checkout '…/debt-dead-code' belongs to, so stayfixed cannot tell where the store is: `git` gave this question no answer within its time limit, which a heavily loaded machine causes; run the command again ``.

## Review

A review of the first commit (6336ecb6) found four things, and each was reproduced before it was fixed:
- **Signal exit.** A `-9` exit read as "the repository answered nothing", and `main_checkout(side) == side` came back `True`.
- **Unpinned remedy.** Swapping the broken-`git` remedy for "run again" left the affected modules green: 1002 passed.
- **Inferred timeout.** The cause of a `-1` was inferred from a later `--version` probe. That probe cost another bound, and under the worst load it brought the original misdiagnosis back.
- **Oracle red.** The first commit's own new `except` orphaned the "PartialLink" mutation, and the new gone-directory skip made the `prunable` entry's test unable to see that guard break.

The redesign above is the fix for the inferred timeout. The others are pinned by tests and mutations.

## Verification

Run on `e220a5d1`, which is `dev` at `bf363714` merged in (macOS):

```
uv run pytest -n auto --cov --cov-fail-under=92            # 6130 passed, 4 skipped
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .        # All checks passed! / 380 files already formatted
uv run mypy                                                # Success: no issues found in 379 source files
uv run python scripts/release.py check                     # one version everywhere: 0.2.0
uv run python scripts/mutation_oracle.py src/stayfixed/gitenv.py   # all 45 mutations were caught
uv run python scripts/mutation_oracle.py outbound / launch         # all 41 / all 25 caught
```

Mutations:
- **New:** "a question that ran out of time reads as a broken git", "a question asked in a removed worktree reads as a broken git", "a git a signal ended reads as a repository that answered nothing", "a git that cannot be started is told to run the command again", "a broken git is told to run the command again", "a probe that ran out of time reads as a broken git", "the refusal about which checkout owns a worktree names none", "a worktree removed mid-walk fails the whole attach".
- **Moved to `_ask`:** the six "the git runner …" entries, and "a broken git reads as a repository that answered".
- **Retargeted:** "attach's PartialLink forgets the links made before the failing call" and "attach links into a worktree git reports as prunable".

author: frankbria
body:
## Summary
Implements #968: since #792 nobody can finish signing up without the verification email, a missing provider is invisible to the user, and no health check knew about the frontend's email settings.

- `GET /api/health` on the frontend answers `{"status": "ok", "email": {"configured": true, "provider": "resend"}}`. It is public, reads the environment on every request, is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and never returns the key or the from-address.
- `emailProvider()` in `frontend/src/lib/email.ts` decides the answer: `resend` or `sendgrid` with an API key, `console` in development, otherwise none.
- `scripts/staging_health_probe.py` fails unless that route says email is configured, so `staging-health.yml` raises its alert when the provider is lost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] An unauthenticated frontend route reports whether an email provider is configured, by a boolean and the provider's name
- [x] "Not configured" when the provider is unset, unknown, or has no API key, by the rule a send uses: a test runs each case through both and requires them to agree
- [x] `staging-health.yml` fails when the route reports "not configured"
- [x] Tests cover configured, unset, unknown provider and missing key

Evidence from a real frontend and backend with the probe pointed at them: `docs/demos/2026-10-11-issue-968-email-health.md`.

- **"Configured" is not "working".** A known provider with a key present counts. An invalid key or an unverified sender still reports configured.

Deploy this build to staging, read `/api/health` there, and keep the deploy only if it reports a provider. The build also carries #792, so if email is not configured the deploy is rolled back to `sha-e5641d3` and the setting is the operator's step.

author: wps0
body:
Based on `main`. Together with #29 and #21, this is the "make it faster" pass.

## How I measured
- **Render counter:** a fake React DevTools hook, injected into an unminified production build, counts every component that actually rendered. React leaves a "performed work" flag on components it skipped, so a component only counts when its hook state changed, which React replaces on every real render.
- **Timing:** CDP's `ScriptDuration` for each interaction, median of 3 runs.
- **Scenarios:** 15 interactions, scripted in Playwright with sample data.

## Before → after (this PR)
| Interaction | Renders before | Renders after | Script time |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Calendar: type 10 chars in a new event's title | 840 | **390** | 18 → 14 ms |
| Projects: type 10 chars in the new-task field | 300 | **10** | 8 → 5 ms |
| Week: tick one session | 25 | **11** | 3 → 3 ms |
| Week: type 10 chars in task notes | 342 | **244** | 11 → 10 ms |
| Calendar: drag an event 2 h (20 moves) | 1045 | **947** | ~43 ms |
| Calendar: open an event card | 153 | 153 | 14 ms |
| Calendar: save the new event | 220 | 220 | 9 ms |
| Calendar: next week (`j`) | 312 | 312 | ~12 ms |
| Projects: open a project panel | 311 | 311 | ~8 ms |

Earlier PRs for comparison:
- **#29** (`App` no longer re-renders on popovers): opening an event card went from 7 `Column` + 7 `Strip` re-renders to 0. Deleting an event went from 14 to 1.
- **#21** (memoized days): ticking a session re-renders 1 day.

## What this PR does
- **`Select`, `TimeSelect`, `DateField`, `HoursInput`, `CapacityBadge`:** wrapped in `memo`. These are pure presentational widgets that re-rendered whenever their parent did, for example on every keystroke in a field next to them.
- **`WhenFields`** (date, times and all-day in both event editors): re-renders only when those values change, and its `onChange` is now stable.

## Not changed, on purpose
- **Script time is already small** for every interaction (≤ 20 ms), so I kept the changes local and readable rather than restructuring.
- **Typing task notes in the Week view** still re-renders the week's sessions once when the text is saved, because item titles come through a shared lookup object. Making that per-item would mean a store subscription in every row; it's not worth it at 10 ms.
- **Dragging** still re-renders the columns a few times per drag, when dnd-kit's active or over state changes, but not on every pointer move.

## Test plan
- [x] Benchmark before and after, as above.
- [x] `npm run lint`, `format:check`, `typecheck`, `test` (64), `build`.

author: caomyer
body:
## Intent

A single branch was refused three separate times, each by a different mechanism, on one ordinary rebase.
A fourth instance then refused a branch that had never been pushed anywhere.
Every recovery needed a first mate verification plus an explicit authorisation the pipeline would not perform itself.
That is a direct tax on the concurrency `AGENTS.md:321` is written to allow, which permits dispatching overlapping work precisely because "the selected delivery path can reconcile ordinary rebases or conflicts".
Today it cannot.

A scout reproduced all four refusals end to end on the version we run, on throwaway repositories with their own isolated daemon, and brought five options.
The captain chose `merge-only`: "Switch to merge-based integration and update the daemon, and leave the guard upstream as it is."
Answered 2026-10-11 through quarterdeck.
The report is `report:nm-rebase-guard-1`; the decision page is `page:task/nm-rebase-guard-1/nm-rebase-guard`.

**Why the refusals happen.**
no-mistakes keeps a private copy of every submitted branch - a gate mirror - written on every submission, including branches that never reach GitHub.
When a branch is resubmitted, a guard checks that nothing vanished by asking whether the stored copy's content is still present.
It answers with a per-file `git patch-id` plus a two-tree `git merge-tree` check.
A patch-id covers the surrounding context lines, so it moves whenever the new base touched a neighbouring line.
The merge-tree check fails whenever any later commit edited the same lines, including the pipeline's own review fixes.
A faithful, lossless rebase therefore reads as data loss.

The scout's control isolates the cause exactly: in two otherwise identical journeys, main editing line 8 - two lines below the feature's insertion, inside the patch-id's context window - is refused, while main editing line 12 is accepted and the run starts.
The trigger is the proximity of an unrelated edit, not loss.
Three further mechanisms compound it: a fresh submission gets no ownership exception even when the gate head is its own earlier submission; custody recovery after an abort uses the same merge-tree proof and dead-ends with no supported action; and the rebase step targets `origin/<branch>` first, so a main-based head gets rebased onto its own stale published head.

**Why merging fixes all four.**
A merge never rewrites history, so the old head stays an ancestor of the new one.
`planStaleBranchReconciliation` accepts that before any content test is attempted, so none of the four mechanisms can fire.
The guard is not weakened: an ancestry check is an exact proof of preservation where patch-id is an approximation that also misses whitespace-only losses.

no-mistakes v1.79.0, the version we run, already supports and tests `rebase.strategy: merge`.
The scout ran the worst journey under it: main conflicting mid-validation and the pipeline merging it additively, main moving again while review waited, the worker aborting, custody reporting `blocked_pipeline_owned_recoverable` with plain `axi sync --recover` returning it, a fresh run merging the newer main and being approved, and publication as a plain fast-forward of the first published head.
All five steps passed, including the recovery that is a dead end today.

**What it costs.**
Branches carry merge commits, but quarterdeck squash-merges every PR, so main never sees them.
Workers must stop rebasing a branch once it has been submitted, which is why the instruction change below is not optional - the current wording is the direct cause.

## What Changed

- Adds a root `.no-mistakes.yaml` that sets `rebase.strategy: merge`. no-mistakes now brings a moved main into a branch with a merge commit instead of rebasing it. Because the earlier submitted head stays an ancestor, the resubmission check accepts the branch before it compares any content.
- Updates `AGENTS.md` so agents run `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` instead of rebasing. It also says never to rebase a branch once it has been submitted to no-mistakes. `engine/AGENTS.md` now describes the concurrency condition as a delivery path that can "bring in a moved default branch and reconcile ordinary conflicts", where it used to say "reconcile ordinary rebases".
- Adds `scripts/nmconfig.test.mjs` to `pnpm test`, plus `yaml` as a dev dependency. The test checks that `.no-mistakes.yaml` is at the repository root and that it parses to `rebase.strategy: merge`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change adds a small root `.no-mistakes.yaml` that sets `rebase.strategy: merge`, rewrites the clone-workflow instruction in AGENTS.md from rebase to merge, and adjusts one sentence in engine/AGENTS.md. The round-1 fix is in place: the guard test now parses the file with the real `yaml` package, checks the meaning of the setting, and asserts the file sits at the repository root. The dependency and lockfile changes are consistent with that.

## Testing

I ran the new guard test on the target commit. Then I checked it in a temporary clone: the quoted and inline-map spellings pass, while removing the setting, commenting it out, changing it to rebase, or moving the file off the root all fail. These are unit-level checks of the guard, not live runs, so their scenarios are recorded as untested. I also replayed the scout's nearby-line control in a scratch git repository. Rebasing, the old instruction, rewrote history so the submitted head was no longer an ancestor. Merging, the new instruction, kept it as one with both edits intact. A merge over uncommitted changes was refused, as the new wording says. I could not drive the daemon live, because this gate phase may not run `no-mistakes init` or start a run; the scout's report says it already ran that path on v1.79.0. There is no UI surface, so there are no screenshots. Temporary clones were removed and the worktree is clean.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 2 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The repo's no-mistakes config sits at the root and its parsed rebase.strategy is merge, so `pnpm test` passes | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: this was a unit-level parsing test of the config (guard-test-head.txt), not the daemon consuming it. |
| Adversarial: changing, commenting out, removing, or moving the setting off the root fails the guard test, while valid quoted and inline-map YAML still passes | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: this ran the guard test against changed copies of the config in a temporary clone (guard-test-mutations.txt), which checks the guard, not the live da… |
| A worker following the new AGENTS.md instruction (`git merge origin/main`) after main edits a line next to its submitted change keeps the submitted head as an ancestor; the old rebase instruction does… | ✅ pass | live | git-merge-vs-rebase.txt |
| A worker who merges with uncommitted changes is refused and the branch is left unchanged, as the new 'commit first, then merge, then push' wording says | ✅ pass | live | git-merge-vs-rebase.txt |
| The no-mistakes v1.79.0 daemon reads rebase.strategy: merge from the default-branch root copy and accepts a resubmitted branch whose main moved nearby, including custody recovery after an abort | ⏸️ untested | no | The gate-phase boundary forbids running `no-mistakes init`, starting a run, or controlling another pipeline, and the daemon honours the setting only from main's copy, so it takes effect after landing.… |

body:
# Description

`backends/LND.test.ts` only covered `getURL`. This adds `backends/LND.request.test.ts` (100 tests) for the shared request core. It is a separate file so it does not conflict with the open PRs that edit `LND.test.ts`.

- Request assembly: method, URL, macaroon and content-type headers, JSON body, query params, the lndhub URL/token fallback, `certVerification` to `trusty`, default and per-call transport timeouts.
- 2xx parsing, including newline-delimited stream bodies.
- Error fallback: status 300, string bodies, empty and non-string bodies ("Connection error"), transport rejections.
- The 30 s transport timeout race and the in-flight call cache (sharing, cache key includes the body, eviction after success, failure and timeout, `clearCachedCalls`).
- Tor path: body, headers, `.onion` TLS bypass, timeout pass-through, eviction on failure.
- `payLightningInvoice`: the timed-out result at `timeout_seconds` + 1 s beats the transport timeout at + 5 s, the 60 s default, a node answer before and after the deadline.
- All 47 fixed capability flags by exact value, and each of the 12 version-gated flags at its minimum version and one patch below.

Each key test was checked by temporarily breaking the targeted line in `LND.ts` and confirming the test fails.

Problems found, not fixed here (tests pin current behavior):
- `restReq` builds an `Error` from `errorInfo.message` inside a `try` whose own `catch` discards it, so every non-2xx response rejects with the raw body string (e.g. `{"code":2,"message":"invoice is already paid"}`). Screens using `errorToUserFriendly` re-parse it; anything showing `err.message` shows raw JSON. A fix will update the "raw body" tests.
- A request that times out can, when its fetch finally resolves, delete a newer identical request from the call cache.
- The 30 s race timer is not cleared after a response.

#4492 changes the `payLightningInvoice` timed-out shape and adds `supportsPaymentLookup`; four payment tests and the flag table will need updating if it lands first. #4963 adds `supportsChannelMemo`.

author: pawper
body:
0.9.1: the runner path never on Windows and never assuming hosted minutes, a Deploy workflow nothing has to fill, a sync by feature that will not add competing tools, the real migration folder, old duplicates as cleanup, the guard's throttle off by default, a queue that runs from a copy, a fallback that says so

Closes #62, closes #63, closes #64.

Deploys (Drawabit #62, ZestyZealy #64, Stations #63)
- The runner path is only a Linux or macOS runner. On Windows the build cannot write the output without Developer Mode, and with it Vercel rejects the prebuilt upload: Next 16's segment functions are symlinks that Windows does not upload as symlinks (ZestyZealy run 38185111455). runner_os_pick and deploy_path take the runner's OS and whether hosted minutes exist; the setup refuses a runner path with only Windows runners.
- A private repository is assumed to have no hosted minutes (DEPLOY_HOSTED overrides), so the plan and the Vercel-built fallback run on the runner; with neither, the setup chooses the guard, which needs no workflow.
- deploy.yml reads where its jobs run from the DEPLOY_RUNNER and DEPLOY_JOBS_ON variables and its interval from .claude/deploy.json, so neither the sync nor the setup edits it. It needs no jq, every step is bash on Linux or macOS, and on the guard path it exits with one line instead of failing every hour.
- A fallback to a Vercel build raises a warning in the run, and the nightly audit names it, so a project does not pay build minutes silently.
- The guard's throttle is off by default: a throttled build waits for the next push, and the day's last merge would not ship. Turning it on prints that risk.
- .claude/deploy.json takes neverShips, the project's own folders that never ship (DEPLOY_NEVER_SHIPS at setup).
- The setup uses gh only with a GitHub remote; without one gh waited for an answer.

Sync
- templates/OWNED.txt groups the plugin's files by feature, each with a main file. The sync refreshes every plugin file a project has but adds missing files only for a feature whose main file is present; others are reported as not used, since the project may have its own tools (Drawabit's own board-state script and status builder). --only FEATURE applies one feature and reports nothing else. Replayed on Drawabit: plain mode adds only its two missing deploy files; --only deploy adds those five and nothing else.
- Copied scripts are pinned to LF in .gitattributes when the repository would check them out CRLF (tested on a fresh CRLF repository).
- RUNS_ON is never copied from an expression, and a placeholder is filled only as a whole word (DEPLOY_RUNS_ON would have been mangled).
- The config defaults come only with the core feature.
- A migration glob that matches no file while a common folder holds migrations is reported with the line to write, and a numbering.txt the sync adds gets the real folder (Stations: "migrations/*.sql" against supabase/migrations).
- A hand-written guard is replaced by the guard path, merged or not.
- Every command printed names the plugin by its real path; the brief prints it on a "Plugin:" line, and the rules say $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is empty in the Bash tool.

Numbering and the queue
- next-number warns when its glob matches nothing and names the folder that fits, instead of answering 0001.
- numbering-check reports a duplicate already on the base as one-time cleanup and fails only on duplicates the change adds; the "D56twice" message has its space.
- The merge queue copies its scripts to a temporary folder at start and runs from there, so switching the checkout mid-drain cannot change it.

Version 0.9.1; 621 tests.

author: copilot
body:
In the iOS mini app (`app.html`), some game rows weren't tappable, and friend profiles gave no way to browse a friend's games, wishlist or achievements. The user also wants alerts delivered when the app isn't open. This PR covers the first two points; the third is not changed (see below).

- **Game info from any row**
  - Taps on game rows now open the game detail screen from every list: library, favourites, home, friend games, friend wishlist, and rows inside an open detail screen. Previously friend game rows were opted out and the detail overlay had no click handler.
  - Rows carry an optional `data-open-f` (owner) attribute. `findGame(p, t, f)` looks in your library, then the friend's library, then your favourites, then falls back to `{title, platform}`. A game outside your library still opens, with reduced detail.
  - Click handling is shared through `openFromEvent`, which skips the favourite button.

- **Friend detail tabs**
  - Games shows the friend's full library. It was previously capped at 5 recent games.
  - Wishlist is loaded from `accounts/<user>/wishlist.json`, or from demo storage in demo mode.
  - Achievements is unchanged apart from the cap, which goes from 10 to 50.
  - Wishlist rows are also tappable. Small tab styles are added to `styles.css`.

- **Service worker**
  - The cache version in `sw.js` is bumped to `v6` so installed PWAs pick up the new `app.html`.

**Not changed: background notifications.** Closed-app delivery already depends on the existing Web Push path, which needs `gameOS_pushBackendUrl` or `gameOS_devBackendUrl` and an API token saved on the device. It also needs notification permission, iOS 16.4 or later, and the app added to the Home Screen. Without those, alerts only arrive while the app is open. Fixing this means configuring or deploying the push backend, not a client change.

body:
Refs #458 (the PR targets the release branch, so the issue is closed by hand: "Fixed in #PR (1.4.49-beta)").

## What changed
- `parseSVG()` (`lib/snugcut.js`): after the part's center is known and before `measureScale()`/`buildOutline()`, every sampled point must be finite and within 1e9 mm of the center (`COORD_LIMIT`, 1e12 Clipper units, far below the 2^52 range where Clipper stops returning; 1e9 leaves room for later unit or DPI changes). Otherwise it throws `svg.tooLarge`.
- `dxfToSVG()`: `P()`, through which every emitted point passes, throws `dxf.tooLarge` for a coordinate that is not finite or is past 1e9 mm.
- New messages `svg.tooLarge` and `dxf.tooLarge` in `MESSAGES`, `app/strings-en.js` (`lib.*`) and the README "Library messages" table. Six repro files in `fixtures/security/`, listed in `fixtures/README.md`. 1.4.49-beta, CHANGELOG entry (Security), rebuilt `snugcut.html`.

## Verified
Each repro run in its own headless Chrome, killed after 20 s:

| File | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| huge-svg-coords.svg (`M0 0 H1e13 V1e13 Z`) | HANG (killed at 20 s) | `svg.tooLarge`, 1 ms |
| huge-svg-arc.svg (`A1e-9 1e9 ...`) | HANG | `svg.tooLarge`, 1 ms |
| huge-dxf-polyline.dxf (closed LWPOLYLINE, 1e15) | HANG | `dxf.tooLarge`, 1 ms |
| huge-dxf-lines.dxf (3 LINEs, 1e15) | HANG | `dxf.tooLarge`, 1 ms |
| huge-dxf-circle.dxf (CIRCLE r 1e15) | HANG | `dxf.tooLarge`, 1 ms |
| huge-dxf-bulge.dxf (bulge 1e300) | HANG | `dxf.tooLarge`, 1 ms |

Message: "<name> has coordinates beyond 1,000,000,000 mm, so it is too large and wasn't added."

Boundary (one path, 100 mm viewBox, each in its own Chrome): squares of 1e6, 1e8, 4e8 and 1.9e9 mm import in 1 ms; 2.1e9 mm is refused; a 50 mm square 1e8 mm from the origin imports normally (the limit is from the part's center).

## Regression
`python3 tools/regression.py origin/release/1.5.0-beta snugcut.html`, run with the six new fixtures set aside (the old build hangs on them, which is the bug):
```

```
With the new fixtures in place, new against new: 108 compared, 0 differ (OK, byte-identical), so they are handled the same way each run. Note: until this is the baseline, `tools/regression.py` against an older build will hang on these six fixtures.

`build.py --check` and `qa_workbooks.py --check` pass.

# Description

`backends/CLNRest.test.ts` only covered `getURL`. This adds `backends/CLNRest.request.test.ts` (95 tests). It is a separate file so it does not conflict with the open PRs that edit `CLNRest.test.ts`.

- Request path: URL, `Rune` and content-type headers, method, body, query params, `certVerification` to `trusty`, default and per-call timeouts, newline-delimited responses, the in-flight call cache, "Request timeout" and cache eviction, Tor arguments.
